2.5.1.1: Nārada said: We have heard the excellent, bliss-giving account of Śambhu as a householder, together with the good stories of the Gaṇas, Skanda and others. ॥1॥
2.5.1.2: Now, with great kindness, tell the excellent, supreme account of how Śaṅkara, as Rudra, slew the wicked while sporting. ॥2॥
2.5.1.3: How did the mighty Lord burn the three cities of the enemies of the gods simultaneously with a single arrow—with what arrow? ॥3॥
2.5.1.4: Narrate all this account of the moon-crested one, the Lord who ever sports through his māyā, which always gives delight to gods and sages. ॥4॥
2.5.1.5: Brahmā said: O best of sages, when this was asked in the same way long ago by Vyāsa, Sanatkumāra related it; that very account I now narrate. ॥5॥
2.5.1.6: Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O greatly wise Vyāsa, to the account of the moon-crested one—how the destroyer of the universe burned Tripura with a single arrow. ॥6॥
2.5.1.7: When the demon Tāraka had been slain by Skanda, Śiva's son, his three sons, the Daityas, were sorely grieved, O lord of sages. ॥7॥
2.5.1.8: Tārakākṣa was the eldest, Vidyunmālī the middle one, and Kamalākṣa the youngest; all were always equal in strength. ॥8॥
2.5.1.9: They had conquered their senses, were well prepared, self-restrained, truthful, firm-minded, great heroes—and yet hostile to the gods. ॥9॥
2.5.1.10: Those three went to a cave of Meru and, giving up all fine and most charming enjoyments, performed a most wondrous austerity. ॥10॥
2.5.1.11: In spring, abandoning all desires and the sound of song and instruments along with festivity, those three sons of Tāraka performed austerities. ॥11॥
2.5.1.12: In summer, overcoming the sun's glare, they kindled fires in the four directions and, standing in their midst, reverently offered oblations for the sake of success. ॥12॥
2.5.1.13: Struck down by the great heat, all of them became utterly faint; in the rains, free of fear, they bore the downpour on their heads. ॥13॥
2.5.1.14: In autumn, though hungry, they gave away abundant food—delightful, rich, wholesome, heart-pleasing, excellent fruits and roots— ॥14॥
2.5.1.15: —and conquering hunger and thirst through restraint, giving these and drinks of every kind to the hungry, they became like stones. ॥15॥
2.5.1.16: In winter those great-souled ones, taking refuge on a mountain, stood without support, facing the four directions, with supreme fortitude. ॥16॥
2.5.1.17: In the cold season, their bodies covered with frost, wrapping their bodies in water-soaked linen garments, they stood in the midst of water. ॥17॥
2.5.1.18: Then, undaunted, they all gradually increased their austerity; those three excellent sons of his practised penance directed towards Brahmā (Vidhi). ॥18॥
2.5.1.19: Undertaking fierce austerity and established in supreme discipline, those foremost Dānavas emaciated their own bodies by penance. ॥19॥
2.5.1.20: For a hundred years, placing one foot on the ground and standing there, those very mighty ones performed supreme austerity. ॥20॥
2.5.1.21: For a thousand years those most fierce, evil-minded ones lived on air and performed austerity, reaching extreme torment. ॥21॥
2.5.1.22: Likewise for a thousand years they stood on their heads, and for a hundred years they stood with arms raised up. ॥22॥
2.5.1.23: Thus these Daityas, bent on obstinate resolve, underwent extreme hardship; in this manner those Daityas remained, tireless day and night. ॥23॥
2.5.1.24: Thus a long time passed for those sons of Tāraka, who practised good austerity with minds fixed on Brahmā, in a righteous way—such is my view, O sage. ॥24॥
2.5.1.25: Then Brahmā, the great preceptor of gods and demons, of great fame, pleased by their austerity, appeared in order to grant a boon. ॥25॥
2.5.1.26: Then, together with sages, gods and demons, the grandsire of all beings addressed all of them with these soothing words: ॥26॥
2.5.1.27: Brahmā said: I am pleased with your austerity, O great Daityas —O sage. I will give you everything; state the boon you desire. ॥27॥
2.5.1.28: For what purpose has this great austerity been performed? Tell me, O enemies of the gods. I am always the giver of the fruit of everyone's austerity, the maker of all. ॥28॥
2.5.1.29: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing his words, all of them, with joined palms, bowed to the Grandsire and slowly spoke what was in their minds. ॥29॥
2.5.1.30: The demons said: If you are pleased, O lord of gods, and if a boon is to be given by you, grant us invulnerability for all of us from all beings. ॥30॥
2.5.1.31: Make us enduring, O lord of the world; may all adversaries such as old age and disease spare us, and may death never approach us anywhere. ॥31॥
2.5.1.32: May we all become free from old age and immortal—this is our wish. We shall make all others in the three worlds subject to death. ॥32॥
2.5.1.33: What use is vast wealth, what use are splendid cities, other abundant pleasures, or again position and sovereignty— ॥33॥
2.5.1.34: when one is surely seized by death within five days? For such a one everything is in vain, O Brahmā—this is indeed our firm conviction. ॥34॥
2.5.1.35: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of the ascetic Daityas, Brahmā (Vidhi), remembering his own lord Śiva, Giriśa, replied. ॥35॥
2.5.1.36: Brahmā said: There is no complete immortality; therefore desist, O Asuras. Choose another boon, whatever kind pleases you. ॥36॥
2.5.1.37: Any creature that is born will surely be slain somewhere, O Asuras; none in the world, on the earth, will be free from old age and immortal— ॥37॥
2.5.1.38: except Khaṇḍaparaśu (Śiva), the Death of Death, and likewise Hari; those two are beyond dharma and adharma, unmanifest yet having manifest forms. ॥38॥
2.5.1.39: Even if austerity is performed for the oppression of the world, it should be known to have become fruitful; therefore your austerity has been well performed. ॥39॥
2.5.1.40: Considering this yourselves with your intellect—that which is impossible for gods and demons, rare or extremely hard to accomplish—evade death by some other means, O sinless ones. ॥40॥
2.5.1.41: Therefore, relying on your resolve, choose some cause for your death, through which death, though not directly chosen, may keep it away from each of you separately. ॥41॥
2.5.1.42: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words of Brahmā, they remained in meditation for a moment; then, having reflected, they spoke to the Grandsire of all the worlds. ॥42॥
2.5.1.43: The demons said: O Lord, though we are possessed of valour, we have no dwelling, unassailable by enemies, in which we may live happily. ॥43॥
2.5.1.44: Construct and give us three most wondrous cities, rich in every kind of wealth and unassailable by the gods. ॥44॥
2.5.1.45: Thus occupying the three cities, we shall roam over this earth, O Lord of the worlds, by your grace, O Teacher of the world. ॥45॥
2.5.1.46: Then Tārakākṣa said: Let Viśvakarman make for me a city of gold that is impenetrable even by the gods. ॥46॥
2.5.1.47: Kamalākṣa asked for a very great city of silver, and Vidyunmālī, delighted, asked for a great one of hard iron. ॥47॥
2.5.1.48: O Brahmā, when these cities stand at one place, at the midday hour of Abhijit, when the moon is positioned in Puṣya, ॥48॥
2.5.1.49: when, one above the other, they are invisible in the sky amid sportive clouds, and when the dark clouds named Puṣkarāvarta are raining, ॥49॥
2.5.1.50: thus at the end of a thousand years we shall meet one another; these cities will become one — not otherwise. ॥50॥
2.5.1.51: Then the god who embodies all the gods, as a marvel to all of us, standing on an impossible chariot furnished with all equipment, ॥51॥
2.5.1.52: may pierce our cities with a single inconceivable arrow. Kṛttivāsas, who is ever without enmity towards us, ॥52॥
2.5.1.53: and who is worthy of our homage, worship and salutation — how could he burn us? Keeping this in mind, we ask it; such a one is hard to find on earth. ॥53॥
2.5.1.54: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard their words, Brahmā, the Grandsire of the worlds and creator, remembering Śiva, said to them, so be it. ॥54॥
2.5.1.55: He also gave command to Maya: Make three cities — one of gold, one of silver and one of iron, O Maya. ॥55॥
2.5.1.56: Having thus instructed Maya, Brahmā visibly entered heaven, his own abode, while those sons of Tāraka looked on. ॥56॥
2.5.1.57: Then the steadfast Maya, by his austerity, made the cities: the golden one for Tārakākṣa, the silver one for Kamalākṣa, ॥57॥
2.5.1.58: and the iron one for Vidyunmālī — a threefold, excellent fortress. They are to be known as situated in heaven, in the sky and on earth respectively. ॥58॥
2.5.1.59: Having given the three cities to those asuras, Maya himself entered there, intent on their welfare. ॥59॥
2.5.1.60: Thus having obtained the three cities and entered them, the sons of Tāraka, of great strength and valour, enjoyed all pleasures. ॥60॥
2.5.1.61: The city was crowded with wish-fulfilling trees, thronged with elephants and horses, crowded with various palaces, and covered with networks of jewels; ॥61॥
2.5.1.62: adorned with aerial cars resembling the sun's disc, facing every direction, made of rubies and shining like the moon; ॥62॥
2.5.1.63: with palaces and divine gate-towers like the peaks of Kailāsa, crowded with celestial women, and with Gandharvas, Siddhas and Cāraṇas; ॥63॥
2.5.1.64: with shrines of Rudra in every house, with established fire-sacrifices, and with excellent twice-born versed in the scriptures, ever devoted to the worship of Śiva; ॥64॥
2.5.1.65: beautifully adorned with step-wells, wells, ponds and long lakes, and with gardens, groves and trees of the finest qualities, as if fallen from heaven; ॥65॥
2.5.1.66: ever adorned with rivers, streams and foremost lotus-lakes, and charming with many trees yielding the fruits of all desires; ॥66॥
2.5.1.67: decorated with herds of rutting elephants, splendid horses, chariots of various shapes and palanquins; ॥67॥
2.5.1.68: with separate pleasure-grounds set apart according to occasion, and with various separate halls for Vedic study; ॥68॥
2.5.1.69: It was never seen, even in mind or word, by sinful men; it is beheld by great souls of virtuous conduct, the meritorious. ॥69॥
2.5.1.70: That excellent place was purified everywhere by chaste wives devoted to serving their husbands and averse to wrongful conduct; ॥70॥
2.5.1.71: it was filled with heroic, highly fortunate Daityas together with their wives and sons, and with twice-born who knew the true meaning of Śruti and Smṛti and were devoted to their own duty; ॥71॥
2.5.1.72: with broad-chested, bull-shouldered warriors, ever skilled in conciliation and in war, some calm and some wrathful, some hunchbacked and some dwarfish; ॥72॥
2.5.1.73: resembling blue lotus petals, with dark curly hair, all protected by Maya, well trained and eager for battle. ॥73॥
2.5.1.74: That city was filled on all sides and well attended by warriors delighting in excellent battles, whose valour was purified by the worship of Brahmā and Śiva, who resembled the Sun, the Maruts and great Indra, crushers of the gods, exceedingly firm. ॥74॥
2.5.1.75: Whatever dharmas are proclaimed in the śāstras, Vedas and Purāṇas, ever dear to Śiva and the gods — those dharmas prevailed there everywhere. ॥75॥
2.5.1.76: Thus, having obtained their boons, those Daityas, the sons of Tāraka, dwelt there, relying on Maya, the devotee of Śiva. ॥76॥
2.5.1.77: Having driven out the inhabitants of all the three worlds and entered the cities, they ruled a great kingdom, ever devoted to the path of Śiva. ॥77॥
2.5.1.78: Then a long time passed, O sage, while they of meritorious deeds dwelt there, ruling a good kingdom as they pleased and to their contentment. ॥78॥
2.5.1.iti: Thus ends the first adhyāya, named Tripura described, in the account of the slaying of Tripura, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥1॥
2.5.2.1: Vyāsa said: O son of Brahmā, O greatly wise one, best of speakers, tell me: what happened after that? And how did the gods become happy? ॥1॥
2.5.2.2: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of Vyāsa, whose intellect is immeasurable, Sanatkumāra spoke, remembering the lotus-feet of Śiva. ॥2॥
2.5.2.3: Sanatkumāra said: Then the gods, Indra and the others, scorched by their (the demons') splendour, having consulted together, all went in distress to Brahmā for refuge. ॥3॥
2.5.2.4: All the gods, having bowed with affection to the Grandsire and gathered around him, then, seeing the right moment, made their misery known. ॥4॥
2.5.2.5: The gods said: O Creator, all of us dwellers of heaven have surely been tormented by Maya, the lord of Tripura, together with the sons of Tāraka. ॥5॥
2.5.2.6: Therefore, O Vidhi, we in distress have come to you for refuge. Devise the means of their destruction, so that we may be happy. ॥6॥
2.5.2.7: Sanatkumāra said: Thus addressed by the gods, Vidhi, the maker of the world, smiled and then replied to all of them, whose minds were afraid of Maya. ॥7॥
2.5.2.8: Brahmā said: O gods, you need not fear those Dānavas in particular. I shall tell you the means of their destruction; Śarva will bring about your welfare. ॥8॥
2.5.2.9: The Daitya was made to prosper by me, so he does not deserve death at my hands. Moreover, merit continues to grow in the city of Tripura. ॥9॥
2.5.2.10: So all of you gods, with Vāsava (Indra), entreat Śiva. If the Lord of all is pleased, he will accomplish your task. ॥10॥
2.5.2.11: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard Vidhi's words, all the gods with Vāsava, distressed, went to where the bull-bannered one (Śiva) dwells. ॥11॥
2.5.2.12: Having bowed with devotion to the Lord of gods, all of them then, with joined palms and bent shoulders, praised Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the worlds. ॥12॥
2.5.2.13: The gods said: Salutation to Hiraṇyagarbha, the ordainer of all creation; salutation to you, the maintainer, Viṣṇu, the mighty one. ॥13॥
2.5.2.14: Salutation to you in the form of Hara, who brings about the destruction of beings; salutation to you, the attributeless, Śiva of immeasurable radiance. ॥14॥
2.5.2.15: Salutation to the one free of states, changeless, pure effulgence, the very self of the great elements, untainted, the great soul. ॥15॥
2.5.2.16: Salutation to you, lord of beings, bearer of the great burden, remover of craving, whose form is free of enmity, of abundant radiance. ॥16॥
2.5.2.17: Salutation to you, the forest-fire that destroys the great forest of great Daityas, the axe for the trees that are the Daityas, the trident-bearer. ॥17॥
2.5.2.18: Salutation to you, O supreme Lord, destroyer of the great Dānavas; salutation to you, husband of Ambikā, O bearer of all weapons. ॥18॥
2.5.2.19: Salutation to you, O lord of Pārvatī, O supreme Self, O Maheśvara; salutation to you, the blue-throated Rudra, who has the form of Rudra. ॥19॥
2.5.2.20: Salutation to you, knowable through Vedānta; salutation to you, who are beyond all paths; salutation to you, whose nature is the guṇas, possessor of guṇas, yet devoid of guṇas. ॥20॥
2.5.2.21: O Mahādeva, salutation to you, the delight of the three worlds; salutation to you as Pradyumna, Aniruddha and Vāsudeva. ॥21॥
2.5.2.22: Salutation to you, the god Saṅkarṣaṇa, slayer of Kaṃsa; to you, crusher of Cāṇūra, O Dāmodara, swallower of poison. ॥22॥
2.5.2.23: O Hṛṣīkeśa, O Acyuta, O all-pervading one, O Mṛḍa, O Śaṅkara, salutation to you; O Adhokṣaja, O foe of the elephant demon, O enemy of Kāma, O drinker of poison. ॥23॥
2.5.2.24: Salutation to the god Nārāyaṇa, to the one devoted to Nārāyaṇa, to the one whose form is Nārāyaṇa, O you who arose from Nārāyaṇa's body. ॥24॥
2.5.2.25: Salutation to you, who have all forms, remover of great hells; salutation to you, destroyer of sin, O you whose mount is the bull. ॥25॥
2.5.2.26: Salutation to you who are Time in the form of moments and the rest, giver of strength to your devotees, of many forms, form itself, crusher of the host of Daityas. ॥26॥
2.5.2.27: Salutation to the god devoted to Brahmins, the benefactor of cows and Brahmins; to you of a thousand forms and a thousand limbs. ॥27॥
2.5.2.28: Salutation, O Hara, to you who are the form of dharma, sattva itself, whose self is sattva; salutation to you whose nature is knowable through the Vedas, who love the Vedas. ॥28॥
2.5.2.29: Salutation to the one whose form is the Veda; salutations again and again to the speaker of the Veda; to the one reached by the path of right conduct, who himself walks the path of right conduct. ॥29॥
2.5.2.30: Salutation to you, Viṣṭaraśravas, the embodiment of truth; salutation to you, lover of truth, truth itself, attainable through truth. ॥30॥
2.5.2.31: Salutation to you, the wielder of Māyā; salutation indeed to the lord of Māyā; salutation to you who abide in Brahman, who are Brahmā, and who are born of Brahmā. ॥31॥
2.5.2.32: Salutation to you, O Lord, who are austerity itself and who grant fruit through austerity; to the one ever worthy of praise, who is praise itself, whose heart is delighted by praise. ॥32॥
2.5.2.33: Salutation to the one pleased by conduct according to the Śruti, who loves the practice of praise, who has a fourfold form, who takes the form of beings born in water and on land. ॥33॥
2.5.2.34: O Lord, all the gods and others are your manifestations by virtue of their excellence. Among the gods you are Indra; among the planets you are considered the Sun. ॥34॥
2.5.2.35: Among the worlds you are Satyaloka; among rivers you are the celestial river (Gaṅgā); among colours you are white; among lakes you are Lake Mānasa. ॥35॥
2.5.2.36: Among mountains you are the father of Girijā (Himavat); among cows you are the wish-granting Kāmadhenu; among oceans the Ocean of Milk; among metals you are gold. ॥36॥
2.5.2.37: Among the classes you are the Brahmin; among men you are the king, O Śaṅkara; among the fields of liberation you are Kāśī; among sacred fords you are the king of tīrthas. ॥37॥
2.5.2.38: Among all stones you are crystal, O Maheśvara; among flowers you are the lotus; and likewise among mountains, the Himālaya. ॥38॥
2.5.2.39: You are the foremost in the dealings of speech; among poets you are Bhārgava (Śukra); among birds you are the Śarabha; among beasts of prey you are esteemed as the lion. ॥39॥
2.5.2.40: Among stones you are the Śālagrāma stone, O bull-bannered one; and among all forms worthy of worship, you are indeed the Narmadā liṅga. ॥40॥
2.5.2.41: You are Nandīśvara; among animals you are the bull, O Supreme Lord; among the Vedas you are in the form of the Upaniṣads; among sacrificers you are the moon, possessor of cool rays. ॥41॥
2.5.2.42: Among the blazing you are fire; among Śaivas you are Acyuta; you are the Bhārata among the Purāṇas, and you are the letter ma among syllables. ॥42॥
2.5.2.43: You are the praṇava (Om) among seed-mantras, poison among dreadful things; among the all-pervading you are indeed the sky, and among selves you are the Supreme Self. ॥43॥
2.5.2.44: Among the senses you are the mind; among gifts you are the gift of fearlessness; among purifiers you are water, and likewise among life-sustainers, nectar. ॥44॥
2.5.2.45: Among gains you are the gain of a son; you are the wind among the swift; among all daily rites you are held to be the sandhyā worship. ॥45॥
2.5.2.46: Among sacrifices you are the Aśvamedha; among the ages, the first age; you are Puṣya among all the lunar mansions; you are the new-moon day among lunar days. ॥46॥
2.5.2.47: Among all seasons you are spring; among all festivals, the saṅkrānti (sun's transit); you are kuśa among kinds of grass, and the banyan among great trees. ॥47॥
2.5.2.48: Among astral yogas you are Vyatīpāta, and among creepers the soma-creeper; among intellects you are the righteous intellect; among friends you are the wife. ॥48॥
2.5.2.49: Among pure spiritual practitioners you are prāṇāyāma, O Maheśvara; among all the Jyotirliṅgas you are held to be Viśveśvara. ॥49॥
2.5.2.50: Among all kinsmen you are dharma; among the life-stages you are the highest; among all aims you are liberation; among the Rudras, Nīlalohita. ॥50॥
2.5.2.51: Among the Ādityas you are Vāsudeva, and Hanumān among monkeys; among sacrifices you are the sacrifice of japa; you are Rāma among weapon-bearers. ॥51॥
2.5.2.52: Among the Gandharvas you are Citraratha; among the Vasus, surely Pāvaka; among months you are the intercalary month; among vows you are the fourteenth lunar day. ॥52॥
2.5.2.53: You are Airāvata among lordly elephants, held to be Kapila among the Siddhas; you are indeed Ananta among the Nāgas, and Aryaman among the ancestors. ॥53॥
2.5.2.54: And you are Time among those who reckon, and Bali among the Daityas. What use is saying more, O Lord of gods? Having pervaded the whole world, ॥54॥
2.5.2.55: you indeed stand with a single portion of yourself, both remaining outside and pervading it within. ॥55॥
2.5.2.56: Sanatkumāra said: Having thus praised Mahādeva, the bull-bannered, the trident-bearer, the Supreme Lord, with hymns of many kinds, divine, all the gods — ॥56॥
2.5.2.57: — distressed, shrewd in their own interest, led by Vāsava, with bowed shoulders and joined palms, spoke in reply of the matter at hand, their own purpose, O sage. ॥57॥
2.5.2.58: The gods said: O Mahādeva, O Lord, all the gods along with Vāsava have been defeated by the sons born of Tāraka — by the eldest together with his two brothers. ॥58॥
2.5.2.59: The three worlds have been brought under their control; likewise the best of sages and all the perfected ones have been crushed, and the whole world laid waste. ॥59॥
2.5.2.60: The dreadful one himself seizes all the sacrificial shares; unrighteousness has been set going by them, and the dharma of the sages has been obstructed. ॥60॥
2.5.2.61: The sons of Tāraka are certainly unslayable by any being; all creatures perform all their actions according to their will, O Śaṅkara. ॥61॥
2.5.2.62: Before the world is destroyed by the terrible Daityas dwelling in Tripura, let a plan be devised by which the world may be protected. ॥62॥
2.5.2.63: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words of the heaven-dwellers led by Indra as they spoke, Śiva gave his reply. ॥63॥
2.5.2.iti: Thus ends the second adhyāya, named The praise by the gods, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥2॥
2.5.3.1: Śiva said: This overlord of Tripura is indeed virtuous at present. Where merit prevails, such a one should never be killed by the wise. ॥1॥
2.5.3.2: O gods, I know the whole great distress of the gods. But those Daityas are very powerful and cannot be killed by gods and asuras. ॥2॥
2.5.3.3: All those sons of Tāraka, together with Maya, are meritorious; the slaying of them, of all the city-dwellers, is hard to accomplish. ॥3॥
2.5.3.4: How could I, though fierce in battle, knowingly commit treachery against a friend? Great sin in betraying a friend was declared long ago by Svayambhū. ॥4॥
2.5.3.5: For the slayer of a brahmin, for the drinker of liquor, for theft and likewise for one who has broken a vow, expiation has been prescribed by the good; for the ungrateful there is no expiation. ॥5॥
2.5.3.6: Those Daityas are my devotees; how can they be slain by me, O gods? Let this be considered by you, knowers of dharma, in accordance with dharma. ॥6॥
2.5.3.7: They should not be slain so long as they practise devotion to me. Nevertheless, O gods, this matter should be reported to Viṣṇu. ॥7॥
2.5.3.8: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard those words thus, all the gods led by Śakra quickly reported them first to Brahmā, O sage. ॥8॥
2.5.3.9: Then, placing Brahmā at their head, all the gods together with Vāsava quickly went to Vaikuṇṭha, which is full of splendour. ॥9॥
2.5.3.10: Having gone there and seen Hari, the gods, overcome with agitation, bowed and praised him with great devotion, their palms joined. ॥10॥
2.5.3.11: Thereafter, as before, they quickly reported the whole cause of their sorrow to that Viṣṇu, the mighty lord. ॥11॥
2.5.3.12: Then, having heard of the gods' distress inflicted by the dwellers of Tripura, and knowing their religious observance, Viṣṇu spoke these words. ॥12॥
2.5.3.13: Viṣṇu said: This statement is true indeed: where eternal dharma is, there sorrow does not arise, just as darkness does not when the sun is seen. ॥13॥
2.5.3.14: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words, the gods fell into sorrow and, their lotus-faces withered, spoke again to Viṣṇu. ॥14॥
2.5.3.15: The gods said: How then should it be done? How is sorrow to be removed? How may we become happy? How shall we survive? ॥15॥
2.5.3.16: How will the dharmas endure while Tripura remains alive? Surely all the dwellers of Tripura are givers of distress to the gods. ॥16॥
2.5.3.17: Either let the slaying of Tripura be arranged here by you, or else let an untimely destruction of the gods certainly be brought about. ॥17॥
2.5.3.18: Sanatkumāra said: Having spoken thus, those gods, grieving again and again, neither stayed at ease nor went away from the best of gods there. ॥18॥
2.5.3.19: Seeing them in such a state, dejected and full of humility, that glorious Nārāyaṇa too pondered thus in his mind: ॥19॥
2.5.3.20: What should be done by me, the helper of the gods, in the affairs of the gods? For those Daityas, the sons of Tāraka, are devotees of Śiva. ॥20॥
2.5.3.21: Having reflected thus at that time, the mighty Viṣṇu then called to mind the imperishable Yajñas for the sake of the gods' purpose. ॥21॥
2.5.3.22: By that mere remembrance of Viṣṇu, those Yajñas came quickly, that very instant, to where the lord of Śrī, Puruṣottama, dwells. ॥22॥
2.5.3.23: Then, bowing to Viṣṇu, the lord of sacrifice, the ancient Person, Hari, they praised him with palms joined. ॥23॥
2.5.3.24: The Lord, the eternal Acyuta, seeing them, the eternal Yajñas, and looking at the gods along with Indra, then spoke. ॥24॥
2.5.3.25: Viṣṇu said: O gods, with this very sacrifice constantly worship the Supreme Lord, for the destruction of the three cities and for the welfare of the three worlds. ॥25॥
2.5.3.26: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing the words of Acyuta, the wise god of gods, those gods lovingly bowed and praised the lord of sacrifice. ॥26॥
2.5.3.27: Having praised thus, the gods then worshipped the Sacrificial Person by the procedure prescribed for sacrifice, with all rites complete, O sage. ॥27॥
2.5.3.28: Then from that sacrificial fire-pit sprang up, by thousands, hosts of bhūtas, huge-bodied, bearing tridents, spears and maces as weapons. ॥28॥
2.5.3.29: The gods saw those hosts of bhūtas by thousands, with tridents, spears and maces in hand, armed with staffs, bows and stones, ॥29॥
2.5.3.30: furnished with various weapons and wearing various garbs, resembling Kālāgnirudra, like the sun at the time of dissolution. ॥30॥
2.5.3.31: Seeing those bhūtas standing before him, the glorious Viṣṇu, lord of sacrifice and upholder of Rudra's command, bowed and spoke to them. ॥31॥
2.5.3.32: Viṣṇu said: O bhūtas, ready for the gods' purpose, hear my words: let all of you go at once to Tripura, for you are exceedingly strong. ॥32॥
2.5.3.33: Having gone, burnt, split and shattered the three cities of the Daityas, O bhūtas, you should return as you came, for the welfare of the worlds. ॥33॥
2.5.3.34: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing the Lord's words, those hosts of bhūtas bowed to that god of gods and went to the three cities of the Daityas. ॥34॥
2.5.3.35: Having gone there and entering it, they were at once reduced to ashes in the splendour of Tripura's lord, like moths in fire. ॥35॥
2.5.3.36: Those few who survived, bent on flight, came out and quickly arrived, distressed, near Hari. ॥36॥
2.5.3.37: Seeing them and hearing that whole incident, the Lord Hari, Puruṣottama, pondered in his mind: ॥37॥
2.5.3.38: What is to be done now?—with anguished mind, having perceived that all the immortals, together with Vāsava, were distressed. ॥38॥
2.5.3.39: How, having destroyed by force the three cities of those Daityas, shall I accomplish the gods' work?—thus he was overwhelmed with anxiety. ॥39॥
2.5.3.40: There is no destruction of the most righteous through hostile magic rites, no doubt—so the Lord himself, who establishes the authority of Vedic conduct, has declared. ॥40॥
2.5.3.41: All those Daityas dwelling in Tripura are indeed most righteous; therefore those foremost of Asuras have attained invulnerability, and not otherwise. ॥41॥
2.5.3.42: Even having committed a very great sin, they worship Rudra; thereby they are freed from all sins, as a lotus leaf remains untouched by water. ॥42॥
2.5.3.43: O gods, through the worship of Rudra all desires are indeed fulfilled; the wealth of manifold enjoyments comes under one's control on earth. ॥43॥
2.5.3.44: Therefore the Daityas, devoted to the worship of the liṅga, are enjoyers of that—of manifold wealth here and of liberation too in the hereafter. ॥44॥
2.5.3.45: Therefore, having created an obstacle to the dharma of those very Daityas by my own māyā, for the sake of the gods' cause I shall destroy Tripura in a moment. ॥45॥
2.5.3.46: Having reflected thus, the Lord, the Supreme Person, then set about creating an obstacle to the dharma of those enemies of the gods. ॥46॥
2.5.3.47: As long as the Vedic dharmas remain, as long as there is worship of Śaṅkara, and as long as there are pure observances, so long there can be no destruction of them. ॥47॥
2.5.3.48: Therefore it must be done thus: the Vedic dharma should then depart from them; the Daityas will abandon the worship of the liṅga—there is no doubt. ॥48॥
2.5.3.49: Having thus resolved, Viṣṇu then devised, for obstructing the dharma of those Daityas, a means: the refutation of the Veda (śruti). ॥49॥
2.5.3.50: Then Viṣṇu, the helper of the gods, commissioned by Śiva himself at Śiva's command for the protection of the three worlds, spoke to the gods. ॥50॥
2.5.3.51: Viṣṇu said: O gods, all of you go to your own abodes, surely. I shall accomplish the gods' task according to my understanding; there is no doubt. ॥51॥
2.5.3.52: With great effort I shall certainly make them averse to Rudra; and knowing them to be bereft of devotion to him, I shall reduce them to ashes. ॥52॥
2.5.3.53: Sanatkumāra said: O sage, those immortals, reassured, placing his command on their heads, went to their respective abodes, trusting and supremely delighted. ॥53॥
2.5.3.54: Then Viṣṇu did what was supremely beneficial for the gods' sake; let that very account, destroyer of all sins, be heard properly. ॥54॥
2.5.3.iti: Thus ends the third adhyāya, named The bhūtas and the dharma of Tripura, in the account of the slaying of Tripura, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥3॥
2.5.4.1: Sanatkumāra said: And Acyuta, of great splendour, created a man born from his own self, a single being made of illusion (māyā), for the purpose of obstructing their dharma. ॥1॥
2.5.4.2: He was shaven-headed, in soiled clothes, furnished with a bowl, holding a broom in his hand and moving it at every step; ॥2॥
2.5.4.3: likewise with a hand holding a cloth, always placed at his mouth, a sage uttering dharma in a faltering voice. ॥3॥
2.5.4.4: Having bowed to that Viṣṇu, he then stood before him, and there, with joined palms, he spoke these words to Hari. ॥4॥
2.5.4.5: O destroyer of foes, Acyuta, worshipful one, what shall I do? Command me that. What are my names, O God? And tell me also my abode, O Lord. ॥5॥
2.5.4.6: Having heard his auspicious words thus, Lord Viṣṇu, pleased at heart, spoke these words. ॥6॥
2.5.4.7: Viṣṇu said: Learn for what purpose you have been created; I shall tell you. O you born of my body, O greatly wise one, you are of my own form, no doubt. ॥7॥
2.5.4.8: Born from my body, you ought to do my work. You are mine and will always be worthy of worship, no doubt. ॥8॥
2.5.4.9: Your name shall be Arihan; other names are not auspicious. I shall tell you your abode later; now listen attentively to the matter at hand. ॥9॥
2.5.4.10: O illusionist, a treatise made of illusion, of sixteen thousand verses, opposed to śruti and smṛti, devoid of varṇa and āśrama, ॥10॥
2.5.4.11: a treatise in Apabhraṃśa, consisting likewise of the doctrine of karma — compose it with effort; its spread will come about. ॥11॥
2.5.4.12: I grant you the capacity for its composition; it will come about. And varied illusion will quickly be under your control. ॥12॥
2.5.4.13: Having heard those words of Hari, the Supreme Self, the illusionist bowed and replied to Janārdana. ॥13॥
2.5.4.14: The shaven-headed ascetic said: Whatever I must do, O God, command that quickly, O Lord. By your command all my work will be fruitful. ॥14॥
2.5.4.15: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this, Viṣṇu taught him the treatise made of illusion, which holds that the experience of heaven and hell is here alone and not otherwise. ॥15॥
2.5.4.16: Viṣṇu, remembering Śiva's lotus feet, spoke to him again: All these demons dwelling in Tripura are to be deluded. ॥16॥
2.5.4.17: They must surely be initiated and taught with effort. By my command no sin will attach to you, O great-minded one. ॥17॥
2.5.4.18: There the dharmas of śruti and smṛti shine forth, no doubt. By this lore they must all certainly be shattered, O ascetic. ॥18॥
2.5.4.19: O shaven one, you should go for the destruction of the dwellers of Tripura. Proclaiming the dharma of darkness (tamas), destroy the three cities. ॥19॥
2.5.4.20: And then, going again from there, you must remain in the desert region, O mighty one, according to your own dharma, until Kali arrives. ॥20॥
2.5.4.21: When that age has begun, let your own dharma be proclaimed; and it must be carried on by you again through disciples and disciples' disciples. ॥21॥
2.5.4.22: By my command your dharma will certainly spread. Ever intent on my permission, you will attain my state. ॥22॥
2.5.4.23: Thus the command was then given by the mighty Viṣṇu; and Hari, following at heart the command of the God of gods, vanished. ॥23॥
2.5.4.24: Then that shaven one, obeying Hari's command, created four disciples resembling his own form, and then himself taught them the treatise made of illusion. ॥24॥
2.5.4.25: As he himself was, so were those four splendid shaven ones; having bowed to Hari, the Supreme Self, they stood there. ॥25॥
2.5.4.26: And Hari too, supremely pleased, the upholder of Śiva's command, then himself spoke there to those four sages. ॥26॥
2.5.4.27: As your teacher is, so shall you be by my command. You are blessed; you will attain a good state here, no doubt. ॥27॥
2.5.4.28: Then those four shaven ones, adopting a heretical dharma, holding bowls in their hands and wearing cloths over their mouths, ॥28॥
2.5.4.29: wearing only soiled garments, sparing of speech, and saying with great delight, may you have the gain of dharma (dharmo lābhaḥ), the supreme truth, ॥29॥
2.5.4.30: carrying brooms made of strips of cloth, and moving very slowly out of fear of harming living beings, indeed; ॥30॥
2.5.4.31: all of them then, full of joy, bowed again to the divine Lord there, O sage, and stood before him. ॥31॥
2.5.4.32: Then Hari took them by the hand and entrusted them to the teacher, and with great affection declared their names specifically: ॥32॥
2.5.4.33: As you are, so too these are mine, no doubt. And your name, of the primal form — because you are worshipful, you are called Pūjya. ॥33॥
2.5.4.34: Ṛṣi, Yati, Ākīrya and Upādhyāya — let these names too become well known for you. ॥34॥
2.5.4.35: And my auspicious name too should be taken up by you: Arihan — that name, destroyer of sin, is to be meditated upon. ॥35॥
2.5.4.36: And you must do work that brings happiness to the world; for those who act in accord with the world there will be the highest state. ॥36॥
2.5.4.37: Sanatkumāra said: Then the illusionist, with his disciples, bowed to him, the doer of Śiva's will, and at once went himself to Tripura, O sage. ॥37॥
2.5.4.38: Having swiftly entered that city, the self-controlled sage, urged on by that great master of illusion Viṣṇu, then worked his illusion. ॥38॥
2.5.4.39: Taking up residence with his disciples in a grove near the city, he then set in motion an illusion that could delude even the masters of illusion. ॥39॥
2.5.4.40: But because of the power of their worship of Śiva, O sage, his illusion did not quickly take effect in Tripura, and the ascetic then became dejected. ॥40॥
2.5.4.41: Then he remembered Viṣṇu and praised him much in his heart, his enthusiasm lost, his mind confused, with a heart that was distressed. ॥41॥
2.5.4.42: Remembered by him, Viṣṇu quickly remembered Śaṅkara in his heart; having received his command mentally, he swiftly called Nārada to mind. ॥42॥
2.5.4.43: As soon as Viṣṇu remembered him, Nārada appeared; having bowed and praised, he then stood before him with joined palms. ॥43॥
2.5.4.44: Then Viṣṇu, foremost of the wise, ever devoted to the welfare of the worlds and accomplishing the gods' work, spoke to Nārada. ॥44॥
2.5.4.45: By Śiva's command it is said, dear one: go quickly to Tripura. The sage has gone there with his disciples to delude its inhabitants. ॥45॥
2.5.4.46: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing his words, Nārada, best of sages, went quickly to where that sage, foremost of illusionists, was. ॥46॥
2.5.4.47: Nārada too, likewise wielding illusion by the command of the lord of illusion, entered that city and was initiated by that illusionist. ॥47॥
2.5.4.48: Then Nārada went into the presence of the lord of Tripura and, after inquiring about his welfare and so forth, reported everything to the king. ॥48॥
2.5.4.49: Nārada said: A certain ascetic has come here, devoted to dharma, truly excelling in all knowledge and endowed with supreme Vedic learning. ॥49॥
2.5.4.50: Though we have seen many dharmas, none is equal to this. Having seen this eternal dharma here, we have been duly initiated. ॥50॥
2.5.4.51: If you have a desire for that dharma, O best of Daityas, then, great king, you too should take initiation into that dharma. ॥51॥
2.5.4.52: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing his words, pregnant with great meaning, the lord of the Daityas was amazed at heart and, deluded, spoke there. ॥52॥
2.5.4.53: Since Nārada has been initiated, we too shall receive initiation. Knowing this, he went there himself. ॥53॥
2.5.4.54: Then, seeing his form and thus deluded by illusion, he bowed to that great soul and spoke these words to him. ॥54॥
2.5.4.55: The lord of Tripura said: You must give me initiation, O sage of pure intent. I shall become your disciple—truly, truly, without doubt. ॥55॥
2.5.4.56: Hearing these sincere words of the Daitya king, that ancient sage replied with great care. ॥56॥
2.5.4.57: If my command is to be carried out, O best of Daityas, then I shall give initiation—not otherwise, even with countless efforts. ॥57॥
2.5.4.58: Hearing these words, the king became wholly possessed by illusion and, with joined palms, quickly spoke to that ascetic. ॥58॥
2.5.4.59: The demon said: Whatever command you give, it shall be done just so and not otherwise. I will not transgress your command—truly, truly, without doubt. ॥59॥
2.5.4.60: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing then these words of the lord of Tripura, the best of sages removed the cloth from his mouth and spoke. ॥60॥
2.5.4.61: Take this initiation, O lord of Daityas, the very highest among all dharmas, by the rite of which you will attain fulfilment. ॥61॥
2.5.4.62: Having said this, that illusionist swiftly gave the Daitya king the initiation prescribed by his own dharma, according to rule. ॥62॥
2.5.4.63: When the Daitya king had been initiated together with his brothers, O sage, all the inhabitants of Tripura there became initiated. ॥63॥
2.5.4.64: Then, O sage, the whole of Tripura was quickly pervaded by the disciples and disciples' disciples of that great illusionist sage. ॥64॥
2.5.4.iti: Thus ends the fourth adhyāya, named The rite of initiation in Tripura, in the dialogue of Sanatkumāra and Pārāśarya, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥4॥
2.5.5.1: Vyāsa said: When the king of the Daityas had been initiated and deluded by that deceiver, what did the deceiver say then, and what did that lord of the Daityas do? ॥1॥
2.5.5.2: Sanatkumāra said: Having given initiation to him, the ascetic Arihan, whose lotus feet were served by disciples such as Nārada, spoke to the king of the Daityas. ॥2॥
2.5.5.3: Arihan said: Listen, O lord of the Daityas, to my words, filled with true knowledge, the whole essence of Vedānta, a secret supreme and most excellent. ॥3॥
2.5.5.4: Worldly existence is beginningless and self-established, devoid of a creator and of action; it arises of itself and dissolves of itself. ॥4॥
2.5.5.5: From Brahmā down to a blade of grass, whatever is bound to a body—there the self alone is the one lord; there is no second ruler over it. ॥5॥
2.5.5.6: As for the names Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra, these names belong to embodied beings, just as for us the name Arihan and the like is spoken. ॥6॥
2.5.5.7: Just as the body of us and others dissolves in its own time, so too the body of all from Brahmā down to the mosquito dissolves in its own time. ॥7॥
2.5.5.8: When this body is examined, nothing is greater anywhere in one than another; food, sexual union, sleep and fear are the same everywhere. ॥8॥
2.5.5.9: Every embodied being, when hungry and obtaining its measure of food, attains the same satisfaction, neither greater nor otherwise. ॥9॥
2.5.5.10: Just as we, when thirsty, become free of thirst on joyfully drinking a drink, so too do others who are thirsty; there is no difference, lesser or greater. ॥10॥
2.5.5.11: Let there be thousands of women, abodes of form and loveliness; yet at the time of love-making only one is enjoyed here. ॥11॥
2.5.5.12: Let there be hundreds of excellent horses, let there be many of many kinds; yet for riding only one serves a person, not a second. ॥12॥
2.5.5.13: The happiness that arises in sleep for those who lie on couches—that same happiness comes through sleep to beings who lie on the ground. ॥13॥
2.5.5.14: Just as embodied beings like us fear death, so do all from Brahmā down to the worm fear death. ॥14॥
2.5.5.15: If it is considered with the intellect, all embodied beings are equal. Having determined this, no one should harm anyone anywhere. ॥15॥
2.5.5.16: Nowhere on the face of the earth is there a dharma equal to compassion for living beings; therefore people should practise compassion for living beings with every effort. ॥16॥
2.5.5.17: When one living being is protected, the three worlds are protected; when one is killed, they are likewise killed. Therefore one should protect and not kill. ॥17॥
2.5.5.18: Non-violence is the highest dharma; sin is the tormenting of oneself; liberation is independence from others; heaven is eating what one desires. ॥18॥
2.5.5.19: This has been declared with certainty by earlier sages as true authority; therefore men who fear hell should not commit violence. ॥19॥
2.5.5.20: In the three worlds with their moving and unmoving beings there is no sin like violence. The violent man goes to hell; the non-violent goes to heaven. ॥20॥
2.5.5.21: There are many gifts—what use are they, yielding trifling fruit? Here there is not even one supreme gift equal to granting freedom from fear. ॥21॥
2.5.5.22: Here four gifts have been declared by the great sages, after considering various scriptures, for welfare in this world and the next. ॥22॥
2.5.5.23: Freedom from fear should be given to the frightened, medicine likewise to the sick; knowledge should be given to seekers of knowledge, and food to one afflicted by hunger. ॥23॥
2.5.5.24: Whatever many gifts have been spoken of here by the sages, they are not worth a sixteenth part of the gift of fearlessness to living beings. ॥24॥
2.5.5.25: Indeed the power of gems, mantras and herbs is of inconceivable efficacy; it should be practised with effort for acquiring fame and wealth. ॥25॥
2.5.5.26: Having acquired wealth abundantly, the twelve āyatanas should be worshipped all around; what is the use of worshipping others here? ॥26॥
2.5.5.27: The group of five organs of action, the five organs of perception, mind and intellect—these are here declared to be the auspicious twelve āyatanas. ॥27॥
2.5.5.28: Heaven and hell for living beings are right here, not anywhere else. Happiness is called heaven, and suffering is indeed hell. ॥28॥
2.5.5.29: The giving up of the body while pleasures are being enjoyed—this alone should be known by thinkers on reality as the supreme liberation. ॥29॥
2.5.5.30: When the afflictions together with their latent impressions are certainly uprooted, the cessation of ignorance—this should be known by thinkers on reality as liberation. ॥30॥
2.5.5.31: This scriptural text is declared authoritative by those who expound the Veda: One should not harm any beings. No other text that promotes violence is authoritative. ॥31॥
2.5.5.32: The text agniṣṭomīyam, prescribing the victim, is misleading, upheld by the wicked here; for the wise it is no authority, since it causes the slaughter of animals. ॥32॥
2.5.5.33: Having cut down trees, killed animals, made a mire of blood, and burnt sesame, ghee and the like in the fire—how strange that heaven is desired thereby. ॥33॥
2.5.5.34: Having thus declared his own doctrine to the lord of Tripura and made all the citizens hear it, the ascetic spoke again with earnestness— ॥34॥
2.5.5.35: —then he taught dharmas laid down in the Buddhist scriptures, outside the Veda, which produce conviction through visible results and serve solely to accomplish bodily pleasure. ॥35॥
2.5.5.36: What is declared by śruti thus—'bliss is the form of Brahman'—should be understood here exactly so; the notion of multiplicity is false. ॥36॥
2.5.5.37: As long as this body is healthy, as long as the senses are not impaired, as long as old age is far off, so long should one secure pleasure. ॥37॥
2.5.5.38: In ill health, in impairment of the senses, and in old age, whence can there be pleasure? Therefore those who seek happiness should give even their body to supplicants. ॥38॥
2.5.5.39: He whose life is not spent in gratifying the wishes of those who beg—by him this earth is burdened, not by oceans, mountains and trees. ॥39॥
2.5.5.40: The body passes away swiftly; accumulations end in decline. Knowing this, the wise one should secure bodily pleasure. ॥40॥
2.5.5.41: This body is a morning meal for dogs, crows and worms, and that body ends in ashes: this truth is recited in the Veda. ॥41॥
2.5.5.42: This distinction of caste is imagined in the worlds for nothing. Since humanity is common to all, who is low and who is high? ॥42॥
2.5.5.43: This is the creation beginning with Brahmā, so the elders declare. Two sons were born to him, renowned as Dakṣa and Marīci. ॥43॥
2.5.5.44: By Kaśyapa, son of Marīci, thirteen fair-eyed daughters of Dakṣa were married, indeed by the lawful path. ॥44॥
2.5.5.45: And now, by present-day mortals of little intellect and strength, this deliberation — this woman may be approached, that one may not — is made in vain. ॥45॥
2.5.5.46: The four classes, born from the mouth, arms and thighs of the Creator, arose together; this notion devised by the ancients does not hold up on examination. ॥46॥
2.5.5.47: If ever four sons were born in a single body, or from a single father, how could they obtain different classes? ॥47॥
2.5.5.48: Therefore this division into class and non-class does not appear true. Hence no one should anywhere consider distinction among human beings. ॥48॥
2.5.5.49: Sanatkumāra said: Having spoken thus to the lord of the Daityas and to the citizens, O sage, that ascetic, with his disciples, zealously destroyed the Vedic dharmas. ॥49॥
2.5.5.50: He undermined the great dharma of women, centred on devotion to the husband, and likewise the self-control of all men. ॥50॥
2.5.5.51: He undermined especially the duties toward the gods, and likewise the rites of śrāddha, the duties of sacrifice, vows and the like, and particularly śrāddha at sacred fords; ॥51॥
2.5.5.52: especially the worship of Śiva preceded by the adoration of the liṅga, and the worship of Viṣṇu, Sūrya, Gaṇeśa and others performed according to rule; ॥52॥
2.5.5.53: and all bathing, giving and the like, particularly at the time of the festival days — all this that ascetic, the deluder, foremost of illusionists, demolished. ॥53॥
2.5.5.54: What need of saying much, O best of brahmins? In Tripura, by that deluder, whatever Vedic dharmas there were — all of them were driven far away. ॥54॥
2.5.5.55: All the women of Tripura, deluded and taking refuge in the ascetic's doctrine, abandoned the excellent disposition of serving their husbands. ॥55॥
2.5.5.56: Having practised the art of attraction and also that consisting of subjugation, the men, deluded, made them fruitful with others' wives. ॥56॥
2.5.5.57: The women moving in the inner apartments, likewise the young princes, the citizens and the city's women too — all were deluded by them. ॥57॥
2.5.5.58: Thus, when all the citizens had become wholly averse to their own dharmas, adharma flourished exceedingly. ॥58॥
2.5.5.59: And, O lord, the Māyā of Viṣṇu, god of gods, by his command — and Alakṣmī herself by his order — went to Tripura. ॥59॥
2.5.5.60: The Lakṣmī whom they had obtained through austerity as a boon from the lord of gods abandoned them and went out, at the order of lord Brahmā. ॥60॥
2.5.5.61: Having given them such delusion of mind, fashioned by the Māyā of Viṣṇu, that Nārada at once became one whose purpose was accomplished. ॥61॥
2.5.5.62: Nārada too had taken the same form as the deluder; even so he was not perverted, owing to the grace of the Supreme Lord. ॥62॥
2.5.5.63: The king of the Daityas too, O sage, together with his two brothers and with Maya, had his power blunted there, by the will of Śiva. ॥63॥
2.5.5.iti: Thus ends the fifth adhyāya, named The deluding of Tripura, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥5॥
2.5.6.1: Vyāsa said: When that lord of the Daityas, together with the citizens and his brothers, had been thus deluded, what happened then, O Sanatkumāra? Tell it all, O lord. ॥1॥
2.5.6.2: Sanatkumāra said: When Tripura had become like this, the Daitya having abandoned the worship of Śiva, the entire dharma of women destroyed, and wicked conduct established, ॥2॥
2.5.6.3: Hari, the lord of Lakṣmī, as though his purpose were accomplished, went with the gods to Kailāsa to report that conduct to the lord of Umā. ॥3॥
2.5.6.4: Having stationed himself near it with the gods, that lord of Ramā, and then Brahmā too, with supreme and intense concentration— ॥4॥
2.5.6.5: having reached the Omniscient One with the mind, then Hari, the Supreme Person, together with Brahmā, praised Śaṅkara with pleasing words. ॥5॥
2.5.6.6: Viṣṇu said: Salutation to you, the god Maheśvara, the Supreme Self, Nārāyaṇa, Rudra, Brahman, whose form is Brahman. ॥6॥
2.5.6.7: Having done so and prostrated like a staff before Mahādeva, he recited the Rudra mantra that originates from Dakṣiṇāmūrti. ॥7॥
2.5.6.8: Standing in water, the lord, with his mind absorbed in him, recited it one and a half crore times, remembering in his mind Śambhu, his own lord, the Supreme Lord. ॥8॥
2.5.6.9: Meanwhile, then, all the gods, with their minds fixed on him, praised Maheśvara. ॥9॥
2.5.6.10: The gods said: Salutation to you, the Self of all, Śaṅkara, remover of affliction, Rudra, the blue-throated one, whose form is consciousness, the wise one. ॥10॥
2.5.6.11: You indeed are always our refuge, the remover of all calamities; you alone are always to be worshipped by all souls, O slayer of the gods' enemies. ॥11॥
2.5.6.12: You are the beginning and you are beginningless, self-blissful, the imperishable lord, the direct creator of Prakṛti and of Puruṣa too, the lord of the world. ॥12॥
2.5.6.13: You alone are the maker of the worlds, the sustainer, and you alone the destroyer, becoming Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Hara through the guṇas of rajas, sattva and tamas. ॥13॥
2.5.6.14: You are the deliverer in this world, the imperishable ruler of all, the giver of boons, consisting of speech, the one to be expressed, yet free from the distinction of expressed and expresser. ॥14॥
2.5.6.15: You, the Lord, are to be entreated for liberation by yogins who are the best knowers of yoga; you indeed dwell in the cavity of the heart-lotus of yogins. ॥15॥
2.5.6.16: The Vedas and the virtuous declare you to be of the nature of the Supreme Brahman; they now call you the Reality, the mass of radiance, higher than the highest. ॥16॥
2.5.6.17: That which they call the Supreme Self in this world, O lord, is you alone, O Śarva, O Self of all, O lord of the three worlds, O Bhava. ॥17॥
2.5.6.18: All that is seen, heard, praised and known is you, O guru of the world; they call you smaller than the atom and greater even than the great. ॥18॥
2.5.6.19: That which has hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads and faces everywhere, ears and noses everywhere—you I salute on every side. ॥19॥
2.5.6.20: O all-pervading one, you the omniscient, lord of all, unveiled, of universal form, the odd-eyed one—you I salute on every side. ॥20॥
2.5.6.21: You, the lord of all, overseer of worldly existence, the Truth, the auspicious, the unsurpassed, radiant like ten million suns—you I salute on every side. ॥21॥
2.5.6.22: You, the god of the universe, without beginning or end, comprising the thirty-six principles, having no lord above you, and the impeller of all—you I salute on every side. ॥22॥
2.5.6.23: You, the impeller of Prakṛti, the great-grandsire of all, the Lord whose body is everything—you I salute on every side. ॥23॥
2.5.6.24: Thus do the Śrutis, and those who know the essence of the Śrutis, describe you—the boon-giver, the abode of all, the self-born, the knower of the essence of the Śrutis. ॥24॥
2.5.6.25: Whatever, invisible to us and manifold, has been made by you in the world is you; the gods, Asuras, Brāhmaṇas and others too, the stationary and the moving, resort to you alone. ॥25॥
2.5.6.26: Protect us gods, who have no other refuge, O Śambhu, beloved of the gods, who are nearly ruined because of Tripura, by slaying the Asuras in an instant. ॥26॥
2.5.6.27: They are now deluded by your māyā, O Supreme Lord; by the device declared by Viṣṇu they have been made to forsake dharma, O lord. ॥27॥
2.5.6.28: Those Daityas, having wholly abandoned all dharma and taken refuge in the Buddhist scriptures, have become so by the power of our good fortune, O you who love your devotees. ॥28॥
2.5.6.29: You are always the accomplisher of the gods' tasks, O giver of refuge; we have taken refuge in you—do as you wish. ॥29॥
2.5.6.30: Sanatkumāra said: Having thus praised Maheśāna, the gods stood before him, with palms joined, dejected, their bodies bowed down. ॥30॥
2.5.6.31: Thus praised by Indra and the other gods, and by Viṣṇu's japa, the Lord of all came there, delighted, mounted on his bull. ॥31॥
2.5.6.32: Having descended from Nandin and embraced Viṣṇu, with a gracious mind, his hand supported by Nandin, he looked there upon all with a kindly glance. ॥32॥
2.5.6.33: Then Hara, the lord of Pārvatī, pleased, looking upon the gods and Hari with a compassionate gaze, spoke in a deep voice. ॥33॥
2.5.6.34: Śiva said: I have now understood this task of the gods, O lord of the gods, and also the power of Viṣṇu's māyā and of the wise Nārada. ॥34॥
2.5.6.35: I shall bring about the destruction of the three cities of those Daityas devoted to adharma, O best of gods; there is no doubt. ॥35॥
2.5.6.36: But those great Daityas are my devotees, firm of mind. Should they then be slain by me myself, when they have abandoned the highest dharma only through a ruse? ॥36॥
2.5.6.37: Let Viṣṇu or someone else slay them, since all the Daityas dwelling in Tripura have been made to abandon dharma and are devoid of devotion to me. ॥37॥
2.5.6.38: Hearing these words of Śambhu, all the heaven-dwellers became downcast, and Hari too, O lord of sages. ॥38॥
2.5.6.39: Seeing the gods and Viṣṇu dispirited, Brahmā the ordainer, maker of the world, with joined palms before Śambhu, spoke these words. ॥39॥
2.5.6.40: Brahmā said: There is no sin whatsoever for you, since you are the foremost knower of yoga, the Supreme Lord, the Supreme Brahman, ever the protector of gods and sages. ॥40॥
2.5.6.41: By your command alone they are deluded; you are the one who impels them. Though they have abandoned their own dharma and your worship, still they cannot be slain by others. ॥41॥
2.5.6.42: Therefore, O Mahādeva, protector of the lives of gods and sages, the barbarian (mleccha) races must be slain by you for the protection of the good. ॥42॥
2.5.6.43: For a king who does this, that sin does not exist according to dharma, and so for you too. Therefore a king should protect the twice-born and the good, and should clear away the thorns. ॥43॥
2.5.6.44: Thus should a king act, here and elsewhere, if he desires his own kingdom. Yours is the lordship of all worlds; therefore protect us without delay. ॥44॥
2.5.6.45: The chief sages and lords, likewise the sacrifices, the Vedas, the scriptures and all the rest, are your subjects, O lord of the gods of gods; and I and Viṣṇu too, certainly. ॥45॥
2.5.6.46: You are the sovereign over the gods, the emperor, the lord of all, O Lord. This entire world, beginning with Hari, is your retinue alone. ॥46॥
2.5.6.47: Hari is your crown prince, O Unborn One; I, Brahmā, am your royal priest; Śakra is the executor of royal affairs, the guardian of your command. ॥47॥
2.5.6.48: The other gods too, O lord of all, governed by your command, always perform their respective duties. This is true, true; there is no doubt. ॥48॥
2.5.6.49: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard this speech of Brahmā, the Supreme Lord Śaṅkara, protector of the gods, pleased at heart, replied to Vidhi (Brahmā). ॥49॥
2.5.6.50: Śiva said: O Brahmā, if I am proclaimed king of the gods and emperor, I have none of the corresponding equipment which I, as lord, might take up here. ॥50॥
2.5.6.51: There is no great divine chariot of that sort, together with a charioteer, nor bow, arrows and the like that bring victory in battle, ॥51॥
2.5.6.52: mounting which, taking up bow and arrows and fixing my mind, I would slay the demons in battle, however powerful they may be. ॥52॥
2.5.6.53: Sanatkumāra said: Now the gods, with Brahmā, with Indra and Upendra, overjoyed on hearing the Lord's words, bowed and spoke to Maheśvara. ॥53॥
2.5.6.54: The gods said: O lord of the gods, O Maheśvara, we shall become that equipment of yours—the chariot and the rest—ready for battle, O Master. ॥54॥
2.5.6.55: Having said this, all the gods together, understanding Śiva's wish, pleased and with joined palms, spoke individually. ॥55॥
2.5.6.iti: Thus ends the sixth adhyāya, named The praise of Śiva, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥6॥
2.5.7.1: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words of all the gods and the others, Hara, the refuge of all and loving to his devotees, accepted them with great delight. ॥1॥
2.5.7.2: Meanwhile, O sage, the goddess Śivā, accompanied by her two sons, came to the place where Hara was, attended by the gods. ॥2॥
2.5.7.3: Then, seeing Śivā arrived, all of them, Viṣṇu and the others, quickly bowed down, very humble, astonished, their agitation gone. ॥3॥
2.5.7.4: O sage, all of them uttered the good and auspicious word, victory, and then remained silent, not knowing the reason for her coming. ॥4॥
2.5.7.5: Then the goddess, praised by all the gods and full of wondrous playfulness, spoke lovingly to her lord, who is skilled in manifold sports. ॥5॥
2.5.7.6: The Goddess said: O mighty one, best among those who have sons, look at your son, the six-faced one, playing, shining like the sun, adorned with excellent ornaments. ॥6॥
2.5.7.7: Sanatkumāra said: Thus addressed with these words by the Mother of the worlds, Śiva, the Lord, could not be sated as he drank the nectar of Skanda's face. ॥7॥
2.5.7.8: Maheśvara did not remember the gods who had come, oppressed by his own splendour; embracing Skanda and smelling his head, he rejoiced greatly. ॥8॥
2.5.7.9: Then the Mother of the world, skilled in many sports, having conferred with the Lord right there and stayed a little while, rose up. ॥9॥
2.5.7.10: Then Śambhu, with Nandin, together with the six-faced one and with her, the daughter of the king of mountains, playfully entered the palace, being saluted by all the gods. ॥10॥
2.5.7.11: Then all those gods, O sage, greatly perturbed and dejected, stood beside the door of the wise God of gods. ॥11॥
2.5.7.12: What is to be done? Where shall we go? Who will give us happiness? What now, what now? Thus it came about, and they cried, alas, we are ruined! ॥12॥
2.5.7.13: Looking at one another, Śakra and the others became extremely distressed; cursing their own fate, they spoke broken words. ॥13॥
2.5.7.14: Some gods said, we here are sinners; others, we are unfortunate; and still others, those lords of the Daityas are fortunate. ॥14॥
2.5.7.15: Just then, hearing their many cries, the greatly powerful Kumbhodara struck the gods with his staff. ॥15॥
2.5.7.16: Seized with fear, the gods fled crying alas, alas; others, the sages, fell down, and there was utter distress. ॥16॥
2.5.7.17: Indra, extremely shaken, sank to the ground on his knees; other divine sages, greatly distressed, fell on the earth. ॥17॥
2.5.7.18: All the sages and gods, equally agitated, came together and gathered near Vidhi (Brahmā) and Hari, whose minds were friendly to them. ॥18॥
2.5.7.19: Ah, this is the power of fate! So then all the sages, Kaśyapa and the others, said to Hari, the remover of the world's fear. ॥19॥
2.5.7.20: Other Brahmins said, through misfortune the task has not been accomplished; others, greatly astonished, said, why has this obstacle arisen? ॥20॥
2.5.7.21: Hearing these words spoken by Kaśyapa and the others, O sage, Hari, comforting the sages and gods, took up speech. ॥21॥
2.5.7.22: Viṣṇu said: O gods and all sages, listen attentively to my words. Why have you fallen into sorrow? Give up all sorrow. ॥22॥
2.5.7.23: O gods, consider that the worship of the Great One is not easy to accomplish; it is heard that in worshipping the Great One sorrow comes first, and, O gods, knowing your firmness, he surely becomes pleased — ॥23॥
2.5.7.24: — Śiva, the supreme Lord, the ruler of all the gaṇas, becomes pleased quickly. Let all of you consider in your hearts how he may be won over. ॥24॥
2.5.7.25: First uttering the praṇava (Om), one should then say namaḥ, then śivāya, and after that śubha twice; ॥25॥
2.5.7.26: then kuru twice is prescribed, then again śivāya, and namaḥ and the praṇava — this mantra, O wise ones, repeat always. ॥26॥
2.5.7.27: If you repeat it again for Śambhu's sake, then, having thus done one crore (ten million) of japa, Śiva will accomplish the task. ॥27॥
2.5.7.28: When this had been said then by the mighty Hari, the gods again performed the worship of Hara accordingly, O sage. ॥28॥
2.5.7.29: Hari too, together with Vidhi (Brahmā), his mind fixed on Śiva, performed japa for the accomplishment of the gods' purpose and especially that of the sages. ॥29॥
2.5.7.30: Repeatedly saying Śiva, the gods, endowed with fortitude, completed a count of a crore and then remained waiting, O best of sages. ॥30॥
2.5.7.31: Meanwhile Śiva himself appeared in person, in the form described, and spoke these words: ॥31॥
2.5.7.32: Śrī Śiva said: O Hari, O Vidhi, O gods and sages of auspicious vows, I am pleased with this japa; ask for the boon you desire. ॥32॥
2.5.7.33: The gods said: If you are pleased, O lord of gods, lord of the world, Śaṅkara, then, knowing the gods to be distressed, let the three cities be destroyed. ॥33॥
2.5.7.34: Protect us, O supreme Lord, friend of the afflicted, source of compassion; by you alone have the gods always been protected from calamities again and again. ॥34॥
2.5.7.35: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words spoken by them along with Hari and Vedhas (Brahmā), Maheśa then laughed inwardly, O Brahmin, and spoke again. ॥35॥
2.5.7.36: Maheśa said: O Hari, O Vidhi, O gods and all sages, listen attentively to my words, considering the three cities as already destroyed. ॥36॥
2.5.7.37: The chariot, a divine charioteer, the bow and the excellent arrow — all that was previously agreed upon, provide without delay. ॥37॥
2.5.7.38: O Viṣṇu, O Vidhi, you are surely the lord of the three worlds; you should carefully make for me all the arrangements befitting a supreme sovereign. ॥38॥
2.5.7.39: Considering the three cities as destroyed, you two, entrusted with creation and preservation, will with effort render help to the gods. ॥39॥
2.5.7.40: This mantra is greatly meritorious, producing my pleasure, auspicious, bestowing enjoyment and liberation, granting all desires, and bringing one to the Śaiva state. ॥40॥
2.5.7.41: It is blessed, bringing fame and long life to men who seek heaven and desires; for the desireless it is final emancipation, and for the liberated it grants enjoyment and liberation. ॥41॥
2.5.7.42: The man who, having become pure, always recites this mantra, or hears it, or causes others to hear it, would obtain all desires. ॥42॥
2.5.7.43: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words of Śiva, the Supreme Self, all the gods attained joy, and likewise Hari and Brahmā rejoiced even more. ॥43॥
2.5.7.44: By his command, Viśvakarmā fashioned, for the sake of the world, a divine, supremely beautiful chariot composed of all the gods. ॥44॥
2.5.7.iti: Thus ends the seventh adhyāya, named The praise by the gods, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥7॥
2.5.8.1: Vyāsa said: O Sanatkumāra, all-knowing, foremost of Śaivas, of noble mind, dear one, this wondrous story of the Supreme Lord has been narrated to me. ॥1॥
2.5.8.2: Now tell me about the building of the supreme chariot made of the gods, the divine chariot that was made for Śiva by the wise Viśvakarman. ॥2॥
2.5.8.3: Sūta said: Having heard these words of Vyāsa, that lord of sages Sanatkumāra spoke, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva. ॥3॥
2.5.8.4: Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O Vyāsa of great wisdom, O sage, to the making of the chariot and the rest. I shall tell it as far as I understand, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva. ॥4॥
2.5.8.5: Then for the god Rudra, Viśvakarman built with effort and reverence a divine chariot made of all the worlds, ॥5॥
2.5.8.6: made of all beings, golden, approved by all. Its right wheel was the Sun, and its left the Moon. ॥6॥
2.5.8.7: The right wheel had twelve spokes and the left sixteen. In those spokes of the right wheel, O best of Brahmins, were the twelve Ādityas. ॥7॥
2.5.8.8: The sixteen spokes of the left wheel were the digits of the Moon, O you of good vows; and likewise the constellations were the ornament of that same left wheel. ॥8॥
2.5.8.9: The six seasons were the rims of those two wheels, O bull among Brahmins; the mid-space was the puṣkara front body, and Mandara was the chariot's seat. ॥9॥
2.5.8.10: The Setting Mountain and the Rising Mountain, those two are known as the shafts; the great Meru was the base, and the Keśara mountains the supports. ॥10॥
2.5.8.11: The years were its speed; the two solar courses (ayanas) the junctions of the wheels; the muhūrtas were its frame-pieces, and the kalās are known as its yoke-pins. ॥11॥
2.5.8.12: Its kāṣṭhās are known as the nose-points, the kṣaṇas as the axle-rods, the nimeṣas as the bottom-boards, and the lavas as the poles. ॥12॥
2.5.8.13: Heaven was the protective cover of this chariot; heaven (svarga) and liberation (mokṣa) its two banners; Bhramā and Kāmadughā are known as the two tips at the ends of its yoke. ॥13॥
2.5.8.14: Likewise the manifest principle was the pole-shaft, and growth (vṛddhi) its naḍvala reed-frame; ego (ahaṅkāra) its corners, and the elements are known as its strength. ॥14॥
2.5.8.15: The senses were its ornaments all around, and faith was the motion of this chariot, O best of sages. ॥15॥
2.5.8.16: Then the six Vedāṅgas were its ornaments, and the Purāṇas, Nyāya, Mīmāṃsā and the Dharmaśāstras its secondary ornaments, O you of good vows. ॥16॥
2.5.8.17: The excellent ones, endowed with all auspicious marks, were the supports of its strength; the mantras are known as its bells, the varṇas as their feet, and likewise the āśramas. ॥17॥
2.5.8.18: Then the binding was Ananta, adorned with a thousand hoods; the directions were the feet of this chariot, and also the intermediate directions. ॥18॥
2.5.8.19: Puṣkara and the others were the banners, golden and adorned with gems; the four oceans are known as its chariot-blankets. ॥19॥
2.5.8.20: The Gaṅgā and the other foremost rivers, adorned with all ornaments, with chowries held at their fingertips, all shining in women's forms, ॥20॥
2.5.8.21: taking their places here and there, beautified the chariot. Likewise the seven winds Āvaha and the rest were the excellent golden stairway. ॥21॥
2.5.8.22: The Lokāloka mountain formed its side-steps all around; and likewise the outer region and the splendid Mānasa lake and the rest were part of it. ॥22॥
2.5.8.23: All the boundary mountains of the varṣas are known as its cords all around; and all the dwellers of the nether regions were the floors of that chariot. ॥23॥
2.5.8.24: The charioteer was Lord Brahmā, and the gods are known as the holders of the reins; the goad of that Brahmā was the praṇava, whose deity is Brahmā. ॥24॥
2.5.8.25: The syllable a was the great umbrella, Mandara the bearer of the side-staff; the lord of mountains was his bow, and the bowstring the king of serpents himself. ॥25॥
2.5.8.26: The bell of the bow was the goddess Sarasvatī in the form of the Veda; the arrow was Viṣṇu of great splendour, and Agni is declared the arrowhead. ॥26॥
2.5.8.27: Its horses, likewise, are said to be the four Vedas, O sage; the remaining luminaries beyond these were their ornaments. ॥27॥
2.5.8.28: The army was born of poison; the winds are known as the musicians; and the sages headed by Vyāsa became the drivers of the steeds. ॥28॥
2.5.8.29: I tell it in few syllables—what use is much speech, O lord of sages? Whatever thing exists in the cosmic egg, that is held to be in the chariot. ॥29॥
2.5.8.30: Thus the auspicious arrangement of the chariot and the rest was properly made by the wise Viśvakarman at the command of Brahmā and Viṣṇu. ॥30॥
2.5.8.iti: Thus ends the eighth adhyāya, named The chariot and the other arrangements for the battle, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥8॥
2.5.9.1: Sanatkumāra said: Brahmā harnessed the Vedas as horses to that chariot, so made, supremely divine and full of many wonders, and offered it to Śiva. ॥1॥
2.5.9.2: Having presented it to Śambhu and having entreated many times the lord of gods, honoured by Viṣṇu and the other gods, he made the trident-bearer mount it. ॥2॥
2.5.9.3: Then Śambhu, the great Lord, who embodies all the gods, mounted that divine chariot fitted with its protective rampart. ॥3॥
2.5.9.4: And he was praised by the sages, by gods, gandharvas and serpents, by Viṣṇu and Brahmā, and by the guardians of the worlds. ॥4॥
2.5.9.5: Surrounded by troops of apsarases skilled in song, the boon-giving Śambhu shone; and he looked at the charioteer. ॥5॥
2.5.9.6: As he was mounting the chariot fashioned and assembled from the worlds, the horses born of the Vedas fell headlong to the ground. ॥6॥
2.5.9.7: The earth shook, all the mountains trembled, and Śeṣa suddenly quaked, distressed, unable to bear that weight. ॥7॥
2.5.9.8: Then the blessed Lord, the upholder of the earth, taking the form of a great bull, rose from beneath this chariot and held it steady for a moment. ॥8॥
2.5.9.9: In another moment the great bull too sank to the earth on his knees, unable to bear the intense splendour of Maheśa mounted on the chariot. ॥9॥
2.5.9.10: Then the blessed Brahmā, reins in hand, lifted up the horses and, at the god's command, set the excellent chariot steady. ॥10॥
2.5.9.11: Then Brahmā, standing on the excellent chariot, urged on the harnessed horses made of the Vedas, swift as mind and wind, ॥11॥
2.5.9.12: toward the three cities of the mighty Dānavas, which stood in the sky, once Maheśa had taken his seat. ॥12॥
2.5.9.13: Then the blessed Rudra Śaṅkara, looking at the gods, said: Grant me lordship over the paśus (bound beings); then I will slay the asuras. ॥13॥
2.5.9.14: O best of gods, only after assigning the state of paśu separately to the gods and likewise to the others can those chief Daityas be slain, not otherwise. ॥14॥
2.5.9.15: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of the wise god of gods, all fell into dejection, apprehensive about becoming paśus. ॥15॥
2.5.9.16: Then, knowing their feeling, Śambhu, god of gods and husband of Ambikā, smiled and out of compassion spoke thus to those gods. ॥16॥
2.5.9.17: Śambhu said: O best of gods, let there be no fall for you even in the state of paśu. Hear the release from paśu-hood, and let it be practised. ॥17॥
2.5.9.18: Whoever practises the divine Pāśupata vow will be released from paśu-hood—this I truly promise you; listen attentively. ॥18॥
2.5.9.19: And any others who perform my Pāśupata vow will also be released from paśu-hood, O best of gods; there is no doubt. ॥19॥
2.5.9.20: Whoever performs this service lifelong, or for twelve years, or half that, or for three years, is freed from paśu-hood. ॥20॥
2.5.9.21: Therefore, O best of gods, you will practise this supreme divine vow; then you will be released from paśu-hood—of this there is no doubt. ॥21॥
2.5.9.22: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of Maheśa, the supreme Self, the gods, Hari, Brahmā and the rest, said, so be it. ॥22॥
2.5.9.23: Therefore all the foremost gods and asuras are the paśus of the Lord, and Rudra is Paśupati, the releaser from the bonds of the paśus. ॥23॥
2.5.9.24: Then this name of the great Lord, Paśupati, truly became renowned in all the worlds, bestowing welfare. ॥24॥
2.5.9.25: Then all the gods and sages, joyfully crying victory, rejoiced exceedingly—the lord of gods, Brahmā, Viṣṇu and others too. ॥25॥
2.5.9.26: The form that the great-souled one assumed at that time cannot be described even in hundreds of years. ॥26॥
2.5.9.27: Thus Maheśāna, lord of Maheśānī and of all, the giver of happiness to all, went forth to destroy Tripura. ॥27॥
2.5.9.28: Then, following that god of gods as he went to destroy Tripura, all of them, radiant as the sun, led by the king of immortals, went on elephants, horses, excellent lions, chariots and bulls. ॥28॥
2.5.9.29: With ploughs, trees, maces and bhuśuṇḍīs, weapons like great mountains, themselves mountain-like, their arms bearing various weapons, the lords of gods then went forth delighted. ॥29॥
2.5.9.30: Rich in various weapons, supremely radiant, in great festivity, proclaiming Śambhu's victory, those led by Indra, the lotus-born Brahmā and Viṣṇu then went before that Maheśvara. ॥30॥
2.5.9.31: All the sages, staff in hand and wearing matted locks, rejoiced; the sky-goers, siddhas and cāraṇas showered rains of flowers. ॥31॥
2.5.9.32: And all the lords of the gaṇas went to the three cities, O chief of brahmins. Who can count them? I shall name some. ॥32॥
2.5.9.33: Bhṛṅgī, foremost of all gaṇa-chiefs, surrounded by gaṇa-lords and hosts of gods, mounted an aerial car like great Indra and went with his forces to destroy Tripura. ॥33॥
2.5.9.34: Keśa, Vigatavāsa, Mahākeśa, Mahājvara, Somavallīsavarṇa, Somapa and Sanaka; ॥34॥
2.5.9.35: Somadhṛk, Sūryavarcas, Sūryapreṣaṇaka, Sūryākṣa, Sūrināman, Sura and Sundara; ॥35॥
2.5.9.36: Praskanda, Kundara, Caṇḍa, Kampana and Atikampana, Indra and Indrajava, Yantā and Himakara; ॥36॥
2.5.9.37: Śatākṣa, Pañcākṣa, Sahasrākṣa, Mahodara, Satījuha, Śatāsya, Raṅka and Karpūrapūtana; ॥37॥
2.5.9.38: Dviśikha and Triśikha, likewise Ahaṅkārakāraka, Ajavaktra, Aṣṭavaktra, Hayavaktra and Ardhavaktraka— ॥38॥
2.5.9.39: these and many other heroic, immeasurable gaṇa-leaders, beyond all definable marks, went forth surrounding the Lord. ॥39॥
2.5.9.40: Surrounding Mahādeva, they then attended the Pināka-bearer—they who could burn the universe with all its moving and unmoving beings in a moment by mere thought. ॥40॥
2.5.9.41: His gaṇas are capable of burning this entire world; so why would Pinākī himself need to go here to burn Tripura? And what need does Śambhu have here of a chariot, of his arrow, of gaṇas, or of the hosts of gods? ॥41॥
2.5.9.42: Yet he himself, the Pināka-wielder, O Vyāsa, went there together with his own gaṇas to burn those three cities of the enemies of the gods — he who is the wondrous helper even of the gods. ॥42॥
2.5.9.43: What other reason was there for that? I tell you, O best of sages: it was indeed to proclaim in the worlds his glory, which removes the supreme impurity. ॥43॥
2.5.9.44: And this is another reason: indeed, to convince the wicked, since among all the gods no other surpasses him. ॥44॥
2.5.9.iti: Thus ends the ninth adhyāya, named The description of Śiva's march, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥9॥
2.5.10.1: Sanatkumāra said: Then Śambhu, the great god, standing on the chariot and fully equipped, became ready to burn the entire Tripura of the enemies of the gods. ॥1॥
2.5.10.2: Taking up the foremost stance, the most wondrous pratyālīḍha posture, fitting the finest arrow, and making that bow ready, ॥2॥
2.5.10.3: and setting the arrow in his firm grip and fixing his gaze upon the target, he stood there motionless for a hundred thousand years. ॥3॥
2.5.10.4: Then the lord of the Gaṇas, stationed on his thumb, kept pricking it incessantly, and those cities did not come within the aim of the trident-bearer. ॥4॥
2.5.10.5: Then Hara, holding bow and arrow, with hair of muñja grass and odd eyes, heard from the sky a most auspicious voice: ॥5॥
2.5.10.6: O, O Lord, lord of the lords of the world, so long as that Vināyaka has not been worshipped, you will not now destroy the cities. ॥6॥
2.5.10.7: Hearing these words, the slayer of Andhaka then summoned Bhadrakālī and worshipped the elephant-faced one. ॥7॥
2.5.10.8: When Vināyaka, the foremost, had been duly worshipped and was fully pleased with joy, then Lord Hara saw in the sky ॥8॥
2.5.10.9: the three cities of the Daityas, the mighty sons of Tāraka, joined together just as they should be. Some indeed speak thus: ॥9॥
2.5.10.10: that in the case of Maheśvara, the Supreme Brahman, lord of gods, worshipped by all, success in an undertaking through the grace of another does not apply. ॥10॥
2.5.10.11: He is independent, the Supreme Brahman, with attributes and also without attributes, imperceptible to all, the Lord, the Supreme Self, stainless. ॥11॥
2.5.10.12: He embodies the five deities, is worshipped by the five deities, the supreme Lord. There is none whom he must worship; he alone is to be worshipped, the abode of all. ॥12॥
2.5.10.13: Or else, O sage, everything comes about through his play — the conduct of the god of gods, the great Lord, the giver of boons. ॥13॥
2.5.10.14: While Mahādeva remained there, having worshipped the lord of the Gaṇas, the cities there quickly came into union in due time. ॥14॥
2.5.10.15: When Tripura had come into union there, O sage, a tumultuous joy arose among the gods and other great beings. ॥15॥
2.5.10.16: Then all the hosts of gods, the Siddhas and the great sages uttered cries of victory, praising the eight-formed Śiva. ॥16॥
2.5.10.17: Then Brahmā and Viṣṇu, lord of the worlds, said thus: The time has come for the act of slaying the Daityas. ॥17॥
2.5.10.18: O Maheśvara, the three cities of those sons of Tāraka have come into union; O all-pervading one, accomplish the task of the gods. ॥18॥
