2.5.10.19: O lord of gods, before the cities separate, release the arrow and reduce Tripura to ashes. ॥19॥
2.5.10.20: Then Śarva, stringing the bow and fitting that arrow, meditated on the venerable Pāśupata weapon and on Tripura. ॥20॥
2.5.10.21: Then the god Mahādeva, skilled in the play of granting boons, for some reason looked at it here with disdain. ॥21॥
2.5.10.22: The gods said: Virūpākṣa, the supreme Lord, refuge of the virtuous, is able to turn the three cities to ashes in an instant — let this be known. ॥22॥
2.5.10.23: The lord of gods is able to burn the three worlds with a glance; yet for the increase of our glory you should release the arrow here. ॥23॥
2.5.10.24: Thus praised then by all the immortals, Viṣṇu, Brahmā and the rest, Maheśvara wished to burn the three cities with the arrow. ॥24॥
2.5.10.25: In the auspicious hour called Abhijit, drawing the wondrous bow and making the bowstring twang with an utterly unbearable sound, ॥25॥
2.5.10.26: proclaiming his own name and addressing the great Asuras, the fierce one released the shaft, whose form was like ten million suns. ॥26॥
2.5.10.27: That swift arrow, pure and destructive, made of Viṣṇu, with fire as its tip, blazing mightily, burned those three Daityas dwelling in Tripura. ॥27॥
2.5.10.28: Then the cities, burned, fell together to the earth girdled by the four oceans — all three burned to ashes. ॥28॥
2.5.10.29: The Daityas were burned in hundreds by the fire in his arrow, crying out in anguish, because of their transgression of Śiva's worship. ॥29॥
2.5.10.30: Tārakākṣa, being burned along with his two brothers, remembered his own lord, the god Śaṅkara, who loves his devotees. ॥30॥
2.5.10.31: Filled with supreme devotion, uttering various words, he gazed at Mahādeva and spoke to him in his mind. ॥31॥
2.5.10.32: Tārakākṣa said: O Bhava, you are known to us. If you are pleased with us along with our kinsmen, then by that truth, whenever you burn us again, let it be so. ॥32॥
2.5.10.33: We have obtained what is rare, unattainable even by gods and Asuras. May our minds be imbued with devotion to you in every birth. ॥33॥
2.5.10.34: Speaking thus, those Dānavas, burned wondrously by that fire at Śiva's command, were reduced to ashes, O sage. ॥34॥
2.5.10.35: Other Dānavas too, children and old men, were quickly burned by that fire at Śiva's command and reduced to ashes, O Vyāsa. ॥35॥
2.5.10.36: Women or men, and the vehicles that were there — all were burned by that fire, as the world is at the end of an aeon. ॥36॥
2.5.10.37: Some fine women were burned letting go of husbands clinging to their necks; some women were asleep, some intoxicated, some wearied from lovemaking. ॥37॥
2.5.10.38: Half-burned and awakened, they wandered about, stupefied by delusion. By that terrible fire of Tripura not even the tiniest thing ॥38॥
2.5.10.39: was left unburned or spared, whether stationary or moving — except the Daitya Maya, the imperishable craftsman (Viśvakarman), ॥39॥
2.5.10.40: who was not hostile to the gods, a true devotee who had taken refuge in Maheśa even in time of calamity, and was protected by Śambhu's power. ॥40॥
2.5.10.41: For we are those for whom there exists no destructive coming-together with the Daityas or other beings, whether in existence or non-existence, in what is done or not done. ॥41॥
2.5.10.42: Therefore a well-considered effort must indeed be made by the good. Through censure a person declines; one should not perform such an act. ॥42॥
2.5.10.43: It should be arranged so that there may be no contact with those dwellers of Tripura—this indeed is the view of all—should it by fate arise from any quarter. ॥43॥
2.5.10.44: Those Daityas there who, with their kinsmen, were worshipping Rudra even then all attained the rank of gaṇa-chiefs by the power of the rite of Śiva-worship. ॥44॥
2.5.10.iti: Thus ends the tenth adhyāya, named The description of the burning of Tripura, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥10॥
2.5.11.1: Vyāsa said: O son of Brahmā, O greatly wise one, blessed are you, O best of Śaiva devotees. What did all the gods do then, after Tripura had been burnt? ॥1॥
2.5.11.2: Where did Maya, who was not burnt, go? Where did those ascetics go? Tell me all that fully, if it pertains to the story of Śambhu. ॥2॥
2.5.11.3: Sūta said: Having heard Vyāsa's words, the blessed Sanatkumāra, son of the creator of the world (Brahmā), spoke, remembering the pair of Śiva's feet. ॥3॥
2.5.11.4: Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O Vyāsa of great intellect, O son of Parāśara, to the deeds of the great Lord, which destroy all sins — the Lord who conforms to worldly play. ॥4॥
2.5.11.5: When the whole of Tripura, crowded with Daityas, had been burnt by Maheśvara, the gods there became exceedingly astonished. ॥5॥
2.5.11.6: The gods, Indra, Upendra (Viṣṇu) and the rest, said nothing then; all were agitated on seeing Rudra of great splendour — ॥6॥
2.5.11.7: — greatly terrifying, fierce, blazing in the ten directions, shining like ten million suns, resembling the fire of cosmic dissolution. ॥7॥
2.5.11.8: Merely on beholding the God and the Goddess, daughter of Himavat, all the leading gods were afraid out of fear and stood bowed down. ॥8॥
2.5.11.9: Seeing then the host of gods frightened, the foremost sages said nothing; they stood still and bowed on all sides. ॥9॥
2.5.11.10: Then Brahmā too, very frightened on seeing Śaṅkara's form, yet glad at heart, praised him attentively together with the gods, ॥10॥
2.5.11.11: and with the frightened Viṣṇu, he praised the God of gods, Bhava, Hara, the enemy of Tripura, together with Girijā, subject to his devotees, Maheśvara. ॥11॥
2.5.11.12: Brahmā said: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, bestower of grace on devotees, be gracious, O supreme Lord, giver of welfare to all the gods. ॥12॥
2.5.11.13: Be gracious, O Lord of the worlds; be gracious, O giver of bliss; be gracious, O Śaṅkara, O master; be gracious, O supreme Lord. ॥13॥
2.5.11.14: Salutation to you, the Oṃkāra, O you who carry beings across beyond form; be gracious, O Lord of all gods, O destroyer of Tripura, O Maheśvara. ॥14॥
2.5.11.15: Salutation to the God denoted by many names, O Śaṅkara, lover of those who bow; salutation to you, the attributeless, O you who are beyond Prakṛti and Puruṣa. ॥15॥
2.5.11.16: Salutation to you, the changeless, the eternal, the ever-content, the radiant, the stainless, the divine, the possessor of the three guṇas. ॥16॥
2.5.11.17: Salutation to you with attributes; salutation to you, lord of heaven; to Sadāśiva, the tranquil, Maheśa, the wielder of the Pināka bow. ॥17॥
2.5.11.18: Salutation to you, the omniscient, the refuge, Sadyojāta; to Vāmadeva, Rudra, and also to Tatpuruṣa. ॥18॥
2.5.11.19: Salutation to you, Aghora, well worthy of service, subject to devotees; to Īśāna, the most excellent, bestower of bliss on devotees. ॥19॥
2.5.11.20: Protect, protect, O Mahādeva, all of us frightened immortals. By burning Tripura you have made all the immortals fulfilled in their purpose. ॥20॥
2.5.11.21: Having praised thus, all the deities, Brahmā and the rest, supremely pleased, made obeisance to Sadāśiva each separately. ॥21॥
2.5.11.22: Then Brahmā himself, bowing, with shoulders lowered and palms joined, praised the God Maheśvara, enemy of Tripura. ॥22॥
2.5.11.23: Brahmā said: O Lord, Lord of the God of gods, destroyer of Tripura, Śaṅkara, O Mahādeva, may I have supreme, unfailing devotion to you. ॥23॥
2.5.11.24: May the charioteership of you always be mine, O Lord of gods, Śaṅkara. Be always favourable, O all-pervading one, O supreme Lord. ॥24॥
2.5.11.25: Sanatkumāra said: Having thus praised Śambhu, loving to his devotees, Vidhi (Brahmā) of noble mind, bowing, with lowered shoulders and joined palms, fell silent. ॥25॥
2.5.11.26: The blessed Janārdana too, having bowed to Maheśvara and joined his palms in cupped reverence, praised Maheśvara. ॥26॥
2.5.11.27: Viṣṇu said: O overlord of gods, great Lord, friend of the afflicted, source of compassion, be gracious, O supreme Lord; show compassion, O lover of those who bow. ॥27॥
2.5.11.28: Salutation to you, the attributeless, and again to you with attributes; again to you in the form of Prakṛti, and again to you as Puruṣa. ॥28॥
2.5.11.29: Then, bowing, I offer salutation to you whose nature is the guṇas, the soul of the universe; to the lover of devotion, the tranquil, Śiva, the supreme Self. ॥29॥
2.5.11.30: Salutation to Sadāśiva, Rudra, lord of the worlds. May my devotion to you be firm and ever-increasing from today. ॥30॥
2.5.11.31: Sanatkumāra said: Having spoken thus, he, the best among the foremost Śaivas, fell silent. Then all the gods, bowing, spoke to that supreme Lord. ॥31॥
2.5.11.32: The gods said: O Lord of gods, Mahādeva, source of compassion, Śaṅkara, be gracious, O Lord of the worlds; be gracious, O supreme Lord. ॥32॥
2.5.11.33: Be gracious; you are the maker of all. We bow to you with joy. May our devotion to you be firm, constant and unfailing. ॥33॥
2.5.11.34: Sanatkumāra said: Thus praised by Brahmā, Hari and the immortals, the Lord of gods, Śaṅkara, benefactor of the world, replied with a pleased heart. ॥34॥
2.5.11.35: Śaṅkara said: O Vidhi, O Hari, O gods, I am especially pleased. All of you, after reflection, ask for the boon your mind desires. ॥35॥
2.5.11.36: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words spoken by Hara, O best of sages, all the gods replied with pleased inner hearts. ॥36॥
2.5.11.37: All the gods said: If you are pleased, O Lord, and if a boon is to be given by you to us, O Lord of the God of gods, knowing us gods to be your servants — ॥37॥
2.5.11.38: — whenever distress arises for the gods, O best of gods, then always become manifest and destroy that distress. ॥38॥
2.5.11.39: Sanatkumāra said: Thus addressed by Brahmā, Hari and the immortals all at once, the blessed Rudra, pleased at heart, said: So be it, ever. ॥39॥
2.5.11.40: I am pleased with these hymns too, O gods; I shall surely always grant whatever is most desired in the world to those who recite or hear them. ॥40॥
2.5.11.41: Having spoken thus, Śaṅkara, pleased, who is ever the remover of the gods' sorrow, bestowed everything that was indeed dear to all the gods. ॥41॥
2.5.11.iti: Thus ends the eleventh adhyāya, named The description of the gods' hymn of praise, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥11॥
2.5.12.1: Sanatkumāra said: Meanwhile, seeing Śambhu pleased, the Dānava Maya, who had not been burnt thanks to the power of Śiva's grace, came there, greatly delighted. ॥1॥
2.5.12.2: He lovingly bowed to Hara and indeed to the other gods as well; with joined palms and bent shoulders, he bowed again to Śiva. ॥2॥
2.5.12.3: Then, rising and looking at Śiva, Maya, the best of Dānavas, his heart full of devotion and his sweet voice choked with love, praised him. ॥3॥
2.5.12.4: Maya said: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, O Śaṅkara, loving to devotees, you are the very form of the wish-fulfilling tree, free of all partiality. ॥4॥
2.5.12.5: You whose form is light, salutation be to you; O universal form, salutation be to you. Salutation to you, the pure-souled; to the purifier, salutations again and again. ॥5॥
2.5.12.6: Salutation to you of wondrous form, the eternal, beyond form; salutation to the one of divine form, the divine, of supremely divine shape. ॥6॥
2.5.12.7: Salutation to the auspicious-souled one who destroys all the afflictions of those who bow down; salutations again and again to the creator, sustainer and destroyer of the three worlds. ॥7॥
2.5.12.8: Salutation to you, attainable by devotion, compassionate to devotees, granter of the true fruit of austerity, O beloved of Śivā, O Lord Śiva. ॥8॥
2.5.12.9: I do not know how to offer praise, O supreme Lord fond of praise. Be pleased, O Lord of all; protect me, who have come to you for refuge. ॥9॥
2.5.12.10: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing this hymn spoken by Maya, the supreme Lord became pleased, O best of twice-born, and spoke respectfully to Maya. ॥10॥
2.5.12.11: Śiva said: Ask for a boon, O Maya, best of Dānavas; I am pleased. Whatever your mind desires, that I shall give; there is no doubt. ॥11॥
2.5.12.12: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing Śambhu's auspicious words, Maya, the bull among Dānavas, bowed to the Lord and, with bent shoulders and joined palms, replied. ॥12॥
2.5.12.13: Maya said: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, if you are pleased with me, and if I am worthy of a boon, then grant me everlasting devotion to you. ॥13॥
2.5.12.14: Grant me constant friendship with your devotees, constant compassion for the afflicted, and indifference towards other beings who are wicked, O supreme Lord. ॥14॥
2.5.12.15: May a demonic disposition never arise in me, O Maheśvara. May I always be fearless, O Lord, absorbed in your auspicious worship. ॥15॥
2.5.12.16: Sanatkumāra said: Being thus entreated, Śaṅkara, the supreme Lord, the master, pleased and loving to devotees, replied to Maya. ॥16॥
2.5.12.17: Maheśvara said: O bull among Dānavas, you are blessed, my devotee, free from perversion. All the boons that you now desire are granted to you. ॥17॥
2.5.12.18: By my command, go with your own retinue to the world Vitala, which is more delightful even than heaven. ॥18॥
2.5.12.19: Dwell there fearless, joyful and always devoted. By my command, a demonic disposition will never arise in you. ॥19॥
2.5.12.20: Sanatkumāra said: Thus, placing the command of the great-souled Śaṅkara on his head, and bowing to him and to the gods as well, he went to Vitala. ॥20॥
2.5.12.21: Meanwhile the shaven-headed ones also arrived, and bowing, they spoke to all those gods, Viṣṇu, Brahmā and the rest. ॥21॥
2.5.12.22: Where shall we go, O gods? What work shall we do? Command us quickly, for we carry out your orders. ॥22॥
2.5.12.23: A wicked deed has been done by us, O Hari, O Vidhi, O gods: the devotion to Śiva of the Daityas, who were Śiva's devotees, has been destroyed. ॥23॥
2.5.12.24: Our dwelling in hell will be for ten million kalpas; surely there will be no deliverance for those who oppose Śiva's devotees. ॥24॥
2.5.12.25: Yet this wicked deed was done by us at your wish. Out of compassion, tell us its expiation; we have come to you for refuge. ॥25॥
2.5.12.26: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing their words, those gods, Viṣṇu, Brahmā and the rest, spoke to the shaven-headed ones standing before them with joined palms. ॥26॥
2.5.12.27: Viṣṇu and the others said: You need never be afraid, O shaven-headed ones; this whole excellent episode came about by Śiva's command. ॥27॥
2.5.12.28: No painful evil destiny will ever be yours, since you are servants of Śiva who act for the good of gods and sages. ॥28॥
2.5.12.29: Śambhu works for the good of gods and sages, and one who works for the good of gods and sages is dear to him; for men who work for the good of gods and sages there is never an evil destiny. ॥29॥
2.5.12.30: From today on, for men who enter this doctrine in the Kali age, there will be an evil destiny; we speak the truth, there is no doubt in this. ॥30॥
2.5.12.31: O steadfast shaven-headed ones, by my command you should dwell in the desert land in concealment until the Kali age arrives. ॥31॥
2.5.12.32: And when Kali has come, you will establish your own doctrine; in Kali, deluded fools will adopt your doctrine. ॥32॥
2.5.12.33: Thus commanded by the lords of the gods, O lord of sages, those shaven-headed ones paid homage and went to their own hermitage as directed. ॥33॥
2.5.12.34: Then the blessed Rudra, the great yogin, having burnt the inhabitants of Tripura, his task accomplished, was worshipped by Brahmā and the others. ॥34॥
2.5.12.35: Then the Lord, accompanied by all his Gaṇas, by the goddess Śivā and by his sons, having accomplished the great task of the immortals, disappeared. ॥35॥
2.5.12.36: When the god Śiva with his retinue had vanished, the bow, together with the arrow, the chariot and the rest, and the enclosure also disappeared. ॥36॥
2.5.12.37: Then Brahmā, Hari, the gods, sages, Gandharvas, Kinnaras, Nāgas, serpents, Apsarases and humans, all delighted, ॥37॥
2.5.12.38: went joyfully each to his own place, extolling Śaṅkara's glory; and having reached their own places, they attained supreme bliss. ॥38॥
2.5.12.39: Thus I have told you the whole great story of the moon-crested Śiva, which narrates the destruction of Tripura and is full of supreme divine play. ॥39॥
2.5.12.40: It is blessed, conferring fame and long life, increasing wealth and grain, granting heaven and liberation too. What more do you wish to hear? ॥40॥
2.5.12.41: Whoever always reads or listens to this supreme narrative, having enjoyed all desires here in this world, would attain liberation at the end. ॥41॥
2.5.12.iti: Thus ends the twelfth adhyāya, named The description of the gods' hymn after the slaying of Tripura, Maya's hymn, the settling of the shaven-headed ones and the gods' return to their own places, in the dialogue of Sanatkumāra and Pārāśarya, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥12॥
2.5.13.1: Vyāsa said: O Brahman, O venerable one, O son of Brahmā, I have heard before that the Lord Śaṅkara slew the great demon Jalandhara. ॥1॥
2.5.13.2: Therefore, O greatly wise one, tell me in detail the deeds of the moon-crested Śiva. Who, hearing his spotless glory, could ever be satiated? ॥2॥
2.5.13.3: Sūta said: Thus questioned by Vyāsa, the great sage, the son of Brahmā, skilled in speech, spoke words full of meaning, without agitation. ॥3॥
2.5.13.4: Sanatkumāra said: Once, O sage, Jīva Bṛhaspati and Śakra Indra, with supreme devotion, eagerly went to Kailāsa to have the sight of the Lord. ॥4॥
2.5.13.5: Then the Lord Śaṅkara, knowing of the coming of the Guru Bṛhaspati and Indra, wished to test the understanding of those two, whose minds were intent on seeing him. ॥5॥
2.5.13.6: Then, naked, he who is the true refuge of the good blocked their path and stood there with his head bound in matted locks, his face radiant. ॥6॥
2.5.13.7: Then those two, the Guru and Śakra, travelling joyfully, saw in the middle of the path a fearsome man of wondrous form, ॥7॥
2.5.13.8: greatly radiant, calm, his head bound with matted locks, mighty-armed, broad-chested, fair, with terrifying eyes. ॥8॥
2.5.13.9: Then Purandara Indra, arrogant because of his authority, questioned that man standing in his path, not recognising him as Śaṅkara. ॥9॥
2.5.13.10: Purandara said: Hey, who are you? Where have you come from? What is your name? Tell me truly. Is Śambhu, the Lord, staying in his own abode, or has he gone elsewhere? ॥10॥
2.5.13.11: Sanatkumāra said: Though questioned thus by Śakra, the ascetic said nothing. Śakra asked again, but the naked one did not speak. ॥11॥
2.5.13.12: Again Purandara, the supreme ruler of the worlds, asked; the great yogin, the Lord who had assumed a form in play, remained silent. ॥12॥
2.5.13.13: Thus questioned again and again by Śakra, the naked Lord said nothing, in order to test Śakra's understanding. ॥13॥
2.5.13.14: Then the lord of the gods, proud of his sovereignty over the three worlds, became angry, and rebuking that wearer of matted locks, he spoke these words. ॥14॥
2.5.13.15: Indra said: Hey, even though I am questioning you, you have given no answer. Therefore I will strike you with my thunderbolt. Who is there to protect you, O fool? ॥15॥
2.5.13.16: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this, the wielder of the thunderbolt glared at him in anger and raised his thunderbolt to strike the naked one. ॥16॥
2.5.13.17: Seeing Purandara with the thunderbolt in hand, the god Sadāśiva, Śaṅkara, paralysed the fall of his thunderbolt. ॥17॥
2.5.13.18: Then Rudra, filled with anger, with fierce eyes and terrifying, at once blazed up with radiance as if he would burn everything. ॥18॥
2.5.13.19: The lord of Śacī burned within with rage born of the paralysis of his arm, like a serpent whose power has been checked by a spell. ॥19॥
2.5.13.20: Seeing that man blazing with his own radiance, Bṛhaspati quickly recognised him by his insight as Hara, and bowed to the Lord. ॥20॥
2.5.13.21: Then the noble-minded Guru, with joined palms, bowing down to the ground like a staff, began to praise the Lord. ॥21॥
2.5.13.22: The guru said: Salutation to the God of gods, to Mahādeva, to the Self, to Maheśvara, the Lord, the three-eyed one, the wearer of matted hair. ॥22॥
2.5.13.23: Salutation to the protector of the wretched, the all-pervading one, the slayer of Andhaka, the destroyer of Tripura, to Śarva, to Brahman, the supreme one. ॥23॥
2.5.13.24: Salutation to you, the odd-eyed one, Rudra, the many-formed, Śambhu; to the misshapen one, the one of surpassing form, the one beyond all form. ॥24॥
2.5.13.25: Salutation to you, destroyer of the sacrifice and giver of the fruits of sacrifices, whose form is the sacrifice, who sets in motion the actions of others. ॥25॥
2.5.13.26: Salutation to you, the ender of Kāla, who are Time itself, who wear the serpents of Time; salutation to the supreme Lord, the all-pervading one. ॥26॥
2.5.13.27: Salutation to the cutter of Brahmā's head, to the one praised by Brahmā and the Moon; salutation be to you, friend of brāhmaṇas; salutation to you, the supreme Self. ॥27॥
2.5.13.28: You are fire, wind, and sky; you alone are water and earth; you are the sun, the moon, the stars; you indeed are the circle of luminaries. ॥28॥
2.5.13.29: You alone are Viṣṇu, you are Brahmā; praised by them, you are the supreme Lord. You are the sages beginning with Sanaka; you are Nārada, rich in austerity. ॥29॥
2.5.13.30: You alone are the lord of all worlds; you alone are the soul of the universe; connected with all, yet distinct from all, you alone are beyond Prakṛti. ॥30॥
2.5.13.31: Through rajas, bearing the name Vidhi Brahmā, you create the worlds; through sattva, in the form of Hari, you sustain the whole universe. ॥31॥
2.5.13.32: You alone, O Mahādeva, through tamas, assuming the form of Hara, dissolve in play the entire world made of the five elements. ॥32॥
2.5.13.33: By the power of meditation on you, O creator of the universe, the sun shines, the moon pours down nectar upon the world, and the wind blows. ॥33॥
2.5.13.34: By the power of meditation on you, O Śaṅkara, the clouds rain water; by the power of meditation on you Śakra protects the three worlds like a son. ॥34॥
2.5.13.35: By the power of meditation on you, the clouds, all the gods, and the lords of sages perform their own duties, trembling from fear of you. ॥35॥
2.5.13.36: Through service of your lotus feet alone, O Rudra, men on earth disregard the gods and enjoy sovereignty over the worlds. ॥36॥
2.5.13.37: Through service of your lotus feet alone, devotees have reached the supreme state, unattainable even by those rich in yoga and hard for all to gain. ॥37॥
2.5.13.38: Sanatkumāra said: Having thus praised Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the worlds, Bṛhaspati made Purandara fall at the feet of that Lord. ॥38॥
2.5.13.39: Having made Indra, lord of the gods, fall down with bowed neck, Bṛhaspati, bent low in humility, said this to Śiva: ॥39॥
2.5.13.40: Bṛhaspati said: O protector of the helpless, O Mahādeva, raise up Indra who is bowed at your feet, and make calm your own anger born from your eye. ॥40॥
2.5.13.41: Be pleased, O Mahādeva; protect Indra, who has come to you for refuge. May this fire, born from the eye on your forehead, be quenched. ॥41॥
2.5.13.42: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words of the preceptor, Maheśvara, the god of gods, the ocean of compassion, spoke in a voice deep as the rumbling of clouds. ॥42॥
2.5.13.43: Maheśvara said: O Bṛhaspati, how can I hold back the wrath that has already issued from my eye? How indeed does a snake put on again the slough it has cast off? ॥43॥
2.5.13.44: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of Śaṅkara, Bṛhaspati, distressed in appearance, his mind agitated with fear, spoke. ॥44॥
2.5.13.45: Bṛhaspati said: O god, O Lord, devotees are ever to be shown compassion. O Śaṅkara, make true your name Bhaktavatsala (affectionate to devotees). ॥45॥
2.5.13.46: O lord of gods, you should cast your extremely fierce energy elsewhere. O deliverer of all devotees, deliver Purandara (Indra). ॥46॥
2.5.13.47: Sanatkumāra said: Thus addressed by the preceptor, Rudra, who bears the name affectionate to devotees and removes the distress of those who bow to him, replied with a gracious heart to the priest of the gods. ॥47॥
2.5.13.48: Śiva said: Pleased by this hymn, dear one, I grant you an excellent boon: since you have obtained life for Indra, become famed as Jīva. ॥48॥
2.5.13.49: This fire which has arisen from my forehead eye, the slayer of the lord of gods—I shall cast it far away, so that it may not afflict Indra. ॥49॥
2.5.13.50: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this, taking in his hand that wondrous fire of his own energy, born from his forehead eye, he hurled it into the salt ocean. ॥50॥
2.5.13.51: Then Rudra, the Lord, performer of great sports, vanished. The preceptor and Śakra, freed from fear, attained supreme happiness. ॥51॥
2.5.13.52: Having obtained the sight of him for whose sake they had set out, the preceptor and Śakra, their purpose fulfilled, joyfully returned to their own abodes. ॥52॥
2.5.13.iti: Thus ends the thirteenth adhyāya, named The saving of Śakra's life, in the account of the slaying of Jalandhara, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥13॥
2.5.14.1: Vyāsa said: O Sanatkumāra, all-knowing son of Brahmā, salutation to you. Today I have heard this wondrous story of the great-souled Śambhu. ॥1॥
2.5.14.2: O Brahman, when his own fiery energy, born from the eye on his forehead, was cast into the salt ocean, what happened there, dear one? Tell me that quickly. ॥2॥
2.5.14.3: Sanatkumāra said: Listen, dear one of great wisdom, to Śiva's most wondrous sport, hearing which with faith a devotee would attain the goal of yogins. ॥3॥
2.5.14.4: Then that energy of Śiva, born of his forehead-eye, once thrown into the salt ocean, at once took the form of a child. ॥4॥
2.5.14.5: There, at the confluence of the Gaṅgā river with the ocean, that child, terrifying to all the worlds, cried out loudly. ॥5॥
2.5.14.6: By the sound of his crying the earth shook again and again, and heaven and Satyaloka were deafened by that noise. ॥6॥
2.5.14.7: By the child's crying alone all the worlds were terrified, and the guardians of the worlds everywhere had their minds thrown into agitation. ॥7॥
2.5.14.8: What need of saying more, O best of brahmins? The whole universe, with its moving and unmoving beings, shook, dear one, O lord, from the crying of that infant. ॥8॥
2.5.14.9: Then all the gods, distressed, together with the sages, quickly went for refuge to Brahmā, the Grandsire, the preceptor of the worlds. ॥9॥
2.5.14.10: Having gone there, those gods and sages along with Vāsava (Indra) bowed, praised him well, and spoke to that Supreme One (Parameṣṭhin). ॥10॥
2.5.14.11: The gods said: O lord of the worlds, lord of the gods, a danger has come upon us. Destroy it, O great yogin, for this wondrous roar has arisen. ॥11॥
2.5.14.12: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard their words thus, Brahmā, the Grandsire of the worlds, then wished to go there, astonished, thinking, what is this? ॥12॥
2.5.14.13: Then, dear one, Brahmā with the gods descended from Satyaloka to the earth, and wishing to learn about that, he went to the ocean. ॥13॥
2.5.14.14: As soon as Brahmā, the Grandsire of all worlds, arrived there, he saw that child in the lap of the ocean. ॥14॥
2.5.14.15: Seeing Vidhi (Brahmā) arrived, the Ocean, taking a divine form, bowed his head and placed the child in his (Brahmā's) lap. ॥15॥
2.5.14.16: Then Brahmā, filled with wonder, said to the Ocean: O mass of waters, tell me quickly, whose is this wondrous infant? ॥16॥
2.5.14.17: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing Brahmā's words, the Ocean, delighted, bowed, praised the lord of creatures, and with joined palms replied. ॥17॥
2.5.14.18: The Ocean said: O Brahmā, O protector of all worlds, I suddenly found this child in the Gaṅgā river, without knowing his origin. ॥18॥
2.5.14.19: O preceptor of the world, perform for him the rites beginning with the birth ceremony (jātakarman). O Creator, please tell all the results foretold by his horoscope. ॥19॥
2.5.14.20: Sanatkumāra said: While the Ocean was speaking thus, that child, son of the Ocean, seized Brahmā by the neck as he kept shaking again and again. ॥20॥
2.5.14.21: Because of this shaking of Vidhi, the maker of all worlds, and his being pained, water came from his eyes, O Kāleya (Vyāsa). ॥21॥
2.5.14.22: Having somehow freed his neck from the hands of that mighty son born of the ocean, Brahmā spoke respectfully. ॥22॥
2.5.14.23: Brahmā said: Listen, O Ocean: with my mind concentrated, I shall tell you all the results foretold in the horoscope of this son of yours. ॥23॥
2.5.14.24: Since water was held (dhṛta) from my eyes by him, therefore let him be known here by the name Jalandhara. ॥24॥
2.5.14.25: Even now he is a youth, master of the meaning of all scriptures, of great valour, steadfast, a warrior, and fierce in battle. ॥25॥
2.5.14.26: He will be profound like you and, in war, like Guha (Skanda); a conqueror of all in battle, resplendent with every kind of prosperity. ॥26॥
2.5.14.27: This child will become the overlord of all the Daityas. He will be a conqueror even of Viṣṇu; there will be no defeat for him from any quarter. ॥27॥
2.5.14.28: He will be unslayable by all beings except Rudra. He will now return there whence he arose. ॥28॥
2.5.14.29: His wife will be devoted to her husband, increasing his good fortune, beautiful in every limb, charming, an ocean of sweet speech and good conduct. ॥29॥
2.5.14.30: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this, Brahmā summoned Śukra and had him (Jalandhara) consecrated to kingship; then, taking leave of the lord of rivers, he vanished. ॥30॥
2.5.14.31: Then the Ocean, his eyes wide with joy at seeing him, took up that son of his and went joyfully to his own home. ॥31॥
2.5.14.32: Delighted at heart, he nourished with great efforts his own child, beautiful in every limb, charming, and of most wondrous splendour. ॥32॥
2.5.14.33: Then the Ocean summoned the great asura Kālanemi and asked for his daughter named Vṛndā to be his son's wife. ॥33॥
2.5.14.34: The asura Kālanemi, heroic, foremost of asuras, wise and skilled in his own duties, approved the Ocean's request, O sage. ॥34॥
2.5.14.35: To the heroic Jalandhara, born of the Ocean, he gave his own daughter, dear as life, according to the Brāhma rite. ॥35॥
2.5.14.36: Then there was a great festival at their wedding; the male and female rivers and all the asuras attained happiness, O sage. ॥36॥
2.5.14.37: The Ocean was exceedingly happy on seeing his son with a wife, and gave gifts according to rule to the twice-born and to others too. ॥37॥
2.5.14.38: The Daityas who had earlier been defeated by the gods and dwelt in Pātāla came to the earth, fearless, taking refuge in him. ॥38॥
2.5.14.39: Then those asuras headed by Kālanemi, having given the daughter to that son of the Ocean, became exceedingly joyful, relying on him for the conquest of the gods. ॥39॥
2.5.14.40: And that hero too, the child of the ocean, named Jalandhara, the mightiest hero among the heroic asuras, having obtained an exceedingly beautiful wife, and being self-controlled, ruled the kingdom through the power of Kavi Śukra. ॥40॥
2.5.14.iti: Thus ends the fourteenth adhyāya, named The description of the birth and marriage of Jalandhara, in the account of the slaying of Jalandhara, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥14॥
2.5.15.1: Sanatkumāra said: Once the son of the ocean, the lord of Vṛndā, noble-minded and heroic, was seated with his wife, accompanied by all the Asuras. ॥1॥
2.5.15.2: Then Bhārgava Śukra, very pleased and radiant, came there, like a mass of splendour in bodily form, illuminating all the directions. ॥2॥
2.5.15.3: Seeing their preceptor coming, all those Asuras quickly bowed with joyful minds; the son of the ocean too bowed respectfully. ॥3॥
2.5.15.4: Having given them words of blessing, Bhārgava, the treasure of splendour, sat on a beautiful seat; they too remained seated as before. ॥4॥
2.5.15.5: Then the heroic son of the ocean, Jalandhara, whose excellent command was never thwarted, seeing his own assembly with affection, became delighted. ॥5॥
2.5.15.6: Seeing Rāhu present there with his head severed, that king of the Daityas, the son of the ocean, quickly asked Bhārgava this: ॥6॥
2.5.15.7: Jalandhara said: By whom was this beheading of Rāhu done, O lord? Tell me the whole event exactly and truly, O preceptor. ॥7॥
2.5.15.8: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of the son of the ocean, Bhārgava, remembering the lotus-feet of Śiva, replied truthfully. ॥8॥
2.5.15.9: Śukra said: O Jalandhara, great hero, helper of all the Asuras, listen: I shall tell you the whole story exactly. ॥9॥
2.5.15.10: Formerly there was the heroic and mighty Bali, son of Virocana and great-grandson of Hiraṇyakaśipu, O best of the knowers of dharma. ॥10॥
2.5.15.11: Defeated by him, the gods together with Vāsava Indra went for refuge to the lord of Ramā Viṣṇu, and, seeking their own ends, related their plight. ॥11॥
2.5.15.12: Then, at his command, the gods, skilled in deceitful deeds, made a truce with the Asuras to accomplish their own purpose, dear one. ॥12॥
2.5.15.13: Then, for the sake of nectar, all those gods, with Viṣṇu as their helper, zealously churned the ocean together with the Asuras. ॥13॥
2.5.15.14: Then the enemies of the Daityas carried off the jewels; the gods took them with effort and also drank the nectar by deceit. ॥14॥
2.5.15.15: Then, with Viṣṇu's help, those gods with Śakra, strengthened by drinking the nectar, defeated the Asuras. ॥15॥
2.5.15.16: In the assembly of the gods, Hari, always partial to Hari Indra, cut off the head of Rāhu as he was drinking the nectar. ॥16॥
2.5.15.17: Sanatkumāra said: Thus Kavi Śukra narrated to him the beheading of Rāhu and the churning of the ocean for nectar caused by the gods, ॥17॥
2.5.15.18: and the seizure of the jewels, the defeat of the Daityas, and the drinking of nectar by the gods — all this in detail. ॥18॥
2.5.15.19: Hearing that — the churning of his own father — the mighty great hero, the child of the ocean, then became furious, his eyes red with anger. ॥19॥
2.5.15.20: Then, summoning his excellent messenger named Ghasmara, he told him the whole story that the self-possessed preceptor had related. ॥20॥
2.5.15.21: Then, honouring him greatly with affection and granting him safety, he sent that skilful messenger of his to the presence of Śakra. ॥21॥
2.5.15.22: The wise Ghasmara, messenger of the ocean's child, went swiftly to Triviṣṭapa heaven, filled with all the gods. ॥22॥
2.5.15.23: Having gone there and quickly reached the hall Sudharmā, that messenger, holding his head high out of pride, spoke these words to the lord of the gods. ॥23॥
2.5.15.24: Ghasmara said: Jalandhara, son of the ocean, lord of all the Daitya folk, very valorous, a great hero, himself has Kavi Śukra as his helper. ॥24॥
2.5.15.25: I am the messenger of that hero, named Ghasmara, yet not a devourer; sent by that hero, I have come here into your presence. ॥25॥
2.5.15.26: Jalandhara, of lofty intellect, whose command is unobstructed everywhere, who has conquered all the enemies of the Daityas — hear what he has said. ॥26॥
2.5.15.27: Jalandhara said: Why was my father, the ocean, churned by you with a mountain? And all my father's jewels carried off, O vilest of gods? ॥27॥
2.5.15.28: What you did was not proper; give them back to me quickly today. Reflecting thus, come to me for refuge together with the gods. ॥28॥
2.5.15.29: Otherwise, O vilest of gods, great danger will befall you, and the destruction of your kingdom too — this I tell you truly. ॥29॥
2.5.15.30: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of the messenger, Indra, lord of the thirty gods, astonished, filled with fear and anger, recalling the past, spoke to him. ॥30॥
2.5.15.31: Because the mountains, terrified out of fear of me, were given shelter in his own belly, and other Daityas, my enemies, were also protected by him in the past — ॥31॥
2.5.15.32: therefore I indeed took away all his collection of jewels. No one hostile to me remains at ease — I speak the truth. ॥32॥
2.5.15.33: Likewise, formerly the Daitya Śaṅkha, a son of the ocean, hating me, became deluded in mind, having abandoned the company of the good. ॥33॥
2.5.15.34: That evil-minded, most sinful one, a tormentor of the community of the good, was slain within the ocean by my younger brother Hari. ॥34॥
2.5.15.35: So go quickly, messenger, and tell this son of the ocean truly the whole reason for the churning of the ocean. ॥35॥
2.5.15.36: Sanatkumāra said: Thus dismissed by Indra, the very intelligent messenger named Ghasmara then went swiftly to where the hero Jalandhara was. ॥36॥
2.5.15.37: Then the king of the Daityas was told by that wise messenger all these words spoken by Śakra. ॥37॥
2.5.15.38: Hearing that, the Daitya, his lip trembling with rage, swiftly made preparations, desiring to conquer all the gods. ॥38॥
2.5.15.39: Then, at the war-preparation of the lord of Asuras, the sons of Diti arrived from all directions and likewise from Pātāla, by crores upon crores. ॥39॥
2.5.15.40: Then the mighty great hero, the son of the ocean, set out with Śumbha, Niśumbha and others, and with crores of army commanders. ॥40॥
2.5.15.41: Surrounded by his whole army, he at once reached Triviṣṭapa heaven. The ocean-born one blew his conch, and the warriors roared on every side. ॥41॥
2.5.15.42: Having gone to heaven, the Daitya stationed himself in the garden Nandana, surrounding it with his whole army and roaring like a lion. ॥42॥
2.5.15.43: Seeing that great host of troops standing and besieging the city, the gods, clad in armour, sallied out of Amarāvatī to fight. ॥43॥
2.5.15.44: Then battle broke out between the armies of the gods and the Dānavas, with pestles, iron clubs, arrows, maces, axes and spears. ॥44॥
2.5.15.45: The two armies rushed at each other and struck one another; in a moment both armies were drenched in floods of blood. ॥45॥
2.5.15.46: With elephants, horses, chariots and foot-soldiers fallen and falling, the ground in battle shone as if covered with banks of twilight clouds. ॥46॥
2.5.15.47: There in the battle Bhārgava Śukra revived those Daityas who had died, by means of the lore that revives the dead, with drops of water charged with mantras. ॥47॥
2.5.15.48: Likewise, in that battle Aṅgiras (Bṛhaspati) revived the gods again and again, bringing divine herbs from Mount Droṇa. ॥48॥
2.5.15.49: Seeing them thus risen up again in the battle, Jalandhara, overcome by anger, spoke these words to Bhārgava. ॥49॥
2.5.15.50: Jalandhara said: The gods were slain by me in battle—how do they rise again? The reviving lore is known to be with you alone and nowhere else. ॥50॥
2.5.15.51: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of the son of the Ocean, Bhārgava—the preceptor Śukra—replied to Jalandhara with a pleased mind. ॥51॥
2.5.15.52: Śukra said: Bringing divine herbs from Mount Droṇa, this Aṅgiras revives the gods, dear son; know my word to be true. ॥52॥
2.5.15.53: If you desire victory, dear son, hear my auspicious counsel: then quickly carry that Droṇa with your two arms and cast it into the ocean. ॥53॥
2.5.15.54: Sanatkumāra said: Thus addressed by the preceptor Bhārgava, that lord of the Daityas went swiftly to where that king of mountains stood. ॥54॥
2.5.15.55: Then the Daitya forcefully lifted that Droṇa with his two arms and swiftly hurled it into the ocean—no wonder in one born of Hara's energy. ॥55॥
2.5.15.56: The great hero, son of the Ocean, came back to the great battle and, exerting great might, struck down the gods with various weapons. ॥56॥
2.5.15.57: Then, seeing the gods slain, the preceptor, honoured by the gods, went to Mount Droṇa; but there he did not see that lord of mountains. ॥57॥
2.5.15.58: Knowing that Droṇa had been carried off by the Daitya, Dhiṣaṇa—Jīva Bṛhaspati—overwhelmed with fear and troubled in mind, came and spoke to the gods. ॥58॥
2.5.15.59: The guru said: Flee, all you gods. The great mountain Droṇa is gone; surely it has been destroyed by the Daitya, the son of the Ocean. ॥59॥
2.5.15.60: This great Daitya Jalandhara cannot be conquered, for he is born of a portion of Rudra, the crusher of all the immortals. ॥60॥
2.5.15.61: I know his power and how he himself came into being, O gods; remember fully the deed of Śakra, who insulted Śiva. ॥61॥
2.5.15.62: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing those words spoken by the preceptor of the gods, the gods, overwhelmed with fear, gave up hope of victory. ॥62॥
2.5.15.63: Being smitten severely on all sides by that king of the Daityas, the gods together with Vāsava Indra abandoned their courage and fled in the ten directions. ॥63॥
2.5.15.64: Seeing the gods put to flight, the Daitya, son of the Ocean, entered Amarāvatī amid the sounds of conches, kettledrums and cries of victory. ॥64॥
2.5.15.65: When the Daitya had entered the city, the gods headed by Śakra, tormented by the Daitya, reached a cave of the golden mountain Meru and dwelt there. ॥65॥
2.5.15.66: At that very time, O sage, the Asura duly installed Śumbha and other leading Daityas, each separately, in all the offices of Indra and the other gods, and himself went to the cave of the golden mountain. ॥66॥
2.5.15.iti: Thus ends the fifteenth adhyāya, named The description of the battle between the gods and Jalandhara, in the account of the slaying of Jalandhara, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥15॥
2.5.16.1: Sanatkumāra said: Seeing the demon approaching once more, the gods together with Indra all trembled with fear and fled away together in haste. ॥1॥
2.5.16.2: They all went to Vaikuṇṭha, placing Prajāpati (Brahmā) at their head; and all those gods, together with the Prajāpatis, bowed and praised Viṣṇu. ॥2॥
2.5.16.3: The gods said: O Hṛṣīkeśa, mighty-armed one, O Lord, slayer of Madhu, salutation to you, lord of the god of gods, destroyer of all demons. ॥3॥
2.5.16.4: Salutation to you, O Viṣṇu, in the form of a fish, who brought back the Vedas, who sported in the ocean of dissolution with the good king Satyavrata. ॥4॥
2.5.16.5: Salutation to you in the form of a tortoise, who bore Mount Mandara for the gods as they strenuously exerted themselves in churning the ocean. ॥5॥
2.5.16.6: Salutation to you, O blessed Lord, who are the sacrifice itself in the form of a boar; salutation to you who bear on your head the earth, the support of beings. ॥6॥
2.5.16.7: Salutation to you, Vāmana, Viṣṇu called Upendra, who in the guise of a brahmin outwitted Bali, lord of the demons, O all-pervading one. ॥7॥
2.5.16.8: Salutation to you, Paraśurāma, who rid the earth of kṣatriyas, who did good to your mother, wrathful, the foe of the wicked. ॥8॥
2.5.16.9: Salutation to you, Rāma, delight of the world, the ideal man of propriety, who swiftly ended Rāvaṇa, husband of Sītā. ॥9॥
2.5.16.10: Salutation to you, Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Self, hidden in knowledge, who delights in sporting with Rādhā and performs many divine plays. ॥10॥
2.5.16.11: Salutation to you of hidden body, who censured the Vedas, the teacher of yoga, the Jaina, the one in Buddha's form, O lord of Mā (Lakṣmī). ॥11॥
2.5.16.12: Salutation to you in the form of Kalki, destroyer of the barbarians, whose form is infinite power, and establisher of true dharma. ॥12॥
2.5.16.13: Salutation to you in the form of Kapila, the great soul, who taught Sāṅkhya-yoga to Devahūti, to the teacher of Sāṅkhya, O Lord. ॥13॥
2.5.16.14: Salutation to the Paramahaṃsa who imparts the supreme knowledge, to the Ordainer whose form is knowledge, by whom the self becomes serene. ॥14॥
2.5.16.15: Salutation to Vedavyāsa, who divided the Vedas and composed the Purāṇas for the welfare of all the worlds. ॥15॥
2.5.16.16: Thus, salutation to you, O Lord, who through bodies such as the fish are intent on the work of your devotees, the maker of creation, preservation and destruction, who are Brahman. ॥16॥
2.5.16.17: Salutation to you, Hari, remover of the distress of your servants, giver of happiness, the auspicious one, clad in yellow, who ride on Tārkṣya (Garuḍa). Salutation, salutation to the sole agent of all actions, the refuge of all. ॥17॥
2.5.16.18: O thunderbolt that shatters the sorrows and other ills of the immortals tormented by demons, salutation to you who lie on the couch of Śeṣa, whose eyes are the sun and moon. ॥18॥
2.5.16.19: O ocean of compassion, lord of Ramā, protect us who have come to you for refuge. All the gods have been driven out of heaven by Jalandhara. ॥19॥
2.5.16.20: The sun has been driven from his place, and likewise the moon and fire; the king of serpents has been driven from Pātāla, and Dharmarāja (Yama) has been expelled. ॥20॥
2.5.16.21: Those gods wander about like mortals and no longer shine. We have come to you for refuge; let his slaying be considered. ॥21॥
2.5.16.22: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these piteous words of the gods, Madhusūdana, the ocean of compassion, spoke in a voice resounding like thunder. ॥22॥
2.5.16.23: Viṣṇu said: Give up fear, O gods. I shall go to battle; I shall display my prowess against the demon Jalandhara. ॥23॥
2.5.16.24: Having said this, the foe of demons, loving to his devotees, rose up at once, troubled in mind, and out of compassion swiftly mounted Garuḍa. ॥24॥
2.5.16.25: Seeing her beloved departing with the gods, Lakṣmī, born of the ocean, with joined palms and tearful eyes, spoke these words. ॥25॥
2.5.16.26: Lakṣmī said: O lord, if I am your beloved and always devoted to you, then how can my brother be slain by you in battle, O treasure of compassion? ॥26॥
2.5.16.27: Viṣṇu said: I shall display my prowess against the demon Jalandhara; praised by them, I shall go in haste to battle. ॥27॥
2.5.16.28: Because he is born of a portion of Rudra, because of Brahmā's word, and out of love for you, this Jalandhara is not to be slain by me. ॥28॥
2.5.16.29: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this, Viṣṇu, mounted on Garuḍa and bearing conch, discus, mace and sword, swiftly went to fight together with the gods headed by Śakra. ॥29॥
2.5.16.30: He quickly reached the very place where the demon Jalandhara was, roaring like a lion, with the gods blazing with Viṣṇu's splendour. ॥30॥
2.5.16.31: Then, battered by the wind from the swift wings of Aruṇa's younger brother (Garuḍa), the demons, whirled about by the gale, spun in the sky like clouds. ॥31॥
2.5.16.32: Then Jalandhara, seeing the demons afflicted by the gale, raised his voice in anger and quickly advanced against Viṣṇu. ॥32॥
2.5.16.33: Meanwhile the gods, exultant, strengthened by Hari's splendour and endowed with great might, joined battle. ॥33॥
2.5.16.34: Seeing the army of the gods arrayed and ready for battle, Jalandhara commanded the demons, who were exceedingly fierce in combat. ॥34॥
2.5.16.35: Jalandhara said: Ho, ho, best of demons, wage a fierce battle today against the immortals led by Śakra, who seem mighty now but are ever cowardly. ॥35॥
2.5.16.36: The Mauryas numbering a hundred thousand, the Dhaumras numbering a hundred, the Asuras numbering ten million, and likewise the Kālakeyas, ॥36॥
2.5.16.37: and of the Kālakas, Daurhṛdas and Kaṅkas by the hundred thousand—these and others too, joined with their own forces, let them march out at my command. ॥37॥
2.5.16.38: March out, all of you, equipped, accompanied by great armies, furnished with various weapons and missiles, fearless and free of doubt. ॥38॥
2.5.16.39: Ho, ho, Śumbha and Niśumbha, you two of very great valour, destroy in an instant the paltry gods, cowardly in battle. ॥39॥
2.5.16.40: Sanatkumāra said: Thus commanded by Jalandhara, those Daityas, skilled in warfare—all those Asuras, accompanied by their fourfold army—fought. ॥40॥
2.5.16.41: With maces and sharp arrows, with tridents, paṭṭiśas and lances, and some with axes and spears, they struck one another. ॥41॥
2.5.16.42: There, those mighty ones struck with various other weapons. Likewise the gods, great heroes endowed with the strength of Hṛṣīkeśa, fought, hurling sharp arrows and roaring like lions. ॥42॥
2.5.16.43: Some with very sharp arrows, some with pestles and lances, some with axes and spears—they struck one another. ॥43॥
2.5.16.44: Thus a great battle took place between the gods and the Daityas, exceedingly fierce, indeed causing fear to the sages and the Siddhas. ॥44॥
2.5.16.iti: Thus ends the sixteenth adhyāya, named The description of the gods' battle, in the account of the slaying of Jalandhara, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥16॥
2.5.17.1: Sanatkumāra said: Then the mighty Daityas struck down all the gods, whose minds were distraught with fear, with spears, axes and paṭṭiśa blades. ॥1॥
2.5.17.2: Their bodies pierced by the weapons of the Daityas, all the gods together with Vāsava Indra, their minds distraught with fear, fled from the battle. ॥2॥
2.5.17.3: Then, seeing the gods intent on flight, Hṛṣīkeśa, Viṣṇu, mounted on Garuḍa, quickly came forward to fight. ॥3॥
2.5.17.4: Flashing on all sides with radiance from the discus Sudarśana, his lotus-hand finely adorned by it, he who grants fearlessness to his devotees shone forth. ॥4॥
2.5.17.5: Bearing the conch, sword, mace and the bow Śārṅga, filled with anger, wielding fierce weapons, the great hero, skilled in every kind of warfare, came on. ॥5॥
2.5.17.6: Twanging the bow named Śārṅga, he roared; by that mighty sound of his, O sage, the three worlds were filled. ॥6॥
2.5.17.7: And with the arrows issuing from Śārṅga, Lord Viṣṇu, seething with rage, cut off the heads of the sons of Diti by the crore. ॥7॥
2.5.17.8: Then, battered by the wind of the swift wings of Aruṇa's younger brother Garuḍa, the Daityas, whirled about by the gale, wheeled in the sky like clouds. ॥8॥
2.5.17.9: Then Jalandhara, the great Daitya who terrified the hosts of gods, seeing the Daityas battered by the gale, grew exceedingly angry. ॥9॥
2.5.17.10: Seeing him crushing the Daityas, the hero, his lip quivering, rushed forward with speed to fight with Hari. ॥10॥
2.5.17.11: That lord of the Daityas let out a great roar that terrified gods and asuras; ears were split from hearing it. ॥11॥
2.5.17.12: Then, filled by the dreadful, mighty roar of the Daitya Jalandhara, the whole world trembled. ॥12॥
2.5.17.13: Then a great battle arose between Viṣṇu and the lord of the Daityas, who with their arrows made the sky as if it had no space left. ॥13॥
2.5.17.14: And by that fearsome battle between the two of them, O sage, great amazement arose among the gods, asuras, sages and Siddhas alike. ॥14॥
2.5.17.15: With floods of arrows Viṣṇu cut down the Daitya's banner, parasol, bow and arrows, and struck him in the heart with a single arrow. ॥15॥
2.5.17.16: Then the Daitya, leaping up swiftly, mace in hand, struck Garuḍa on the head and felled him to the ground. ॥16॥
2.5.17.17: Filled with anger, his lip quivering, the Daitya struck Viṣṇu in the heart with a sharp spear blazing with light. ॥17॥
2.5.17.18: Viṣṇu, the slayer of Daityas, as if laughing, cut the mace with his sword, and twanging Śārṅga, pierced him with sharp arrows. ॥18॥
2.5.17.19: Viṣṇu, the slayer of the gods' foes, overcome with wrath, swiftly struck the Daitya Jalandhara with a terrifying, exceedingly sharp arrow. ॥19॥
2.5.17.20: Seeing that arrow of his approaching, the mighty Daitya cut it with an arrow and quickly struck Viṣṇu in the heart. ॥20॥
2.5.17.21: Keśava too, the hero, cut that mighty arrow shot by the asura into pieces the size of sesame seeds and roared. ॥21॥
2.5.17.22: Trembling with anger, he again fitted an arrow to the bow; then the mighty one Jalandhara cut that shaft with an arrow. ॥22॥
2.5.17.23: Vāsudeva, in anger, again fitted an arrow to his bow for the destruction of the gods' enemy, and roared like a lion. ॥23॥
2.5.17.24: Then Jalandhara, the mighty lord of the Daityas, biting his lip in fury, cut Viṣṇu's bow called Śārṅga with an arrow of his own. ॥24॥
2.5.17.25: And again, with very sharp arrows, the great hero of fierce valour, the terror of the gods, struck Madhusūdana. ॥25॥
2.5.17.26: Lord Keśava, protector of the worlds, his bow cut, hurled his supreme mace for the destruction of Jalandhara. ॥26॥
2.5.17.27: That mace, hurled by Hari, resembling a blazing fire and unfailing in its course, swiftly struck his body. ॥27॥
2.5.17.28: Struck by it, the great Daitya Jalandhara, drunk with pride, did not move in the least, as though hit by a garland of flowers. ॥28॥
2.5.17.29: Then the wrathful Jalandhara, terror of the gods, frenzied in battle, hurled at Hari a trident that looked like fire. ॥29॥
2.5.17.30: Then Viṣṇu, remembering the lotus-feet of Śiva, forcefully and quickly cut that trident with his sword named Nandaka. ॥30॥
2.5.17.31: When the trident was cut, the lord of the Daityas suddenly leapt up, came quickly, and struck Viṣṇu in the chest with his firm fist. ॥31॥
2.5.17.32: That great hero Viṣṇu too, disregarding the pain of it, struck Jalandhara in the chest with his firm fist. ॥32॥
2.5.17.33: Then the two mighty ones fought hand to hand, with arms, fists and knees, making the earth resound. ॥33॥
2.5.17.34: Having thus fought for a very long time with that asura, he Viṣṇu was astonished, O best of sages, and felt weariness in his heart. ॥34॥
2.5.17.35: Then the Lord, the master of māyā, foremost of those who know illusion, being pleased, spoke to the king of Daityas in a voice deep as a thundercloud. ॥35॥
2.5.17.36: Viṣṇu said: O, O best among the foremost Daityas, frenzied in battle, you are blessed, since you, a great lord, are not afraid of these great and excellent weapons. ॥36॥
2.5.17.37: By these very fierce weapons many Daityas have been slain; arrogant heroes in great battles, their bodies cut apart, have gone to death. ॥37॥
2.5.17.38: I am pleased with your fighting, O great Daitya; you are great. No hero equal to you has been seen in the three worlds with their moving and unmoving beings. ॥38॥
2.5.17.39: Choose a boon, O lord of Daityas; I am pleased by your valour. I will give you even what should not be given—whatever is in your mind. ॥39॥
2.5.17.40: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of Viṣṇu, Hari, the master of illusion, the greatly intelligent king of the Daityas, Jalandhara, replied. ॥40॥
2.5.17.41: Jalandhara said: If you are pleased, O gracious one, grant me this boon: dwell in my house together with my sister and with me, along with your attendants. ॥41॥
2.5.17.42: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard those words of the great demon, the lord of the gods, the blessed Hari, with a dejected mind, said, so be it. ॥42॥
2.5.17.43: Then that Viṣṇu, having come to the city named Jalandhara together with Ramā, dwelt there along with all the hosts of gods. ॥43॥
2.5.17.44: Then the demon Jalandhara, having reached his own abode, lived there with his sister and with Viṣṇu, his mind overflowing with joy. ॥44॥
2.5.17.45: Then Jalandhara, having installed the Dānavas in the offices of the gods, returned joyfully to the surface of the earth. ॥45॥
2.5.17.46: Whatever jewels had been amassed among the gods, Gandharvas and Siddhas, the son of the Ocean brought them under his own control and remained there. ॥46॥
2.5.17.47: Having installed the very mighty demon Niśumbha in the realm of Pātāla, the powerful one brought Śeṣa and the others up to the earth. ॥47॥
2.5.17.48: Making the hosts of gods, Gandharvas and Siddhas, and serpents, Rākṣasas and humans citizens in his own city, he ruled the three worlds. ॥48॥
2.5.17.49: Thus Jalandhara, having made the gods subject to his will, protected his subjects righteously, like his own sons. ॥49॥
2.5.17.50: While he ruled the kingdom righteously, no one was seen who was sick, nor sorrowful, nor emaciated, nor wretched. ॥50॥
2.5.17.iti: Thus ends the seventeenth adhyāya, named The description of the battle between Viṣṇu and Jalandhara, in the account of Jalandhara, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥17॥
2.5.18.1: Sanatkumāra said: While that great Asura was thus ruling the earth righteously, the gods became miserable, O lord of sages, because they had lost their lordship. ॥1॥
2.5.18.2: All those distressed gods went in their minds for refuge to Śiva, to Śaṅkara, the god of gods, the lord of all, the master. ॥2॥
2.5.18.3: To end their own sorrow they praised with pleasing words the blessed Maheśvara, the giver of all, who is loving toward his devotees. ॥3॥
2.5.18.4: That Mahādeva, who grants all desires to his devotees, summoned Nārada and sent him forth, wishing to accomplish the gods' task. ॥4॥
2.5.18.5: Then the divine sage Nārada, wise, a devotee of Śambhu and the refuge of the good, went by Śiva's command to the gods in the city of the Daitya. ॥5॥
2.5.18.6: All those agitated gods, led by Vāsava, seeing the sage Nārada coming, quickly rose up. ॥6॥
2.5.18.7: Bowing, those gods headed by Śakra, with eager faces, lovingly offered a seat to the sage Nārada. ॥7॥
2.5.18.8: Having bowed deeply to that excellent sage, comfortably seated on the seat, the dejected gods led by Vāsava again addressed the lord of sages. ॥8॥
2.5.18.9: The gods said: O best among excellent sages, O mine of compassion, hear our sorrow; having heard it, destroy it quickly, for you are able, being dear to Śaṅkara. ॥9॥
2.5.18.10: We gods have been utterly routed by the Daitya Jalandhara from our own places and from our lordship; we are distressed and bewildered. ॥10॥
2.5.18.11: The hot-rayed Sun and likewise the Moon have been expelled from their own places, as have Fire, the King of Dharma, and the other guardians of the worlds. ॥11॥
2.5.18.12: All the gods have been sorely oppressed by that exceedingly mighty one; we have met with great sorrow and have come to you for refuge. ॥12॥
2.5.18.13: In battle that mighty one, the great Daitya Jalandhara, crusher of all the immortals, brought Hṛṣīkeśa under his control. ॥13॥
2.5.18.14: Subject to him and bound by a boon, Hari has dwelt in his house—that Viṣṇu, together with Lakṣmī, who is the accomplisher of all our aims. ॥14॥
2.5.18.15: O great-minded one, make an effort for Jalandhara's destruction. You have come to us by the power of destiny, you who always accomplish every aim. ॥15॥
2.5.18.16: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words of the immortals, Nārada, tiger among sages and mine of compassion, comforted them and spoke. ॥16॥
2.5.18.17: Nārada said: I know, O gods, that you have been defeated by the king of the Daityas, have met with sorrow, are oppressed, and have indeed been expelled from your places. ॥17॥
2.5.18.18: With my own power I will accomplish your aim; of this there is no doubt. I am favourable to you here, since you, O immortals, have met with sorrow. ॥18॥
2.5.18.19: Sanatkumāra said: Having spoken thus and comforted all the gods, the best of sages went to Jalandhara's assembly to see the beloved of the Dānavas. ॥19॥
2.5.18.20: Then, seeing the best of sages arrive, the Daitya Jalandhara rose and with supreme devotion gave him an excellent, foremost seat. ॥20॥
2.5.18.21: Having duly honoured him, the lord of the Dānavas, greatly amazed, then laughed heartily and spoke these words to the best of sages. ॥21॥
2.5.18.22: Jalandhara said: From where have you come, O Brahmin? And what have you seen anywhere? Command me, O sage, regarding the purpose for which you have come here. ॥22॥
2.5.18.23: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words of the lord of the Daityas, the great sage Nārada, pleased at heart, replied to Jalandhara. ॥23॥
2.5.18.24: Nārada said: O Jalandhara, lord of all Dānavas and Daityas, O great-minded one, you are blessed, O lord of all worlds; you alone are the enjoyer of jewels. ॥24॥
2.5.18.25: Hear the reason for my coming, O best of Daitya lords; I will tell you all of it—the purpose for which I have come here. ॥25॥
2.5.18.26: O lord of the Daityas, I went by chance to the peak of Kailāsa, a great forest of wish-fulfilling trees extending ten thousand yojanas, ॥26॥
2.5.18.27: filled with hundreds of wish-granting cows, brilliantly lit by wish-fulfilling gems, made wholly of gold, divine, and everywhere adorned with wonders. ॥27॥
2.5.18.28: There I saw Śaṅkara seated with Umā—beautiful in every limb, fair-complexioned, three-eyed, moon-crested. ॥28॥
2.5.18.29: Seeing that great marvel, a question then arose in me: could such prosperity exist anywhere else in the three worlds or not? ॥29॥
2.5.18.30: At that moment, O lord of the Daityas, I remembered your prosperity too; wishing to behold it, I have come here into your presence. ॥30॥
2.5.18.31: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing this from Nārada, that Daitya lord Jalandhara respectfully showed him his entire prosperity. ॥31॥
2.5.18.32: Having seen it, the wise Nārada, a skilled accomplisher of the gods' task, spoke to that Daitya lord Jalandhara, prompted by the Lord. ॥32॥
2.5.18.33: Nārada said: Indeed, O excellent hero, you now possess complete and splendid prosperity. You are the lord of the three worlds—so what wonder is possible here? ॥33॥
2.5.18.34: Gems, heaps of jewels, riches such as elephants—these shine in your house here today, and whatever precious things there are, those too. ॥34॥
2.5.18.35: You have brought the jewel among elephants, Śakra's Airāvata, and likewise, O great hero, the jewel among horses, the Sun's steed Uccaiḥśravas. ॥35॥
2.5.18.36: You have brought the wish-fulfilling tree and the treasures of Dhanada (Kubera), and you have brought the swan-yoked aerial chariot of Vedhas (Brahmā). ॥36॥
2.5.18.37: Thus, O lord of the Daityas, whatever excellent jewels exist in heaven, on earth and in the netherworld, all of them shine in your house on every side. ॥37॥
2.5.18.38: Seeing this prosperity of yours, complete and manifold, splendidly adorned with elephants, horses and the like, I am pleased, O great hero. ॥38॥
2.5.18.39: But, O Jalandhara, the supreme jewel of a wife is not in your house. You ought especially to bring that jewel among women. ॥39॥
2.5.18.40: O Jalandhara, in whose house all fine jewels exist, if there is no jewel of a wife, those do not shine—they are surely in vain. ॥40॥
2.5.18.41: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words of the great-souled Nārada, the king of the Daityas, his mind agitated by desire, spoke. ॥41॥
2.5.18.42: Jalandhara said: O Nārada, O divine sage, salutations to you, O great lord. Tell me now where that finest jewel of a wife is to be found. ॥42॥
2.5.18.43: If that jewel exists anywhere at all in the universe, I shall bring it from there, O Brahmin — truly, truly, there is no doubt. ॥43॥
2.5.18.44: Nārada said: On Kailāsa, which is exceedingly delightful and filled with every kind of riches, there dwells Śambhu, bearing the form of a yogin, sky-clad. ॥44॥
2.5.18.45: His wife is truly most lovely, marked with all auspicious marks, beautiful in every limb, enchanting, named Pārvatī. ॥45॥
2.5.18.46: Such a form, unmatched by any other, has never been seen anywhere — full of wonder, utterly marvellous, bewitching even to accomplished yogins, most lovely to behold, and bestowing supreme prosperity. ॥46॥
2.5.18.47: I reckon in my own mind today, O hero Jalandhara, that in the three worlds there is no one more prosperous than Śiva, who is endowed with this jewel of a wife. ॥47॥
2.5.18.48: Immersed in the ocean of her loveliness, the four-faced Brahmā once lost his composure — to which woman can she be compared? ॥48॥
2.5.18.49: By her, through her own playful charm, even the foe of Madana, though free of passion and wholly self-dependent, was brought under her control. ॥49॥
2.5.18.50: Such prosperity as belongs to him who enjoys that jewel among women is not yours, O lord of the Daityas, even though you are master of all jewels. ॥50॥
2.5.18.51: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this, the divine sage Nārada, renowned throughout the worlds, departed through the sky, intent on rendering service to the gods. ॥51॥
2.5.18.iti: Thus ends the eighteenth adhyāya, named The dialogue of the divine sage and Jalandhara, in the account of the slaying of Jalandhara, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥18॥
2.5.19.1: Vyāsa said: O all-knowing Sanatkumāra, when Nārada had gone to heaven, what did that king of the Daityas do? Tell me that in full detail. ॥1॥
2.5.19.2: Sanatkumāra said: When Nārada had taken leave of the Daitya and gone to heaven, the king of the Daityas, from hearing of her beauty, became tormented by the fever of love. ॥2॥
2.5.19.3: Then the Daitya Jalandhara, under the sway of Time, his reason destroyed and deluded, summoned his messenger, the son of Siṃhikā Rāhu. ॥3॥
2.5.19.4: Seeing him arrive, Jalandhara, son of the Ocean, his mind overpowered by desire, addressed him properly and spoke. ॥4॥
2.5.19.5: Jalandhara said: O best among excellent messengers, accomplisher of every task, O greatly wise son of Siṃhikā, go to Mount Kailāsa. ॥5॥
2.5.19.6: There lives a yogin called Śambhu, an ascetic wearing matted locks, his whole body adorned with ash, dispassionate, with senses subdued. ॥6॥
2.5.19.7: Having gone there, O messenger, you must speak thus, with a fearless heart, to that dispassionate yogin Śaṅkara who wears matted locks: ॥7॥
2.5.19.8: O yogin, ocean of compassion, what use is a jewel of a wife to you, a forest-dweller attended by bhūtas, pretas, piśācas and the like? ॥8॥
2.5.19.9: In a world of which I am lord, O yogin, such a state of affairs is not fitting. Therefore give your own jewel of a wife to me, the enjoyer of jewels. ॥9॥
2.5.19.10: Whatever fine jewels exist in the three worlds, they are mine. Know that the whole world, moving and unmoving, is under my control. ॥10॥
2.5.19.11: Indra's jewel of an elephant, and the supreme jewel Uccaiḥśravas, were seized suddenly by force, as was the Pārijāta tree. ॥11॥
2.5.19.12: The aerial chariot yoked with swans, a jewel, greatly divine, excellent and wondrous, belonging to Brahmā, stands in my courtyard. ॥12॥
2.5.19.13: The divine jewel-treasures, Mahāpadma and the rest, of the giver of wealth Kubera, and Varuṇa's umbrella that streams gold, are in my house. ॥13॥
2.5.19.14: The great filamented garland of ever-unfading lotuses that belonged to my father is now mine alone, and so too is the noose of the lord of waters Varuṇa. ॥14॥
2.5.19.15: Death's excellent spear, which causes the departure of life, was taken by me by force. Agni gave me two divine garments purified by fire. ॥15॥
2.5.19.16: Thus, O lord of yogins, all jewels shine in my possession. Therefore you too, O wearer of matted locks, give me your jewel of a wife. ॥16॥
2.5.19.17: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard his words, Rāhu, admitted by Nandin, went to the assembly hall of Ugra Śiva, his eyes wide with wonder. ॥17॥
2.5.19.18: Having gone there, he saw Śiva himself, the God of gods, the great Lord, who dispels darkness by his own splendour, resplendent with a coating of ash, ॥18॥
2.5.19.19: shining with the honours of a great king, most wondrous, beautiful in every limb, Hara adorned with divine ornaments. ॥19॥
2.5.19.20: His body overwhelmed by that splendour, the messenger named Rāhu, falling from his pride, bowed to him and drew near to Śambhu. ॥20॥
2.5.19.21: Then the son of Siṃhikā, seated before him and eager to speak, prompted by a sign, addressed these words to the Three-eyed One. ॥21॥
2.5.19.22: Rāhu said: I am the messenger of the lord of the three worlds, who is ever served by Daityas and serpents; sent by him, I have come here into your presence. ॥22॥
2.5.19.23: Jalandhara, son of the Ocean, lord of all the Daitya folk, has become ruler of the three worlds and supreme commander of all. ॥23॥
2.5.19.24: That mighty king of the Daityas, like Death to the gods, has said something addressed to you, the yogin; hear it. ॥24॥
2.5.19.25: O bull-bannered one, hear the command of that lord, the master of the Daityas, of great divine power, lord of all jewels. ॥25॥
2.5.19.26: How can the lovely daughter of Himavat be the wife of you, who always dwell in cremation grounds, wear a garland of bones and go naked? ॥26॥
2.5.19.27: I am the overlord of jewels, and she is called a jewel among women; therefore she is fit for me alone, not for you who live on alms. ॥27॥
2.5.19.28: The three worlds are under my control; I enjoy the shares of the sacrifices. Whatever jewels there are in these three worlds are in my palace. ॥28॥
2.5.19.29: We are enjoyers of jewels, whereas you are surely a naked yogin. Give me your jewel of a wife; subjects should bring happiness to their king. ॥29॥
2.5.19.30: Sanatkumāra said: As Rāhu was speaking thus, from between the brows of the trident-bearer there arose a fierce being with a roar like a violent thunderbolt. ॥30॥
2.5.19.31: He had a lion's face with a darting tongue, fiery blazing eyes; huge, with hair standing on end and a gaunt body, he was like a second Nṛsiṃha. ॥31॥
2.5.19.32: With a huge body, mighty arms and legs like palm trees, terrifying, that being rushed swiftly and with force at Rāhu. ॥32॥
2.5.19.33: Seeing him coming to devour him, Rāhu, stricken with fear, ran outside at great speed; but he caught hold of him. ॥33॥
2.5.19.34: Rāhu said: O God of gods, great Lord, protect me who have come to you for refuge. You are the Lord, ever to be worshipped by gods and demons, possessed of supreme sovereignty. ॥34॥
2.5.19.35: O Mahādeva, O Īśāna, this most terrifying being, your servant, has come to devour me, a Brāhmaṇa. ॥35॥
2.5.19.36: Protect me from him, O Lord of gods, you who are tender to those who seek refuge, so that he does not devour me. Salutations to you again and again. ॥36॥
2.5.19.37: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing then the words of the Brāhmaṇa, O sage, Mahādeva, the Lord who loves the wretched and helpless, spoke to that gaṇa of his. ॥37॥
2.5.19.38: Mahādeva said: Spare this Brāhmaṇa messenger named Rāhu, a lord in his own right, who has sought refuge; those who seek refuge are to be protected, not punished, O best of gaṇas. ॥38॥
2.5.19.39: Sanatkumāra said: Thus addressed by the compassionate Lord of Girijā, the gaṇa, having heard the word Brāhmaṇa, at once released Rāhu. ॥39॥
2.5.19.40: Then that being, having released Rāhu in the sky, came near to Śiva and addressed Mahādeva in a plaintive voice. ॥40॥
2.5.19.41: The being said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, mine of compassion, Śaṅkara, you who are tender toward those who come for refuge, you have made me give up my food. ॥41॥
2.5.19.42: Hunger torments me, O Lord, and I am utterly emaciated with hunger. What is to be my food, O Lord of gods? Command me that, O master. ॥42॥
2.5.19.43: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of that being, the great Lord, of wondrous ways, playful, and the doer of good to his own, replied. ॥43॥
2.5.19.44: Maheśvara said: If your hunger is very great, if hunger torments you, then quickly eat the flesh of your own hands and feet. ॥44॥
2.5.19.45: Sanatkumāra said: Thus commanded by Śiva, that being ate his own flesh from the hands and feet, until only the head remained. ॥45॥
2.5.19.46: Seeing that only the head was left, Sadāśiva, greatly pleased and amazed, spoke to that being of terrible deeds. ॥46॥
2.5.19.47: Śiva said: O great Gaṇa, you are blessed, a keeper of my command. I am exceedingly pleased with you for this deed, O best of the good. ॥47॥
2.5.19.48: Named Kīrtimukha, be always my door-keeper, a great Gaṇa, a great hero, causing fear to all the wicked. ॥48॥
2.5.19.49: You are dear to me; in my worship you shall always be worshipped by my people. Those who do not worship you are by no means doers of what pleases me. ॥49॥
2.5.19.50: Sanatkumāra said: Having thus received the boon from Śambhu, that being rejoiced. From that time on, Kīrtimukha has stood at the door of the Lord of gods. ॥50॥
2.5.19.51: That Gaṇa is to be worshipped especially in the worship of Śiva. Those here who do not worship him first, their worship would be in vain. ॥51॥
2.5.19.iti: Thus ends the nineteenth adhyāya, named The dialogue of the messenger, in the account of the slaying of Jalandhara, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥19॥
2.5.20.1: Vyāsa said: O Sanatkumāra, all-knowing one, you have let me hear a wonderful story, in which the purifying sport (līlā) of the great lord Śaṅkara is told. ॥1॥
2.5.20.2: Now, O great sage, showing kindness towards me, tell me with great affection: where did Rāhu go after he was released by the Puruṣa? ॥2॥
2.5.20.3: Sūta said: Hearing these words of Vyāsa of boundless intellect, the great sage, son of Brahmā, replied with a pleased heart. ॥3॥
2.5.20.4: Sanatkumāra said: Rāhu, who had been released by him, fell in that Barbara region; therefore he became a Barbara — thus he gained renown on earth. ॥4॥
2.5.20.5: Then, regarding himself as born again, humbled and with his pride gone, he slowly went to the city of Jalandhara. ॥5॥
2.5.20.6: Approaching Jalandhara, the lord of the Daityas, he related to him in detail, O Vyāsa, everything that Īśa had done. ॥6॥
2.5.20.7: Hearing that, Jalandhara, the mighty son of the Ocean, best of Daitya chiefs, had his body agitated with rage. ॥7॥
2.5.20.8: Then the best of Daityas, his mind overpowered by anger, ordered the mobilisation of all the Daitya armies. ॥8॥
2.5.20.9: Jalandhara said: Let all the Daityas headed by Kālanemi march forth, and likewise the heroes led by Śumbha and Niśumbha, together with their forces. ॥9॥
2.5.20.10: Let crores born of heroic families go, and those of the Kambu clan, the Daurhṛdas, the Kālakas, the Kālakeyas, the Mauryas and likewise the Dhaumras. ॥10॥
2.5.20.11: Having commanded thus, the valourous lord of the Asuras, son of the Ocean, quickly marched out, surrounded by crores of Daityas. ॥11॥
2.5.20.12: Then in front of him appeared Śukra, and Rāhu with severed head; and his crown, slipping through the force of his movement, fell to the ground. ॥12॥
2.5.20.13: The sky appeared filled with clouds as in the rainy season; many ill omens arose, foretelling the great sleep of death. ॥13॥
2.5.20.14: Seeing his preparations thus, the gods together with Vāsava went unseen to Kailāsa, the abode of Śaṅkara. ॥14॥
2.5.20.15: Going there and seeing Śiva, all the gods with Vāsava bowed deeply, and with shoulders bent and palms joined they praised him. ॥15॥
2.5.20.16: The gods said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, mine of compassion, Śaṅkara, salutation be to you, O great lord; protect us who have come to you for refuge. ॥16॥
2.5.20.17: O lord, we are terribly distressed by the dreadful calamity caused by Jalandhara; together with the king of gods we have been expelled from our places and dwell on the earth. ॥17॥
2.5.20.18: How is it, master, that you do not know of this calamity of the gods, O lord? Therefore, to protect us, slay the son of the Ocean. ॥18॥
2.5.20.19: Garuḍa-bannered Viṣṇu, whom you formerly appointed for our protection, O master, is today unable to protect us. ॥19॥
2.5.20.20: Subject to him, he lives in his house together with Ramā; and we gods too stay there, subject to his commands. ॥20॥
2.5.20.21: Unnoticed, we have come here into your presence, O Śambhu. That mighty son of the Ocean is coming to make war with you. ॥21॥
2.5.20.22: Therefore, master, all-knowing one, you should slay that Jalandhara in battle without delay; protect us who have sought refuge. ॥22॥
2.5.20.23: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this, all the gods with Vāsava bowed to the lord and stood humbly, gazing at the feet of Maheśa. ॥23॥
2.5.20.24: Hearing these words of the gods, the Bull-bannered one laughed, quickly summoned Viṣṇu, and spoke these words. ॥24॥
2.5.20.25: Īśvara said: O Hṛṣīkeśa, great Viṣṇu, the gods have come here to me for refuge, greatly distressed and oppressed by Jalandhara. ॥25॥
2.5.20.26: O Viṣṇu, how is it that Jalandhara was not slain by you in battle? And you have even gone to his house, abandoning your own Vaikuṇṭha. ॥26॥
2.5.20.27: For you were appointed by me, the independent sporting one, for the protection of the good and for the restraint of the wicked. ॥27॥
2.5.20.28: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of Maheśa, Hari, the Garuḍa-bannered, humble in spirit, bowing with joined palms, replied. ॥28॥
2.5.20.29: Viṣṇu said: Because he was born from a portion of you, and because he is the brother of Śrī, I did not slay him in battle; you slay this Dānava. ॥29॥
2.5.20.30: He is of great strength, a great hero, invincible to all the gods and to others as well, O lord of gods; I tell you this truly. ॥30॥
2.5.20.31: I fought with him for a long time, together with the gods, but my means did not prevail against that bull among Dānavas. ॥31॥
2.5.20.32: Pleased by his valour, I said, ask for a boon. Hearing my words, he chose an excellent boon: ॥32॥
2.5.20.33: Live in my house with the gods, together with my sister and me, subject to me, O great Viṣṇu. Thus I went to his house. ॥33॥
2.5.20.34: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of Viṣṇu, Śaṅkara, the great lord, compassionate and loving to his devotees, laughed and, well pleased, spoke. ॥34॥
2.5.20.35: Maheśvara said: O Viṣṇu, best of gods, listen attentively to my words: I shall slay the great Daitya Jalandhara, there is no doubt. ॥35॥
2.5.20.36: Go to your own abode without fear; let the gods too surely go, fearless and free of doubt, considering the lord of the Asuras as already slain. ॥36॥
2.5.20.37: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of Maheśa, the lord of Ramā, his doubt removed, quickly went with the gods to his own abode. ॥37॥
2.5.20.38: Meanwhile, O Vyāsa, that mighty lord of the Daityas, of great prowess, went to the foot of the mountain together with the armed Asuras. ॥38॥
2.5.20.39: Then, besieging Kailāsa with a vast army, the great one stood there like Death, roaring like a lion. ॥39॥
2.5.20.40: Then, hearing the tumult arising from the roars of the Daityas, the great lord Maheśāna, of mighty sport, destroyer of the wicked, became exceedingly angry. ॥40॥
2.5.20.41: Having taken count of them, Mahādeva Hara, of great might and fond of sport, commanded his own very powerful gaṇas, Nandin and the rest. ॥41॥
2.5.20.42: By Śiva's command all the gaṇas, headed by Nandin, the elephant-faced one and the Commander Kārttikeya, armed themselves for battle, filled with great haste. ॥42॥
2.5.20.43: All the gaṇas, frenzied with wrath, descended from Kailāsa, great heroes leaping and raising battle cries, eager indeed for the fight. ॥43॥
2.5.20.44: Then on the foothills of Kailāsa there arose a terrible battle between the lords of the pramathas and the daityas, thronged with weapons and missiles. ॥44॥
2.5.20.45: With masses of kettledrums, mṛdaṅgas and conches, with sounds that thrilled the heroes, and with the noise of elephants, horses and chariots, the earth resounded and trembled. ॥45॥
2.5.20.46: With masses of spears, javelins and arrows, with clubs, nooses and paṭṭiśa-axes, the sky, filled with them, shone as if strewn with pearls. ॥46॥
2.5.20.47: The earth shone with slain elephants, horses and foot-soldiers, just as of old it was thickly covered with the great mountains struck down by the thunderbolt. ॥47॥
2.5.20.48: With masses of daityas slain by the pramathas, and likewise of gaṇas slain by the daityas, the earth then became impassable, thick with a mire of fat, blood and flesh. ॥48॥
2.5.20.49: Bhārgava Śukra revived the masses of daityas slain by the pramathas, again and again in the battle, by the power of the Mṛtasañjīvanī lore. ॥49॥
2.5.20.50: Seeing those daityas stirring again, all the gaṇas, stricken with fear, reported to the God of gods all that Śukra was doing. ॥50॥
