2.5.20.51: Hearing that, Lord Rudra became violently angry; he became terrifying and exceedingly fierce, setting the directions ablaze. ॥51॥
2.5.20.52: Then from Rudra's mouth there arose a Kṛtyā, exceedingly dreadful, with legs like palm trees, a mouth like a cavern, and breasts that crushed the trees. ॥52॥
2.5.20.53: She swiftly reached the battlefield, O best of sages; that very terrible one roamed about, devouring the great asuras. ॥53॥
2.5.20.54: Then, fearless, she went quickly into the very midst of the battle, where Bhārgava stood surrounded by the foremost lords of the daityas. ॥54॥
2.5.20.55: Pervading the sky with her own radiance and filling the earth too, O sage, she held Bhārgava in her yoni and, vanishing, went off into the sky. ॥55॥
2.5.20.56: Seeing Bhārgava seized, the troops of the daitya army, though frenzied for war, withdrew from the battle with faces downcast. ॥56॥
2.5.20.57: Then the army of the daityas, stricken with fear of the gaṇas, broke apart, like a heap of grass scattered by the force of the wind. ॥57॥
2.5.20.58: Seeing the daitya army broken through fear of the gaṇas, the commanders Niśumbha and Śumbha, and Kālanemi, utterly unable to bear it, grew furious. ॥58॥
2.5.20.59: Those three mighty ones held back the army of the gaṇas, releasing showers of arrows like clouds in the rainy season. ॥59॥
2.5.20.60: Then those masses of daitya arrows, like swarms of locusts, blotted out the sky and all the directions, and made the gaṇa army tremble. ॥60॥
2.5.20.61: The gaṇas, pierced by hundreds of arrows and pouring streams of blood, looked like kiṃśuka trees in spring, and were aware of nothing at all. ॥61॥
2.5.20.62: Then, seeing their own force routed, Nandin, Lambodara and Kārttikeya, unable to bear it and full of haste, forcibly held back the foremost daityas. ॥62॥
2.5.20.iti: Thus ends the twentieth adhyāya, named The description of the general battle between the gaṇas and the Asuras, in the account of the slaying of Jalandhara, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥20॥
2.5.21.1: Sanatkumāra said: Seeing those lords of the gaṇas, Nandī, the elephant-faced one and the six-faced one, the Dānavas rushed at them in indignation for single combat. ॥1॥
2.5.21.2: Kālanemi rushed at Nandī, Śumbha likewise at Lambodara, and Niśumbha, wary, rushed at the six-faced god. ॥2॥
2.5.21.3: Niśumbha forcefully pierced Kārttikeya's peacock in the breast with five arrows, and it fell down in a swoon. ॥3॥
2.5.21.4: Then the wielder of the spear, enraged, with five arrows pierced his horses and his charioteer on the chariot. ॥4॥
2.5.21.5: With another sharp arrow the hero, battle-mad, swiftly struck Niśumbha, enemy of the gods, and roared. ॥5॥
2.5.21.6: The asura named Niśumbha too, a great and exceedingly mighty hero, struck that roaring Kārttikeya in battle with his own arrow. ॥6॥
2.5.21.7: Then, just as Kārttikeya seized his spear in anger, Niśumbha swiftly felled him with his own spear. ॥7॥
2.5.21.8: Thus, O Vyāsa, a great battle took place right there between Kārttikeya and Niśumbha, both roaring heroic cries. ॥8॥
2.5.21.9: Then Nandīśvara pierced Kālanemi with arrows, and with seven more cut down his horses, banner, chariot and charioteer. ॥9॥
2.5.21.10: Kālanemi, greatly enraged, cut Nandī's bow with very sharp arrows released from his own bow. ॥10॥
2.5.21.11: Then the hero Nandīśvara, driving back that great asura Kālanemi, struck him hard in the chest with his trident. ॥11॥
2.5.21.12: He, his heart pierced by the trident, his horses and charioteer slain, tore off a mountain peak and struck Nandī with it. ॥12॥
2.5.21.13: Then Śumbha and Gaṇeśa, riding chariot and mouse respectively, fighting, pierced each other with volleys of arrows. ॥13॥
2.5.21.14: Gaṇeśa then pierced Śumbha in the breast with an arrow, and with three arrows knocked his charioteer to the ground. ॥14॥
2.5.21.15: Then Śumbha too, furious, pierced the lord of the gaṇas with a shower of arrows and the mouse with three, and roared with a voice like a thundercloud. ॥15॥
2.5.21.16: The mouse, its body pierced by arrows, staggered in severe pain; and Lambodara, fallen, indeed became a foot-soldier. ॥16॥
2.5.21.17: Then Lambodara struck Śumbha in the breast with his axe and felled him to the ground, and he remounted the mouse. ॥17॥
2.5.21.18: The elephant-faced lord was again ready for battle; the two demons, laughing, struck the great elephant-faced one in anger with a goad. ॥18॥
2.5.21.19: Kālanemi and Niśumbha, both together, in anger swiftly struck Lambodara at once with arrows like venomous serpents. ॥19॥
2.5.21.20: Seeing him being harassed, the mighty Vīrabhadra rushed forward swiftly, accompanied by ten million bhūtas. ॥20॥
2.5.21.21: Kūṣmāṇḍas, Bhairavas, Vetālas, hosts of Yoginīs, Piśācas, bands of Ḍākinīs and gaṇas too went along together. ॥21॥
2.5.21.22: Then, resounding with shrill kila-kila cries, lion-roars with rumbling, and with ḍamarus, the earth trembled. ॥22॥
2.5.21.23: Then the bhūtas, rushing forward, devoured the Dānavas; leaping up they felled them, and danced on the battlefield. ॥23॥
2.5.21.24: Meanwhile, O Vyāsa, those two, Nandī and Guha, having regained consciousness, rose up and roared mightily in battle. ॥24॥
2.5.21.25: Nandī and Kārttikeya, coming together in haste, struck down the Daityas in battle with ceaseless streams of arrows. ॥25॥
2.5.21.26: With its Daityas cut, pierced, slain, felled and devoured, that army became distraught, with downcast faces. ॥26॥
2.5.21.27: Thus Nandī, Kārttikeya, the valiant Vikaṭa, Vīrabhadra and other gaṇas roared mightily in the battle. ॥27॥
2.5.21.28: Niśumbha and Śumbha, those two generals of the son of the Ocean, the great Daitya Kālanemi, and other asuras were defeated. ॥28॥
2.5.21.29: Then, seeing his army routed, the mighty son of the Ocean advanced against the gaṇas in a chariot with lofty banners. ॥29॥
2.5.21.30: Then even the defeated Daityas became greatly elated; ready for battle, O Vyāsa, they roared loudly. ॥30॥
2.5.21.31: All the gaṇas of Rudra too, flushed with victory, roared, O sage: Nandī, Kārttika, the elephant-faced one, Vīrabhadra and others. ॥31॥
2.5.21.32: The clamour of elephants, horses and chariots, the sound of conches and kettledrums, and lion-roars arose in both armies. ॥32॥
2.5.21.33: By Jalandhara's volleys of arrows, like sheets of mist, the space between heaven and earth became covered. ॥33॥
2.5.21.34: Having pierced Śailādi with five, Gaṇeśa with five arrows and Vīrabhadra with twenty, he roared with a voice like a thundercloud. ॥34॥
2.5.21.35: Then Kārttikeya, the great hero, son of Rudra, swiftly pierced the Daitya Jalandhara with his spear and roared. ॥35॥
2.5.21.36: That Daitya, his eyes rolling, his body pierced by the spear, fell to the ground; but the mighty one quickly rose up. ॥36॥
2.5.21.37: Then Jalandhara, chief of the Daityas, his mind seized by fury, struck Kārttikeya on the chest with his mace. ॥37॥
2.5.21.38: Showing the mace's power to be effective, owing to the boon granted by Brahmā, O Vyāsa, the son of Śaṅkara quickly fell to the ground. ॥38॥
2.5.21.39: Likewise Nandī, struck by the mace, fell to the ground; that great hero and slayer of foes was somewhat confused in mind. ॥39॥
2.5.21.40: Then the lord of the gaṇas, enraged and exceedingly strong, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, came up and cut the Daitya's mace with his axe. ॥40॥
2.5.21.41: Vīrabhadra pierced the Dānava in the heart with three arrows, and with seven he cut down his horses, banner, bow and parasol. ॥41॥
2.5.21.42: Then the lord of the Daityas, greatly enraged, raised a dreadful spear, struck down the leader of the Gaṇas, and mounted another chariot. ॥42॥
2.5.21.43: Then that mighty lord of the Daityas, full of fury, rushed forward swiftly, disregarding that Vīrabhadra in his heart. ॥43॥
2.5.21.44: He quickly struck that Vīrabhadra with a sharp serpent-like arrow, and the great hero Jalandhara, king of the Daityas, roared. ॥44॥
2.5.21.45: Vīrabhadra too, enraged, cut that arrow with a sharp-edged shaft and pierced him with a great arrow. ॥45॥
2.5.21.46: Then those two, resplendent like the sun, the foremost of the best heroes, fought each other for a long time with various weapons and missiles. ॥46॥
2.5.21.47: Then Vīrabhadra felled his horses with arrows, and swiftly cut the bow and banner of the chariot-warrior. ॥47॥
2.5.21.48: Then that king of the Daityas, wielding an iron club, leapt down, and the mighty one quickly reached the side of Vīrabhadra. ॥48॥
2.5.21.49: The mighty hero, son of the Ocean, struck Vīrabhadra on the head with a very huge iron club and roared. ॥49॥
2.5.21.50: His head split by the very huge club, Vīrabhadra, lord of the Gaṇas, fell to the ground and shed much blood. ॥50॥
2.5.21.51: Seeing Vīrabhadra fallen, Rudra's Gaṇas, out of fear, left the battle and fled, crying out to Maheśvara. ॥51॥
2.5.21.52: Then, hearing the uproar of the Gaṇas, the moon-crested Śiva asked the heroes, the best of the Gaṇas, standing at his side. ॥52॥
2.5.21.53: Śaṅkara said: Why has this great uproar arisen among my Gaṇas? Let it be looked into, O great heroes; peace must surely be made by me. ॥53॥
2.5.21.54: While the lord of the gods was thus respectfully questioning the Gaṇas, those excellent Gaṇas arrived before the Lord. ॥54॥
2.5.21.55: Seeing them distressed, Lord Rudra asked about their welfare, and the Gaṇas recounted in detail what had happened, just as it was. ॥55॥
2.5.21.56: Hearing that, the blessed Lord Rudra, performer of great divine play, granted them freedom from fear, increasing their great enthusiasm. ॥56॥
2.5.21.iti: Thus ends the twenty-first adhyāya, named The description of the special battle, in the account of Jalandhara, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥21॥
2.5.22.1: Sanatkumāra said: Then Rudra, the great Lord, assuming a fierce form and mounted on his bull, advanced into the battle with his heroic gaṇas, as if laughing. ॥1॥
2.5.22.2: Seeing Rudra coming, the fierce gaṇas who had earlier been defeated turned back again to the battle with lion-roars. ॥2॥
2.5.22.3: And those other gaṇas of Śaṅkara too, raising heroic shouts, joyful and armed, struck down the daityas with showers of arrows. ॥3॥
2.5.22.4: All the daityas, seeing the terrifying Rudra, fled out of fear of him, as sins flee on seeing a devotee of Śaṅkara. ॥4॥
2.5.22.5: Then Jalandhara, seeing the daityas turning back from the battle, rushed at the Lord of Caṇḍī, discharging arrows by the thousands. ॥5॥
2.5.22.6: And thousands of daitya chiefs, led by Niśumbha and Śumbha, swiftly charged at Śiva, biting their lips in fury. ॥6॥
2.5.22.7: Likewise the hero Kālanemi, Khaḍgaromā, Balāhaka, Ghasmara, Pracaṇḍa and others too went against Śiva. ॥7॥
2.5.22.8: They quickly covered Rudra's gaṇas with arrows, and all those heroes headed by Śumbha hacked at their limbs, O sage. ॥8॥
2.5.22.9: Hara, seeing the army of gaṇas shrouded in a darkness of arrows, cut through that net of arrows and covered the sky with his own arrows. ॥9॥
2.5.22.10: Then he tormented the daityas with gales of arrows, and with floods of fierce arrow-nets felled them to the ground. ॥10॥
2.5.22.11: Likewise with his axe he severed Khaḍgaromā's head from his body, and with his khaṭvāṅga he split Balāhaka's head in two. ॥11॥
2.5.22.12: Having bound the daitya Ghasmara with his noose, he struck him down on the ground; and he cut down the great hero Pracaṇḍa with his trident. ॥12॥
2.5.22.13: Some were killed by the bull, some were felled by arrows; the asuras could not stand their ground, like elephants harassed by a lion. ॥13॥
2.5.22.14: Then the great daitya Jalandhara, his mind seized by anger, reproached the daityas in battle; and, steadfast, he spoke laughingly to Śumbha and the others. ॥14॥
2.5.22.15: Jalandhara said: What use are you, mere refuse cast out by your mothers, running away and being struck from behind? The slaying of the frightened is neither praiseworthy nor does it grant heaven to those who think themselves heroes. ॥15॥
2.5.22.16: If you have faith in battle, or any strength in your hearts, O petty ones, stand before me just for a moment—unless you crave vulgar comforts. ॥16॥
2.5.22.17: Death in battle is excellent, granting the fruit of all desires; above all it bestows fame, and it is declared to grant liberation as well. ॥17॥
2.5.22.18: The renunciant of supreme knowledge, and he who is slain in battle facing the foe, pierce the orb of the sun and go to the supreme abode. ॥18॥
2.5.22.19: The wise should never, anywhere, fear death, since it cannot be averted even by all possible means. ॥19॥
2.5.22.20: O heroes, for those who are born, death is born together with the body. Whether today or at the end of a hundred years, death is certain for living beings. ॥20॥
2.5.22.21: Therefore, casting off the fear of death, fight joyfully in battle; in every way there is supreme bliss both here and hereafter, without doubt. ॥21॥
2.5.22.22: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this, he exhorted his warriors repeatedly; but they did not take courage, and out of fear fled swiftly from the battle. ॥22॥
2.5.22.23: Then, seeing that army of his intent on flight, the mighty hero Jalandhara, son of the Ocean, became extremely angry. ॥23॥
2.5.22.24: Then Jalandhara, his mind seized by wrath, with a voice like a fierce thunderbolt, angrily challenged Rudra to battle. ॥24॥
2.5.22.25: Jalandhara said: Fight with me today. What is gained by slaying these? Whatever strength you have, show it, O wearer of matted locks. ॥25॥
2.5.22.26: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this, the great daitya Jalandhara struck the bull-bannered Śambhu, whose deeds are effortless, with seventy arrows. ॥26॥
2.5.22.27: Mahādeva, as if laughing, swiftly cut down those arrows of Jalandhara before they reached him, with his own sharp arrows. ॥27॥
2.5.22.28: Then with seven arrows he cut down the horses, banner, parasol and bow of the daitya Jalandhara; that was no wonder for Hara, O sage. ॥28॥
2.5.22.29: His bow cut and chariotless, the asura, son of the Ocean, enraged and swift, raised his mace and rushed at Śiva. ॥29॥
2.5.22.30: And the Lord Maheśvara, of great playfulness, at once swiftly split with his arrows into two the mace hurled by him, O son of Parāśara. ॥30॥
2.5.22.31: Even so, the great asura, greatly enraged, raised his fist and charged at that Rudra with great speed, wishing to kill him. ॥31॥
2.5.22.32: Just then that Jalandhara was quickly driven back a krośa's distance by floods of arrows from the Lord, the doer of effortless deeds. ॥32॥
2.5.22.33: Then the daitya Jalandhara, judging Rudra superior in strength, created a wondrous Gāndharva illusion to bewilder Rudra. ॥33॥
2.5.22.34: Through the power of his illusion, many troops of gandharvas and apsarases appeared, in order to bewilder Rudra. ॥34॥
2.5.22.35: Then the troops of gandharvas and apsarases sang and danced, while others played cymbals, flutes and mṛdaṅga drums. ॥35॥
2.5.22.36: Seeing that great marvel, Rudra together with his gaṇas was bewildered; he did not even notice the weapons falling from his hands. ॥36॥
2.5.22.37: Seeing Rudra wholly absorbed, the daitya Jalandhara, driven by lust, quickly went to where Gaurī was staying. ॥37॥
2.5.22.38: Having stationed the mighty Śumbha and Niśumbha in the battle, he became one with ten staff-like arms, five faces, three eyes and matted locks, ॥38॥
2.5.22.39: mounted on a great bull, in every way resembling Rudra—thus did Jalandhara become through his asura illusion, O Vyāsa. ॥39॥
2.5.22.40: Then Bhava's beloved, seeing Rudra approaching, came forward from the midst of her companions and came within his range of sight. ॥40॥
2.5.22.41: The moment the lord of the Dānavas beheld Pārvatī of lovely limbs, at that very moment he released his semen and then became numb in his limbs. ॥41॥
2.5.22.42: Then Gaurī, recognising the Dānava, overwhelmed with fear, vanished and swiftly went to the northern Mānasa lake. ॥42॥
2.5.22.43: Then the Daitya, no longer seeing her, who had vanished in an instant like a streak of lightning, went back swiftly to fight where the god Maheśvara was. ॥43॥
2.5.22.44: Pārvatī too then remembered the great Viṣṇu in her mind; at once she saw that god seated near her. ॥44॥
2.5.22.45: Seeing that Viṣṇu bowing with joined palms, Pārvatī, the Mother of the world, beloved of Śiva, spoke with a gracious mind. ॥45॥
2.5.22.46: Pārvatī said: O Viṣṇu, the Daitya Jalandhara has done a most astonishing thing. Is that conduct of the evil-minded one not known to you? ॥46॥
2.5.22.47: Hearing those words of the Mother of the world, the Garuḍa-bannered one, bowing to Śivā with joined palms and bent neck, replied. ॥47॥
2.5.22.48: The Lord said: By your grace, O Goddess, that event is known to me. Whatever you command me, O Mother, I shall do with your permission. ॥48॥
2.5.22.49: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing those words of Viṣṇu, Pārvatī spoke again, the Mother of the world, instructing Hṛṣīkeśa well in the policy of dharma. ॥49॥
2.5.22.50: Pārvatī said: The path has been shown by him alone; understand it in just the same way. By my command, violate the dharma of wifely chastity of his wife. ॥50॥
2.5.22.51: Otherwise that great Daitya cannot be slain, O lord of Ramā; there is no other dharma on the face of the earth equal to wifely chastity. ॥51॥
2.5.22.52: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing this command and receiving it on his head, Hari quickly went again to Jalandhara's city to practise deceit. ॥52॥
2.5.22.iti: Thus ends the twenty-second adhyāya, named The description of Jalandhara's battle, in the account of the slaying of Jalandhara, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥22॥
2.5.23.1: Vyāsa said: O Sanatkumāra, all-knowing one, best of speakers, tell me: what did Hari do there, and how did she abandon her dharma? ॥1॥
2.5.23.2: Sanatkumāra said: Viṣṇu, having gone to Jālandhara, the city of the demon, set his mind on breaking the wifely chastity of Vṛndā. ॥2॥
2.5.23.3: He, the best of illusionists, caused Vṛndā to see a dream, while he himself, in a wondrous form, stayed in the garden of her city. ॥3॥
2.5.23.4: Then, at night, the goddess Vṛndā, his wife of good vows, through the power of Hari's māyā, saw a bad dream. ॥4॥
2.5.23.5: Within the dream, through Viṣṇu's māyā, she saw her husband mounted on a buffalo, smeared with oil, naked, ॥5॥
2.5.23.6: adorned with ornaments of black flowers, attended by hosts of flesh-eaters, gone to the southern direction, shaven-headed, and enveloped in darkness then; ॥6॥
2.5.23.7: and her own city suddenly sunk in the ocean together with herself — such and many other bad dreams she saw at the end of the night. ॥7॥
2.5.23.8: Then, waking up, the young woman, pondering that dream of hers, saw the risen sun again and again as full of holes and lustreless. ॥8॥
2.5.23.9: Knowing this to be an ill omen, weeping and overwhelmed with fear, she found no comfort anywhere — on the gate-towers, the turrets, or the grounds. ॥9॥
2.5.23.10: Then, accompanied by two friends, she went to the city garden; though she went there too, the young woman found happiness nowhere. ॥10॥
2.5.23.11: Then that wife of Jalandhara, her mind dejected and agitated, went from forest to forest, not then knowing even herself. ॥11॥
2.5.23.12: Wandering, the young woman then saw two extremely terrifying rākṣasas with lion faces, gleaming with teeth. ॥12॥
2.5.23.13: Seeing those two, extremely distraught and intent on fleeing, she then saw a calm ascetic with his disciple, observing silence. ॥13॥
2.5.23.14: Then, out of fear, placing her creeper-like arms around his neck, she said: O sage, protect me; I have come for refuge. ॥14॥
2.5.23.15: The sage, seeing her distraught and pursued by the rākṣasas, quickly turned those two dreadful ones away with a mere huṃ sound. ॥15॥
2.5.23.16: Seeing those two, terrified by fear of that huṃ, turn and go away, the wife of the demon-lord became greatly amazed in her heart, O sage. ॥16॥
2.5.23.17: Then Vṛndā, freed from fear, with joined palms, prostrating like a staff on the ground before that lord of sages, spoke these words. ॥17॥
2.5.23.18: Vṛndā said: O lord of sages, ocean of compassion, remover of others' suffering, I have been protected by you from this dreadful danger arising from the wicked ones. ॥18॥
2.5.23.19: You are capable in every way and all-knowing too, O treasury of compassion. I wish to submit something; kindly listen to it. ॥19॥
2.5.23.20: Jalandhara, my husband, has gone to fight Rudra, O lord. How is he faring there in battle? Tell me that, O you of good vows. ॥20॥
2.5.23.21: Sanatkumāra said: The sage, hearing her words, maintaining a deceitful silence, skilled in contrivance, to accomplish his own purpose, looked upward as if in compassion. ॥21॥
2.5.23.22: Meanwhile two monkey-chiefs arrived, bowed to him and stood before him; then, directed by a sign of his creeper-like eyebrow, they went into the sky. ॥22॥
2.5.23.23: Having taken half a moment, they came back and again stood before him; with them were his Jalandhara's head, trunk and two hands, O lord of sages. ॥23॥
2.5.23.24: Seeing the head, trunk and two hands of the Ocean's son, she fell unconscious to the ground, grieved by her husband's calamity. ॥24॥
2.5.23.25: Vṛndā said: O lord, you who formerly delighted me with pleasant conversations — how is it that you do not speak today to me, your beloved, who am blameless? ॥25॥
2.5.23.26: He by whom the gods along with the Gandharvas, together with Viṣṇu, were conquered — how has that conqueror of the three worlds been slain today by an ascetic? ॥26॥
2.5.23.27: You, not knowing the true nature of Rudra, did not accept my word, O best of demons, when I said that Śiva is the supreme Brahman. ॥27॥
2.5.23.28: Hence you were truly understood by me through the power of my service to you; but you, proud and under the sway of bad company, did not understand at all. ॥28॥
2.5.23.29: Having spoken thus in many ways, his beloved, firm in her own dharma, lamented in diverse ways with a burning heart. ॥29॥
2.5.23.30: Then, taking courage and heaving sighs of grief, she bowed deeply with joined palms and spoke to that best of sages. ॥30॥
2.5.23.31: O treasury of compassion, best of sages, devoted to helping others, O good one, showing compassion to me, revive this lord of mine. ॥31॥
2.5.23.32: Since you are, in my view, able to bring him back to life, therefore revive this lord of my life, O lord of sages. ॥32॥
2.5.23.33: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this, the demon's wife, devoted to wifely fidelity, fell at his feet, heaving sighs of grief. ॥33॥
2.5.23.34: The sage said: This one, slain by Rudra in battle, cannot be revived; those slain by Rudra in battle never live again. ॥34॥
2.5.23.35: Nevertheless, filled with compassion, I shall revive him, knowing the eternal dharma that those who come for refuge must be protected. ॥35॥
2.5.23.36: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this and revived her husband, O sage, that sage — Viṣṇu, the best of all illusionists — then vanished. ॥36॥
2.5.23.37: Quickly revived by him, the son of the Ocean rose up and, embracing Vṛndā, kissed her face with a delighted mind. ॥37॥
2.5.23.38: Then Vṛndā too, seeing her husband, delighted in mind, cast off all her grief and considered it all in her heart as a dream. ॥38॥
2.5.23.39: Then, with a joyful heart and with desire arisen in her, she sported with him for many days, staying in the middle of that forest. ॥39॥
2.5.23.40: Once, at the end of their lovemaking, having seen that it was indeed Viṣṇu himself, Vṛndā, filled with anger, rebuked him and spoke these words. ॥40॥
2.5.23.41: Vṛndā said: Fie on such conduct, O Hari, of one who goes to the wives of others! I have come to know you fully: you are the deceiver who appeared before my eyes as an ascetic. ॥41॥
2.5.23.42: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this, she, devoted to wifely fidelity, fell into a rage and, displaying her own power, cursed Keśava, O Vyāsa. ॥42॥
2.5.23.43: O you vilest of the vile, enemy of the Daityas, corrupter of another's dharma, take, O rogue, this curse given by me, fiercer than every poison. ॥43॥
2.5.23.44: Those two whom you, by your illusion, presented to me as your own attendants, those very two, becoming Rākṣasas, will carry off your wife. ॥44॥
2.5.23.45: And you too, tormented by grief for your wife, shall wander in the forest with monkeys as your helpers, together with this lord of serpents who has become your disciple. ॥45॥
2.5.23.46: Having said this, Vṛndā then entered the fire, even though she was being held back by Viṣṇu, whose mind was attached to her. ॥46॥
2.5.23.47: At that moment, O sage, all the gods headed by Brahmā arrived in the sky together with their wives, eager to witness her blessed destiny. ॥47॥
2.5.23.48: Then that supreme, great radiance of the wife of the Daitya lord swiftly went to the realm beyond the worlds, while all the gods looked on. ॥48॥
2.5.23.49: That radiance of Vṛndā became merged in the body of Śivā; and cries of victory, victory arose among the ranks of immortals stationed in the sky. ॥49॥
2.5.23.50: Thus Vṛndā, the great queen, the excellent daughter of Kālanemi, attained supreme liberation, O sage, through the power of her wifely fidelity. ॥50॥
2.5.23.51: Then Hari, remembering her again and again, smeared with the dust of the ashes of Vṛndā's pyre, remained right there; though consoled by the hosts of gods and Siddhas, he found no peace. ॥51॥
2.5.23.iti: Thus ends the twenty-third adhyāya, named The description of the breaking of Vṛndā's wifely chastity and her giving up of her body, in the account of the slaying of Jalandhara, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥23॥
2.5.24.1: Vyāsa said: O best son of Vidhi (Brahmā), O wise one, you have narrated this wondrous story. And then what happened in the battle? How was the demon slain? Tell me. ॥1॥
2.5.24.2: Sanatkumāra said: When the lord of demons had come back to the battle and the Gandharva illusion had vanished, Vṛṣadhvaja (Śiva), not seeing Girijā there, regained his awareness. ॥2॥
2.5.24.3: Seeing that the illusion had disappeared, Śaṅkara, the Destroyer, understood; and adopting worldly behaviour, he became exceedingly angry. ॥3॥
2.5.24.4: Then Śiva, astonished in mind, went again in wrath to fight Jalandhara. And that demon too, seeing Śiva come back, covered him in the battle with floods of arrows. ॥4॥
2.5.24.5: The Lord Hara swiftly cut down with his own excellent arrows that fierce net of arrows hurled by the exceedingly mighty Jalandhara; there is nothing wonderful in this for the destroyer of the three worlds. ॥5॥
2.5.24.6: Then Jalandhara, seeing Rudra of wondrous valour, created Gaurī by illusion, as if to delude the Three-eyed One. ॥6॥
2.5.24.7: Śiva saw Pārvatī placed upon a chariot, bound and weeping, being beaten by the demons Niśumbha and Śumbha. ॥7॥
2.5.24.8: Seeing Gaurī in such a state, Śiva too, displaying worldly behaviour, became distressed in mind like an ordinary person. ॥8॥
2.5.24.9: He, skilled in manifold sports, stood silent with face downcast, limbs slack, dejected in spirit, forgetting his own prowess. ॥9॥
2.5.24.10: Then Jalandhara swiftly pierced that Rudra with three arrows, sunk in up to the feathers, in the head, the chest and the belly. ॥10॥
2.5.24.11: Then the Lord Rudra, of great sport, grasping the truth in an instant, assumed a terrible form, exceedingly fearsome with garlands of flames. ॥11॥
2.5.24.12: Seeing his exceedingly terrible form, the great asuras could not stand before him; they fled to the ten directions. ॥12॥
2.5.24.13: Even Niśumbha and Śumbha, who were famed as the best of heroes, were not at all able to stand in the battle, O lord of sages. ॥13॥
2.5.24.14: And the illusion created by Jalandhara vanished that very moment; a great cry of dismay arose on every side of the battlefield. ॥14॥
2.5.24.15: Then Rudra, filled with anger, seeing those two, Śumbha and Niśumbha, fleeing, reproached them and pronounced a curse upon them. ॥15॥
2.5.24.16: Rudra said: You two are wicked, utterly vile, offenders against me, inflicters of punishment on Pārvatī, and have turned your backs on this battle. ॥16॥
2.5.24.17: One who has turned his back is not to be slain—hence you two are not to be slain by me. Having escaped from my battle, you shall be slain by Gaurī. ॥17॥
2.5.24.18: As the Lord of Gaurī spoke thus, Jalandhara, son of the Ocean, resembling a blazing fire, became exceedingly enraged at Rudra. ॥18॥
2.5.24.19: In the battle he rained sharp arrows on Rudra with great force, and the surface of the earth became covered in a darkness of arrows. ॥19॥
2.5.24.20: While Rudra swiftly cut down his volleys of arrows, the mighty demon quickly struck the bull with an iron club. ॥20॥
2.5.24.21: By that blow the bull turned back from the battlefield; though pulled by Rudra, it would not stay on the field of battle. ॥21॥
2.5.24.22: Then the great Rudra displayed to everyone in the world his own utterly unbearable splendour—this is true, O lord of sages. ॥22॥
2.5.24.23: Then the Lord Rudra, supremely enraged, bearing a terrible body, suddenly became dreadful like the fire of dissolution. ॥23॥
2.5.24.24: Seeing the demon standing before him like a peak of Meru, and though he had heard of the demon's invulnerability to others, he became ready to slay him. ॥24॥
2.5.24.25: Upholding Brahmā's word, the Lord, protector of the worlds, extending grace in his heart, set his mind on slaying him. ॥25॥
2.5.24.26: Becoming supremely angry, the Trident-bearer playfully, with his big toe, quickly made in the great waters a terrible and wondrous discus. ॥26॥
2.5.24.27: Having made the sharp discus in the waters of the ocean, the blessed Lord, enemy of the cities—slayer of Dakṣa's sacrifice, of Andhaka, of Antaka and of the three cities, bringer of the end of the three worlds—remembering that the three worlds had been afflicted by this demon, spoke, laughing. ॥27॥
2.5.24.28: Mahārudra said: O Jalandhara, a discus has been fashioned with my foot in the great waters. If you are strong enough to lift it out, stay and fight—otherwise not. ॥28॥
2.5.24.29: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing those words of his, he, his eyes blazing with anger, looking at Śaṅkara as if to burn him with his eyes, spoke. ॥29॥
2.5.24.30: Jalandhara said: Having lifted up the line you drew, and having slain you together with your Gaṇas, O Śaṅkara, and having slain the worlds along with the gods, I shall take my own share, as Garuḍa took his. ॥30॥
2.5.24.31: I am able to slay all that moves and does not move, along with Vāsava (Indra). O Maheśvara, who in the three worlds is not pierceable by my arrows? ॥31॥
2.5.24.32: Even in my childhood the blessed Brahmā, the mightiest, together with the sages and the foremost gods, was overcome by me in my place through austerity alone. ॥32॥
2.5.24.33: By me the whole triple world with its moving and unmoving beings was burned in a moment by austerity. What, O Rudra—has even the Lord Brahmā been conquered by you? ॥33॥
2.5.24.34: Indra, Agni, Yama, the Lord of Wealth (Kubera), Vāyu, the Lord of Waters (Varuṇa) and others could not withstand me, just as serpents cannot bear the scent of the lord of birds. ॥34॥
2.5.24.35: O Śaṅkara, no vehicle worthy of me was found in heaven or on earth; reaching all the mountains, I assailed the lords of the Gaṇas. ॥35॥
2.5.24.36: The glorious Mandara, king of mountains, Nīla, and the most beautiful Meru were crushed by my staff-like arm to rid me of an itch. ॥36॥
2.5.24.37: The Gaṅgā was held back by my two arms on the Himālaya mountain for sport; and by my servants victory was won over my enemies, the heaven-dwellers. ॥37॥
2.5.24.38: Seizing the mare (Vaḍavā) with my hand, I bound her mouth; at that very instant everything then became a single ocean. ॥38॥
2.5.24.39: Airāvata and the other elephants were flung onto the waters of the ocean, and the blessed Indra with his chariot was flung a hundred yojanas. ॥39॥
2.5.24.40: Even Garuḍa, together with Viṣṇu, was bound by me with a serpent-noose; Urvaśī and the other women were brought by me into prison. ॥40॥
2.5.24.41: O Rudra, you do not know me, the conqueror of the three worlds, Jalandhara, the great demon, the son of the Ocean, of great strength. ॥41॥
2.5.24.42: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this to Mahādeva, the son of the Ocean then neither wavered nor remembered the Dānavas slain in battle. ॥42॥
2.5.24.43: By that arrogant, ill-mannered one, slapping his two arms in the pride of his arm-strength, Mahādeva was insulted with words of harsh syllables. ॥43॥
2.5.24.44: Hearing those inauspicious words uttered by the demon, Mahādeva laughed and took on supreme anger. ॥44॥
2.5.24.45: Rudra took in his hand the discus called Sudarśana, which had been fashioned by the drawing of his big toe, and with it he made ready to kill Jalandhara. ॥45॥
2.5.24.46: Lord Hara hurled that discus called Sudarśana, which shone like ten million suns and resembled the fire of the cosmic dissolution. ॥46॥
2.5.24.47: Burning heaven and earth with its speed, it reached Jalandhara and swiftly cut off his head with its large, wide eyes. ॥47॥
2.5.24.48: The body fell from the chariot to the ground, making the surface of the earth resound, and so did the head of the Ocean's son; a great cry of lament arose. ॥48॥
2.5.24.49: His body fell in two, like the immovable Añjana mountain, just as a great mountain split in two by the thunderbolt falls into the ocean. ॥49॥
2.5.24.50: With his terrible blood the world became filled; then the whole earth became disfigured, O lord of sages. ॥50॥
2.5.24.51: By Rudra's command all that blood, and the flesh too, reached Mahāraurava and became the pool of blood (Raktakuṇḍa) there. ॥51॥
2.5.24.52: His radiance, issuing from the body, merged into Rudra, just as that which arose from Vṛndā's body had dissolved into Gaurī. ॥52॥
2.5.24.53: Seeing Jalandhara slain, the gods, Gandharvas and serpents became greatly delighted and said, well done, O God! ॥53॥
2.5.24.54: All the gods, Siddhas and great sages became joyful; showering flowers, they loudly sang his glory. ॥54॥
2.5.24.55: The celestial women, overcome with love, danced in great delight; sweet-voiced, they sang melodious songs together with the Kinnaras. ॥55॥
2.5.24.56: When Vṛndā's husband was slain, O sage, all the quarters became clear, and the winds of all three kinds blew pure and pleasant to the touch. ॥56॥
2.5.24.57: The moon became cool, the sun shone with fine brilliance, the fires blazed calmly, and the sky became undisturbed. ॥57॥
2.5.24.58: Thus, O sage, the entire three worlds attained greater well-being when that son of the Ocean was slain by Hara of infinite forms. ॥58॥
2.5.24.iti: Thus ends the twenty-fourth adhyāya, named The description of Jalandhara, in the account of the slaying of Jalandhara, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥24॥
2.5.25.1: Sanatkumāra said: Then the gods headed by Brahmā, and likewise all the sages, bowing low, praised the Lord of the god of gods with pleasing words. ॥1॥
2.5.25.2: The gods said: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, loving to those who seek refuge, you indeed always grant happiness to the good and destroy the sorrow of your devotees. ॥2॥
2.5.25.3: You perform great and wondrous noble sports; you are reached through devotion, hard to approach, and hard for the wicked to propitiate. O Lord, be ever gracious. ॥3॥
2.5.25.4: Even the Veda does not truly know your greatness; all great souls sing your true glory according to their understanding. ॥4॥
2.5.25.5: Sahasravadana (the thousand-mouthed Śeṣa) and others always sing with great love your deeply hidden majesty; thereby they purify their own speech. ॥5॥
2.5.25.6: By your grace, O Lord of gods, even a dull person can become a knower of Brahman. You are always reached through devotion — so indeed the Vedas declare. ॥6॥
2.5.25.7: You are indeed compassionate to the afflicted and ever all-pervading. Changeless, the refuge of the good, you manifest yourself through true devotion. ॥7॥
2.5.25.8: Through devotion to you alone, O Maheśāna, many who were afflicted, having enjoyed every happiness here, attained perfection through steadfastness. ॥8॥
2.5.25.9: Formerly the devotee Dāśārha, lord of the Yadus, attained perfection, and so did his wife Kalāvatī, attaining the supreme state through devotion alone, O Lord. ॥9॥
2.5.25.10: Likewise King Mitrasaha and his beloved Madayantī attained supreme liberation (kaivalya) through devotion to you alone, O Lord of gods. ॥10॥
2.5.25.11: So too the daughter named Saumini of the foremost Kaikeya king, through devotion to you, attained supreme happiness, hard to gain even for true yogins. ॥11॥
2.5.25.12: King Vimarṣaṇa, best of kings, having enjoyed various pleasures over seven births, O Lord, attained the good state through devotion to you. ॥12॥
2.5.25.13: Candrasena, best of kings, enjoying all pleasures through devotion to you, freed from sorrow, attained supreme happiness here and hereafter. ॥13॥
2.5.25.14: Śrīkara, the son of a cowherdess and disciple of the great hero, through devotion to you, having enjoyed life here, attained the good state and supreme happiness in the hereafter. ॥14॥
2.5.25.15: You removed the sorrow of King Satyaratha and granted him the good goal; and you rescued Prince Dharmagupta and made him happy here. ॥15॥
2.5.25.16: Likewise, O great Lord, out of compassion you made the brahmin Śucivrata, who followed devotion to you along with his mother, free from poverty and endowed with wisdom. ॥16॥
2.5.25.17: Citravarmā, best of kings, having constantly enjoyed in this world pleasures hard even for the immortals to obtain, attained the good state through devotion to you. ॥17॥
2.5.25.18: Prince Candrāṅgada, together with his wife Sīmantinī, casting off all sorrow, became happy and attained the great state. ॥18॥
2.5.25.19: Even the brahmin named Mandara, a wicked and vile frequenter of prostitutes, becoming your devotee and worshipping you, O Śiva, attained the good state together with her. ॥19॥
2.5.25.20: Bhadrāyu, the prince, your devotee, freed from distress, gained happiness, and through the grace of devotion to you, together with his mother, the supreme state, O Lord. ॥20॥
2.5.25.21: A wicked man addicted to enjoying all women, who constantly ate forbidden food, also became liberated through service to you, O Maheśvara. ॥21॥
2.5.25.22: Śambara, devoted to Śaṅkara and always wearing ashes from the funeral pyre, went to your city with his wife, O Śambhu, through the observance of wearing ash. ॥22॥
2.5.25.23: Likewise, O Lord, the son of Bhadrasena and the minister's son, Sudharma and Śubhakarma, always wore rudrākṣa beads. ॥23॥
2.5.25.24: By your grace those two, who in a former birth were a monkey and a cock adorned with Rudra's ornament rudrākṣa, having enjoyed true happiness here, became liberated. ॥24॥
2.5.25.25: Piṅgalā and Mahānandā, the two courtesans, attained the good state through devotion to you, O Lord intent on uplifting devotees. ॥25॥
2.5.25.26: Śāradā, a brahmin's daughter widowed in childhood, by the power of devotion to you became blessed with sons and marital good fortune. ॥26॥
2.5.25.27: Binduga, a brahmin in name only and a consorter with prostitutes, and his beloved Vañcukā, having heard your glory, attained the supreme state. ॥27॥
2.5.25.28: Thus and in other ways, many beings have attained perfection through the feeling of devotion to you, O Lord, O Maheśāna, friend of the afflicted, abode of compassion. ॥28॥
2.5.25.29: You are Brahman, beyond Prakṛti and beyond Puruṣa, O Supreme Lord; attributeless, the support of the three guṇas, having the nature of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Hara. ॥29॥
2.5.25.30: You ever perform manifold works, yet are changeless, the Lord of all. We all, Brahmā and the rest, are your servants, O Maheśvara. ॥30॥
2.5.25.31: Be gracious, O Lord of gods; protect us always, O Śiva. We are your subjects, O Lord, and have ever taken refuge in you. ॥31॥
2.5.25.32: Sanatkumāra said: Having thus praised him, those gods headed by Brahmā, together with the chief sages, then fell silent, their minds fixed on Śiva's two feet. ॥32॥
2.5.25.33: Then Śambhu, the great Lord, having heard the auspicious hymn of the gods and granted excellent boons at once, vanished right there. ॥33॥
2.5.25.34: All the gods, headed by Brahmā, their enemy slain, joyful and pleased, went each to his own abode, singing Śiva's true glory. ॥34॥
2.5.25.35: This supreme narrative of the crushing of Jalandhara is a holy account of Maheśa's deeds, destroying great floods of sin. ॥35॥
2.5.25.36: This holy hymn of the gods destroys all sins, always grants every happiness, and gives delight to Maheśa. ॥36॥
2.5.25.37: Whoever reads or causes to be read this twofold narrative, having enjoyed supreme happiness here, will attain the status of a leader of Śiva's gaṇas. ॥37॥
2.5.25.iti: Thus ends the twenty-fifth adhyāya, named The description of the gods' hymn of praise, in the account of the slaying of Jalandhara, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥25॥
2.5.26.1: Vyāsa said: O son of Brahmā, salutations to you. You are blessed, O best of Śaiva devotees, for you have made me hear this most divine and auspicious story of Śaṅkara. ॥1॥
2.5.26.2: Now, O sage, kindly tell me the story of Viṣṇu: having deluded Vṛndā, what did he do, and where did he go? ॥2॥
2.5.26.3: Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O Vyāsa of great wisdom, foremost among Śaivas, most excellent one, to the very pure story of Viṣṇu, rich with the deeds of Śambhu. ॥3॥
2.5.26.4: When the gods headed by Brahmā had fallen silent, Maheśvara Śambhu, very pleased and loving towards those who seek refuge, spoke. ॥4॥
2.5.26.5: Śambhu said: O Brahmā and all you best of gods, for your sake I have slain Jalandhara, though he was a portion of myself — I speak the truth, the truth. ॥5॥
2.5.26.6: Dear ones, have you attained happiness or not? Tell me truly, O immortals. For it is for your sake that I, ever free from change, perform my sport. ॥6॥
2.5.26.7: Sanatkumāra said: Then the gods headed by Brahmā, their eyes wide with joy, bowed their heads to Rudra and reported what Viṣṇu had done. ॥7॥
2.5.26.8: The gods said: O Mahādeva, O god, you have protected us from the fear arising from the enemy. But something else has come up; what shall we do about it? ॥8॥
2.5.26.9: O Lord, Vṛndā was deliberately deluded by Viṣṇu; she quickly turned to ashes in the fire and attained the supreme state. ॥9॥
2.5.26.10: Infatuated by Vṛndā's beauty, Viṣṇu remains deluded, bearing the ashes of her pyre, bewildered by your māyā. ॥10॥
2.5.26.11: Though we, along with the hosts of Siddhas and sages, have earnestly tried to awaken him, Hari does not come to his senses, deluded as he is by your māyā. ॥11॥
2.5.26.12: Show compassion, O Maheśāna; awaken Viṣṇu, awaken him. All this material world, with its moving and unmoving beings, is subject to you. ॥12॥
2.5.26.13: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words of the heaven-dwellers, Maheśa, whose sport is great and who acts at his own will, replied to them as they stood with joined palms. ॥13॥
2.5.26.14: Maheśa said: O Brahmā, O all you gods, listen attentively to my words: my māyā, which deludes all the worlds, is hard to overcome. ॥14॥
2.5.26.15: The whole world — gods, demons and humans — is under her control. By her alone was Viṣṇu deluded; Hari became a slave to desire. ॥15॥
2.5.26.16: She is the great goddess called Umā, the supreme mother of the three gods, renowned as Primordial Nature (mūlaprakṛti), most lovely, embodied as Girijā. ॥16॥
2.5.26.17: Go, O gods, for the removal of Viṣṇu's delusion, and take refuge with the māyā called Śivā, the refuge-giving enchantress who grants all desires. ॥17॥
2.5.26.18: Offer to her, my Śakti, a hymn that will please her. If she is well pleased, she will accomplish the whole task. ॥18॥
2.5.26.19: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this to the gods, the five-faced lord Śambhu, Hara, quickly vanished, O Vyāsa, together with all his attendants. ॥19॥
2.5.26.20: And by Śambhu's command the gods headed by Brahmā, along with Indra, praised in their minds Primordial Nature, who is loving to her devotees. ॥20॥
2.5.26.21: The gods said: We bow to that Primordial Nature from whom arise the guṇas sattva, rajas and tamas, which bring about creation, preservation and destruction, and by whose will this universe unfolds its existence and dissolution. ॥21॥
2.5.26.22: Protect the twenty-three well-named principles, O Supreme one who presides over the entire world. We bow to that Primordial Nature whose forms and deeds even the three worlds do not know. ॥22॥
2.5.26.23: We bow ever to that Primordial Nature, loving to her devotees, through devotion to whom people never meet poverty, delusion, death, birth and the like. ॥23॥
2.5.26.24: Accomplish the task of us gods, O Mahādevī, O supreme Mistress. Remove Viṣṇu's delusion, O Śivā, O Durgā; O Devī, salutations to you. ॥24॥
2.5.26.25: O Śivā, when the battle had begun between Jalandhara and Śambhu, the dweller of Kailāsa, for the purpose of killing him, by Gaurī's command… ॥25॥
2.5.26.26: …Vṛndā was deliberately deluded by Viṣṇu, O Devī, and made to abandon her own virtue; she turned to ashes in the fire and attained her goal. ॥26॥
2.5.26.27: Jalandhara was slain in battle, and we were freed from fear of him by Giriśa, who showed compassion and bestows grace on his devotees. ॥27॥
2.5.26.28: By his command we have all come to you for refuge. For you and Śambhu — you two, O Devī, are devoted to uplifting your devotees. ॥28॥
2.5.26.29: Infatuated by Vṛndā's beauty, Viṣṇu remains there, bearing the ashes of her pyre, bereft of wisdom and deluded. ॥29॥
2.5.26.30: Though admonished by the hosts of perfected beings and gods, O Maheśvarī, Hari does not come to his senses, deluded by your māyā. ॥30॥
2.5.26.31: Show compassion, O Mahādevī; awaken Hari, awaken him, so that, his mind restored, he may protect his own world and accomplish the gods' work. ॥31॥
2.5.26.32: As the gods were praising thus, they saw there in the sky a sphere of light whose flames pervaded the space of the quarters. ॥32॥
2.5.26.33: From its midst, O Vyāsa, all the immortals headed by Brahmā, along with Indra, heard a wish-granting voice moving in the sky. ॥33॥
2.5.26.34: The heavenly voice said: It is I alone who, divided threefold by the three guṇas — rajas, sattva and tamas — abide as Gaurī, Lakṣmī and Surā, the Radiance. ॥34॥
2.5.26.35: Go there, all of you, respectfully into their presence. By my command, they, being pleased, will accomplish what you desire. ॥35॥
2.5.26.36: Sanatkumāra said: While the gods, their eyes wide with wonder, were hearing this speech, that radiance then vanished, O sage. ॥36॥
2.5.26.37: Then all those gods, having respectfully heard that utterance and urged on by it, bowed to Gaurī, Lakṣmī and Surā. ॥37॥
2.5.26.38: And all the gods headed by Brahmā, with heads bowed, praised those goddesses with great devotion in words of many kinds. ॥38॥
2.5.26.39: Then at once, O Vyāsa, those goddesses appeared before them, illuminating the expanse of the quarters with their own most wondrous radiance. ॥39॥
2.5.26.40: Then the immortals, seeing them, with hearts full of joy, bowed, praised them with devotion, and made known their own purpose. ॥40॥
2.5.26.41: Then these goddesses, affectionate to their devotees, seeing the gods bowed down, gave them seeds and spoke words to them respectfully. ॥41॥
2.5.26.42: The goddesses said: Sow these seeds there where Viṣṇu is staying; then your purpose will attain success. ॥42॥
2.5.26.43: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this, those goddesses then vanished, O sage — they were indeed the powers of Rudra, Viṣṇu and Brahmā, constituted of the three guṇas. ॥43॥
2.5.26.44: Then all the gods, Brahmā and the rest together with Indra, delighted, took those seeds and went to where Hari was staying. ॥44॥
2.5.26.45: Those gods scattered them on the ground of Vṛndā's funeral pyre, remembering those goddesses, portions of Śiva's śakti, who were present there, O sage. ॥45॥
2.5.26.46: From the seeds that were sown arose three plants: Dhātrī, Mālatī and Tulasī, O lord of sages. ॥46॥
2.5.26.47: Dhātrī is held to have arisen from Dhātrī Brahmā's śakti, Mālatī from Mā Lakṣmī, and Tulasī from Gaurī; they are the guṇas tamas, sattva and rajas. ॥47॥
2.5.26.48: Then, O sage, when Viṣṇu saw the plants in the form of women, an agitation of excessive passion for them arose in him. ॥48॥
2.5.26.49: Seeing them, he, out of delusion, with a mind attached to desire, solicited them; and Tulasī and Dhātrī too looked upon him with passion. ॥49॥
2.5.26.50: And the seed that had earlier been offered by Lakṣmī with mere illusion — the woman born from it became filled with jealousy toward him. ॥50॥
2.5.26.51: Hence she received the name Barbarī, which is greatly despised. Dhātrī and Tulasī, because of their love, are always pleasing to him. ॥51॥
2.5.26.52: Then that Viṣṇu, his grief forgotten, went together with the two of them to Vaikuṇṭha, pleased, saluted by all the gods. ॥52॥
2.5.26.53: In the month of Kārttika, O best of brahmins, Dhātrī and Tulasī should always be known as dear to all the gods, and especially to Viṣṇu. ॥53॥
2.5.26.54: Even among these, Tulasī is blessed and supremely excellent, O great sage; except for Gaṇeśa, she gives delight to all and grants all desires. ॥54॥
2.5.26.55: Seeing Hari established in Vaikuṇṭha, those immortals, Brahmā, Indra and the rest, bowed to and praised the great Viṣṇu and went each to his own abode. ॥55॥
2.5.26.56: Vaikuṇṭha Viṣṇu too, dwelling in his own world, his delusion gone and possessed of clear understanding, became happy, O best of sages, remembering Śiva as before. ॥56॥
2.5.26.57: Thus this narrative destroys masses of sin, grants all desires to men, removes all perturbations of desire, and increases all knowledge. ॥57॥
2.5.26.58: Whoever, devoted, recites this daily or has it recited, or hears it or causes it to be heard, attains the supreme state. ॥58॥
2.5.26.59: The wise hero who, having recited this most excellent narrative, enters battle will be victorious; there is no doubt. ॥59॥
2.5.26.60: This gives knowledge of Brahman to brahmins, victory to kṣatriyas, all wealth to vaiśyas, and happiness to śūdras. ॥60॥
2.5.26.61: O Vyāsa, it grants devotion to Śambhu, destroys the sins of all, and always bestows a good destiny in this world and the next. ॥61॥
2.5.26.iti: Thus ends the twenty-sixth adhyāya, named The description of the hymn to the Goddess after the slaying of Jalandhara and the dispelling of Viṣṇu's delusion, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥26॥
2.5.27.1: Sanatkumāra said: Now, O sage, listen with love to another account of Śambhu, by the mere hearing of which devotion to Śiva becomes firm. ॥1॥
2.5.27.2: It tells how the heroic Dānava named Śaṅkhacūḍa, a thorn to the gods, was slain by Śiva with the trident at the forefront of battle. ॥2॥
2.5.27.3: Listen, O Vyāsa, with great delight to that divine, purifying, sin-destroying account of Śambhu; I tell it to you out of deep affection. ॥3॥
2.5.27.4: The sage Kaśyapa, son of Marīci who was the son of the Creator, was most righteous, a maker of creation, instructed in sacred knowledge, a Prajāpati. ॥4॥
2.5.27.5: Dakṣa lovingly gave him thirteen of his own daughters. Their progeny, being very extensive, cannot be fully told. ॥5॥
2.5.27.6: From them the whole world, moving and unmoving, beginning with the gods, came into being. Who in the three worlds is able to relate that in detail? ॥6॥
2.5.27.7: Hear the account at hand, which is bound up with Śambhu's divine play; that alone I narrate today. Listen to it, for it increases devotion. ॥7॥
2.5.27.8: Among those wives of Kaśyapa, one was Danu, an excellent lady, extremely beautiful, virtuous, and blessed with her husband's favour. ॥8॥
2.5.27.9: That Danu had many exceedingly mighty sons; their names are not told, O sage, for fear of prolixity. ॥9॥
2.5.27.10: Among them was one, Vipracitti, of great strength and valour. His son was Dambha, righteous, a devotee of Viṣṇu, with senses subdued. ॥10॥
2.5.27.11: He had no heroic son, and so he became absorbed in anxiety. Making Śukrācārya his guru and obtaining the Kṛṣṇa mantra, ॥11॥
2.5.27.12: he performed supreme austerity at Puṣkara for a hundred thousand years; firmly fixing his posture, he repeated the Kṛṣṇa mantra for a long time. ॥12॥
2.5.27.13: As he performed austerity, a blazing radiance issued from his head and spread everywhere; that radiance was utterly unbearable. ॥13॥
2.5.27.14: Scorched by it, all the gods, the sages and likewise the Manus, placing Indra at their head, went to Brahmā for refuge. ॥14॥
2.5.27.15: Bowing to the Ordainer, giver of all riches, they praised him and, distressed, told him their situation in detail. ॥15॥
2.5.27.16: Hearing that, the Ordainer too went with them to Vaikuṇṭha to report it fully to Viṣṇu. ॥16॥
2.5.27.17: Having gone there, all of them, humbly, with joined palms, bowed to Viṣṇu, lord of the three worlds, the supreme protector, and praised him. ॥17॥
2.5.27.18: The gods said: O God of gods, we do not know what cause has arisen here. We have all become scorched; by whose radiance? Tell us that. ॥18॥
2.5.27.19: O friend of the afflicted, you are the protector of your dependents whose hearts are scorched. Protect, protect us, O Lord of Ramā; you are the refuge of those who seek shelter. ॥19॥
2.5.27.20: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of the heaven-dwellers led by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, loving to those who seek refuge, smiled and spoke affectionately. ॥20॥
2.5.27.21: Viṣṇu said: Be at ease and untroubled; do not be afraid, O immortals. No calamities will occur; it is not the time of dissolution. ॥21॥
2.5.27.22: A Dānava named Dambha, my devotee, is performing austerity, desiring a son. I shall pacify him by granting a boon. ॥22॥
2.5.27.23: Sanatkumāra said: Thus addressed, O sage, all the gods led by Brahmā took courage and, reassured, went each to his own abode. ॥23॥
2.5.27.24: Acyuta too went to Puṣkara to grant the boon, where that Dānava named Dambha was performing austerity. ॥24॥
2.5.27.25: Having gone there, Hari, consoling with kind and pleasant words his devotee who was repeating his mantra, said: Ask for a boon. ॥25॥
2.5.27.26: Hearing Viṣṇu's words and seeing him standing before him, Dambha bowed with great devotion and praised him again and again. ॥26॥
2.5.27.27: Dambha said: O God of gods, lotus-eyed one, salutation to you. O Lord of Ramā, Lord of the three worlds, show me your grace. ॥27॥
2.5.27.28: Grant me a son devoted to you, of great strength and valour, a hero who conquers the three worlds and is invincible to the gods. ॥28॥
2.5.27.29: Sanatkumāra said: Thus addressed by the lord of Dānavas, Hari granted him that boon and, having made him desist from his fierce austerity, then vanished, O sage. ॥29॥
2.5.27.30: When Hari had gone, the lord of Dānavas bowed toward that direction and, his austerity fulfilled and his desire accomplished, went to his own home. ॥30॥
2.5.27.31: In a short time his fortunate wife became pregnant. She shone exceedingly with radiance, illuminating the interior of the house. ॥31॥
2.5.27.32: The cowherd named Sudāmā, foremost of Kṛṣṇa's attendants, entered her womb, because, O sage, he had been cursed by Rādhā. ॥32॥
2.5.27.33: Then in due time the virtuous lady bore a radiant son. The father, summoning many sages, duly performed the birth rite. ॥33॥
2.5.27.34: When he was born, O best of the twice-born, there was a very great festival. On an auspicious day his father named him Śaṅkhacūḍa. ॥34॥
2.5.27.35: He grew up in his father's house like the moon in the bright fortnight. Having mastered learning in childhood, he became very brilliant. ॥35॥
2.5.27.36: With his childish play he constantly spread joy to his parents, and he became dear to all, especially to the members of his family. ॥36॥
2.5.27.iti: Thus ends the twenty-seventh adhyāya, named The description of the birth of Śaṅkhacūḍa, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥27॥
2.5.28.1: Sanatkumāra said: Then that Śaṅkhacūḍa, following the instruction of Jaigīṣavya, performed austerities with great delight for a long time at Brahmā's Puṣkara. ॥1॥
2.5.28.2: With senses controlled, he repeated the Brahma-knowledge given by his guru, becoming single-minded and restraining his faculties. ॥2॥
2.5.28.3: To that Dānava Śaṅkhacūḍa, practising austerity at Puṣkara, Brahmā, the all-pervading teacher of the worlds, quickly went to grant a boon. ॥3॥
2.5.28.4: Then the Creator said to the lord of Dānavas, ask for a boon. Seeing him, Śaṅkhacūḍa bowed very humbly and praised him with fine words. ॥4॥
2.5.28.5: He asked Brahmā for the boon of being unconquerable by the gods. The Creator, with a well-pleased mind, said to him, so be it. ॥5॥
2.5.28.6: He gave Śaṅkhacūḍa the divine armour of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the most auspicious of auspicious things for the world, which grants victory everywhere. ॥6॥
2.5.28.7: Go to Badarī; there marry Tulasī. She is performing austerities there out of desire for a husband. ॥7॥
2.5.28.8: She is the daughter of Dharmadhvaja, so the Creator instructed him; and at that very moment he quickly vanished as Śaṅkhacūḍa looked on. ॥8॥
2.5.28.9: Then Śaṅkhacūḍa, perfected by austerity in the excellent Puṣkara, tied around his neck the armour, most auspicious for the world. ॥9॥
2.5.28.10: At Brahmā's command he too, his wish fulfilled through austerity, came swiftly with a joyful face to the Badarikā hermitage. ॥10॥
2.5.28.11: The Dānava Śaṅkhacūḍa came, as if by chance, to the place where Tulasī, daughter of Dharmadhvaja, was performing austerities. ॥11॥
2.5.28.12: Beautiful, sweetly smiling, slender, adorned with fine ornaments, she looked with sidelong glances at that very excellent man. ॥12॥
2.5.28.13: Seeing her, graceful, charming, well-mannered, beautiful and chaste, he stayed near her and spoke to her sweetly. ॥13॥
2.5.28.14: Śaṅkhacūḍa said: Who are you? Whose daughter are you? What are you doing, staying here? Why are you silent? You should honour me, your servant, here with a reply. ॥14॥
2.5.28.15: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words, she spoke to him, who was full of desire. ॥15॥
2.5.28.16: Tulasī said: I am the daughter of Dharmadhvaja, an ascetic woman performing austerities, and I dwell in this penance-grove. Who are you? Go as you please. ॥16॥
2.5.28.17: Womankind is bewitching, like poison even to Brahmā and the others; blameworthy, a cause of faults, an illusion, and indeed a fetter for those attached to them. ॥17॥
2.5.28.18: Sanatkumāra said: Having spoken thus charmingly to him, Tulasī fell silent. Seeing her smiling, he too began to speak. ॥18॥
2.5.28.19: Śaṅkhacūḍa said: O goddess, what you have said is not all false; some is true and some false. Hear the rest from me. ॥19॥
2.5.28.20: Among women devoted to their husbands, you are the foremost. I am not a lustful man with sinful gaze, and neither are you sinful—such is my view. ॥20॥
2.5.28.21: I come to you now at Brahmā's command. O lovely one, I shall take you by the Gāndharva form of marriage. ॥21॥
2.5.28.22: I am Śaṅkhacūḍa himself, the one who puts the gods to flight. Do you not know me, good lady? Have you never heard of me? ॥22॥
2.5.28.23: I am a Dānava of Danu's lineage, specifically the son of Dambha. Formerly I was the cowherd named Sudāmā, an attendant of Hari. ॥23॥
2.5.28.24: Now, through Rādhikā's curse, I am the lord of the Dānavas. I remember my former birth and know everything by Kṛṣṇa's power. ॥24॥
2.5.28.25: Sanatkumāra said: Having spoken thus, Śaṅkhacūḍa fell silent before her. Addressed by the Dānava lord with these true words respectfully, Tulasī, pleased, began to speak with a smile. ॥25॥
2.5.28.26: Tulasī said: Now I have been defeated by you through your judgement of truth. Blessed in the world is the man who is not conquered by a woman. ॥26॥
2.5.28.27: The man who is conquered by a woman is ever impure, even if he performs good rites; the ancestors, the gods and all humans censure him. ॥27॥
2.5.28.28: A brāhmaṇa becomes pure in ten days after birth- or death-impurity, a kṣatriya in twelve days, a vaiśya in fifteen days. ॥28॥
2.5.28.29: A śūdra becomes pure in a month—such is the Vedic injunction. But a man conquered by a woman is never pure anywhere, except by burning on the funeral pyre. ॥29॥
2.5.28.30: Therefore the ancestors do not willingly accept his rice-ball offerings and libations, nor do the gods accept flowers, fruits and the like given by him. ॥30॥
2.5.28.31: What use to him are knowledge, good austerity, japa, fire-offerings and worship? What use are learning or charity to one whose mind has been stolen by women? ॥31॥
2.5.28.32: I tested you to know the power of your learning. A woman should choose her husband only after testing her beloved. ॥32॥
2.5.28.33: Sanatkumāra said: While Tulasī was speaking thus, at that moment Brahmā, the Creator, came there and then spoke these words. ॥33॥
2.5.28.34: Brahmā said: O Śaṅkhacūḍa, why are you conversing with her? Take her by the Gāndharva form of marriage. ॥34॥
2.5.28.35: You are a jewel among men, and this chaste lady is a jewel among women. The union of a clever woman with a clever man is surely virtuous. ॥35॥
2.5.28.36: O king, who would give up unobstructed happiness that is hard to obtain? He who renounces happiness free from conflict is a beast—no doubt about it. ॥36॥
2.5.28.37: O chaste one, why do you test such a virtuous beloved, the crusher of gods, asuras and Dānavas? ॥37॥
2.5.28.38: O beautiful one, sport with him for a very long time, always, in place after place as you wish, throughout all the worlds. ॥38॥
2.5.28.39: In the end he will again attain Śrī Kṛṣṇa in Goloka; and when he has died, you will attain the four-armed Viṣṇu in Vaikuṇṭha. ॥39॥
2.5.28.40: Sanatkumāra said: Having given this blessing, Brahmā went to his own abode, and the Dānava took her as wife by the Gāndharva form of marriage. ॥40॥
2.5.28.41: Having thus married Tulasī, he went to his father's place. He delighted there together with her, beautiful as Ramā, in a charming dwelling-house. ॥41॥
2.5.28.iti: Thus ends the twenty-eighth adhyāya, named The description of Śaṅkhacūḍa's austerities and marriage, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥28॥
2.5.29.1: Sanatkumāra said: When that Śaṅkhacūḍa, having performed penance and obtained a boon, had married and returned to his own home, the Dānavas and the others rejoiced. ॥1॥
2.5.29.2: Quickly setting out from their own world, accompanied by their preceptor, all the Asuras gathered together and came to his presence. ॥2॥
2.5.29.3: Having bowed to him humbly and praised him with manifold respect, they remained right there with great affection, regarding him as a radiant, mighty lord. ॥3॥
2.5.29.4: He too, the son of Dambha, seeing that family preceptor arrived, bowed to him with great devotion, prostrating with all eight limbs, with the highest reverence. ॥4॥
2.5.29.5: Then Śukra, the family preceptor, having looked upon him, bestowed an unsurpassed blessing and then narrated the history of the gods and the Dānavas. ॥5॥
2.5.29.6: He told of that natural enmity, the defeat of the Asuras, the victory of the gods, and the help given by Jīva (Bṛhaspati). ॥6॥
2.5.29.7: Then the preceptor, having obtained the consent of all the Asuras, with a grand festival made him the overlord of the Dānavas and other Asuras. ॥7॥
2.5.29.8: Then there was a great celebration among the joyful Asuras, and all of them gladly gave him presents. ॥8॥
2.5.29.9: Then the heroic and valourous Śaṅkhacūḍa, son of Dambha, having received the royal consecration, shone forth as king of the Asuras. ॥9॥
2.5.29.10: Leading a vast army of Daityas, Dānavas and Rākṣasas, he mounted his chariot and went swiftly to conquer Indra's city. ॥10॥
2.5.29.11: As he went, that lord of the Dānavas shone amid those attending on him like the moon among the stars, like the king of planets among the planets. ॥11॥
2.5.29.12: Hearing that Śaṅkhacūḍa was approaching, Ākhaṇḍala (Indra), king of heaven, along with all the immortals, made ready to fight him. ॥12॥
2.5.29.13: Then a tumultuous battle took place between the Asuras and the gods, delighting the heroes, frightening the cowards, making the hair stand on end. ॥13॥
2.5.29.14: A great uproar arose from the heroes roaring in battle, and there was also the sound of musical instruments, increasing heroism. ॥14॥
2.5.29.15: The gods, enraged and being the stronger, fought with the Asuras; the Asuras suffered defeat and fled in fear. ॥15॥
2.5.29.16: Seeing them fleeing, lord Śaṅkhacūḍa himself fought with the gods, roaring a lion's roar. ॥16॥
2.5.29.17: Swiftly and suddenly he made a slaughter of the heaven-dwellers; all the gods fled, unable to bear his great splendour. ॥17॥
2.5.29.18: Wretched, they stayed here and there, even in mountain caves, subject to him and not independent, lustreless like stilled oceans. ॥18॥
2.5.29.19: That valiant, mighty son of Dambha, lord of the Dānavas, having conquered all the worlds, seized the offices of the gods. ॥19॥
2.5.29.20: He brought the three worlds under his control, and the sacrificial shares in their entirety; he himself even became Indra, and the whole world was ruled by him. ॥20॥
2.5.29.21: By his own power he exercised the offices of Kubera, the Moon, the Sun, Agni, Yama and Vāyu. ॥21॥
2.5.29.22: Of the gods, Asuras, Dānavas and Rākṣasas, of the Gandharvas, Nāgas, Kinnaras and the dwellers of Rasātala — ॥22॥
2.5.29.23: — of the three worlds and of all others, that great hero Śaṅkhacūḍa of immense strength became the supreme lord. ॥23॥
2.5.29.24: Thus the great Śaṅkhacūḍa, emperor over kings, enjoyed sovereignty over all the worlds for many years. ॥24॥
2.5.29.25: In his kingdom there was no famine, no plague, no inauspicious planets, no mental or bodily ailments at all, and the people were always happy. ॥25॥
2.5.29.26: The earth, yielding crops without tilling, gave grain in abundance; and the various herbs were always fruitful and full of sap. ॥26॥
2.5.29.27: The mines abounded in gems, the oceans were mines of jewels, the trees always bore flowers and fruits, and the rivers carried excellent water. ॥27॥
2.5.29.28: Except for the gods, all beings were happy and free from affliction; all others, people of the four varṇas and āśramas, abided in their respective dharma. ॥28॥
2.5.29.29: While he ruled the three worlds, no one was unhappy; only the immortals were distressed, owing to their fraternal enmity. ॥29॥
2.5.29.30: That mighty Śaṅkhacūḍa was the supreme friend of Kṛṣṇa, the dweller in Goloka — a virtuous one, ever devoted to Kṛṣṇa. ॥30॥
2.5.29.31: Through the force of a former curse he had taken birth in a Dānava womb; yet, O sage, even as a Dānava he did not have a Dānava's mind. ॥31॥
2.5.29.32: Then all the hosts of gods, defeated and robbed of their kingdom, having taken counsel together with the sages, went, dear one, to Brahmā's assembly. ॥32॥
2.5.29.33: There, seeing the Creator, they bowed and praised him especially, and in distress told Brahmā the whole account. ॥33॥
2.5.29.34: Then Brahmā, having consoled all the gods and the sages, went with them to the world of Vaikuṇṭha, which gives happiness to the good. ॥34॥
2.5.29.35: There Brahmā, with the hosts of gods, saw the Lord of Lakṣmī, wearing a crown and earrings, adorned with a garland of forest flowers, ॥35॥
2.5.29.36: the four-armed god holding conch, discus, mace and lotus, clad in yellow garments, attended by Sanandana and other Siddhas. ॥36॥
2.5.29.37: Seeing Viṣṇu, all the gods headed by Brahmā, together with the chief sages, bowed and, with joined palms, praised the Lord with devotion. ॥37॥
2.5.29.38: O God of gods, Lord of the universe, ruler of Vaikuṇṭha, O master, protect us who have come to you for refuge, O Śrī Hari, preceptor of the three worlds. ॥38॥
2.5.29.39: You alone are the protector of the worlds, O Lord of the three worlds, O Acyuta, O master; O abode of Lakṣmī, Govinda, life of your devotees — salutations to you. ॥39॥
2.5.29.40: Having praised thus, all the gods wept before Hari. Hearing that, Lord Viṣṇu said this to Brahmā. ॥40॥
2.5.29.41: Viṣṇu said: Why have you come to Vaikuṇṭha, which is hard even for yogins to reach? What trouble has arisen for you? Tell me that, here before me. ॥41॥
2.5.29.42: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of Hari, Brahmā bowed again and again, joined his palms together, and with his neck bent in humility, ॥42॥
2.5.29.43: he then narrated, before Viṣṇu the Supreme Self, the account of what Śaṅkhacūḍa had done, a full telling of the gods' distress. ॥43॥
2.5.29.44: Having heard his words, the Lord Hari, who knows the nature of all things in every respect, smiled and spoke that secret to Vidhi (Brahmā). ॥44॥
2.5.29.45: The Lord said: O lotus-born one, I know the whole story of Śaṅkhacūḍa, who formerly was a cowherd, my devotee, of great splendour. ॥45॥
2.5.29.46: Listen to that whole account, an ancient history. No doubt should be entertained: Śaṅkara will bring about well-being. ॥46॥
2.5.29.47: Above all is his Śivaloka, higher than the highest, where Śambhu shines, the Supreme Brahman, the Supreme Lord, ॥47॥
2.5.29.48: who is the presiding ruler of Prakṛti and of Puruṣa as well, bearer of the three powers; he is both without attributes and with attributes, the supreme light possessing form. ॥48॥
2.5.29.49: O Brahmā, from his body were born the three who bring about creation and the rest, endowed with the qualities sattva and the others, named Viṣṇu, Brahmā and Hara. ॥49॥
2.5.29.50: That very Supreme Self sports there together with Umā, free from Māyā, the creator of the eternal and the non-eternal. ॥50॥
2.5.29.51: Near it is Goloka, the cow-pen of Śaṅkara. By his will Kṛṣṇa, who is of my form, dwells there. ॥51॥
2.5.29.52: Commanded by him to protect his cows, he is ever happy; having obtained happiness from that, he too, skilled in pastimes, sports there. ॥52॥
2.5.29.53: His consort is renowned as Rādhā, mother of the world, the supreme embodiment of Prakṛti, the fifth form, delighting in pastimes. ॥53॥
2.5.29.54: Many cowherds and cowherdesses live there, born from their bodies, ever devoted to delightful pastimes, followers of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. ॥54॥
2.5.29.55: That very one cowherd, deluded now by this Māyā through Śambhu's play, has needlessly, because of a curse, obtained a demonic birth that brings him sorrow. ॥55॥
2.5.29.56: His death by Rudra's trident was ordained long ago by Kṛṣṇa. Then, abandoning his body, he will become an attendant of Śiva. ॥56॥
2.5.29.57: Knowing this, O lord of the gods, you should not be afraid. Go to Śaṅkara for refuge; he will at once bring about well-being. ॥57॥
2.5.29.58: I, you, and all the gods — let us remain here free from fear. ॥58॥
2.5.29.59: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this, Viṣṇu, together with Vidhi, went to Śivaloka, remembering in his mind Śambhu, the Lord of all, loving to his devotees. ॥59॥
2.5.29.iti: Thus ends the twenty-ninth adhyāya, named The description of Śaṅkhacūḍa's rule of the kingdom, followed by the description of the story of what happened in his previous birth, in the account of the slaying of Śaṅkhacūḍa, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥29॥
2.5.30.1: Sanatkumāra said: Then, O Vyāsa, Rameśvara (Viṣṇu), together with Vidhi (Brahmā), going at once to Śivaloka, which is supremely divine, needs no support and is not made of material elements, ॥1॥
2.5.30.2: Viṣṇu, full of joy and with a delighted face, went inside that world, which was set all around with many kinds of gems, glittering and intensely radiant. ॥2॥
2.5.30.3: Reaching the first gate, wondrous, attended by the gaṇas, adorned with supreme splendour, very lofty and exceedingly beautiful, ॥3॥
2.5.30.4: he saw the gatekeepers seated on jewelled thrones, resplendent in white garments and adorned with jewelled ornaments, ॥4॥
2.5.30.5: five-faced and three-eyed, with fair and handsome bodies, heroes bearing tridents and other weapons, shining with sacred ash and rudrākṣa beads. ॥5॥
2.5.30.6: Brahmā and Rameśa (Viṣṇu), humbly bowing to them, explained the matter, namely their purpose of seeing the Lord. ॥6॥
2.5.30.7: They gave him permission, and by their permission he entered the next gate, very delightful, wondrous and supremely radiant. ॥7॥
2.5.30.8: To that gatekeeper he reported the matter, with the aim of going into the Lord's presence; and permitted by him, he entered another gate. ॥8॥
2.5.30.9: Having thus passed through fifteen gates, the lotus-born (Brahmā) came to the great gate, and there he saw Nandin. ॥9॥
2.5.30.10: Having duly bowed to him and praised him, and being permitted, as before, by that Nandin, Viṣṇu slowly and joyfully went inside. ॥10॥
2.5.30.11: Going there, he saw the lofty assembly-hall of Śambhu, brilliantly radiant, surrounded by attendants with shining bodies and well adorned, ॥11॥
2.5.30.12: attendants having the very form of Maheśvara: ten-armed, of auspicious lustre, five-faced, three-eyed, blue-throated, greatly radiant, ॥12॥
2.5.30.13: adorned with ornaments of rudrākṣa set with fine gems and with sacred ash. The hall was shaped like the orb of the new moon, square and charming, ॥13॥
2.5.30.14: beautified with necklaces made of the finest gems and with choice diamonds, built of priceless jewels and adorned with lotus petals, ॥14॥
2.5.30.15: variegated with festoons of ruby lattices and many kinds of decorations, fashioned of the finest rubies, wondrous by Śaṅkara's will, ॥15॥
2.5.30.16: furnished with hundreds of steps made of Syamantaka gems, and with lovely sandal sprays tied with knots of golden thread, ॥16॥
2.5.30.17: encircled by pillars of sapphire, most charming, well arranged everywhere and perfumed by fragrant breezes, ॥17॥
2.5.30.18: a thousand yojanas in extent and filled with many servants. There Viṣṇu, lord of the gods, saw Śaṅkara together with Ambā, ॥18॥
2.5.30.19: dwelling in the centre like the moon surrounded by stars, seated on a wondrous throne made of priceless jewels, ॥19॥
2.5.30.20: wearing a crown and earrings, adorned with a jewelled garland, his whole body smeared with ash, holding a lotus for play, ॥20॥
2.5.30.21: watching with a smile and with delight the singing and dancing before him, ॥21॥
2.5.30.22: tranquil, of serene mind, the beloved of Umā, greatly exultant, chewing betel given by the Goddess, fragrantly perfumed, ॥22॥
2.5.30.23: served with supreme devotion by the gaṇas with white fly-whisks, and being praised by the Siddhas whose necks were bowed in devotion, ॥23॥
2.5.30.24: Śiva, beyond the guṇas, the supreme lord, father of the three gods, all-pervading, free of mental constructs, formless, yet taking form by his own will, ॥24॥
2.5.30.25: free of māyā, unborn, primordial, master of māyā, higher than the highest, beyond both Prakṛti and Puruṣa, ever his own lord. ॥25॥
2.5.30.26: Seeing him thus distinguished, most perfectly complete and impartial, Viṣṇu and Brahmā bowed with joined palms and praised him. ॥26॥
2.5.30.27: Viṣṇu and Brahmā said: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, O supreme Brahman, O lord of all, O you who are beyond the three guṇas, untroubled, father of the three gods, O Lord, ॥27॥
2.5.30.28: we have come to you for refuge. Protect us, O all-pervading one, who are distressed, tormented and afflicted by Śaṅkhacūḍa, yet have you as our protector, O supreme Lord. ॥28॥
2.5.30.29: This world that is presided over by you is known as Goloka. Its ruler, the mighty Kṛṣṇa here, is himself under your authority. ॥29॥
2.5.30.30: His foremost attendant Sudāmā, impelled by fate and cursed by Rādhā, then became the Dānava Śaṅkhacūḍa. ॥30॥
2.5.30.31: Driven out by him, O Śambhu, oppressed on all sides and stripped of their offices, the gods wander on the earth. ॥31॥
2.5.30.32: Without you he cannot be slain by any of the dwellers of heaven. Slay him, O Maheśāna, and bring happiness to the worlds. ॥32॥
2.5.30.33: You alone are without qualities, the truth, infinite, of infinite valour; you are also with qualities and the abode of all, beyond Prakṛti and Puruṣa. ॥33॥
2.5.30.34: Through rajas, at the time of creation, you are Brahmā the creator, O Lord; through sattva, in preservation, you are Viṣṇu, the protector of the three worlds; ॥34॥
2.5.30.35: through tamas, at dissolution, you are Rudra, the destroyer of the world; in the state beyond the three guṇas you are called Śiva, the Fourth, whose nature is light. ॥35॥
2.5.30.36: By your ordinance in Goloka you are the protector of the cows, and Kṛṣṇa, dwelling amid your cowsheds, plays day and night. ॥36॥
2.5.30.37: You are the cause of all, the master, the supreme lord of Vidhi (Brahmā) and Viṣṇu, changeless, the eternal witness, the supreme Self, the highest lord. ॥37॥
2.5.30.38: You are the helper of the wretched and the helpless, the protector of the afflicted, the friend of the distressed, lord of the three worlds, loving toward those who seek refuge. ॥38॥
2.5.30.39: Rescue us, O lord of Gaurī; be gracious, O supreme Lord. We depend on you, O Master; do as you wish. ॥39॥
2.5.30.40: Sanatkumāra said: O Vyāsa, having spoken thus, those two gods, Hari and Brahmā, then fell silent, having bowed to Śiva with joined palms, humble as they were. ॥40॥
2.5.30.iti: Thus ends the thirtieth adhyāya, named The hymn to the God of gods, in the slaying of Śaṅkhacūḍa, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥30॥
2.5.31.1: Sanatkumāra said: Then, having heard the words of the deeply distressed Hari and Brahmā, Śambhu, laughing, spoke in a voice as deep as the rumbling of clouds. ॥1॥
2.5.31.2: Śiva said: O Hari, dear child, O Brahmā, give up entirely the fear arising from Śaṅkhacūḍa. Good will come about, without doubt. ॥2॥
2.5.31.3: I know in truth the whole story of Śaṅkhacūḍa, who formerly was the cowherd Sudāman, a devotee of Kṛṣṇa, O lord. ॥3॥
2.5.31.4: By my command Hṛṣīkeśa, having assumed the form of Kṛṣṇa, dwelt in the cowshed in lovely Goloka, which is presided over by me. ॥4॥
2.5.31.5: Formerly, thinking of himself, I am independent, he fell into delusion; deluded, he performed many sports as if acting at his own will. ॥5॥
2.5.31.6: Seeing him thus, I deluded him intensely by my own māyā; withdrawing their good sense, I caused a curse to be pronounced, indeed. ॥6॥
2.5.31.7: Having thus performed my sport, I withdrew that māyā. Then they became endowed with knowledge, freed from delusion, of sound understanding. ॥7॥
2.5.31.8: They came near me, humbled, bowed to me, and, meek with joined palms, offered fine praise with devotion. ॥8॥
2.5.31.9: With minds agitated by shame they told the whole story; wretched, before me they spoke the words, protect, protect. ॥9॥
2.5.31.10: Then I, Bhava, being pleased, spoke these words to them: O Kṛṣṇa, give up fear, all of you, by my command. ॥10॥
2.5.31.11: I am ever your protector out of love; great good will be yours. All this has happened by my will, there is no doubt. ॥11॥
2.5.31.12: Go to your own abode together with Rādhā and the attendant. But this one will become a Dānava here in Bhārata, no doubt. ॥12॥
2.5.31.13: I shall surely bring about the release from the curse for you two in due time. Holding my words thus on his head, together with Rādhā, ॥13॥
2.5.31.14: the wise Śrī Kṛṣṇa rejoiced greatly and went to his own abode. The two remained there with fear, intent on worshipping me, ॥14॥
