2.5.31.15: considering everything as dependent on me and themselves as not independent. That Sudāman, through Rādhā's curse, became the lord of the Dānavas, ॥15॥
2.5.31.16: named Śaṅkhacūḍa, an enemy of the gods, though versed in dharma. That evil-minded one constantly oppresses the entire host of gods with great force. ॥16॥
2.5.31.17: Deluded by my māyā, he has very wicked ministers as his helpers. Therefore give up that fear quickly, since I am the chastiser. ॥17॥
2.5.31.18: Sanatkumāra said: While Śiva was thus telling the story before Hari and Brahmā, meanwhile another event took place; hear that, O sage. ॥18॥
2.5.31.19: At that very moment Kṛṣṇa came with Rādhā, his attendants and good cowherds, to propitiate the lord Śambhu. ॥19॥
2.5.31.20: Having bowed to the Lord with true devotion and having respectfully met Hari, and being welcomed with affection by Brahmā, he stood there at Śiva's command. ॥20॥
2.5.31.21: Then, bowing again to Śambhu with joined palms, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, freed from delusion and having understood Śiva's true nature, praised him. ॥21॥
2.5.31.22: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, Supreme Brahman, refuge of the good, forgive my offence; be gracious, O Supreme Lord. ॥22॥
2.5.31.23: From you, O Śarva, is everything, and everything is in you, O Maheśvara; you are everything, O lord of all; be gracious, O Supreme Lord. ॥23॥
2.5.31.24: You are manifestly the supreme light, all-pervading, eternal. With you as our master, O lord of Gaurī, all of us are protected. ॥24॥
2.5.31.25: Thinking myself above all, I sported and fell into delusion. I have reaped its fruit: I received a curse, together with my beloved. ॥25॥
2.5.31.26: My foremost attendant, the cowherd named Sudāman, has, through Rādhā's curse, O master, entered a Dānava birth. ॥26॥
2.5.31.27: Uplift us, O lord of Durgā; be gracious, O Supreme Lord. Bring about the release from the curse today; protect us who have come for refuge. ॥27॥
2.5.31.28: Having said this, Śrī Kṛṣṇa fell silent together with Rādhā. Then Śiva, kind to those who seek refuge, became pleased. ॥28॥
2.5.31.29: Śrī Śiva said: O Kṛṣṇa, lord of the gopīs, give up fear and be happy. All this, dear one, was done by me in order to show favour. ॥29॥
2.5.31.30: Good will come to you; go to your excellent abode. You should always remain attentive in your own office. ॥30॥
2.5.31.31: Sport as you wish, knowing me to be higher than the highest. Do your own work undisturbed, together with Rādhā and your attendants. ॥31॥
2.5.31.32: In the excellent Vārāha kalpa, he, together with young Rādhā, having undergone the effect of the curse, will return to his own abode. ॥32॥
2.5.31.33: Sudāman, your attendant, O Kṛṣṇa, dearest of the dear, having entered a Dānava birth, now torments the world. ॥33॥
2.5.31.34: Through the power of Rādhā's curse he is an enemy of the gods, a Dānava named Śaṅkhacūḍa, a strong partisan of the Daityas, hostile to the gods. ॥34॥
2.5.31.35: By him the gods, including Indra, have been driven out and constantly oppressed; stripped of their offices and miserable, they have all gone off in the ten directions. ॥35॥
2.5.31.36: For that very reason Brahmā and Acyuta have come here to me for refuge. I shall free them from their distress; there is no doubt about this. ॥36॥
2.5.31.37: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this to Kṛṣṇa, Śaṅkara again respectfully addressed Hari and Brahmā and spoke words that destroy distress. ॥37॥
2.5.31.38: Śiva said: O Hari, O Brahmā, listen with love to these words of mine. Go quickly, dear ones, without fear, for the joy of the gods, ॥38॥
2.5.31.39: to Rudra who dwells on Kailāsa, who is my own form, complete and supreme, manifested for the gods' purpose and bearing a separate shape. ॥39॥
2.5.31.40: For this very purpose the Lord, my own form, most perfect, abides on Mount Kailāsa, under the sway of his devotees, O Hari. ॥40॥
2.5.31.41: There is no difference between me and you; he alone is to be served by you both, and always by all moving and unmoving beings and by the gods and others. ॥41॥
2.5.31.42: Whoever makes a distinction between us two, that man goes to hell; even here he suffers hardship, deprived of sons and grandsons. ॥42॥
2.5.31.43: Having bowed again and again to the lord of Durgā who had spoken thus, Kṛṣṇa, together with Rādhā and with his attendants, went to his own abode. ॥43॥
2.5.31.44: O Vyāsa, Hari and Brahmā, both joyful and freed from fear, bowed again and again to the Lord and quickly went to Vaikuṇṭha. ॥44॥
2.5.31.45: Having arrived there and reported the whole event to the gods, those two, Brahmā and Viṣṇu, taking them along, went to Mount Kailāsa. ॥45॥
2.5.31.46: There, having seen Maheśāna, the Lord, beloved of Pārvatī, who had assumed a body to protect the distressed, endowed with attributes, the leader of the gods, ॥46॥
2.5.31.47: they all praised him as before with devotion, in a voice choked with emotion, with joined palms, bowed shoulders, and full of humility. ॥47॥
2.5.31.48: The gods said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, lord of Girijā, Śaṅkara, we have come to you for refuge; protect the gods who are distraught with fear. ॥48॥
2.5.31.49: Slay Śaṅkhacūḍa, lord of the Dānavas, the destroyer of the gods; by him the gods have been tormented and defeated in battle. ॥49॥
2.5.31.50: Deprived of their positions, they wander on the earth like men; indeed, out of fear of him, the world of the gods has become hard for them even to behold. ॥50॥
2.5.31.51: O uplifter of the distressed, ocean of compassion, O Maheśāna, rescue the gods from this crisis, and Śakra from fear, by slaying that lord of the Dānavas. ॥51॥
2.5.31.52: Having heard these words of the gods, Śambhu, affectionate to his devotees, smiling, spoke in a voice deep as the rumble of clouds. ॥52॥
2.5.31.53: Śrī Śaṅkara said: O Hari, O Vidhi, O gods, go to your own abodes without worry; I shall slay Śaṅkhacūḍa together with his followers—there is no doubt of this. ॥53॥
2.5.31.54: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these nectar-like words of Maheśa, they all became joyful, regarding the Dānava as already destroyed. ॥54॥
2.5.31.55: Then Hari went to Vaikuṇṭha and Vidhi to Satyaloka; and having bowed to Maheśa, the gods and others went to their own stations. ॥55॥
2.5.31.iti: Thus ends the thirty-first adhyāya, named Śiva's instruction, in the slaying of Śaṅkhacūḍa, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥31॥
2.5.32.1: Sanatkumāra said: Then Īśāna, the great Rudra, who is death to the wicked and the refuge of the good, resolved in his mind on the slaying of Śaṅkhacūḍa, in accordance with the wish of the gods. ॥1॥
2.5.32.2: Making Citraratha, the esteemed lord of the Gandharvas, his messenger, he gladly and swiftly dispatched him to Śaṅkhacūḍa. ॥2॥
2.5.32.3: At the command of the Lord of all, that messenger went to his city, which surpassed the city of great Indra and excelled the abode of Kubera. ॥3॥
2.5.32.4: Having gone there, he saw in its midst the splendid palace of Śaṅkhacūḍa, adorned with twelve gates and furnished with gatekeepers. ॥4॥
2.5.32.5: Having seen it, Puṣpadanta saw the principal gate and fearlessly told the gatekeeper the purpose of his coming. ॥5॥
2.5.32.6: Passing through that gate, he gladly went inside, into a place exceedingly beautiful, delightful, spacious and well adorned. ॥6॥
2.5.32.7: Going on, he saw that Śaṅkhacūḍa, lord of the Dānavas, seated on a jewelled throne in the midst of a circle of heroes. ॥7॥
2.5.32.8: He was surrounded by Dānava chiefs and attended by three crores of them, and by a hundred crores of others moving about with weapons in hand. ॥8॥
2.5.32.9: Seeing him thus, Puṣpadanta, filled with wonder, related the message about battle that Śaṅkara had spoken. ॥9॥
2.5.32.10: Puṣpadanta said: O king of kings, I am Śiva's messenger named Puṣpadanta, O lord. Listen to what Śaṅkara himself has said; I tell it to you. ॥10॥
2.5.32.11: Śiva said: Give back now the kingdom and the rightful offices of the gods; if not, then fight a battle with me, the Supreme Lord of the good. ॥11॥
2.5.32.12: The gods have sought refuge in me, Śaṅkara, lord of the gods and of the good. Angered, I, the great Rudra, shall slay you without doubt. ॥12॥
2.5.32.13: I am Hara; I have granted freedom from fear to all the gods. I am indeed the bearer of the rod of punishment for the wicked, and loving to those who come for refuge. ॥13॥
2.5.32.14: Will you give back the kingdom, or will you wage battle? Consider well, O lord of the Dānavas, and tell me truly which one of the two. ॥14॥
2.5.32.15: Puṣpadanta said: What Maheśa said thus to you, I have conveyed. Śambhu's word is never false, O lord of the Dānavas. ॥15॥
2.5.32.16: I wish to return quickly to my own master Hara. Tell me here what I should say to Śambhu when I go. ॥16॥
2.5.32.17: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of Puṣpadanta, the messenger of Śiva, lord of the good, the king laughed and spoke to him. ॥17॥
2.5.32.18: Śaṅkhacūḍa said: I will not give the kingdom to the gods; the earth is to be enjoyed by heroes. I shall give you battle, O Rudra, partisan of the gods. ॥18॥
2.5.32.19: The hero against whom another marches first is the lowest in the world. Therefore, O Rudra, I shall march against you first, without doubt. ॥19॥
2.5.32.20: Considering the heroes' march, I shall come at dawn. Go, and tell Rudra these words of mine. ॥20॥
2.5.32.21: Hearing these words of Śaṅkhacūḍa, Śambhu's messenger laughed heartily and spoke to the proud lord of the Dānavas. ॥21॥
2.5.32.22: Puṣpadanta said: O king of kings, you are not fit to stand even before the other attendants (gaṇas) of Śaṅkara—how much less before him. ॥22॥
2.5.32.23: So give back to the gods all their offices entirely, and go quickly to Pātāla if you wish to live. ॥23॥
2.5.32.24: Do not regard him as an ordinary god, O best of Dānavas. Śaṅkara is indeed the Supreme Self, the Lord of the lords of all. ॥24॥
2.5.32.25: All the gods headed by Indra always abide by his command, as do the Prajāpatis, the Siddhas, the sages and the lords of serpents. ॥25॥
2.5.32.26: He is the master of Hari and of Brahmā; he is both without attributes and with attributes. By the mere knitting of his brow the dissolution of all would occur. ॥26॥
2.5.32.27: He is the full form of Śiva, the bringer of the world's destruction, the refuge of the good, the slayer of the wicked, changeless, higher than the highest. ॥27॥
2.5.32.28: He is the overlord of Brahmā and the great lord of Hari as well. His command, O bull among Dānavas, must never be disregarded. ॥28॥
2.5.32.29: What use is saying much, O king of kings? Reflecting well in your mind, know Rudra, Maheśāna, to be the supreme Brahman, whose nature is consciousness. ॥29॥
2.5.32.30: Give back the kingdom and all the offices of the gods entirely. Thus it will be well with you, dear friend; otherwise there will be danger. ॥30॥
2.5.32.31: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing this, the mighty Śaṅkhacūḍa, lord of the Dānavas, deluded by what was destined to be, spoke to that messenger of Śiva. ॥31॥
2.5.32.32: Śaṅkhacūḍa said: Of my own accord I will not give up the kingdom, nor the offices—this is my firm resolve—without a battle with Maheśa. This I tell you truly. ॥32॥
2.5.32.33: The whole world, with its moving and unmoving beings, should be understood as subject to Time. Everything comes into being from Time and perishes through Time. ॥33॥
2.5.32.34: Go to Śaṅkara, Rudra, and tell him faithfully what I have said. Let him then do what is fitting; do not prolong the talk. ॥34॥
2.5.32.35: Sanatkumāra said: Thus addressed, that messenger of Śiva, Puṣpadanta, went to his own master and reported everything exactly as it was, O good sage. ॥35॥
2.5.32.iti: Thus ends the thirty-second adhyāya, named The going of the messenger, in the slaying of Śaṅkhacūḍa, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥32॥
2.5.33.1: Sanatkumāra said: Then, having heard those words of the messenger, Giriśa, the sovereign of the gods, spoke in anger to Vīrabhadra and the other gaṇas. ॥1॥
2.5.33.2: Rudra said: O Vīrabhadra, O Nandin, O Kṣetrapālas and eight Bhairavas, all you gaṇas, armed, bearing weapons and endowed with strength, ॥2॥
2.5.33.3: let them go forth today by my command, together with the two Kumāras; and let Bhadrakālī go forth for battle with her own army. I myself am setting out swiftly today for the slaying of Śaṅkhacūḍa. ॥3॥
2.5.33.4: Sanatkumāra said: Having thus given the command, the great Lord set out accompanied by the army; all the heroic gaṇas, greatly delighted, followed him. ॥4॥
2.5.33.5: Meanwhile Skanda and Gaṇeśa, leaders of the whole army, joyful, armored and bearing weapons, went to Śiva's side. ॥5॥
2.5.33.6: Vīrabhadra and Nandī, Mahākāla, Subhadraka, Viśālākṣa and Bāṇa, Piṅgalākṣa, Vikampana, ॥6॥
2.5.33.7: Virūpa and Vikṛti, Maṇibhadra and Bāṣkala, the one named Kapila, Dīrghadaṃṣṭra, Vikara, Tāmralocana, ॥7॥
2.5.33.8: Kālaṅkara, Balībhadra, Kālajihva, Kuṭīcara, Balonmatta, Raṇaślāghya, Durjaya and likewise Durgama — ॥8॥
2.5.33.9: These and others were the lords of the gaṇas, excellent commanders of the armies. I shall tell their count; listen attentively. ॥9॥
2.5.33.10: Śaṅkhakarṇa, crusher of foes, was accompanied by a crore of gaṇas; Kekarākṣa by ten crores, and Vikṛta by eight. ॥10॥
2.5.33.11: Viśākha with sixty-four, Pāriyātrika with nine, the glorious Sarvāntaka with six, and likewise Vikṛtānana. ॥11॥
2.5.33.12: Jālaka, the foremost of gaṇas, with twelve crores; the glorious Samada with seven, and Dundubha with eight. ॥12॥
2.5.33.13: Karālākṣa with five, the excellent Sandāraka with six; and here Kanduka and likewise Kuṇḍaka with crores upon crores. ॥13॥
2.5.33.14: Viṣṭambha, a gaṇa-leader best of all, with eight; Pippala with a thousand, and Sannāda likewise. ॥14॥
2.5.33.15: Āveśana likewise with eight, Candratāpana with eight, and the gaṇa-leader Mahākeśa surrounded by a thousand crores. ॥15॥
2.5.33.16: Kuṇḍī with twelve heroes, and likewise the auspicious Parvataka; Kāla and Kālaka, and Mahākāla with a hundred. ॥16॥
2.5.33.17: Agnika with a hundred crores, Agnimukha with a crore, Āditya with half a crore, and likewise Ghanāvaha. ॥17॥
2.5.33.18: Sannāha with a hundred, Kumuda likewise with crores; Amogha, Kokila, and Sumantraka with a hundred crores. ॥18॥
2.5.33.19: Kākapāda with sixty crores, Santānaka likewise with sixty, Mahābala with nine, and Madhupiṅgala with five. ॥19॥
2.5.33.20: Nīla, a lord among gods, with ninety, and likewise Pūrṇabhadra; and the mighty Caturvaktra with seven crores. ॥20॥
2.5.33.21: Likewise, with hundreds and twenties of thousands of crores of crores, all those heroes came there to the festival of battle. ॥21॥
2.5.33.22: Vīrabhadra came with a thousand crores of bhūtas, three crores of pramathas, sixty-four crores, and three crores of the Lomajas. ॥22॥
2.5.33.23: Kāṣṭhārūḍha with sixty-four, Sukeśa and Vṛṣabha likewise, and the blessed, eternal Virūpākṣa with sixty-four. ॥23॥
2.5.33.24: Tālaketu, Ṣaḍāsya, the valiant Pañcāsya, Saṃvartaka, likewise Caitra, and Laṅkulīśa, the lord himself; ॥24॥
2.5.33.25: Lokāntaka of blazing self, and likewise the lord Daityāntaka; the glorious god Bhṛṅgīriṭi, beloved of the God of gods, ॥25॥
2.5.33.26: Aśani and Bhānuka with sixty-four thousands; Kaṅkāla, Kālaka, Kāla, Nandī, and likewise Sarvāntaka. ॥26॥
2.5.33.27: These and other innumerable, mighty gaṇa-leaders went forth gladly and fearlessly to fight with Śaṅkhacūḍa. ॥27॥
2.5.33.28: All were thousand-handed, wearing crowns of matted hair, adorned with the crescent moon, blue-throated and three-eyed. ॥28॥
2.5.33.29: All were adorned with rudrākṣa ornaments and wore sacred ash, decorated with necklaces, earrings, armlets, crowns and the like. ॥29॥
2.5.33.30: Resembling Brahmā, Indra and Viṣṇu, endowed with powers such as aṇimā, radiant like a crore of suns, skilled in the work of war. ॥30॥
2.5.33.31: Some moved on the earth, some in the netherworld, some in the sky, and some in the seven heavens, O sage. ॥31॥
2.5.33.32: What need of saying more, O divine sage? All Śiva's gaṇas, dwelling in all the worlds, went to fight with the Dānavas. ॥32॥
2.5.33.33: The eight fierce Bhairavas and the eleven Rudras swiftly, the eight Vasus, Vāsava (Indra), and the twelve Ādityas quickly went. ॥33॥
2.5.33.34: Hutāśana (Agni) and Candra, Viśvakarmā and the two Aśvins, Kubera and Yama, Nirṛti and Nalakūbara, ॥34॥
2.5.33.35: Vāyu and Varuṇa, Budha and Maṅgala, and the other planets, along with Maheśa, and the valiant Kāmadeva, ॥35॥
2.5.33.36: Ugradaṃṣṭra and Ugradaṇḍa, Koraṭa and likewise Koṭabha; and the hundred-armed goddess Bhadrakālī herself, the great sovereign, ॥36॥
2.5.33.37: seated upon a celestial chariot made of the finest gems, clad in red garments, with red garlands and red unguents, ॥37॥
2.5.33.38: dancing, laughing, and singing sweetly with joy, she gave fearlessness to her own and fear to the enemies, ॥38॥
2.5.33.39: bearing a dreadful, playfully moving tongue a yojana long, and conch, discus, mace, lotus, sword, shield, bow and arrows, ॥39॥
2.5.33.40: She bore a skull-bowl, round in shape, deep and a yojana wide; a trident touching the sky, and a spear a yojana long; ॥40॥
2.5.33.41: a hammer, a pestle-club, a thunderbolt, a sword, a formidable shield, the Vaiṣṇava missile, the Vāruṇa missile, the Vāyavya missile, the serpent-noose, ॥41॥
2.5.33.42: the Nārāyaṇa missile, the Gāndharva, the Brahmā missile and likewise the Gāruḍa, the Pārjanya and the Pāśupata, the Jṛmbhaṇa missile and the Pārvata, ॥42॥
2.5.33.43: the Mahāvīra and the Saura, the Kālakāla, the Mahānala, the Māheśvara missile and the Yāmya, the Daṇḍa and likewise the Sammohana, ॥43॥
2.5.33.44: and the potent divine missile, and a hundred other supreme divine missiles — bearing these and others as well in all her hands, she then ॥44॥
2.5.33.45: came and stood there with three crores of yoginīs, together with three crores of fearsome ḍākinīs. ॥45॥
2.5.33.46: Bhūtas, pretas and piśācas, kūṣmāṇḍas, brahmarākṣasas, vetālas and rākṣasas, and yakṣas along with kinnaras also came. ॥46॥
2.5.33.47: Surrounded by them, Skanda, having bowed to the moon-crested Śiva, stayed at his father's side as his helper, by his command. ॥47॥
2.5.33.48: Then Śambhu, Rudra, having gathered his entire army, fearlessly went forth to battle with Śaṅkhacūḍa. ॥48॥
2.5.33.49: On the bank of the river Candrabhāgā, at the foot of a charming banyan tree, there Mahādeva stationed himself for the deliverance of the gods. ॥49॥
2.5.33.iti: Thus ends the thirty-third adhyāya, named The description of Mahādeva's march to battle, in the slaying of Śaṅkhacūḍa, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥33॥
2.5.34.1: Vyāsa said: O dear son of Brahmā, O sage of great intellect, may you live for many years. You have narrated the very great and wonderful story of the moon-crested Śiva. ॥1॥
2.5.34.2: When Śiva's messenger had gone from there, what did that mighty Dānava Śaṅkhacūḍa do? Tell me this truly and in full detail. ॥2॥
2.5.34.3: Sanatkumāra said: Then, when the messenger had gone, the mighty Śaṅkhacūḍa went into the inner apartment and told Tulasī that news. ॥3॥
2.5.34.4: Śaṅkhacūḍa said: O goddess, having heard from the mouth of Śambhu's messenger, I am ready for battle. Therefore I am going to fight; surely give me your leave. ॥4॥
2.5.34.5: Having spoken thus and consoled his beloved with many kinds of counsel, that wise one sported joyfully with her, disregarding Śaṅkara. ॥5॥
2.5.34.6: That couple sported through the night, immersed in an ocean of bliss, with various arts of love and with hundreds of endearing words. ॥6॥
2.5.34.7: Rising at the Brāhma-muhūrta, he performed the morning rites, and having first done his daily duties, he gave limitless gifts. ॥7॥
2.5.34.8: He made his son the sovereign king over all the Dānavas, and entrusted to his son his wife, the kingdom and all its wealth. ॥8॥
2.5.34.9: The king again comforted his beloved, who was weeping and trying to prevent his departure, telling her many things. ॥9॥
2.5.34.10: Summoning his own heroic commander-in-chief, he, honoured by all, armed and eager to wage war, gave him orders. ॥10॥
2.5.34.11: Śaṅkhacūḍa said: O commander, today let all the heroes skilled in war, fully equipped for every action, march out to battle. ॥11॥
2.5.34.12: Let the valiant Daityas and Dānavas, eighty-six clans with weapons raised, and the armies of the mighty Kaṅkas quickly march out, fearless. ॥12॥
2.5.34.13: Let fifty clans of Asuras, of immense valour (koṭi-vīrya), march out indeed to fight with Śambhu, the partisan of the gods. ॥13॥
2.5.34.14: And let a hundred clans of the Dhaumras, armed, quickly march out by my command to battle with Śambhu. ॥14॥
2.5.34.15: Let the Kālakeyas, Mauryas, Daurhṛdas and likewise the Kālakas, ready for war, march out by my command to fight with Rudra. ॥15॥
2.5.34.16: Sanatkumāra said: Having given these orders, the very mighty lord of the Asuras, king of the Dānavas, marched out with a great army, surrounded by many thousands. ॥16॥
2.5.34.17: His commander too was expert in the science of war, a great chariot-warrior, a great hero, the foremost of chariot-fighters in battle. ॥17॥
2.5.34.18: Accompanied by three lakh akṣauhiṇīs, he arranged the troops in a circular array, and, terrifying to heroes in battle, he came out of the camp. ॥18॥
2.5.34.19: Mounting an aerial chariot made of the finest jewels and placing his elders in front, he set out for battle, it is said. ॥19॥
2.5.34.20: On the bank of the river Puṣpabhadrā, where stands the auspicious undecaying banyan, at the Siddhāśrama—the field of attainment of the Siddhas, bestowing great success— ॥20॥
2.5.34.21: which is the abode of Kapila, in the holy land of Bhārata, east of the western ocean and west of Malaya, ॥21॥
2.5.34.22: in the region north of Śrīśaila and south of Gandhamādana, five yojanas in breadth and a hundred times that in length. ॥22॥
2.5.34.23: There flows the lovely river Puṣpabhadrā, resembling pure crystal, bestowing great merit in Bhārata, full of water, a form of Sarasvatī, ॥23॥
2.5.34.24: the beloved wife of the salt ocean, ever endowed with good fortune, joined with the Sarasvatī; she issues from the Himālaya. ॥24॥
2.5.34.25: Keeping Gomanta on her left, she enters the western ocean. Having gone there, Śaṅkhacūḍa saw the army of Śiva. ॥25॥
2.5.34.iti: Thus ends the thirty-fourth adhyāya, named The description of Śaṅkhacūḍa's march, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥34॥
2.5.35.1: Sanatkumāra said: Staying there, the lord of the Dānavas made a great and very wise Dānava chief his messenger and sent him to Śaṅkara. ॥1॥
2.5.35.2: The messenger went there and saw the moon-browed Lord seated at the foot of a banyan tree, shining like ten million suns. ॥2॥
2.5.35.3: He was seated in a yogic posture, with a gesture (mudrā) of the gaze, smiling, resembling pure crystal, blazing with the splendour of Brahman. ॥3॥
2.5.35.4: Holding a trident and a paṭṭiśa, clad in a tiger-skin garment, remover of death for his devotees, tranquil, the beloved of Gaurī, the three-eyed one; ॥4॥
2.5.35.5: the giver of the fruits of austerities, the bestower of all riches, quickly pleased, of gracious face, granting favour to his devotees; ॥5॥
2.5.35.6: the lord of the universe, its seed, having the universe as his form, the source of the universe, the ruler of the universe, its maker, and the cause of its dissolution; ॥6॥
2.5.35.7: the cause of causes, the one who carries beings across the ocean of hell, the giver of knowledge, the seed of knowledge, the bliss of knowledge, the eternal one. ॥7॥
2.5.35.8: Seeing him, the messenger, that Dānava chief, got down from his chariot and bowed his head to Śaṅkara together with Kumāra. ॥8॥
2.5.35.9: He bowed also to Bhadrakālī on the left and to Skanda standing in front of him. Kālī, Skanda and Śaṅkara gave him the customary blessings. ॥9॥
2.5.35.10: Then that messenger of Śaṅkhacūḍa, a supreme knower of the scriptures, bowing to Śaṅkara with joined hands, spoke auspicious words. ॥10॥
2.5.35.11: The messenger said: I am Śaṅkhacūḍa's messenger, come here into your presence. What is your wish now? Tell me that, O Maheśvara. ॥11॥
2.5.35.12: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of Śaṅkhacūḍa's envoy, Śaṅkara, the blessed Mahādeva, with a gracious mind, spoke to him. ॥12॥
2.5.35.13: Mahādeva said: Listen, O very wise messenger, to my words, which bring happiness. Having reflected, this should be told to him without dispute. ॥13॥
2.5.35.14: Brahmā, the creator of the worlds, is the father of Dharma and the knower of dharma. Marīci is his son, and Kaśyapa is known as Marīci's son. ॥14॥
2.5.35.15: Dakṣa lovingly gave him thirteen of his own daughters. Among them one was the virtuous Danu, who increased his good fortune. ॥15॥
2.5.35.16: Danu had four sons, the Dānavas, mighty in splendour. Among them one, Vipracitti, was of great strength and valour. ॥16॥
2.5.35.17: His son was the righteous Dambha, a Dānava lord of great intellect. You are his excellent son, a righteous-souled lord of the Dānavas. ॥17॥
2.5.35.18: Formerly you were an attendant, a cowherd, righteous among the cowherds. Now, through Rādhikā's curse, you have been born as the lord of the Dānavas. ॥18॥
2.5.35.19: You have come into a Dānava birth, but in truth you are not a Dānava. Knowing your own former history, give up enmity with the gods now. ॥19॥
2.5.35.20: Do not act with hostility towards them; enjoy your own position respectfully. Having reflected, do not make your rule excessive or disorderly. ॥20॥
2.5.35.21: Give the kingdom of the gods back, O Dānava, and preserve my goodwill. Remain happily in your own kingdom, and let the gods remain in their own places. ॥21॥
2.5.35.22: Enough of hostility towards beings—how much more towards the gods. All of you born in Kaśyapa's line are noble and pure in deeds. ॥22॥
2.5.35.23: Whatever sins there are, such as killing a brahmin, they are not equal to a sixteenth part of the sin born of hostility towards one's kinsmen. ॥23॥
2.5.35.24: Sanatkumāra said: Śaṅkara spoke to him these and many other auspicious words grounded in Śruti and Smṛti, imparting supreme knowledge. ॥24॥
2.5.35.25: That messenger, instructed by Śaṅkhacūḍa, foremost of logicians, bewildered by what was destined, spoke humbly. ॥25॥
2.5.35.26: The messenger said: O god, what you have said is not otherwise; that speech is so. Yet hear my submission, which is somewhat true and to the point. ॥26॥
2.5.35.27: The great sin in hostility towards kinsmen which you have just spoken of—is it, O Lord, only for the asuras and not for the gods? Tell me, O master. ॥27॥
2.5.35.28: If you say it applies to all, then I will speak after reflection. Give your verdict on that today and dispel my doubt. ॥28॥
2.5.35.29: Why, O Maheśvara, did the discus-bearer Viṣṇu cut off the heads of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, the foremost of Daityas, in the ocean of dissolution? ॥29॥
2.5.35.30: Why did you, O Giriśa, wage battle with the Tripuras and reduce them to ashes? It is well known that you are a partisan of the gods. ॥30॥
2.5.35.31: Why was Bali, after all his possessions were taken, sent off to Sutala and the other nether worlds, with the mace-bearer Viṣṇu at his door to raise him up? ॥31॥
2.5.35.32: How was Hiraṇyākṣa, together with his brother, slain by the gods? And how were Śumbha and the other asuras struck down by the gods? ॥32॥
2.5.35.33: Formerly, at the churning of the ocean, the nectar was consumed by the gods. We had our share of the toil there, but they all enjoyed the fruit. ॥33॥
2.5.35.34: This universe is the plaything of Time, the Supreme Self. When he grants it to someone, then sovereignty becomes his. ॥34॥
2.5.35.35: The enmity between gods and Dānavas is perpetual and ever occasioned by circumstance. Their defeat and victory depend on Time, in due succession. ॥35॥
2.5.35.36: Your going to intervene in the conflict of these two would be fruitless. That befits those who are related equally to both, not you, the Lord. ॥36॥
2.5.35.37: For you, the great-souled Lord of all gods and asuras, this present rivalry with us is devoid of shame. ॥37॥
2.5.35.38: For for us there is greater glory in victory and loss in defeat; for you it is the reverse. Let this be considered carefully in your mind. ॥38॥
2.5.35.39: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words, the three-eyed one laughed heartily and spoke fittingly and sweetly to the Dānava chief. ॥39॥
2.5.35.40: Maheśa said: We are dependent on our devotees and never independent. Acting by their wish, we take no one's side. ॥40॥
2.5.35.41: Long ago, at the request of Vidhi (Brahmā), even Hari first fought a battle with Madhu and Kaiṭabha, the foremost of the Daityas, in the ocean of cosmic dissolution. ॥41॥
2.5.35.42: Long ago, at the request of the gods, the slaying of Hiraṇyakaśipu was carried out by him, the benefactor of devotees, for Prahlāda's sake. ॥42॥
2.5.35.43: At the request of the gods, I too long ago waged battle with the Tripuras and then reduced them to ashes; this has been heard by all. ॥43॥
2.5.35.44: Long ago, at the request of the gods, there was a battle of the all-sovereign Mother of all with Śumbha and the others, and their slaying was accomplished by her. ॥44॥
2.5.35.45: Even now all the thirty gods went to Brahmā for refuge; and he, with the gods and the god Hari, came to me for refuge. ॥45॥
2.5.35.46: And so, O messenger, compelled by the entreaty of Hari, Brahmā and the others, I, the lord of the gods, have indeed come for battle. ॥46॥
2.5.35.47: For you are the foremost attendant of the great-souled Kṛṣṇa; of all the Daityas who have been slain, none at all were your equal. ॥47॥
2.5.35.48: What great shame is there for me, O king, in a battle with you? I, the Lord, have been sent humbly for the sake of the gods' cause. ॥48॥
2.5.35.49: Go to Śaṅkhacūḍa, and my words are to be told to him. Let him do here what is fitting; I shall do the gods' work. ॥49॥
2.5.35.50: Having spoken thus, Śaṅkara, the great Lord, fell silent there. The messenger of Śaṅkhacūḍa rose and went into his master's presence. ॥50॥
2.5.35.iti: Thus ends the thirty-fifth adhyāya, named The dialogue of Śiva's messenger, in the slaying of Śaṅkhacūḍa, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥35॥
2.5.36.1: Sanatkumāra said: That messenger went there and delivered Śiva's message in full and accurately, conveying his resolve exactly as it was. ॥1॥
2.5.36.2: Hearing that, Śaṅkhacūḍa, the mighty lord of the Dānavas, gladly accepted nothing but battle. ॥2॥
2.5.36.3: Swiftly he mounted his chariot together with his ministers, and ordered his own army to battle with Śaṅkara. ॥3॥
2.5.36.4: Śiva swiftly urged on his own army and the gods; and he himself, the Lord of all, playfully made ready for battle. ॥4॥
2.5.36.5: The battle began at once; musical instruments sounded in great numbers; an uproar arose, and likewise the cries of heroes. ॥5॥
2.5.36.6: O sage, a battle broke out between the gods and the Dānavas; there the hosts of gods and Dānavas fought according to the rules of righteous combat. ॥6॥
2.5.36.7: Mahendra himself fought with Vṛṣaparvan; Bhāskara (the Sun) fought righteously with Vipracitti. ॥7॥
2.5.36.8: Viṣṇu waged a supreme battle with Dambha; Kāla with Kālāsura, and Hutāśana (Fire) with Gokarṇa. ॥8॥
2.5.36.9: Kubera fought with Kālakeya, Viśvakarman with Maya, Mṛtyu with Bhayaṅkara, and likewise Yama with Saṃhāra. ॥9॥
2.5.36.10: Varuṇa fought with Kālambika, Samīraṇa (Wind) with Cañcala, Budha with Ghaṭapṛṣṭha, and Śanaiścara (Saturn) with Raktākṣa. ॥10॥
2.5.36.11: Jayanta fought with Ratnasāra, the Vasus with the hosts of Varcas, the two Aśvins with the two Dīptimats, and Nalakūbara with Dhūmra. ॥11॥
2.5.36.12: Dharma fought with Dhurandhara, Maṅgala (Mars) with Gaṇakākṣa, Vaiśvāna with Śobhākara, and Manmatha with Pipiṭa. ॥12॥
2.5.36.13: With Gokāmukha, with Cūrṇa, with the asura named Khaḍga, with Dhūmra, with Saṃhala, and with the mighty Viśva— ॥13॥
2.5.36.14: —and with Palāśa, the twelve Ādityas fought righteously. Other immortals, endowed with Śiva's support, fought with the asuras. ॥14॥
2.5.36.15: The eleven great Rudras fought with eleven fearsome heroic asuras of great strength and valour. ॥15॥
2.5.36.16: Mahāmaṇi fought with Ugracaṇḍa and others; Candra (the Moon) with Rāhu, and Jīva (Jupiter) righteously with Śukra. ॥16॥
2.5.36.17: Nandīśvara and all the others fought in the great battle with the foremost Dānavas; they are not described separately in detail. ॥17॥
2.5.36.18: Then Śambhu stayed at the foot of a banyan tree with Kālī's son, and all the masses of troops fought ceaselessly, O sage. ॥18॥
2.5.36.19: And Śaṅkhacūḍa, adorned with jewelled ornaments, sat on a lovely jewelled throne, surrounded by millions of Dānavas. ॥19॥
2.5.36.20: Then a great battle took place, crushing gods and asuras; various divine weapons flew about in that great fight. ॥20॥
2.5.36.21: Maces, double-edged swords, spears, discuses, bhuśuṇḍis, lances, hammers, swords, arrows, iron bars, śaktis, unmukhas and battle-axes— ॥21॥
2.5.36.22: arrows, javelins and swords, śataghnīs by the thousands, bhindipālas and others besides shone in the hands of the heroes. ॥22॥
2.5.36.23: With these the heroes there, in great exultation, cut off the heads of the roaring warriors of both armies in the battle. ॥23॥
2.5.36.24: Many elephants, horses, chariots and foot-soldiers, of various kinds, together with riders and mounts, lay there cut to pieces. ॥24॥
2.5.36.25: Their arms, thighs, hands, waists, pairs of ears and feet were severed; their banners, arrows, swords, armour and fine ornaments were shattered. ॥25॥
2.5.36.26: The earth shone, strewn with heads whose crowns had been knocked off, along with earrings, and with thighs shapely like elephant-trunks, destroyed in the fury. ॥26॥
2.5.36.27: —and with mighty arms severed, still bearing ornaments and weapons, and with other limbs, suddenly strewn as if with clusters swarming with bees. ॥27॥
2.5.36.28: In the battle, warriors, seeing with the eyes of their own severed heads their headless trunks running about, leapt up there with strong arms raising weapons. ॥28॥
2.5.36.29: Leaping about vigourously, the heroes of great strength and valour fought one another there with various weapons and missiles. ॥29॥
2.5.36.30: Some, having slain warriors in battle with golden-tipped arrows, roared heroic roars like rain-laden clouds. ॥30॥
2.5.36.31: One hero covered another hero, together with his chariot and charioteer, on all sides with a mass of arrows, as a cloud covers the sun in the rainy season. ॥31॥
2.5.36.32: Engaging one another, the duelists fought, challenging, pressing forward, and striking each other at the vital points. ॥32॥
2.5.36.33: Everywhere in the great battle bands of heroes were seen, with various arms, banners and weapons, raising lion-like roars. ॥33॥
2.5.36.34: The great heroes, thrilled with delight, each blew their loud-sounding conches and leapt about there. ॥34॥
2.5.36.35: Thus for a very long time there raged between the gods and the Dānavas a great, fierce, terrible battle that delighted the heroes. ॥35॥
2.5.36.36: This is the sport (līlā) of the great Lord Śaṅkara, the Supreme Self, by which everything, including gods, asuras and humans, is bewildered. ॥36॥
2.5.36.iti: Thus ends the thirty-sixth adhyāya, named The description of the battle between the two sides, in the slaying of Śaṅkhacūḍa, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥36॥
2.5.37.1: Sanatkumāra said: Then all the hosts of gods, defeated by the Dānavas, fled in fear, their bodies wounded by weapons and missiles. ॥1॥
2.5.37.2: Turning back, they went for refuge to Śaṅkara, lord of the universe, and said in a trembling voice, save us, save us, O Lord of all. ॥2॥
2.5.37.3: Seeing the defeat of the gods and the others, and hearing their fearful words, Śaṅkara became greatly enraged. ॥3॥
2.5.37.4: Looking on them with a glance of compassion, he granted the gods freedom from fear, and by his power he increased the strength of his own Gaṇas. ॥4॥
2.5.37.5: Then, commanded by Śiva, Skanda, the great hero and son of Hara, fought fearlessly in battle against the hosts of the Dānavas. ॥5॥
2.5.37.6: Growing angry and raising a warrior's cry, the god who was the slayer of Tāraka slew a hundred akṣauhiṇīs in battle. ॥6॥
2.5.37.7: Lotus-eyed Kālī made their blood flow; cutting off their heads, she suddenly devoured them. ॥7॥
2.5.37.8: She drank the blood of those Dānavas on every side, and fought a varied battle, terrifying to gods and Dānavas alike. ॥8॥
2.5.37.9: Likewise in battle, seizing with one hand ten million of the Dānavas' lordly elephants, she playfully tossed them into her mouth. ॥9॥
2.5.37.10: A thousand headless trunks danced wildly on the battlefield; a great uproar arose, terrifying to the cowardly. ॥10॥
2.5.37.11: Again Skanda, flaring into fierce anger, let loose a rain of arrows, and in an instant felled the Asura leaders by the crore. ॥11॥
2.5.37.12: Then all the Dānavas who had escaped death, their bodies wounded by Skanda's net of arrows, fled in fear. ॥12॥
2.5.37.13: Vṛṣaparvan, Vipracitti, Daṇḍa and Vikampana—all of them fought with Skanda one after another. ॥13॥
2.5.37.14: Mahāmārī too fought and did not turn away; and they the demons were wounded in their limbs, sorely afflicted by Skanda's spear. ॥14॥
2.5.37.15: Then, O sage, victory went to Mahāmārī and Skanda; drums resounded in heaven and a shower of flowers fell. ॥15॥
2.5.37.16: Seeing Skanda's fight—most fierce and wondrous, destructive of the Dānavas like a cosmic dissolution— ॥16॥
2.5.37.17: and the havoc wrought by Mahāmārī that was causing their destruction, he Śaṅkhacūḍa suddenly grew exceedingly angry and then armed himself in person. ॥17॥
2.5.37.18: Mounting an excellent aerial chariot, furnished with many kinds of weapons and missiles, safe against all warriors, and adorned with many gems, ॥18॥
2.5.37.19: Śaṅkhacūḍa went forth amid his chariots with great heroes; drawing his bow to his ear, he released a shower of arrows. ॥19॥
2.5.37.20: That rain of his arrows was irresistible and terrifying, and a most dreadful darkness fell upon the field of slaughter. ॥20॥
2.5.37.21: All the gods fled, as did the others, Nandīśvara and the rest; Kārttikeya alone stood at the forefront of the battle. ॥21॥
2.5.37.22: The king Śaṅkhacūḍa sent down an irresistible, terrifying shower of mountains, serpents, elephants and trees. ॥22॥
2.5.37.23: Struck by that shower, Skanda, the son of Śiva, was like the sun covered by dense mist. ॥23॥
2.5.37.24: He Śaṅkhacūḍa worked his own magic of many kinds, taught by Maya; none of the gods or Gaṇas could comprehend it, O best of sages. ॥24॥
2.5.37.25: At that very moment Śaṅkhacūḍa, master of great magic and of great strength, cut his Skanda's bow with a single divine arrow. ॥25॥
2.5.37.26: He shattered his divine chariot, cut down the chariot's guards, and with a divine missile he battered the peacock. ॥26॥
2.5.37.27: He hurled a deadly spear, radiant as the sun, at his chest; by that blow he Skanda suddenly fainted for a moment. ॥27॥
2.5.37.28: Regaining consciousness, Kārtika, slayer of enemy heroes, mounted his own mount, made of the finest gems. ॥28॥
2.5.37.29: Remembering the feet of Maheśa together with Ambikā, the six-faced one took up his weapons and missiles and waged a fierce battle. ॥29॥
2.5.37.30: The son of Śiva in his wrath cut down all the serpents, mountains, trees and rocks with a divine missile. ॥30॥
2.5.37.31: He warded off the fire with a Pārjanya (rain) arrow, and with ease cut down Śaṅkhacūḍa's chariot and bow, ॥31॥
2.5.37.32: his armor, all his steeds, and his crown gleaming with its diadem; he raised a warrior's cry and roared again and again. ॥32॥
2.5.37.33: He hurled a spear radiant as the sun at the chest of the lord of the Dānavas; by that blow he Śaṅkhacūḍa fell into a very long swoon. ॥33॥
2.5.37.34: Shaking off that pain within a mere moment, the mighty one regained consciousness, rose up, and roared like a lion. ॥34॥
2.5.37.35: He in turn struck the mighty Kārtikeya with a spear; he Kārtikeya fell to the ground, honouring the unfailing power of the spear granted by Brahmā. ॥35॥
2.5.37.36: Kālī took him in her lap and carried him into Śiva's presence; and Śiva, by his knowledge, revived him with ease. ॥36॥
2.5.37.37: He gave him boundless strength; the valiant son of Śiva rose up and resolved to go there, to the battle, again. ॥37॥
2.5.37.38: Meanwhile the heroic and mighty Vīrabhadra fought in battle with the powerful Śaṅkhacūḍa. ॥38॥
2.5.37.39: Whatever missiles the Dānava rained down in battle, the hero cut each of them to pieces with ease with his own arrows. ॥39॥
2.5.37.40: The lord of the Dānavas released divine missiles by the hundred; the valiant Vīrabhadra cut them down and struck him with arrows. ॥40॥
2.5.37.41: Then the valiant Śaṅkhacūḍa became exceedingly furious and struck him on the chest with a spear; he trembled and fell to the ground. ॥41॥
2.5.37.42: Regaining consciousness in a moment, the lord of the gaṇas, Vīrabhadra, foremost among the gaṇas, rose up and took up his bow once more. ॥42॥
2.5.37.43: Meanwhile Kālī went to the battle again, at Kārttikeya's wish, to devour the Dānavas and to protect her own side. ॥43॥
2.5.37.44: And the heroes followed her—Nandīśvara and the others—as well as all the gods, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas and serpents. ॥44॥
2.5.37.45: There were wine-vessels in abundance and hundreds of bearers of musical instruments. Once again all the heroes on both sides stood ready for battle. ॥45॥
2.5.37.iti: Thus ends the thirty-seventh adhyāya, named The description of the battle with Śaṅkhacūḍa and his army, in the slaying of Śaṅkhacūḍa, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥37॥
2.5.38.1: Sanatkumāra said: She went to the battle and let out a lion's roar, and at that roar of the Goddess the Dānavas fainted. ॥1॥
2.5.38.2: Again and again she gave out a dreadful, boisterous laugh; then she drank honey-wine and danced at the forefront of the battle. ॥2॥
2.5.38.3: Ugradaṃṣṭrā, Ugradaṇḍā and Koṭavī drank wine, and the other goddesses there in the battle danced and drank wine. ॥3॥
2.5.38.4: Then a great uproar arose in the army of the Gaṇas and gods; all the hosts of gods and the rest rejoiced, roaring loudly. ॥4॥
2.5.38.5: Seeing Kālī, Śaṅkhacūḍa quickly came to the battle; the Dānavas were struck with fear, and the king gave them reassurance. ॥5॥
2.5.38.6: Kālī hurled fire resembling the flames of the fire of cosmic dissolution; the king swiftly destroyed it with ease by a Vaiṣṇava weapon. ॥6॥
2.5.38.7: The Goddess swiftly hurled the Nārāyaṇa missile at him; seeing the Dānava hostile, that weapon grew in power. ॥7॥
2.5.38.8: Seeing it, resembling the flames of the fire of dissolution, Śaṅkhacūḍa fell flat on the ground like a staff and bowed again and again. ॥8॥
2.5.38.9: Seeing the Dānava humbled, that weapon withdrew. Then the Goddess hurled the Brahmā missile, accompanied by mantras. ॥9॥
2.5.38.10: Seeing it blazing, the lord of the Dānavas bowed and stood on the ground, and warded it off with a Brahmā missile. ॥10॥
2.5.38.11: Then the enraged lord of the Dānavas, drawing his bow swiftly, hurled divine missiles at the Goddess, accompanied by mantras. ॥11॥
2.5.38.12: Opening wide her mouth, she devoured them in the battle and roared with loud laughter; the Dānavas were seized with fear. ॥12॥
2.5.38.13: He hurled at Kālī a spear a hundred yojanas long; the Goddess cut it into a hundred pieces with a network of divine missiles. ॥13॥
2.5.38.14: He then hurled the Vaiṣṇava missile at Caṇḍikā, and Kālī warded it off with the Māheśvara missile. ॥14॥
2.5.38.15: Thus the battle between them went on for a very long time, and all the gods and the Dānavas too became spectators. ॥15॥
2.5.38.16: Then the great Goddess Kālī, enraged and like Death in battle, angrily took up the Pāśupata arrow, consecrated with mantras. ॥16॥
2.5.38.17: Before it was released, a bodiless voice arose to forbid it: O Goddess, do not in anger hurl this missile at Śaṅkhacūḍa. ॥17॥
2.5.38.18: O Caṇḍikā, there is no death for the hero Śaṅkhacūḍa even from the unfailing Pāśupata; consider some other means. ॥18॥
2.5.38.19: Hearing this, Bhadrakālī did not hurl that missile; out of hunger she playfully devoured ten million Dānavas. ॥19॥
2.5.38.20: The terrifying one rushed to devour Śaṅkhacūḍa, but the Dānava held her back with the divine Raudra missile. ॥20॥
2.5.38.21: Then the enraged lord of the Dānavas quickly hurled a sword, like the summer sun, sharp-edged and exceedingly terrifying. ॥21॥
2.5.38.22: Seeing it coming, blazing, Kālī in anger opened her mouth and devoured it while he looked on. ॥22॥
2.5.38.23: The lord of the Dānavas cut down her other divine missiles; even before they reached him he broke them into a hundred pieces. ॥23॥
2.5.38.24: Again the great Goddess rushed at him to devour him, but that glorious lord of all siddhis made himself invisible. ॥24॥
2.5.38.25: Not seeing the Dānava, Kālī with a swift blow of her fist smashed his chariot and, it is said, slew his charioteer. ॥25॥
2.5.38.26: Then the illusion-wielding Śaṅkhacūḍa, quickly reappearing, swiftly hurled at Bhadrakālī a discus resembling the flames of the fire of dissolution. ॥26॥
2.5.38.27: The Goddess then playfully caught that discus with her left hand and, in anger, quickly devoured it with her own mouth. ॥27॥
2.5.38.28: With great fury the Goddess swiftly struck him with her fist; the lord of the Dānavas reeled and fainted for a moment. ॥28॥
2.5.38.29: Regaining consciousness in a moment, the mighty one rose up; but regarding her as his mother, he did not engage in hand-to-hand combat with her. ॥29॥
2.5.38.30: The Goddess seized the Dānava, whirled him round again and again, and with great fury flung him swiftly upward. ॥30॥
2.5.38.31: The mighty Śaṅkhacūḍa flew up with speed, and having fallen down, rose again and bowed to Bhadrakālī. ॥31॥
2.5.38.32: Cheerful in mind and not bewildered even in that great battle, he mounted a most charming aerial chariot built of the finest jewels. ॥32॥
2.5.38.33: Kālikā, out of hunger, drank the blood of the Dānavas. Meanwhile a bodiless voice arose there: ॥33॥
2.5.38.34: A hundred thousand arrogant Dānava chiefs now remain in the battle, together with those roaring ones; so you, O Īśvarī, devour them. ॥34॥
2.5.38.35: Do not set your mind on killing the lord of the Dānavas in battle; O Goddess, be certain that this Śaṅkhacūḍa cannot be slain by you. ॥35॥
2.5.38.36: Hearing these words issuing from the sky, the Goddess, having eaten the flesh of many Dānavas and drunk their blood as well, ॥36॥
2.5.38.37: having eaten and drunk, Bhadrakālī came into the presence of Śaṅkara and related the course of the battle in due order, from beginning to end. ॥37॥
2.5.38.iti: Thus ends the thirty-eighth adhyāya, named The description of Kālī's battle, in the slaying of Śaṅkhacūḍa, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥38॥
2.5.39.1: Vyāsa said: Having heard what Kālī said, what did Īśāna do, and what did he say? Tell me the truth, O greatly wise one; my curiosity is intense. ॥1॥
2.5.39.2: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard the words spoken by Kālī, Śaṅkara, the supreme Lord, Śambhu who performs great sports, laughed and reassured her. ॥2॥
2.5.39.3: Having heard the voice from the sky, Śaṅkara, expert in the knowledge of reality, went himself into battle together with his gaṇas. ॥3॥
2.5.39.4: Mounted on the great bull, accompanied by Vīrabhadra and others, attended by the Bhairavas and Kṣetrapālas who were equal to himself, ॥4॥
2.5.39.5: Maheśa reached the battlefield and, having assumed a heroic form, Rudra shone there exceedingly, like Death (Antaka) embodied. ॥5॥
2.5.39.6: Śaṅkhacūḍa, on seeing Śiva, descended from his aerial chariot and bowed with supreme devotion, touching his head to the ground, prostrate like a staff. ॥6॥
2.5.39.7: Having bowed to him by yogic power, he mounted the aerial chariot; swiftly he armed himself and seized his bow together with arrows. ॥7॥
2.5.39.8: The battle between Śiva and the Dānava lasted a hundred years; that shower of arrows was then as fierce as the rain of two clouds pouring down. ॥8॥
2.5.39.9: Śaṅkhacūḍa, the great hero, hurled terrible arrows; Śaṅkara cut them down playfully with his own volleys of arrows. ॥9॥
2.5.39.10: And in anger Mahārudra, the odd-eyed one, the punisher of the wicked and refuge of the good, struck his limbs with floods of weapons. ॥10॥
2.5.39.11: The swift Dānava, taking a sharp sword and a shield, struck on the head the bull, Śiva's excellent mount. ॥11॥
2.5.39.12: When his mount was struck, Rudra playfully and swiftly cut, with a razor-edged arrow, his sword and also his brilliantly shining shield. ॥12॥
2.5.39.13: When his shield was cut, that Asura then hurled a spear; Hara split it in two with his own arrow as it came at him. ॥13॥
2.5.39.14: Swollen with rage, the Dānava Śaṅkhacūḍa hurled a discus; Hara suddenly pulverized that too with a blow of his fist. ॥14॥
2.5.39.15: Whirling a mace with force, he hurled it at Hara; it too, struck suddenly by Śambhu, was shattered and reduced to ashes. ॥15॥
2.5.39.16: Then the lord of the Dānavas, Śaṅkhacūḍa, seizing an axe in his hand and overcome with fury, rushed swiftly at Hara. ॥16॥
2.5.39.17: Striking him with floods of his own arrows, Śaṅkara playfully and quickly felled that axe-wielding Asura to the ground. ॥17॥
2.5.39.18: Then, regaining consciousness in a moment, he mounted his fine chariot and, bearing divine weapons and arrows, shone forth, pervading the whole sky. ॥18॥
2.5.39.19: Seeing him approach, Hara intently sounded his ḍamaru and also made the unbearable twang of his bowstring. ॥19॥
2.5.39.20: The Lord filled the quarters with the blast of his horn, and Giriśa himself roared, terrifying the Asuras then. ॥20॥
2.5.39.21: The lord of bulls, with mighty bellows that made elephants abandon their great pride, suddenly filled the sky, the earth and the eight directions. ॥21॥
2.5.39.22: Mahākāla, leaping up, struck the earth and the sky with his two hands; by that resounding, all earlier sounds were drowned out. ॥22॥
2.5.39.23: The Kṣetrapāla let out an ominous, booming laugh, and Bhairava too made a great roar in that great battle. ॥23॥
2.5.39.24: A great, terrifying uproar arose in the midst of the battle, and then heroic shouts rang out on all sides among the gaṇas. ॥24॥
2.5.39.25: All the Dānavas trembled at those harsh, fear-inspiring sounds; hearing them, the mighty lord of the Dānavas became exceedingly enraged. ॥25॥
2.5.39.26: When Hara cried, stand, stand, O wicked one, the gods and the gaṇas at once shouted, victory, victory! ॥26॥
2.5.39.27: Then the very valourous son of Dambha came forward and hurled at Rudra a spear exceedingly terrible with garlands of flame. ॥27॥
2.5.39.28: As it came on, blazing like a mass of fire, the Kṣetrapāla swiftly advanced and repelled it in the battle with a great meteor issuing from his mouth. ॥28॥
2.5.39.29: Again a great battle began between Śiva and the Dānava; the earth and heaven shook, together with mountains, oceans and lakes. ॥29॥
2.5.39.30: Śambhu then cut the arrows released by Dambha's son, and he cut the arrows sent by him, with fierce arrows, by thousands and by hundreds. ॥30॥
2.5.39.31: Then Śambhu, greatly enraged, struck him with his trident; unable to bear that blow, he quickly fell to the ground unconscious. ॥31॥
2.5.39.32: Then in a moment that Asura regained consciousness and, taking up his bow, struck Rudra and all those gaṇas with arrows. ॥32॥
2.5.39.33: Assuming ten thousand arms, the valourous Śaṅkhacūḍa suddenly covered Śaṅkara with ten thousand discuses. ॥33॥
2.5.39.34: Then Rudra, lord of Durgā and destroyer of the distress of the afflicted, enraged, quickly cut those discuses with his excellent arrows. ॥34॥
2.5.39.35: Then the Dānava, suddenly seizing a mace, surrounded by a great army, rushed with speed to kill Hara. ॥35॥
2.5.39.36: As he charged, Hara, the remover of the pride of the wicked, greatly enraged, swiftly cut his mace with a sharp-edged sword. ॥36॥
2.5.39.37: When his mace was cut, the Dānava became exceedingly enraged; the mighty one seized a blazing spike unbearable to others. ॥37॥
2.5.39.38: As the handsome lord of the Dānavas came on, lance in hand, Hara swiftly pierced him in the heart with his own trident. ॥38॥
2.5.39.39: From Śaṅkhacūḍa's heart, split by the trident, there emerged another mighty person, who said, stand, stand. ॥39॥
2.5.39.40: As he was emerging, Hara then, laughing loudly, quickly cut off his fearsome head with the sword, and he fell to the ground. ॥40॥
2.5.39.41: Then Kālī, opening her mouth wide in anger, fiercely devoured those many asuras, whose necks were crushed by her fangs. ॥41॥
2.5.39.42: The Kṣetrapāla, agitated with rage, devoured many other daityas. Some perished cut down by the Bhairava weapon, and others likewise perished pierced. ॥42॥
2.5.39.43: Vīrabhadra in anger destroyed many other warriors; Nandīśvara slew many others, the oppressors of the immortals. ॥43॥
2.5.39.44: In this way many heroic gaṇas, then arming themselves in fury, destroyed many daityas and asuras, the oppressors of the gods. ॥44॥
2.5.39.45: Thus a very great part of his army perished there, and many other warriors fled, distressed with fear. ॥45॥
2.5.39.iti: Thus ends the thirty-ninth adhyāya, named The description of the slaying of Śaṅkhacūḍa's army, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥39॥
2.5.40.1: Sanatkumāra said: Then, seeing his own army slain, its chief and greater part, and likewise his heroes who were dear to him as life, the Dānava became extremely angry. ॥1॥
2.5.40.2: He spoke these words to Śambhu: I stand in the battle; you too stand firm. What does it matter that these of mine have been slain today? Fight with me face to face. ॥2॥
2.5.40.3: Having said this, O sage, that lord of the Dānavas, armed for battle, made up his mind and went straight towards Śaṅkara. ॥3॥
2.5.40.4: The Dānava hurled divine missiles at the great Rudra and released a shower of arrows, as a cloud releases a shower of rain. ॥4॥
2.5.40.5: He produced many kinds of illusions, invisible and terrifying to behold, which could not be fathomed even by all the hosts of gods, even the best of them. ॥5॥
2.5.40.6: Seeing that illusion, Śaṅkara there playfully discharged the Māheśvara missile, most divine, the destroyer of all illusions. ॥6॥
2.5.40.7: By its brilliance his illusions were then quickly destroyed, and those very divine missiles also became powerless. ॥7॥
2.5.40.8: Then in the battle the mighty Great Lord, to kill him, suddenly seized his trident, irresistible even to the most powerful. ॥8॥
2.5.40.9: At that very moment, to restrain it, a bodiless voice arose: Do not hurl the trident now; hear our request, O Śaṅkara. ॥9॥
2.5.40.10: You are surely capable in every way of destroying the whole cosmic egg in an instant; what then, O Lord, of a single Dānava, Śaṅkhacūḍa, now? ॥10॥
2.5.40.11: Even so, the bounds set by the Veda should not be destroyed by you, the Master. Hear it, O Mahādeva, and make it fruitful in truth. ॥11॥
2.5.40.12: As long as the supreme, most formidable armour of Hari is on his hand body, and as long as the chastity of his chaste wife remains, ॥12॥
2.5.40.13: so long there is no old age or death for this Śaṅkhacūḍa, O Śaṅkara. Make true, O Lord, this word of Brahmā. ॥13॥
2.5.40.14: Hearing the heavenly voice, Hara then said, so be it. Viṣṇu came by Hara's wish, and Hara, the refuge of the good, instructed him. ॥14॥
2.5.40.15: In the guise of an old brāhmaṇa, Viṣṇu, the best of illusionists, went near Śaṅkhacūḍa and then spoke to him. ॥15॥
2.5.40.16: The old brahmin said: Give alms, O lord of the Dānavas, to me who have now come to you. ॥16॥
2.5.40.17: I will not state it openly now to you, who are kind to the needy; I will tell you afterwards, and you will then make your promise true. ॥17॥
2.5.40.18: The great king, with a cheerful face and eyes, said, Om, yes. Then, with clever deceit, the brāhmaṇa said, I am a person who seeks the armour. ॥18॥
2.5.40.19: Hearing that, that lord of the Dānavas, devoted to brāhmaṇas, truthful in speech and mighty, gave that divine armour, dear to him as life, to the brāhmaṇa. ॥19॥
2.5.40.20: Thus by deceit Hari took the armour from him, and in the form of Śaṅkhacūḍa went to Tulasī. ॥20॥
2.5.40.21: Having gone there, Hari, the Lord skilled in illusion, quickly deposited his seed in her womb for the sake of the gods' purpose. ॥21॥
2.5.40.22: Meanwhile, as Hari conveyed his word to Śambhu, the Lord seized the blazing trident to slay Śaṅkhacūḍa. ॥22॥
2.5.40.23: That trident of Śaṅkara, the Supreme Self, named Vijaya, shone forth, illuminating all the directions, heaven and earth. ॥23॥
2.5.40.24: It was like ten million midday suns and the flames of the fire of dissolution; irresistible, unassailable, never failing, the slayer of enemies; ॥24॥
2.5.40.25: a most fierce circle of radiance, the chief of all weapons and missiles, unbearable and terrifying to all gods and asuras; ॥25॥
2.5.40.26: capable of playfully destroying the whole universe, it stood there supreme, blazing, as if all splendour had gathered in one place; ॥26॥
2.5.40.27: a thousand bows in length and a hundred cubits in breadth; of the nature of the individual soul and Brahman, eternal in form and uncreated. ॥27॥
2.5.40.28: Whirling in the sky, that trident, by Śiva's command, fell upon Śaṅkhacūḍa in an instant and swiftly reduced him to ashes. ॥28॥
2.5.40.29: Then the trident of the Great Lord, its task accomplished, swift as thought, quickly returned through the sky to Śaṅkara, O brāhmaṇa. ॥29॥
2.5.40.30: Kettledrums sounded in heaven, Gandharvas and Kinnaras sang, sages and gods offered praise, and the hosts of Apsarases danced. ॥30॥
2.5.40.31: A shower of flowers fell continuously upon Śiva; Hari, Brahmā, Indra and the others, and likewise the sages, praised him. ॥31॥
2.5.40.32: Then Śaṅkhacūḍa, lord of the Dānavas, by Śiva's grace was freed from the curse and regained his former form. ॥32॥
2.5.40.33: From the bones of Śaṅkhacūḍa arose the species of conches; and conch-water is held sacred for all, except for Śaṅkara. ॥33॥
2.5.40.34: Especially to Hari and Lakṣmī conch-water is very dear, and also to those connected with him, but not to Hara, O great sage. ॥34॥
2.5.40.35: Having thus slain him, Śaṅkara, greatly delighted, mounted on his bull and surrounded by Umā, Skanda and the Gaṇas, went to Śivaloka. ॥35॥
2.5.40.36: Hari went to Vaikuṇṭha; Kṛṣṇa became at ease; the gods, filled with supreme bliss, reached their own domains. ॥36॥
2.5.40.37: The world attained great well-being; everything became free of obstacles and happy; the sky became clear, and the whole earth most auspicious. ॥37॥
2.5.40.38: Thus has been told the story of the Great Lord, which brings joy, removes all sorrow, bestows prosperity and fulfils all desires; ॥38॥
2.5.40.39: blessed, bringing fame and long life, warding off all obstacles, granting enjoyment and liberation, and yielding the fruit of all desires. ॥39॥
2.5.40.40: The wise man who constantly listens to this story of the moon-crested Śiva, or causes it to be heard, or reads it, or causes it to be read — ॥40॥
2.5.40.41: Here in this world one would obtain wealth, grain, sons and happiness; there is no doubt. One attains all desires, and above all, devotion to Śiva. ॥41॥
2.5.40.42: This incomparable narrative destroys all calamities, generates supreme knowledge, and increases devotion to Śiva. ॥42॥
2.5.40.43: By hearing it, a brāhmaṇa becomes endowed with the radiance of sacred knowledge, a kṣatriya becomes victorious, one born a vaiśya becomes rich in wealth, and a śūdra attains excellence. ॥43॥
2.5.40.iti: Thus ends the fortieth adhyāya, named The account of the slaying of Śaṅkhacūḍa, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥40॥
2.5.41.1: Vyāsa said: And by what means did the Lord Nārāyaṇa deposit his seed in the womb of Tulasī? Please tell me that. ॥1॥
2.5.41.2: Sanatkumāra said: Nārāyaṇa, the accomplisher of the gods' tasks and the refuge of the good, in the form of Śaṅkhacūḍa sported with his Śaṅkhacūḍa's wife. ॥2॥
2.5.41.3: Hear that very delightful account of Viṣṇu, Hari, the executor of Śiva's command and the mother (nourisher) of the worlds. ॥3॥
2.5.41.4: In the midst of battle, having heard the voice from the sky and been urged by the god Śambhu, Hari, having taken the supreme armour of Śaṅkhacūḍa, ॥4॥
2.5.41.5: Hari, first in the guise of a brahmin, swiftly by his own māyā went in the form of Śaṅkhacūḍa to Tulasī's house. ॥5॥
2.5.41.6: He had the kettledrum sounded near Tulasī's door, and right there, with a cry of victory, he made the beautiful lady aware of his arrival. ॥6॥
2.5.41.7: Hearing that, the virtuous lady, filled with supreme joy, looked at the royal road through the window with great eagerness. ॥7॥
2.5.41.8: Having given wealth to brahmins, she had auspicious rites performed; knowing her own husband had come, she quickly adorned herself. ॥8॥
2.5.41.9: Getting down from the chariot, Viṣṇu—that master of māyā, doer of the gods' work, in the form of Śaṅkhacūḍa—went to the goddess's dwelling. ॥9॥
2.5.41.10: Seeing him, her beloved, arrived before her, she, full of joy, washed his feet, bowed, and wept. ॥10॥
2.5.41.11: She seated the auspicious one on a lovely jewelled throne and gave him betel perfumed with camphor and other fragrances. ॥11॥
2.5.41.12: Today my birth and life have become fruitful, as I see again at home the lord of my life who had gone to battle. ॥12॥
2.5.41.13: Having said this, she looked at him joyfully with sidelong glances and a smile, and asked her beloved in a sweet voice about the events of the battle. ॥13॥
2.5.41.14: Tulasī said: He is the destroyer of countless universes, the foremost of gods, the Lord, whose command the gods Viṣṇu, Brahmā and others always obey. ॥14॥
2.5.41.15: He is the progenitor of the three gods, whose self is the three guṇas yet who is beyond the guṇas; by the wish of his devotees he takes on qualities, and sets Hari and Brahmā to work. ॥15॥
2.5.41.16: At Kubera's request Hara assumed a form with qualities; he dwells on Kailāsa, is lord of the gaṇas, the supreme Brahman, the refuge of the good. ॥16॥
2.5.41.17: By a mere moment of whose time crores of universes are dissolved, and in a mere instant many Viṣṇus, Brahmās and others have passed away— ॥17॥
2.5.41.18: with him you went to wage battle, my lord. How did the war go with him, the ally of the gods? ॥18॥
2.5.41.19: You have come here safe, having conquered that Supreme Lord. How did your victory come about? Tell me just that. ॥19॥
2.5.41.20: Hearing Tulasī's words thus, the lord of Ramā, bearing the form of Śaṅkhacūḍa, laughed and spoke nectar-like words to her. ॥20॥
2.5.41.21: The Lord said: When I, fond of battle, went to the battlefield, a great uproar arose and a mighty battle began. ॥21॥
2.5.41.22: A battle took place between the gods and the Dānavas, both eager for victory; there the Daityas were defeated by the immortals, proud of their strength. ॥22॥
2.5.41.23: Then I fought there with the gods, fierce in strength, and those gods, defeated, went to Śaṅkara for refuge. ॥23॥
2.5.41.24: Rudra too came to the battle to help them, and I, proud of my strength, fought with him for a long time. ॥24॥
2.5.41.25: Our battle, beloved, went on for a full year, and all the Asuras perished, O loving one. ॥25॥
2.5.41.26: Brahmā himself brought about friendship between us two, and by Brahmā's command the gods were given back their offices. ॥26॥
2.5.41.27: I have come to my own home, and Śiva has gone to Śivaloka. Complete well-being has been attained and the trouble is gone. ॥27॥
2.5.41.28: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this, the lord of the worlds went to bed, and there the lord of Ramā joyfully made love with that lady. ॥28॥
2.5.41.29: The chaste lady, because of a difference in the pleasure, the union and the embrace, suspected everything and said, who are you? ॥29॥
2.5.41.30: Tulasī said: Who are you? Tell me quickly. I have been enjoyed by you through deceit; my chastity has been destroyed—now I shall curse you. ॥30॥
2.5.41.31: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing Tulasī's words, Hari, out of fear of the curse, playfully assumed his own most charming form, O brahmin. ॥31॥
2.5.41.32: Seeing that form and recognising Viṣṇu by his marks, Tulasī, enraged at the loss of her wifely fidelity, spoke to him. ॥32॥
2.5.41.33: Tulasī said: O Viṣṇu, you have no compassion; your mind is like stone. By the violation of my wifely dharma my husband has surely been slain. ॥33॥
2.5.41.34: Since you are like stone, pitiless and wicked, therefore by my curse become now a stone in form. ॥34॥
2.5.41.35: Those who call you an ocean of compassion are deluded, no doubt. How was your devotee slain without any offence, for another's sake? ॥35॥
2.5.41.36: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this, Tulasī, the chaste beloved of Śaṅkhacūḍa, stricken with grief, wept bitterly and lamented again and again. ॥36॥
2.5.41.37: Then, seeing her weeping, Viṣṇu the Supreme Lord called to mind the god Śaṅkara, by whom the world is bewildered. ॥37॥
2.5.41.38: Then Śaṅkara, affectionate to his devotees, appeared; he was bowed to and humbly praised by Hari. ॥38॥
2.5.41.39: Seeing Hari overwhelmed with grief and his Śaṅkhacūḍa's beloved lamenting, Śiva consoled him and her with sound counsel, she being tender toward the afflicted. ॥39॥
2.5.41.40: Śaṅkara said: Do not weep, Tulasī, for a person reaps the fruit of his own actions. In this world, an ocean of karma, there is no one who gives happiness or sorrow to another. ॥40॥
2.5.41.41: Listen, free from sorrow, to what is now at hand; Hari too listens with a glad mind. What brings happiness to you both, that I declare for the sake of your happiness. ॥41॥
2.5.41.42: O good lady, penance was performed by you; this is the fruit of that very penance. How could it be otherwise? So it has come to pass in you. ॥42॥
2.5.41.43: Abandoning this body and assuming a divine body, delight forever with Hari; become equal to Ramā (Lakṣmī). ॥43॥
2.5.41.44: This body of yours, cast off, shall become a river here; in Bhārata, holy in form, it will be renowned as the Gaṇḍakī. ॥44॥
2.5.41.45: After some time, O great goddess, by my boon, Tulasī will become the chief means in the worship of the gods. ॥45॥
2.5.41.46: In heaven, in the mortal world and in the netherworld, abide near Hari. Become the Tulasī plant, O beautiful one, the best among flowers. ॥46॥
2.5.41.47: You, the presiding goddess of the plant, divine in form in Vaikuṇṭha, will forever sport in private together with Hari. ॥47॥
2.5.41.48: As the presiding goddess of the river, who bestows great merit in Bhārata, you will become the wife of the Salt Ocean, a portion of Hari. ॥48॥
2.5.41.49: And Hari, in the form of a rock, will take up his abode near the bank of the Gaṇḍakī in Bhārata, because of your curse. ॥49॥
2.5.41.50: There crores of fearsome insects with sharp teeth, boring into it, will make in its hollow its characteristic discus-mark. ॥50॥
2.5.41.51: That indeed is the Śālagrāma stone, extremely meritorious owing to that boring; according to the varieties of discus-marks it will be named Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa and so on. ॥51॥
2.5.41.52: The union of Viṣṇu's Śālagrāma stone with you, Tulasī, which is ever of matching form, greatly increases merit. ॥52॥
2.5.41.53: Whoever separates a Tulasī leaf from the Śālagrāma, O good lady, will in another birth suffer separation from his wife. ॥53॥
2.5.41.54: Whoever, setting aside the conch, separates a Tulasī leaf from it, he too will be without a wife and diseased for seven births. ॥54॥
2.5.41.55: The Śālagrāma, the Tulasī and the conch — the man of great wisdom who keeps them together in one place becomes dear to Śrī Hari. ॥55॥
2.5.41.56: You were the beloved of Śaṅkhacūḍa for the span of one manvantara; your separation from the conch is only a cause of grief to you. ॥56॥
2.5.41.57: Sanatkumāra said: Having spoken thus, Śaṅkara then declared there the greatness of the Śālagrāma stone and of Tulasī, which bestows much merit. ॥57॥
2.5.41.58: Then, having vanished after gladdening Hari and her, Śambhu — ever the giver of bliss to the good — went to his own abode. ॥58॥
2.5.41.59: Having heard these words of Śambhu, Tulasī became pleased; and abandoning that body, she assumed a divine form. ॥59॥
2.5.41.60: The Lord of Kamalā (Viṣṇu) went with her to Vaikuṇṭha, and at once the river Gaṇḍakī came into being, born from her body. ॥60॥
2.5.41.61: Acyuta too became a rock on its bank, bestowing merit on men; and there insects make holes of many kinds, O sage. ॥61॥
2.5.41.62: The stones that fall into the water there are extremely meritorious; those that stay on land are to be known as tawny (piṅgalā) and indeed lead to affliction. ॥62॥
2.5.41.63: Thus all has been told in accordance with your question: the merit-giving story of Śambhu, which grants men all their desires. ॥63॥
2.5.41.64: This holy narrative, blended with the greatness of Viṣṇu and granting enjoyment and liberation, has been narrated. What more do you wish to hear? ॥64॥
2.5.41.iti: Thus ends the forty-first adhyāya, named The description of Tulasī's curse, in the account of the slaying of Śaṅkhacūḍa, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥41॥
2.5.42.1: Nārada said: Having heard of the slaying of Śaṅkhacūḍa, the deed of the moon-crested Śiva, I am not yet satisfied hearing from you, just as a person is never sated having drunk nectar. ॥1॥
2.5.42.2: O Brahmā, tell me the deed of that great-souled Maheśa, who, resorting to māyā, performs noble sport that gives joy to his devotees. ॥2॥
2.5.42.3: Brahmā said: Having heard of the slaying of Śaṅkhacūḍa, Vyāsa, son of Satyavatī, asked about this very matter the son of Brahmā, the lord of sages. ॥3॥
2.5.42.4: Sanatkumāra, having highly praised the deed of Maheśa, which is the abode of auspiciousness, spoke to Vyāsa, son of Satyavatī. ॥4॥
2.5.42.5: Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O Vyāsa, to the auspicious deed of Maheśa: how Andhaka attained the leadership of the gaṇas of Śambhu, the Supreme Self, ॥5॥
2.5.42.6: having first fought a supreme battle with him, O lord of sages, and having propitiated that Maheśāna again and again through a pure (sāttvic) disposition. ॥6॥
2.5.42.7: Hear the wondrous greatness of Śambhu, protector of those who seek refuge, loving towards true devotees, who sports in many kinds of play. ॥7॥
2.5.42.8: Having heard this greatness of the bull-bannered one, the sage, son of Gandhavatī, bowing with devotion, spoke words of great import to that son of Brahmā, the chief of sages. ॥8॥
2.5.42.9: Vyāsa said: Who indeed is Andhaka, O Lord, O master of sages? In whose mighty lineage on earth was that great-souled, strong and foremost one born? Of what nature is Andhaka, and whose son? ॥9॥
2.5.42.10: Tell me all this today with its secrets, O son of Brahmā, out of your grace. For I have learned some of it well from Skanda, the son of Maheśa, of boundless understanding. ॥10॥
2.5.42.11: How did he attain the leadership of the gaṇas of Śambhu of supreme splendour? Exceedingly blessed indeed is that Andhaka who became a lord of gaṇas. ॥11॥
2.5.42.12: Brahmā said: Having heard this speech of Vyāsa, that son of Brahmā then narrated the deeds of Maheśvara, which bring supreme fortune, to the father of Śuka, who was eager to hear them. ॥12॥
2.5.42.13: Sanatkumāra said: Formerly that emperor of the immortals, bestower of grace on devotees, accompanied by the mountain's daughter and the gaṇas, desiring to sport, came from Kailāsa, his own mountain, to Kāśī. ॥13॥
2.5.42.14: Having made his capital there, he performed many deeds that gave happiness to the people; and having made the hero named Bhairava its protector, he sported together with the mountain-born Pārvatī. ॥14॥
2.5.42.15: Once he went to the mountain named Mandara, owing to the excellent power of the boon granted to it. There too, accompanied by Śivā, he sported abundantly with the chief heroes of various gaṇas. ॥15॥
2.5.42.16: Then, on the eastern side of the Mandara mountain, Pārvatī, staying there, playfully and in jest closed the eyes of the matted-haired one of fierce valour. ॥16॥
2.5.42.17: With her lotus-hands bearing the lustre of coral, gold and lotus, she closed his eyes. When Hara's eyes were closed, in an instant a very great darkness arose. ॥17॥
2.5.42.18: Through contact with Maheśvara's touch, the moisture of passion dripped from her hands; and on Śambhu's forehead, heated in a moment by the fire of his eye, a large drop of water issued forth. ॥18॥
2.5.42.19: Then it became an embryo and a being: with a dreadful face, terrifying, given to wrath, ungrateful, blind, misshapen, matted-haired, black, non-human, deformed, and thickly haired. ॥19॥
2.5.42.20: Singing, laughing, weeping, dancing, licking its lips, with a deep and dreadful roar — when that one of wondrous appearance was born, Bhava said to Gaurī with a smile: ॥20॥
2.5.42.21: Śrī Maheśa said: Having closed my eyes, you yourself did the deed; why then, beloved, do you fear this one? Gaurī, having heard these words from Hara, laughing, released his eyes. ॥21॥
2.5.42.22: When light had returned, the one of dreadful form, born from darkness, was still eyeless. Seeing that being of such a kind, Gaurī questioned Maheśa, the Supreme Person. ॥22॥
2.5.42.23: Gaurī said: Who is this misshapen one, O Lord, born before us, dreadful and terrifying? Tell me the truth: for what reason, or by whom, was he created, and whose son is he? ॥23॥
2.5.42.24: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of his beloved, Hara the sportive, maker of creation, smiling slightly, spoke about the blind form to the playful mother of the three worlds. ॥24॥
2.5.42.25: Maheśa said: Listen, Ambikā, doer of wondrous deeds: this one of wondrous, fierce valour has been born. When my eyes were closed by you, he was born of my sweat; his name is Andhaka. ॥25॥
2.5.42.26: You are his maker; he should be protected by you, together with your friends, with compassion, from the gaṇas, as befits. Regarding him as one with you, O noble lady, you should act with understanding. ॥26॥
2.5.42.27: Sanatkumāra said: Then Gaurī, having heard her husband's words, out of compassion, together with her friends, protected him by many and various means, as if he were her own son. ॥27॥
2.5.42.28: Then, at that time in the cool season, Hiraṇyanetra, desirous of a son, having seen the line of sons of his own elder brother, and urged by his wife, set out. ॥28॥
2.5.42.29: Resorting to the forest, the asura born of Kaśyapa then performed penance for a son, motionless like a log, having conquered the fault of anger, in order to behold Maheśvara. ॥29॥
2.5.42.30: Well pleased by his penance, the Pināka-bearer went to grant a boon, O best of the twice-born. Reaching that place, Maheśa, the bull-bannered, spoke to the foremost of the daityas. ॥30॥
2.5.42.31: Maheśa said: O lord of daityas, do not bring ruin on your senses. For what purpose have you undertaken this vow? Tell me your desire; I, Bhava, am the giver of boons. Whatever you wish, I will give it all. ॥31॥
2.5.42.32: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing Maheśa's gracious words, the daitya Kanakākṣa, exceedingly pleased, with joined palms and bowed head, having bowed to Girīśa and praised him in various ways, spoke: ॥32॥
2.5.42.33: Hiraṇyākṣa said: O moon-browed one, I have no son of great valour, befitting the race of the daityas. For that purpose I have undertaken this vow; grant me such a son of great valour, O lord of the gods. ॥33॥
2.5.42.34: Since my brother has five sons of boundless valour, headed by Prahlāda, while I here have none, I am without a line; who will seek to possess this kingdom of mine? ॥34॥
2.5.42.35: He who, having seized another's kingdom by his own strength, enjoys it, or enjoys his own kingdom, known to be his father's — he is called a son here and hereafter; through him that father too becomes one who has a son. ॥35॥
2.5.42.36: The upward course to heaven of those who have sons is declared by the wise, the best of the upholders of dharma. All beings strive thus for that very purpose; hence even beasts proceed so by their own nature. ॥36॥
2.5.42.37: For one without offspring there are no higher worlds; for that reason people seek sons from the gods; always worshipping the lotus-feet of the gods, they pray thus for even a single son. ॥37॥
2.5.42.38: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words of his, the compassionate Bhava, pleased with the daitya king, said to him: O lord of daityas, no son born of your own seed exists for you; but I shall give you a son. ॥38॥
2.5.42.39: My own son, named Andhaka, equal to you in valour and unconquered — choose him as your son; casting off all sorrow, accept that son yourself. ॥39॥
2.5.42.40: Having spoken thus, the great-souled Hara, pleased, accompanied by Gaurī, the lord of the bhūtas and other beings, the fierce enemy of Tripura, gave a son to Hiraṇyanetra. ॥40॥
2.5.42.41: Then that great-souled Daitya, having received the son from Hara, circumambulated him in due order, worshipped Rudra with many hymns, and, satisfied, went to his own kingdom. ॥41॥
2.5.42.42: Then, having obtained the son from Giriśa, the Daitya of fierce valour, after conquering all the gods without exception, carried this earth to Rasātala, his own realm. ॥42॥
2.5.42.43: Then Viṣṇu of infinite might, propitiated by the gods, sages and Siddhas, assumed the supreme boar form, all-pervading, made of sacrifice and terrifying. ॥43॥
2.5.42.44: Splitting the earth with various blows of his snout and entering the depths of Pātāla, he crushed the Daityas by hundreds with his snout and with his foremost, unbroken tusks, ॥44॥
2.5.42.45: and churning up the armies of the night-roamers with kicks shining like thunderbolts, afterwards he of wondrous fierce splendour, with the Sudarśana discus equal to ten million suns, ॥45॥
2.5.42.46: cut off the blazing head of Hiraṇyanetra and burnt up the wicked Daityas. Then, delighted, he there consecrated that Andhaka as king of the lords of the Diti-born. ॥46॥
2.5.42.47: Then the great-souled one, delighted, lifting up the earth from the depths of Pātāla with the tip of his tusk and bringing it to its own place, sustained the land and restored its former portion. ॥47॥
2.5.42.48: Praised by all the gods and the delighted sages, and by that Lotus-born Brahmā, Hari of fierce body, in the form of a boar, the accomplisher of the good task, went to his own world. ॥48॥
2.5.42.49: When Hiraṇyanetra, lord of the asuras, had thus been swiftly slain by the god in boar form, all the gods, all the sages and the other living beings became happy. ॥49॥
2.5.42.iti: Thus ends the forty-second adhyāya, named The slaying of Hiraṇyākṣa, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥42॥
2.5.43.1: Vyāsa said: O Sanatkumāra, all-knowing one, when that enemy of the gods had been slain, what did his elder brother, the great asura, do then? ॥1॥
2.5.43.2: O lord of sages, I have a curiosity here to hear this. Out of compassion, let me hear it, O son of Brahmā; salutation be to you. ॥2॥
2.5.43.3: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of Vyāsa, that lord of sages, Sanatkumāra, spoke, remembering the lotus-feet of Śiva. ॥3॥
