2.5.43.4: Sanatkumāra said: When his brother had thus been slain by Hari in the form of a boar, O Vyāsa, Hiraṇyakaśipu burned with anger and grief. ॥4॥
2.5.43.5: Then he commanded the heroic asuras, who loved slaughter, to carry out a slaughter of the people; for he delighted in enmity toward Hari. ॥5॥
2.5.43.6: Then those asuras, fond of slaughter, receiving their master's command on their heads, wrought slaughter among the subjects of the gods. ॥6॥
2.5.43.7: Then, when the world was harassed by those evil-minded asuras, the gods abandoned heaven and wandered on earth unnoticed. ॥7॥
2.5.43.8: Hiraṇyakaśipu, grieving, performed the hand-offered water libations and other rites for his departed brother, and consoled his wives and others. ॥8॥
2.5.43.9: Then that king of daitya kings wished to make himself invincible, free from old age and death, without rival, and sole ruler. ॥9॥
2.5.43.10: He performed an extremely severe austerity in a valley of Mandara, with arms raised, gaze fixed on the sky, resting on the earth only by his big toes. ॥10॥
2.5.43.11: While he was performing austerity, all the gods, endowed with strength, conquered all the daityas and regained their own places. ॥11॥
2.5.43.12: From his head arose a smoky fire born of austerity; spreading in every direction, it scorched the worlds across, above and below. ॥12॥
2.5.43.13: Scorched by it, the gods left heaven and went to Brahmaloka; with faces distorted by his austerity, they reported to the Creator. ॥13॥
2.5.43.14: Then, informed by those gods, O Vyāsa, the self-born Creator, surrounded by Bhṛgu, Dakṣa and others, went to the hermitage of the lord of the daityas. ॥14॥
2.5.43.15: Then he, who had scorched all the worlds, saw the lotus-born Brahmā who had arrived. Wishing to grant a boon, the Creator, the Grandfather, said to him: Choose a boon. Hearing the sweet speech of the Creator, he of undeluded intellect spoke these words thus. ॥15॥
2.5.43.16: Hiraṇyakaśipu said: O Lord, lord of creatures, Grandfather, O god, may I never have fear of death from the strikes of weapons, missiles, nooses, thunderbolts, dry trees, great mountains, water, fire or enemies, ॥16॥
2.5.43.17: from gods, daityas, sages, siddhas, or beings created by you — why many words? — in heaven or on earth, by day or by night, neither from above nor from below, O lord of creatures. ॥17॥
2.5.43.18: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing such words of his, the lotus-born Brahmā, full of compassion, mentally bowing to Viṣṇu, said to him: O lord of daityas, I am pleased; obtain everything. ॥18॥
2.5.43.19: Enough of your austerity, performed for ninety-six thousand years; your desires are fulfilled. Arise, rule the kingdom of the dānavas. Hearing these words, he became cheerful. ॥19॥
2.5.43.20: Consecrated to kingship by the great-grandfather, he set his mind on destroying the three worlds. Intoxicated with power, he abolished all dharmas and conquered all the gods in battle. ॥20॥
2.5.43.21: Then, out of fear, all the gods led by Indra, oppressed by the best of daityas, having received the Grandfather's instruction, went to the ocean of milk where Hari reclines. ॥21॥
2.5.43.22: They worshipped Viṣṇu intensely, praising him with words, regarding him as the giver of happiness; then each of them related all their own sorrow to the gracious lord. ॥22॥
2.5.43.23: Having heard all their sorrow, the lord of Ramā, pleased, granted them boons. Upendra, rising from that couch, with various words befitting himself, ॥23॥
2.5.43.24: having consoled all the gods and sages, he whose splendour equals fire said: I will forcibly slay the daitya, O lords of the gods; go, contented, to your own abodes. ॥24॥
2.5.43.25: Hearing the words of Ramā's lord, all those lords of the gods, Śakra and the rest, greatly pleased, went to their own abodes, considering the younger brother of Hiraṇyanetra as already slain, O lord of sages. ॥25॥
2.5.43.26: Assuming a form with matted mane, terrifying, with tusks for weapons, sharp claws and a fine nose, part lion and part man, with gaping mouth, resembling ten million suns, most dreadful, ॥26॥
2.5.43.27: with power equal to the fire at the end of the age, pervading the universe — why many words? — when the sun had set, that lord, the great soul, went forth and reached the city of the asuras. ॥27॥
2.5.43.28: Having fought with the mighty daityas, and having slain and seized those hosts of daityas, Nṛsiṃha of wondrous valour roamed there and crushed those asuras one after another. ॥28॥
2.5.43.29: He of incomparable might was seen by the daityas, and all of them likewise set upon him. Seeing that all-pervading lion, Prahlāda by name, son of the lord of Diti's sons, said to the king: This king of beasts pervades the universe; why has he come? ॥29॥
2.5.43.30: Prahlāda said: This is the Lord, the Infinite, who in the mere form of a man-lion has entered within your city. Turn back from battle and go for refuge; I see the dreadful form of the lion, ॥30॥
2.5.43.31: than whom there is no equal warrior even in the three worlds. Rule your kingdom bowing to the king of beasts. Hearing his son's words, the wicked one said to him: Are you afraid here, son? ॥31॥
2.5.43.32: Having spoken thus to his son, that king, overlord of Diti's sons, said to the bull-like daityas, the best of heroes: You heroes, seize this lion with the hideous frowning gaze. ॥32॥
2.5.43.33: At his command those best of daityas, wishing to seize him, rushed into the king of beasts; in a moment they were burnt, like moths eager to enter a fire out of longing for its form. ॥33॥
2.5.43.34: Even though the daityas had been burnt, the king of daityas fought with the lord of beasts using all weapons and likewise all missiles — spears, lances, nooses, goads, fire and the like. ॥34॥
2.5.43.35: While those two, weapons in hand, were fighting, a day of Brahmā passed, O Vyāsa — the two great heroes roaring at each other with heroic cries, their minds full of anger. ॥35॥
2.5.43.36: Then that daitya, suddenly creating many arms holding weapons, and eyeing the Nṛsiṃha form, rushed at the king of beasts, who was fighting, suddenly from all sides. ॥36॥
2.5.43.37: Then, having waged a fierce and most unbearable battle with all weapons and all missiles, the great chief of daityas, when these were exhausted, approached Nṛsiṃha holding a trident. ॥37॥
2.5.43.38: Then he was seized by the lord of beasts with many arms hard as mountains; placing him on his knee, between his arms, with claw-tips that pierce the vital points of dānavas, ॥38॥
2.5.43.39: and tearing out with the weapon of his claws the lotus of the heart, mixed with blood, the daitya departed from life in a moment. Then he was cast aside like a log, all his limbs crushed again and again. ॥39॥
2.5.43.40: When that enemy of the gods had been slain, Viṣṇu of wondrous valour, well pleased, addressed Prahlāda, who had bowed to him, consecrated him in the kingship, and then departed to his unfathomable abode. ॥40॥
2.5.43.41: Then all the lords of the gods, Brahmā and the others, overjoyed, bowed in that direction, O brahmin, to Viṣṇu, the adorable Lord who had accomplished his own task, and went to their own abodes. ॥41॥
2.5.43.42: Thus, in the course of the narrative, have been described the birth of Andhaka from Rudra, the death of Hiraṇyanetra at the hands of the Boar, the destruction of his brother by Nṛsiṃha, and Prahlāda's attainment of the kingship. ॥42॥
2.5.43.43: Now hear from me, O best of brahmins, of Andhaka's might obtained from the creator of the world, of his battle with Hara, and afterwards of his attaining the lordship of the gaṇas of Giriśa. ॥43॥
2.5.43.iti: Thus ends the forty-third adhyāya, named The description of the attainment of the lordship of the gaṇas, the birth of Andhaka, and the slaying of Hiraṇyanetra and Hiraṇyakaśipu, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥43॥
2.5.44.1: Sanatkumāra said: Then once, while Hiraṇyākṣa's son was at play together with those brothers of his, he was made to hear these words from them, who were jesting and blind with intoxication: O blind one, what business have you with the kingdom now? ॥1॥
2.5.44.2: Hiraṇyanetra was indeed a fool, who obtained you—quarrelsome, eyeless, deformed and ugly—by propitiating Giriśa with fierce austerities. ॥2॥
2.5.44.3: So you are surely no sharer in the kingdom; can even one born of another obtain the kingdom? Let this be considered by you yourself; it is we who are truly its sharers. ॥3॥
2.5.44.4: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard those words of theirs and reflected on them with his intellect, he, dejected, pacified them himself with various words and went at night to a deserted forest. ॥4॥
2.5.44.5: There he performed austerity for ten thousand years and repeated the prayer to be muttered, standing on one foot, without food, with arms raised in his vow—an austerity which could not be performed even by gods and demons. ॥5॥
2.5.44.6: Kindling a fire, he offered into it, for a whole year, the flesh of his limbs along with blood, cutting it from his body with a sharp weapon and offering it each day with mantras. ॥6॥
2.5.44.7: Then he was a corpse with only sinews and bones left, and all his blood was exhausted. When there was no flesh left on him, he wished to cast his very body into the fire. ॥7॥
2.5.44.8: Then he was seen by all the dwellers of heaven, who were greatly astonished and filled with fear. Thereupon the Creator, praised with hymns by the immortals, was very quickly propitiated. ॥8॥
2.5.44.9: Then the Grandsire, restraining him, said to him: Choose a boon now. Whatever you desire to obtain, even what is very hard to get in all the world, O Dānava, take it. ॥9॥
2.5.44.10: Hearing the words of the lotus-born one, the Daitya, humble and bowing, said: May those cruel ones by whom my kingdom was snatched away—Prahrāda and the others—become my servants. ॥10॥
2.5.44.11: Likewise, may I, the blind one, have divine sight; may Indra and the others pay me tribute. And may there be no death for me from gods, Daityas, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, serpents or humans, ॥11॥
2.5.44.12: or from Nārāyaṇa, the foe of the lords of Diti's sons, or from any being, or from Śarva who pervades all. Hearing those very dreadful words of his, the lotus-born one, greatly apprehensive, said to him: ॥12॥
2.5.44.13: Brahmā said: O lord of Daityas, all this shall come to pass; but accept also some cause of your death. For there is none, born or yet to be born, who has not entered the mouth of Death. ॥13॥
2.5.44.14: Let good men like you renounce the wish for an excessively long life. Hearing these conciliatory words from the Grandsire, the Daitya spoke again. ॥14॥
2.5.44.15: Andhaka said: Among the women who exist in the three times—the best, the middling and the lowest—there is one, a very jewel among them, who is ever like a mother even to me; ॥15॥
2.5.44.16: a woman unapproachable by body, speech and even mind, and hard to obtain in the world of men. If I desire her, may destruction come to me from my Daitya-lordship, O blessed Self-born one. ॥16॥
2.5.44.17: Hearing those words, the lotus-born one, greatly astonished, remembered the lotus feet of Śaṅkara; and quickly receiving Śambhu's command, he then spoke to Andhaka. ॥17॥
2.5.44.18: Brahmā said: O Daitya, the boons you long for—all of it shall be as your words desire. Rise, O lord of Daityas, obtain your wish, and ever wage war with heroes. ॥18॥
2.5.44.19: O lord of sages, hearing these words of the Ordainer, the son of Hāṭakanetra, reduced to sinews and bones, quickly bowed with devotion to that god, the lord of the worlds, and said to him: ॥19॥
2.5.44.20: Andhaka said: How, O lord, can I enter the enemy's forces and fight with this body? Make this frame of mere sinews and bones full of flesh; touch me now with your holy hand. ॥20॥
2.5.44.21: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing his words, the lotus-born one touched his body with his hand and went to his own abode together with the lords of the gods, being worshipped by hosts of sages and Siddhas. ॥21॥
2.5.44.22: As soon as he was touched, that king of Daityas became full-bodied and strong; with eyes come into being he became handsome, and, delighted, he thus entered his own city. ॥22॥
2.5.44.23: Then the Dānava lords headed by Prahlāda, yielding the whole kingdom to him and knowing that he had come having obtained a boon, became his obedient servants. ॥23॥
2.5.44.24: Then Andhaka, accompanied by his army and with his band of servants, went to conquer heaven; having vanquished all the gods in battle, he made the wielder of the thunderbolt pay him tribute. ॥24॥
2.5.44.25: He conquered in battles the Nāgas, the Suparṇas, the foremost Rākṣasas, Gandharvas, Yakṣas and humans as well, the lords of mountains and the trees, and all quadrupeds, lions and the rest. ॥25॥
2.5.44.26: He brought these three worlds, moving and unmoving, under his control, subjecting them to himself. Then, going to many thousands of agreeable and beautiful women— ॥26॥
2.5.44.27: the lovely damsels in Rasātala, on earth and in heaven—he, united with them, sported on other delightful mountains and riverbanks. ॥27॥
2.5.44.28: Sporting in their midst with great delight, that lord of Dānavas drank, for his enjoyment, divine and choice human drinks left over after they had drunk. ॥28॥
2.5.44.29: Obtaining other divine things full of flavour—fruits and fragrant flowers—vehicles with fine mounts, and excellent mansions built by Maya, ॥29॥
2.5.44.30: beautified with flowers, offerings, incense, food and unguents, and wondrous to behold—thus ten thousands of years passed here for Andhaka as he sported. ॥30॥
2.5.44.31: That foolish Andhaka, chief of Daityas, his mind blinded by pride and having taken to evil company, never knew anything good for the hereafter that would bring happiness to himself. ॥31॥
2.5.44.32: Then, intoxicated, overpowering all the chief sons with sophistical arguments, that mighty one roamed about with the Daityas, destroying all Vedic dharmas. ॥32॥
2.5.44.33: Overcome by the pride of wealth, he respected neither the Vedas nor the brāhmaṇas, nor the immortals nor his elders. Thus, under the sway of fate, his life-span doomed, he took his pleasure, spending his years in days of self-indulgence. ॥33॥
2.5.44.34: Then once, when many crores of years had passed on this earth, he, delighted, went with his army to Mount Mandara. ॥34॥
2.5.44.35: Seeing its golden splendour there, he, maddened with pride, roamed about with his armies; and having reached that king of mountains for sport, he, out of delusion, resolved to dwell there. ॥35॥
2.5.44.36: Having built there a splendid, strong city, the lord of Daityas stayed joyfully by his power; and again, step by step, he settled a most wondrous city on the slope of Mount Mandara. ॥36॥
2.5.44.37: Duryodhana, and the two named Vaidhasa and Hasti, were ministers of that best of Dānavas. Once, on a fair spot of the mountain, all three of them saw a beautiful woman. ॥37॥
2.5.44.38: Those swift chiefs of the Daityas, out of joy, quickly approached the great lord of Daityas, Andhaka, foremost of heroes, and all of them told him with great delight what they had seen. ॥38॥
2.5.44.39: The ministers said: O lord of Daityas, here in a cave we saw a certain sage with eyes closed in meditation, handsome, his crest marked by the crescent moon, with the hide of a great elephant tied round his waist; ॥39॥
2.5.44.40: his whole body encircled by the coils of great serpents, adorned with a garland of skulls, with matted hair; he holds a trident, bears arrows and quiver, has a mighty bow, and a rosary of beads displayed. ॥40॥
2.5.44.41: He bears a sword, a trident and a staff, has matted locks, is four-armed and of a very fair form. He is smeared with ash, shines with splendid radiance, is the foremost of ascetics, and his whole attire is wondrous. ॥41॥
2.5.44.42: Not far from him a man was also seen — monkey-like, terrible-faced and frightful, holding every weapon, rough-handed, standing on guard; and there was an old white bull. ॥42॥
2.5.44.43: And beside that seated ascetic a certain woman was seen — young, charming, of exquisite form, auspicious, a very jewel on earth. ॥43॥
2.5.44.44: Clad in coral, pearls, gems, gold, jewels and garments, beautifully embraced by garlands — whoever has seen her truly has eyes; what purpose is there here in seeing anything else? ॥44॥
2.5.44.45: That divine woman, worthy of a great lord, is the beloved wife of a meritorious sage. O lord of Daityas, enjoyer of fine jewels, having her properly brought here, she is fit to be seen by you. ॥45॥
2.5.44.46: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words of theirs, that Daitya, overcome by lust, all his limbs reeling, at once dispatched Duryodhana and the others to the sage's presence. ॥46॥
2.5.44.47: Having approached that immeasurable sage of great vows, those foremost ministers of his, skilled in sound royal policy, bowed to him, O lord of sages, and spoke the Daitya's command. ॥47॥
2.5.44.48: The ministers said: The great-souled son of Hiraṇyanetra, overlord of the Daityas, named Andhaka, lord of the three worlds, by the command of the Creator, is staying here today, delighting in pleasure. ॥48॥
2.5.44.49: We are indeed his ministers, his personal heroes, and have come near you. Sent by him, O ascetic, listen attentively to what he has said to you. ॥49॥
2.5.44.50: Whose son are you? Why are you sitting here at ease, O wise best of sages? Whose is this young, beautiful woman? This auspicious one should be given to the lord of Daityas, O chief of sages. ॥50॥
2.5.44.51: How does this body of yours, smeared with ash, deformed, adorned with a garland of skulls, go with quivers, fine bows, arrows, swords, bhuśuṇḍis, tridents, thunderbolts and javelins? ॥51॥
2.5.44.52: Where is the most holy Jāhnavī on the crest of your matted locks, and where this moon — or a fragment of corpse-bone? Where the long-mouthed serpent with poisonous fire, and where union with a full-breasted woman? ॥52॥
2.5.44.53: Riding an old bull is not commendable, and such an appearance does not befit one who is forbearing. Where is this dharma of twilight salutation, and where this kind of eating? This is contrary to the world. ॥53॥
2.5.44.54: Give the woman to me peacefully. What austerity are you practising with a woman, O deluded one? This is improper and unbecoming in you, since I am the lord of jewels in the three worlds. ॥54॥
2.5.44.55: As told by me today, cast off your weapons; afterwards practise only pure austerity. If you transgress my irresistible command, you will lose this entire body. ॥55॥
2.5.44.56: Considering Andhaka wicked, the supreme Maheśvara, adopting a worldly manner, having heard the whole speech of the messengers, spoke thus to the Daitya with a smile. ॥56॥
2.5.44.57: Śiva said: If I am Rudra, what is that to you from me? Why do you speak falsely like this? Hear my power, O lord of Daityas: it is not proper for you to speak words in this way. ॥57॥
2.5.44.58: I do not remember my own father anywhere, nor my mother — I, most ignorant and deformed. Within the cave I practise this terrible Pāśupata vow, practised by no other. ॥58॥
2.5.44.59: This rootlessness is well known in me; all this that I have is very hard to give up. This young, beautiful woman is my wife — all-enduring, the very accomplishment of the all-pervading one. ॥59॥
2.5.44.60: Now, whatever pleases you, take that indeed, O Rākṣasa. Having said this much, Śambhu in ascetic's guise fell silent before them. ॥60॥
2.5.44.61: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard this profound speech, those Dānavas bowed to him with their heads and then went to the son of the foremost Daitya, who had vowed the destruction of the three worlds. ॥61॥
2.5.44.62: Undaunted in spirit, they all bowed there to the infatuated king, the lord of Daityas, and, beginning with cries of victory, told him what Rudra had said with a smile. ॥62॥
2.5.44.63: The ministers said: A night-roamer of fickle valour and courage — where is such a Dānava, wretched and devoid of strength, cruel, ungrateful and ever sinful? Where is a Dānava who fears the son of the Sun (Yama)? ॥63॥
2.5.44.64: O king, you, lord of all Daityas, have been addressed with a laugh by that ascetic sage — surely a hero of great might, who by his own understanding regards the three worlds as a straw. ॥64॥
2.5.44.65: He said: Where am I, and where are dreadful weapons, and where battle that terrifies even Death? Where is the warrior resembling a monkey-face, a night-roamer with limbs worn out by old age? ॥65॥
2.5.44.66: Where is this one of fair form, and where the unfortunate one? Where is your strength, and where mere plants? If you are capable, strive to make war — then come and do something. ॥66॥
2.5.44.67: Here is a weapon like the thunderbolt, terrible, destroying those like you. Where is your body, soft as a lotus? Having considered thus, do what pleases you. ॥67॥
2.5.44.68: These and similar words, sir, were spoken by the ascetic, O lord of Dānavas. Battle with him here is not proper for you — so he told you, O king, smiling indeed. ॥68॥
2.5.44.69: If you understand through the many utterances we have spoken, seemingly empty of substance, well; otherwise you will later remember this speech of the sage, the ascetic endowed with austerities. ॥69॥
2.5.44.70: Sanatkumāra said: Then, having heard their words — true and beneficial, yet crooked and very sharp — that dull-witted one blazed with rage like fire sprinkled with ghee. ॥70॥
2.5.44.71: Seizing a sword, intoxicated by the boon, rushing like a fierce wind, pierced by Smara's arrows, he whose fate had turned adverse made ready to go there. ॥71॥
2.5.44.iti: Thus ends the forty-fourth adhyāya, named The dialogue of the messenger, in the account of Andhaka's attainment of the rank of lord of the gaṇas, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥44॥
2.5.45.1: Sanatkumāra said: Then he set out, moving like a rutting lord of elephants, having drunk liquor, his eyes rolling. He was mighty, accompanied by a large army, a fierce hero marching with excellent warriors. ॥1॥
2.5.45.2: Then the demon, pierced by the arrows of Smara (Kāma), saw the cave whose path was blocked by Vīraka, just as an insect called a moth, seeing an oil-fed wick-lamp, rushes towards it. ॥2॥
2.5.45.3: Thus, showing himself quickly again and again, though harassed by Vīraka, that deluded Andhaka, lord of the great demons, had his body thoroughly scorched by the fire of lust. ॥3॥
2.5.45.4: Though harassed by terrors of stones, trees, thunderbolts, water, fire, serpents, weapons and missiles, he could not be driven back again; and he was asked, who are you that have come here? ॥4॥
2.5.45.5: Hearing those words, he declared his intent to him, and then fought with Vīraka for a while, a wondrous and immeasurable fight; in battle the demon was defeated by the greater hero. ॥5॥
2.5.45.6: Then, abandoning the forefront of battle, his throat parched with hunger and thirsty, he went away; his fine sword shattered and himself exhausted, he fled, his pride gone. ॥6॥
2.5.45.7: Then the chief sons of Diti, led by Prahlāda, did battle with Vīraka; their minds driven by the goad of shame, they became very fierce, with many hundreds of weapons. ॥7॥
2.5.45.8: There Virocana fought, and Bali, and thousand-armed Bāṇa, Bhaji, Kujambha and Śambara, and the valiant ones beginning with Vṛtra. ॥8॥
2.5.45.9: Fighting, they were defeated on all sides and cut in two by the gaṇa Vīraka. When many Dānavas had been slain, the hosts of Siddhas proclaimed, he is victorious! ॥9॥
2.5.45.10: On that terrifying field, a mire of blood, where bheruṇḍa creatures were dancing about, amid fat, marrow, flesh and pus, crowded with throngs of flesh-eaters— ॥10॥
2.5.45.11: When the Daityas had been routed, the Lord Pinākin, having consoled Dākṣāyaṇī well, said to her: Beloved, the very dreadful great Pāśupata vow which was formerly performed by me— ॥11॥
2.5.45.12: Śiva said: Therefore that strength of mine has been lost, since the immortal falls through association with mortals. O Devī, through constant attachment to you day and night, a grip that destroys merit has arisen. ॥12॥
2.5.45.13: To produce again that divine, supremely wondrous power, going to an excellent and more dreadful place, I shall therefore practise a still more terrible vow. O beautiful one, be wholly fearless and free from sorrow. ॥13॥
2.5.45.14: Sanatkumāra said: Having spoken these words, the great-souled one, raising a sound, slowly set about it; going there, blazing fiercely with the vow, he went to a most holy and very dreadful forest. ॥14॥
2.5.45.15: —a vow such as could not be practised by gods or demons, lasting a full thousand years. Pārvatī, staying on Mount Mandara, awaiting Bhava's return— ॥15॥
2.5.45.16: —devoted to her husband, endowed with good conduct and virtues, alone and ever frightened, was overcome with grief inside the cave, guarded by her son Vīraka. ॥16॥
2.5.45.17: Then that demon, intoxicated by the boons granted to him, his composure shattered by the arrows born of Māra, came again to that cave together with those leading warriors. ॥17॥
2.5.45.18: There the enraged one, with his troops, giving up food, drink and sleep, fought a most wondrous battle with Vīraka, night and day, for five hundred and five days. ॥18॥
2.5.45.19: With swords, spears and bhindipālas, with maces and bhuśuṇḍīs, with great shafts, arrows, fierce crescent-headed arrows, span-long darts and blazing tortoise-headed missiles, ॥19॥
2.5.45.20: with the finest iron arrows, sharp tridents, axes, lances and hammers, swords, iron balls, mountains and trees, and divine chariot-weapons, assailed by the hosts of Daityas— ॥20॥
2.5.45.21: Lustreless, his body pierced, he fell; the entrance of the cave was entirely covered by those weapons hurled by the Daityas' arms, and afterwards he lay unconscious at the cave's mouth. ॥21॥
2.5.45.22: Vīraka was covered by all the Daityas with nets of missiles for a moment, and it was impossible to uncover him. Seeing the very dreadful sons of Diti, the Devī— ॥22॥
2.5.45.23: —out of fear, the Devī, together with her companions, called to mind the Grandsire and Viṣṇu; staying inside the cave, she also caused the entire army of my best of heroes to be called to mind. ॥23॥
2.5.45.24: As soon as she remembered them, Brahmā and Lord Viṣṇu, bearing female forms, together with all the Indras and their troops, assuming female forms, arrived. ॥24॥
2.5.45.25: Having become women, they then entered the interior of the cave of the daughter of the king of mountains, along with the hosts of great sages of great power, the Siddhas, Nāgas and Guhyakas. ॥25॥
2.5.45.26: Because entry of men into the inner apartments of those seated on royal thrones is forbidden, they therefore displayed thousands, indeed countless numbers, of shapely women— ॥26॥
2.5.45.27: —showing divine and greatly wondrous forms to Gaurī in the cave, the delighted women, together with the noble Vīraka, entered the inner cave of the mountain-king's daughter, the maiden of the king of mountains. ॥27॥
2.5.45.28: By the many thousands and hundreds of women, kettledrums bestowing victory in battle resounded with a roar like the clouds at the end of an aeon, and fine conches were blown by the shapely women. ॥28॥
2.5.45.29: Casting off his swoon, Vīraka, of wondrous and fierce valour, standing in front, seized the weapons of the great chariot-warriors and with those very weapons slew the sons of Diti. ॥29॥
2.5.45.30: Then Brāhmī, staff in hand, opposed them; Gaurī too, her mind seized by anger; and Nārāyaṇī, bearing conch, mace, fine discus and bow, her staff-like arms full— ॥30॥
2.5.45.31: —went forth; another went forth with plough and staff in hand, with sky-like locks, gold-coloured; then Baiḍaujasī (Aindrī), thunderbolt in hand, of fierce speed, teeming with thousands of streams, ॥31॥
2.5.45.32: thousand-eyed, steadfast in battle, very hard to conquer, unassailable by hundreds of Daityas; the power of Vaiśvānara (Agni), with a fierce face; and the fierce Yāmyā, her hand raised with a staff. ॥32॥
2.5.45.33: Nairṛtī, with a dreadful bow, her hand raised with a very sharp sword, came forward; Toyālikā (Vāruṇī), noose in hand, went forth eager for battle. ॥33॥
2.5.45.34: And the goddess born of the fierce wind, her body gaunt as hunger, goad in hand; and she who sprang from Dhanada (Kubera), taking in her hand a mace like the fire at the end of an aeon— ॥34॥
2.5.45.35: —Yakṣeśvarī, sharp-faced, misshapen, with claws for weapons, terrifying even to serpents: these and other goddesses by the hundreds went forth to the crowded battlefield. ॥35॥
2.5.45.36: Seeing that endless army, the goddesses turned pale, greatly astonished, agitated and startled with fear, dejected at heart. ॥36॥
2.5.45.37: Composing their minds, all those wives of the gods, headed by the Śakti of Brahmā, with the full approval of the daughter of the mountain-lord, made Vīraka the commander, a hero of very dreadful valour. ॥37॥
2.5.45.38: The chief sons of Diti, resolving in their minds on either retreat or their own death, waged a great, unprecedented battle; others, emboldened by their boons, fought with the women. ॥38॥
2.5.45.39: Then Gaurī, together with her companions, fought a most wondrous battle there, having made Vīraka, of dreadful valour and wondrous skill of mind, commander in the battle. ॥39॥
2.5.45.40: The king, son of Hiraṇyanetra, skilled in action, quickly formed a great battle-array, very dreadful, named Gila (the Swallower), having taken Viṣṇu into account and observed Yāmyā. ॥40॥
2.5.45.41: When, through the performance of the rite, his face had been made terrible, the Lord Kṛttivāsas (clad in a hide) came, angry, spread with a radiance like that of a thousand fearsome suns at the end of a kalpa. ॥41॥
2.5.45.42: Then, when a mere thousand years had passed, seeing Maheśvara arrived, the women, greatly delighted, fought an exceedingly great battle together with Vīraka. ॥42॥
2.5.45.43: Gaurī bowed with her head to Giriśa and, displaying the very great valour of her husband, joyful Gaurī joined in the fighting. Then Hara, the daughter of the king of mountains… ॥43॥
2.5.45.44: …taking her by the neck, entered the cave; the thousands of women were dismissed. Gaurī too, having honoured them with hundreds of marks of respect, Śiva stationed Vīraka alone at the mouth of the cave. ॥44॥
2.5.45.45: Then the lord of the asuras, skilled in policy, not seeing Gaurī and Giriśa, quickly sent his own messenger named Vidhasa into Śiva's presence. ॥45॥
2.5.45.46: He, whose limbs had been battered in that battle by the various blows hurled by the hosts of gods, entered, bowed his head to Śambhu, and spoke words proud and fierce. ॥46॥
2.5.45.47: The messenger said: Sent by him, I have entered the cave. This Andhaka has spoken this message to you: You have no business at all with a woman; release the young, beautiful woman. ॥47॥
2.5.45.48: You are, for the most part, an ascetic; so keep to that. I put up with the lovely one being inside with you, thinking, a sage is not to be opposed. But you are no sage, O ascetic—you are an enemy. ॥48॥
2.5.45.49: You are an exceedingly great foe of the daityas. Fight with me at once; having crushed you, O roguish ascetic, I shall lead you to Yama's abode, which is like the depths of Pātāla. ॥49॥
2.5.45.50: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words from the messenger's mouth, the skull-garlanded one—the great three-eyed one, refuge of the good, destroyer of the pride of the wicked—blazing with vexation, spoke to him in anger. ॥50॥
2.5.45.51: Śiva said: Your speech is plain and very fierce; the truth has been spoken. Go quickly. Make war on me by force, if indeed you are capable through strength. ॥51॥
2.5.45.52: For one who is powerless on earth, what use are wives or very charming riches? Let the daityas, drunk with strength, come; having considered thus, I have done this. ॥52॥
2.5.45.53: For the powerless, whence even the sustenance of the body? Let them do whatever is ordained for them; and whatever is to be done by me, that I shall do—there is no doubt about this. ॥53॥
2.5.45.54: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words from Hara, Vighasa too went out, delighted; then, roaring and uttering huṃ sounds, he proceeded to the presence of the lord of the daityas. ॥54॥
2.5.45.iti: Thus ends the forty-fifth adhyāya, named The description of the start of the battle and the dialogue of the messenger, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥45॥
2.5.46.1: Sanatkumāra said: And that king of the Daityas, who understood his intention, quickly took up a mace and, with his army, then put in front the one named Gila, exceedingly fierce and impenetrable even by the foremost gods. ॥1॥
2.5.46.2: Reaching the mouth of Maheśvara's cave, he broke it open with weapons blazing like thunderbolts. Then some showered weapons on Vīraka himself, and others likewise on the Mountain's Daughter. ॥2॥
2.5.46.3: Some broke the beautiful gate; they destroyed flowers and leaves, fruits, roots and the pleasant water, and even tore up the garden paths. ॥3॥
2.5.46.4: Some, delighted, churned up the shining peaks of the mountain. Then Hara, the trident-bearer, angered, remembered his own army, summoning it. ॥4॥
2.5.46.5: He summoned other most fearsome beings too, and the gods with their armies, headed by Viṣṇu. As soon as called, the attendants came with their armies, with chariots, elephants, horses, bulls and cows, ॥5॥
2.5.46.6: with camels, donkeys, excellent birds and lions—all those gods with hosts of Bhūtas—with tigers, deer, boars and cranes, with fishes and with dolphins foremost, ॥6॥
2.5.46.7: and with other hosts of creatures of many kinds, with broken-fanged ones, with burst-open cremation grounds, with serpents, hundreds of Pretas and Piśācas, with divine aerial cars and with lotus-ponds, ॥7॥
2.5.46.8: with rivers and streams and with mountains as mounts—having assembled, with joined palms they bowed to Kapardin and stood there with undaunted spirit, having made Vīraka the commander. ॥8॥
2.5.46.9: Then the Pināka-bearer sent forth to battle the gods, whose mounts had rested, with Vīraka as chief, steadfast in battle and victorious; and they, dispatched by Maheśvara, ॥9॥
2.5.46.10: all waged a battle like the end of an age, without bounds, ever dreadful, against Gila and the army of the Daitya lord; but in the fight the gods were swallowed in his fury. ॥10॥
2.5.46.11: At that moment all who were fighting, headed by Brahmā, Indra, Viṣṇu, the Sun and the Moon, were swallowed by that Vighasa; when the army had been swallowed, only Vīraka remained. ॥11॥
2.5.46.12: Leaving the battlefront, entering that cave and bowing his head to Śarva, the valiant Vīraka, best of speakers, stricken with grief, then told the Enemy of Smara what had happened. ॥12॥
2.5.46.13: O Lord, your army has today been swallowed by the Daitya Vighasa; swallowed is Viṣṇu, teacher of the three worlds, crusher of Daityas; swallowed are the Moon and the Sun, and Druhiṇa and Maghavan, the boon-givers; swallowed are they all—Yama, Varuṇa, Vāyu and Dhanada. ॥13॥
2.5.46.14: I alone remain, bowed before you; what should I do here? The Daitya lord, joyful at heart and accompanied by Daityas, is unconquerable. ॥14॥
2.5.46.15: Having come to you, the unconquerable, he is of fearsome mind and swift as the wind. The god Viṣṇu himself, out of devotion, tore Kanakakaśipu, son of Kaśyapa, with sharp nails; even so the Lord, obedient to the righteous, set forth—may he, with gaping mouth, blow away the filth of the three worlds. ॥15॥
2.5.46.16: He was cursed by Vasiṣṭha and the others, the seven sages, lords of the world: You shall again be thus for a very long time, together with the Daityas. ॥16॥
2.5.46.17: Then they were addressed by him with affectionate words beneficial to himself: When, O best of sages, will my release from this terrible state come? Whereupon the angry ones said: At the time of battle, after the swallowing by Vighasa, when your mouth is split by terrible arrows and by fists, ॥17॥
2.5.46.18: then in the forest called Badarī, in Hari's abode, a holy dwelling, restraining yourself and freed of sin, you will go to the Supreme. Then, because of their words, this swallower of Daityas, tormented by hunger, roams daily from battle, again delighted with joy. ॥18॥
2.5.46.19: And this terrible darkness covers the world despite the risen Sun and Moon. Likewise Śukra, your supreme enemy, exceedingly harmful, by the words of the hymn of the immortal-making lore, makes the Daityas slain by the gods again vigourous and joyful, freed of hundreds of wounds. ॥19॥
2.5.46.20: Better that I give up my life for you at the time of battle; you, chosen by me, are witness even for a moment in the doing of this task. ॥20॥
2.5.46.21: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing this from his good son, the Lord of the Pramathas, angered, meditated long, and the Lord of the three worlds first created an incomparable chant called Pragāyat-sāma, with a body shaped like the rays of the sun; then, by laughter (prahāsa), by that name, the darkness was destroyed by it. ॥21॥
2.5.46.22: When this world was lit up, the sage Vīraka again waged a great battle with the distorted-faced Daityas—he who was born of the eminent sage who had eaten stone-dust, and who formerly, having waged battle, had conquered even the city. ॥22॥
2.5.46.23: That great Rudra was at once swallowed outright by the Daitya. Then that Nandin, with sharp arrows, spear and sword, chief of warriors, great even among hundreds of eminent sages, abode of learning, endowed with calm, self-control and great fortitude— ॥23॥
2.5.46.24: Seeing this, the Lord Kapardin then mounted the excellent bull, eager for battle, facing the Daitya Vighasa, and muttering a divine mantra that makes the swallowed be disgorged, stood ready, having made ready his bow and arrows like thunderbolts. ॥24॥
2.5.46.25: Then the sage Vīraka came out from Vighasa's mouth, bringing all his own matchless forces; all were disgorged, with Viṣṇu—the Lotus-born, the Enemy of Bala, the Moon and the Sun; and that army, delighted, again waged a great battle. ॥25॥
2.5.46.26: When he had been defeated, and Śukra thereafter, by the power of his lore, again revived the Daityas slain in battle, then that preceptor of the Dānavas was bound and brought like a beast by the Gaṇas to the Lord of beings, and swallowed by him, the Enemy of Tripura. ॥26॥
2.5.46.27: When the one called Śukra had vanished, that whole abode of the gods' enemies was conquered, destroyed, broken and utterly shattered by the gods, and by vast hosts of Bhūtas relishing the devouring of Daitya corpses, with headless trunks dancing, hands raised holding sharp arrows and spears, ॥27॥
2.5.46.28: by frenzied Vetālas, by birds with very strong talons and beaks, by wolves of many kinds with mouths full of mouthfuls of corpse-flesh—when the battlefield was thus strewn, the descendant in the line of Kanakakaśipu, having fought long, was defeated by Hari, Hara and Mahendra. ॥28॥
2.5.46.29: When the Daityas had fled into Pātāla and likewise into the caves of mountains and oceans, and the army was depleted, the bull among Daityas, the mighty Andhaka—bringer of slaughter, crusher of the world, in the wrath of the gods—had his pride shattered by Hari with terrible blows of the mace. ॥29॥
2.5.46.30: He who never abandons battle, since he had obtained a boon—then, his body tormented by terrible blows from the Lord of the gods, he quickly defeated the gods with floods of weapons and missiles, trees, mountains and waters, roaring loudly and slowly challenging the Lord of the Pramathas. ॥30॥
2.5.46.31: He stood fighting with many kinds of weapons fallen on the battlefield; when all these were spent, he then assailed Girijā and Rudra, likewise with trees, serpents, masses of thunderbolts, showers of weapons, grotesque illusions and hundreds of deceitful Śambara-like contrivances. ॥31॥
2.5.46.32: To conquer the Lord of the mountain he devised yet another trick there—the hero of great might, equal to the Enemy of Tripura, intelligent, not to be slain by the gods, overpowered by the madness of mind born of hundreds of boons; but the Daitya at once had his body battered by abundant weapons and missiles. ॥32॥
2.5.46.33: From the oozing of his blood, the field became pervaded by hosts of Andhakas sprung on the ground, dreadful, distorted-faced, resembling himself; he was most fiercely pierced on the trident by the Lord of beings, the Enemy of Tripura, whose form was like the fire at the end of a kalpa. ॥33॥
2.5.46.34: When from the army slain by Paśupati another army arose, from the very hot drops issuing from his flesh and springing from his wounds, then the wise Viṣṇu, through yoga, having called on the Lord of the Pramathas, created a fierce, invincible female form with a distorted face. ॥34॥
2.5.46.35: a form dreadful and emaciated; and the Lord, angry, overspread with many creeper-like arms, came forth from the ear at the head of Śambhu's Gaṇas. ॥35॥
2.5.46.36: That goddess, standing on the battlefield, the earth adorned by her pair of feet, praised by all the gods, her mind then urged on by the Lord, tormented by hunger, drank up that army issuing from the Daitya and that blood, very hot, and the mire of gore at the battlefront, completely. ॥36॥
2.5.46.37: Then the lone Daitya, even with his blood dried up, fought Giriśa with terrible palm-blows like thunderbolts, with knees and feet, with nails like vajras, with mouth, arms and heads, remembering the eternal, unborn warrior's duty enjoined for his own clan. ॥37॥
2.5.46.38: Afterwards, subdued in battle, his heart pierced by the Lord of the Pramathas, impaled on the trident and held up in the sky like a post, his lower body dried up, his frame wasted by the sun's rays, his body drenched by clouds with downpours and winds, ॥38॥
2.5.46.39: shrivelled by the fierce-rayed sun, then broken into pieces like flakes of frost—even in that state the bull among Daityas did not give up his life. Then Śambhu, that ocean of supreme compassion, being pleased and praised by him, lovingly granted him the rank of a lord of Gaṇas. ॥39॥
2.5.46.40: Then, at the end of the battle, the lords of the worlds with their consorts, having duly worshipped the Lord of the Pramathas with hymns of many kinds—Hari, Brahmā and the others—praised him abundantly with supreme eulogies, their shoulders bowed, delighted and happy, crying out, victory, victory! ॥40॥
2.5.46.41: Hara, delighted, stayed with those gaṇas in a cave of the best of mountains. He dismissed some of his own portions and honoured the good gaṇas with various offerings. Then, having gained the joyful daughter of the best of mountains, and likewise the sinless son freed from the terrible devouring mouth, he issued his commands and engaged in play. ॥41॥
2.5.46.iti: Thus ends the forty-sixth adhyāya, named The description of the battle with Andhaka, in the account of the slaying of Andhaka, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥46॥
2.5.47.1: Vyāsa said: In that great battle, terrible and hair-raising, Śukra, the learned master of the Daityas, was swallowed by the enemy of Tripura Śiva. ॥1॥
2.5.47.2: This I have heard in brief; tell it again in detail. What did that great yogin do while he was in the belly of the Pināka-bearer? ॥2॥
2.5.47.3: How did the fire of Śambhu's belly—the burner at the end of the kalpa, Time itself—not burn that Śukra, though Bhārgava too was of blazing energy? ॥3॥
2.5.47.4: How did the wise one come out of the cage of Śambhu's belly? How, and for how long, did that Bhārgava worship him? ॥4॥
2.5.47.5: And how did he obtain that supreme lore which quells death? What is that supreme lore, dear one, by which death is warded off? ॥5॥
2.5.47.6: How did Andhaka, released from the trident, obtain the leadership of the Gaṇas of Śambhu, the god of gods, the sage who sports in play? ॥6॥
2.5.47.7: O greatly wise one, be gracious and narrate all this fully to me, who am listening, dear one—the nectar of Śiva's sport. ॥7॥
2.5.47.8: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of Vyāsa of boundless splendour, Sanatkumāra spoke, remembering the lotus-feet of Śiva. ॥8॥
2.5.47.9: Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O Vyāsa of great intellect, to the supreme nectar of Śiva's sport. You are blessed, you are foremost among Śaivas, and of yourself you give me joy. ॥9॥
2.5.47.10: While the battle was going on between those two, Śaṅkara and Andhaka, the lords of the impenetrable thunderbolt-array and of the mountain-array, ॥10॥
2.5.47.11: at first victory went to the mighty Daityas; then, O sage, through Śiva's power, victory came to the Pramathas. ॥11॥
2.5.47.12: Hearing that, the great Daitya Andhakāsura became dejected, and he became absorbed in thinking, how may I win? ॥12॥
2.5.47.13: Then the heroic Andhaka, of keen intellect, withdrew from the battle and quickly went alone into Śukra's presence. ॥13॥
2.5.47.14: Getting down from his chariot and bowing to his own guru Kāvya, he, most expert in policy, then reflected and spoke this with joined palms. ॥14॥
2.5.47.15: Andhaka said: O lord, relying on you we hold you in the regard due to a guru; we are never defeated but always victorious. ॥15॥
2.5.47.16: Through your power we have always regarded all the gods with their followers—even those headed by Hara and Upendra—as mere blades of grass. ॥16॥
2.5.47.17: By your grace the gods then fear us, as elephants fear lions and as serpents fear Garuḍas. ॥17॥
2.5.47.18: By your grace the Daityas and Dānavas, scattering the whole army of the Pramathas, entered the impenetrable thunderbolt-array. ॥18॥
2.5.47.19: Having you as our refuge, O Bhārgava, we always stand firm like cattle under their herdsman and move about fearlessly even in battle. ॥19॥
2.5.47.20: Protect, protect on all sides, O brahmin, coming forth, the asuras who have sought refuge in you, harassed by heroic enemies—and even the dead. ॥20॥
2.5.47.21: See my excellent troops, Huṇḍa and others, overrun by the foremost Pramathas of terrible valour, crushers of death itself, slain and fallen. ॥21॥
2.5.47.22: You who long ago, drinking the smoke of chaff for a thousand years, obtained the excellent lore—its time has now come. ॥22॥
2.5.47.23: Today, O Bhārgava, let all the Pramathas see that fruit of the lore of yours, as you mercifully revive all the asuras. ॥23॥
2.5.47.24: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing Andhaka's words thus, the steadfast Bhārgava then reflected with an anguished mind: ॥24॥
2.5.47.25: What should I do now? How may it go well for me? The procedure of reviving those slain in combat is wholly unfitting for me. ॥25॥
2.5.47.26: This lore was obtained from Śaṅkara; should I then employ it against his Gaṇas—to revive those crushed in battle by the heroic Pramathas, Śaṅkara's followers? ॥26॥
2.5.47.27: Yet the duty toward those who seek refuge is supreme above all. Having reflected thus with heart and intellect, Śukra then accepted his words. ॥27॥
2.5.47.28: Then, smiling slightly, Bhārgava, remembering Śiva's lotus-feet with a composed mind, spoke to the lord of the Dānavas. ॥28॥
2.5.47.29: Śukra said: What you have said, dear one, is all true indeed. I acquired this lore for the sake of the Dānavas. ॥29॥
2.5.47.30: Having drunk the unbearable smoke of chaff for a thousand years, I obtained this lore from the Lord; it ever brings happiness to kinsmen. ॥30॥
2.5.47.31: With this lore I shall raise up the Daityas crushed by the Pramathas in battle, as a cloud revives withered crops. ॥31॥
2.5.47.32: In this very moment you will see those Daityas of yours risen up, free of wounds, free of pain, healthy, as if risen again from sleep. ॥32॥
2.5.47.33: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this to Andhaka, the sage Śukra recited the lore, directing it at each Daitya one by one, reverently remembering the Lord of the lore. ॥33॥
2.5.47.34: By the mere recitation of the lore, all those heroic Daityas and Dānavas rose up at once, weapons in hand, as if from sleep, ॥34॥
2.5.47.35: as Vedas constantly practised come forth, or as clouds rise in their season, or as wealth given with faith to brahmins returns in a time of distress. ॥35॥
2.5.47.36: Seeing those great asuras, Huṇḍa and the others, revived, all the asuras roared like clouds full of water. ॥36॥
2.5.47.37: Of great strength and valour, fearless, they were again ready for battle with the Pramathas, roaring dreadful roars. ॥37॥
2.5.47.38: Seeing the Daityas and Dānavas revived by Śukra, all the Pramathas, Nandin and the others, fierce in battle, were then astonished. ॥38॥
2.5.47.39: This whole deed must be reported thus to Śaṅkara, lord of the gods—having considered, the wise ones spoke thus to one another. ॥39॥
2.5.47.40: While that wondrous sacrifice of battle of the lords of the Pramathas was going on thus, Śilāda's son Nandin, indignant at seeing Bhārgava's deed, went to Maheśa. ॥40॥
2.5.47.41: Having said, victory, Nandin spoke to the fierce source of victory (Śiva), who is bright like gold: O God, the battle-deed of the lords of the gaṇas, which is difficult even for the gods together with Indra— ॥41॥
2.5.47.42: that deed of ours Bhārgava (Śukra) has today made futile, O Lord, for he has revived those slain enemies, playfully reciting the vidyā that gives life to the dead, aiming it at each one. ॥42॥
2.5.47.43: The great demon-chiefs Tuhuṇḍa, Huṇḍa and the rest, Kumbha, Jambha, Vipāka, Pāka and others, having returned today from Yama's abode, roam about routing the Pramathas. ॥43॥
2.5.47.44: If he revives here again and again those excellent Daityas who have been struck down, how will victory be ours, O Maheśa? How indeed will there be peace for the lords of the gaṇas? ॥44॥
2.5.47.45: Sanatkumāra said: Thus addressed by Nandin, the lord of the Pramathas, the God who is Lord over the lords of the Pramathas, laughing, then spoke to Nandin, king of all the gaṇa-lords. ॥45॥
2.5.47.46: Śiva said: Nandin, go with the utmost speed, and from the midst of the sons of Diti seize that best of the chief Brahmins and bring him quickly here, as a hawk seizes a young quail. ॥46॥
2.5.47.47: Sanatkumāra said: Thus addressed by the bull-bannered Śiva, Nandin roared with a roar like a bull's or a lion's, and plunging into the army he went quickly to where the lamp of Bhṛgu's lineage was. ॥47॥
2.5.47.48: Though Kāvya (Śukra) was guarded by all the sons of Diti, holding nooses, swords, trees, stones and rocks in their hands, the mighty Nandin, throwing the Daityas into turmoil, carried him off, as a śarabha carries off an elephant. ॥48॥
2.5.47.49: The enemies of the gods followed him, seized by the mighty one, his garments slipping, his ornaments fallen, his hair loosened, as if meaning to free him, sending forth lion-like roars. ॥49॥
2.5.47.50: The Dānava chiefs poured upon Nandīśvara a fierce rain of thunderbolts, tridents, swords and axes, of raised staffs, discuses, stones and kampanas, like rain-clouds. ॥50॥
2.5.47.51: The sovereign of the gaṇas, having got hold of Bhārgava and burnt hundreds of weapons with the fire of his mouth, came to Bhava's side while the battle of asuras and gods raged on, having distressed the enemy side. ॥51॥
2.5.47.52: Here is that Śukra, O Lord — thus he quickly reported to Bhava. And the God of gods took Śukra like an offering presented by a pure devotee. ॥52॥
2.5.47.53: Saying nothing, the protector of beings threw the chief of sages (Śukra) into his mouth like a fruit. All those asuras raised a loud cry of lament, crying ha ha ha again and again. ॥53॥
2.5.47.iti: Thus ends the forty-seventh adhyāya, named The swallowing of Śukra, in the war with Andhaka, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥47॥
2.5.48.1: Vyāsa said: When Śukra had been swallowed by Rudra, what did the Dānavas do, those great heroes whose lord was Andhaka? Tell me the truth, O great sage. ॥1॥
2.5.48.2: Sanatkumāra said: When Kāvya had been swallowed by the Lord of Girijā, the Daityas became bereft of the hope of victory, like lordly elephants deprived of their trunks, and like bulls without horns, ॥2॥
2.5.48.3: like masses of bodies without heads, like twice-born men lacking Vedic study, like hosts of living beings without effort, and like efforts devoid of good fortune, ॥3॥
2.5.48.4: like women bereft of their husbands, like flocks of birds without wings, like life-spans devoid of merit, like Vedic learning devoid of observances, ॥4॥
2.5.48.5: as multitudes of rites become void of their fruits without the one power of divine glory, as kṣatriyas without valour, and just as the whole body of dharma without truth. ॥5॥
2.5.48.6: With Śukra carried off by Nandin and swallowed by the Poison-eater, the Daityas, though striving in the festival of battle, fell into despair. ॥6॥
2.5.48.7: Seeing them disheartened, Andhaka, of great steadfastness and valour, addressed the Daityas Huṇḍa, Huṇḍa and the others. ॥7॥
2.5.48.8: Andhaka said: We have been tricked by Nandin, who carried off Kavi by force. Surely today the life-breaths of all of us have been separated from our bodies. ॥8॥
2.5.48.9: Courage, vigour, recourse, fame, strength, splendour, valour — all has been taken from us at once, now that the one Bhārgava has been taken. ॥9॥
2.5.48.10: Shame on us, by whom the one revered by our race, the best of our race, our all-capable preceptor and protector, was not protected in his calamity! ॥10॥
2.5.48.11: Therefore, O heroes, without delay fight here with the enemies, those heroic Pramathas, remembering the lotus-feet of our preceptor. ॥11॥
2.5.48.12: Remembering the bliss-giving lotus-feet of our preceptor Kāvya, I shall slay all the Pramathas along with Nandin. ॥12॥
2.5.48.13: Today, having slain these helpless ones together with the gods and Vāsava, I shall free Bhārgava, as a yogin frees the soul from karma. ॥13॥
2.5.48.14: Or else that yogin, the master himself, the protector of what remains of us, may by his yoga come out of his body. ॥14॥
2.5.48.15: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of Andhaka, the Dānavas, roaring like clouds, pitiless and resolved to die, spoke as they faced the Pramathas: ॥15॥
2.5.48.16: If our life-span still holds, the Pramathas can never overpower us by force; if our life-span is not to last, what is gained by going off and abandoning our master in battle? ॥16॥
2.5.48.17: Those men, rich in high honour, who go away from here abandoning their master, surely go to the abode Andhatāmisra. ॥17॥
2.5.48.18: Having greatly sullied their renown with the darkness of infamy, those routed on the battlefield would be happy neither here nor hereafter. ॥18॥
2.5.48.19: What use are gifts, what use austerities, what use bathing in sacred fords, if there is bathing in the holy ford of the battleground, which removes the impurity of rebirth? ॥19॥
2.5.48.20: Having thus resolved upon those words, the Daityas and Danujas churned the Pramathas in battle, sounding the war-drum. ॥20॥
2.5.48.21: There, with masses of arrows, swords and thunderbolts, with hard missiles made of stone, with bhuśuṇḍis and bhindipālas, with spears, javelins and axes, ॥21॥
2.5.48.22: with khaṭvāṅgas, paṭṭiśas, tridents, cudgels and maces, striking one another fiercely, they wrought a great slaughter. ॥22॥
2.5.48.23: There arose the sound of drawn bows, of falling arrows, of bhindipālas and bhuśuṇḍis, and of war-cries. ॥23॥
2.5.48.24: With the blare of war-instruments, the many trumpetings of elephants and the neighing of horses, there was a great uproar. ॥24॥
2.5.48.25: The space between heaven and earth was filled with the tremendous noise; the fearless and the fearful alike had their hair standing on end. ॥25॥
2.5.48.26: The armies, filled with the loud, distinct cries of elephants and horses, with banners and flags broken, with weapons spent, ॥26॥
2.5.48.27: variegated with gushing blood, bereft of horses, elephants and chariots, and thirsty — the armies on both sides swooned. ॥27॥
2.5.48.28: Then those heroic Pramathas, led by Nandin, struck down all the Asuras with their might and won victory, O sage. ॥28॥
2.5.48.29: Seeing his army being shattered here and there by the Pramathas, Andhaka himself mounted his chariot and rushed at the Gaṇas. ॥29॥
2.5.48.30: By those missiles hurled in torrents of arrows, the Pramathas perished like mountains under thunderbolt strikes, and vanished like clouds emptied of water. ॥30॥
2.5.48.31: Looking at each one, whether going or coming, far or near, Andhaka pierced him with arrows as numerous as his hairs. ॥31॥
2.5.48.32: Seeing the army being shattered by the mighty Andhaka, Skanda, Vināyaka, Nandin, Somanandin and others, ॥32॥
2.5.48.33: mighty, heroic Pramathas, Śaṅkara's own Gaṇas, of great strength, grew angry and waged a wondrous battle. ॥33॥
2.5.48.34: By Vināyaka, by Skanda, by Nandin, by Somanandin, by the heroic Naigameya, by the mighty Vaiśākha, ॥34॥
2.5.48.35: and by these and other fierce Gaṇas, who rained down streams of tridents, spears and floods of arrows, even Andhaka was made blind. ॥35॥
2.5.48.36: Then a tumult arose between the armies of the Pramathas and the Asuras. At that great sound, Śukra, who was within Śambhu's belly, ॥36॥
2.5.48.37: seeking an opening, wandered about homeless like the wind, and beheld within Rudra's body the seven worlds along with the Pātālas, ॥37॥
2.5.48.38: the wondrous realms of Brahmā, Nārāyaṇa and Indra, along with those of the Ādityas and Apsarases, and the battle of the Pramathas and Asuras. ॥38॥
2.5.48.39: Wandering all around in Bhava's belly for a hundred years, he found no opening in it, just as a wicked man finds no flaw in a pure one. ॥39॥
2.5.48.40: Then Bhārgava, through the Śāmbhava yoga, in the form of semen, having recited this excellent mantra, emerged from the cage of Śambhu's belly. ॥40॥
2.5.48.41: He came out by the path of the liṅga and then bowed to Śiva. Gaurī took him as a son, and he was thereby made free of obstacles by the Goddess. ॥41॥
2.5.48.42: Then, seeing Kāvya the Bhārgava, who had come out by the path of semen, Maheśāna, the treasure-house of compassion, laughed and said: ॥42॥
2.5.48.43: Maheśvara said: Since you have come forth like semen from my liṅga, O delight of Bhṛgu, by that deed you are Śukra; you are my son. Go now. ॥43॥
2.5.48.44: Sanatkumāra said: Thus addressed by the god, Śukra, whose radiance was like the sun's, bowed again to Śiva and, with joined palms, praised him. ॥44॥
2.5.48.45: Śukra said: You have endless feet and endless forms, endless heads; you are the Ender and Śiva; you have endless arms. How shall I, bowing with my head, praise one such as you, who are worthy of praise? ॥45॥
2.5.48.46: You are the eight-formed one, you are the one of endless forms; you are the giver of what is desired to all gods and asuras, and the crusher of the one with evil gaze. How shall I praise one such as you, who are worthy of praise? ॥46॥
2.5.48.47: Sanatkumāra said: Having thus praised Śiva, Śukra bowed again and, at Śiva's command, entered the army of the Dānavas, as the moon enters a garland of clouds. ॥47॥
2.5.48.48: Thus has been told the swallowing of Kavi by Śaṅkara in battle. Now hear also that mantra which was recited by Kavi in Śambhu's belly. ॥48॥
2.5.48.iti: Thus ends the forty-eighth adhyāya, named The swallowing of Śukra, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥48॥
2.5.49.0: Sanatkumāra said: Om, salutation to you: to the Lord of the gods, revered by gods and asuras; to the Great God of past and future; to him whose eyes are green and tawny; to Strength; to him whose form is intellect; to him clad in a tiger-skin garment; to Āraṇeya; to the source of the three worlds; to the Lord; to Hara; to him whose eyes are like Hari's; to him who brings the end of the ages; to Fire; to the lord of the gaṇas; to the guardian of the worlds; to the great-armed, the great-handed; to the trident-bearer; to him with great fangs; to Time; to Maheśvara; to the Imperishable; to him whose form is Time; to the blue-necked; to the great-bellied; to the chief of the gaṇas; to the Self of all; to the creator of all; to the all-pervading; to the slayer of Death; to Pāriyātra-Suvrata; to the celibate; to him who has reached the end of the Veda; to him who has reached the end of austerity; to Paśupati; to Vyaṅga; to him with the trident in hand; to him whose banner is the bull; to Hari; to the one with matted hair; to the one with the crest-lock; to the staff-bearer; to the greatly famed; to the lord of beings; to the cave-dweller; to him who has the lute, the drum and the cymbal; to the Immortal; to the one fair to behold; to him who shines like the rising sun; to the dweller in the cremation ground; to the Blessed One; to Umā's lord; to the subduer of foes; to him who struck out Bhaga's eyes; to the destroyer of Pūṣan's teeth; to the doer of fierce deeds; to him with the noose in hand; to the time of dissolution; to him with a meteor-like face; to him whose banner is fire; to the sage; to the blazing one; to the lord of the people; to the uplifter; to the begetter; to the Fourth; to the best in the worlds; to Vāmadeva; to him who is gracious in speech; to the mendicant on the left side; to him whose form is a mendicant; to the one with matted hair, himself matted-haired; to him who paralysed Śakra's arm; to the restrainer of the Vasus; to the sacrifice; to the maker of sacrifice; to Time; to the wise; to the maker of honey; to the moving one; to the lord of trees; to him worshipped in the Vājasaneya and in all the āśramas; to the sustainer of the world; to the maker of the world; to the Person; to the eternal; to the steadfast; to the overseer of dharma; to him of the three paths; to the producer of beings; to the three-eyed; to the many-formed; to him whose splendour equals ten thousand suns; to the God; to him who sounds all instruments; to him who frees from all afflictions; to the binder; to the bearer of all; to the highest dharma; to Puṣpadanta; to the undivided; to the Face; to the remover of all; to Hiraṇyaśravas; to the door-keeper; to the terrible one; to him of terrible valour: Om, salutation, salutation.
2.5.49.1: Having repeated this excellent mantra, Śukra came out of the cage of Śiva's belly by the path of the liṅga, like Śambhu's potent semen. ॥1॥
2.5.49.2: He was taken by Gaurī as a son; then he was made by the Lord of the universe ageless, immortal and glorious, like a second Śaṅkara. ॥2॥
2.5.49.3: When three thousand years had passed on earth, Śukra, the sage who was a treasury of the Vedas, was born again from Maheśvara. ॥3॥
2.5.49.4: He saw Andhaka on the trident, utterly dried up, the lord of the Dānavas, full of fortitude, an ascetic, meditating on the Supreme Lord — ॥4॥
2.5.49.5: meditating on Mahādeva, the odd-eyed, who wears the half-moon as his crest, the nectar, the eternal, the steadfast pillar, the blue-throated, the bearer of Pināka; ॥5॥
2.5.49.6: the bull-eyed, the greatly-to-be-known, the Person, the giver of all desires, the enemy of Kāma, the burner of Kāma, who takes forms at will, the one with braided hair; ॥6॥
2.5.49.7: the many-formed, Giriśa, the terrible, garlanded, wearing red garments, the yogin, the burner of Time, the destroyer of Tripura, the skull-bearer; ॥7॥
2.5.49.8: of hidden vows, of secret mantra, profound, reached through devotion, the support of the powers beginning with aṇimā, the giver of sovereignty over the three worlds; ॥8॥
2.5.49.9: the hero, the slayer of heroes, the fierce, the deformed, the stout, the skilful, the great eater of flesh, the frenzied, Bhairava, indeed Maheśvara; ॥9॥
2.5.49.10: who makes the three worlds flee, the eager one, the hunter, the destroyer of the sacrifice, accompanied by the son of the Kṛttikās, the frenzied, clad in a hide; ॥10॥
2.5.49.11: wearing an elephant-hide, agitated, adorned with serpents, the giver of support, the Vetāla, the fierce, worshipped by Śākinīs; ॥11॥
2.5.49.12: Aghora, the slayer of fierce Daityas, of terrible roar, the lord of trees, with ash-smeared limbs, matted-haired, pure, served by hundreds of Bheruṇḍa birds; ॥12॥
2.5.49.13: the lord of beings, the master of beings, abiding in the five elements, moving in the sky, wrathful, harsh, fierce, the lord of Caṇḍī, dear to Caṇḍikā; ॥13॥
2.5.49.14: the fierce, the lofty, the winged one, ever partaking of liquor, the one who licks the worlds, the very dreadful, Death, beyond the reach of death; ॥14॥
2.5.49.15: the death of Death, the great commander, dwelling in cremation grounds and forests, passion, dispassion, blind with passion, worshipped by hundreds who are free of passion; ॥15॥
2.5.49.16: sattva, rajas, tamas, dharma and adharma, the younger brother of Vāsava, truth and untruth, of the form of being and of non-being, without cause; ॥16॥
2.5.49.17: the Lord who is half woman, the sun, with the splendour of hundreds of crores of suns, the sacrifice, the lord of sacrifice, Rudra, Īśāna, the giver of boons, Śiva. ॥17॥
2.5.49.18: These are the hundred and eight forms of Śiva, the Supreme Self; meditating on them, the Dānava was freed from that great fear. ॥18॥
2.5.49.19: He was bathed by Kapardin with a divine shower of nectar; released by the pleased Lord, he was lowered from the tip of that trident. ॥19॥
2.5.49.20: Then that great Daitya, the asura Andhaka, was addressed by Maheśāna with conciliation; all this was done by the great-souled one. ॥20॥
2.5.49.21: Īśvara said: O lord of the Daityas, I am pleased with your restraint and observance, with your valour and your fortitude; choose a boon, O you of good vows. ॥21॥
2.5.49.22: I have been constantly worshipped by you, and you are cleansed of all sins; I am the giver of boons and you are worthy of a boon, O best among the great lords of Daityas. ॥22॥
2.5.49.23: Whatever fruit of merit is yours from sustaining your life through three thousand years, by that may you have bliss. ॥23॥
2.5.49.24: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing this, Andhaka, trembling, with joined palms, placing both knees on the ground, spoke to the Blessed Lord of Umā. ॥24॥
2.5.49.25: Andhaka said: O Lord, you who are higher than the highest — what you were called by me earlier on the battlefield, now I, wretched and lowly, address you with a voice faltering with joy. ॥25॥
2.5.49.26: Whatever deeds, condemned in the worlds, I did through delusion, not knowing you — all that, O Lord, do not keep in your mind. ॥26॥
2.5.49.27: And whatever wrong I did toward Pārvatī through the fault of lust, forgive it, O Mahādeva; I am pitiable and deeply afflicted. ॥27॥
2.5.49.28: Compassion should always be shown by you to one who is afflicted, especially to one who is pitiable, wretched and full of devotion. ॥28॥
2.5.49.29: Such am I, wretched and devoted, come to you for refuge; protection should be granted to me — here I have joined my palms. ॥29॥
2.5.49.30: May this Goddess, Mother of the world, be fully pleased with me; abandoning all anger, may she look upon me graciously. ॥30॥
2.5.49.31: Where is her anger, and where am I, a pitiable Daitya, O moon-crested one? I cannot endure it, O you with the half-moon as diadem, O Śambhu, O Maheśvara. ॥31॥
2.5.49.32: Where are you, supremely generous, and where am I, made helpless by faults such as lust and anger, and likewise by old age and death? ॥32॥
2.5.49.33: This son of yours, Vīraka, skilled in battle and very mighty — seeing me pitiable, may he not yield to anger. ॥33॥
2.5.49.34: May I always behold Pārvatī as my mother, with reverence due to an elder — she whose hue is like frost, a pearl necklace, the cool-rayed moon, the conch and the jasmine. ॥34॥
2.5.49.35: Ever devoted to you both, free from enmity with the gods, may I dwell together with the gaṇas, tranquil in spirit, contemplating yoga. ॥35॥
2.5.49.36: May I not again recall my hostile birth as a Dānava; by your grace, O Maheśāna, grant this supreme boon. ॥36॥
2.5.49.37: Sanatkumāra said: Having spoken these words, the lord of the Daityas fell silent, meditating on the three-eyed God and gazing at Pārvatī, his mother. ॥37॥
2.5.49.38: Then, looked upon by Rudra with a gracious eye, he remembered his former history and his wondrous birth. ॥38॥
2.5.49.39: When that history was remembered, his desire was fulfilled; bowing to his mother and father, he then became one who had accomplished his purpose. ॥39॥
2.5.49.40: Smelled on the head in affection by Pārvatī and by the wise Śaṅkara, he thus obtained what he desired from the pleased one who bears the crescent moon as his crest-ornament. ॥40॥
2.5.49.41: All this ancient account of Andhaka's attaining the chieftainship of the gaṇas through the grace of Mahādeva, which bestows supreme happiness, has been narrated to you. ॥41॥
2.5.49.42: And the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra, destroyer of death, has been told; it should be recited with diligence, for it grants the fruit of all desires. ॥42॥
2.5.49.iti: Thus ends the forty-ninth adhyāya, named The hosts of Andhaka regain life, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥49॥
2.5.50.1: Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O Vyāsa, to how the supreme knowledge (vidyā) that quells death was obtained by the sage Kāvya from Śiva, who is called Mṛtyuñjaya. ॥1॥
2.5.50.2: Long ago this descendant of Bhṛgu went to the city of Vārāṇasī and performed austerities for a long time, meditating on the Lord Viśveśvara. ॥2॥
2.5.50.3: Right there he installed a liṅga of Śambhu, the Supreme Self, and in front of it, O Vedavyāsa, he made a very lovely well. ॥3॥
2.5.50.4: With great effort he bathed the Lord of gods a hundred thousand times with the five nectars, each measuring a droṇa, and abundantly with fragrant bathing waters. ॥4॥
2.5.50.5: A thousand times, with great love, he anointed the Lord of gods with sandal paste and yakṣakardama, following fragrant unguent-rubbings. ॥5॥
2.5.50.6: With rājacampaka and dhattūra flowers, with karavīra and lotuses, with mālatī and karṇikāra, with kadamba, bakula and blue lotuses, ॥6॥
2.5.50.7: with mallikā and śatapatrī, with sindhuvāra along with kiṃśuka, with bandhūka flowers, punnāga, and nāgakeśara stamens, ॥7॥
2.5.50.8: with navamallī and cibilika, with kunda along with mucukunda, with mandāra and bilva leaves, with droṇa, marubaka and bṛka, with granthiparṇa and damanaka, and with lovely mango shoots, ॥8॥
2.5.50.9: with tulasī, devagandhārī, bṛhatpatrī and kuśa sprouts, with nandyāvarta and agastya, and with deodars together with śāla, ॥9॥
2.5.50.10: with kāñcanāra and kurabaka, with dūrvā sprouts and kuruṇṭaka — with each of these flowers and with other shoots as well, ॥10॥
2.5.50.11: and with leaves and thousand-petalled lotuses, lovely, of many kinds and auspicious — attentively and with great love he worshipped Śaṅkara. ॥11॥
2.5.50.12: With offerings of song and dance, praising him abundantly with hymns, with the thousand names and with other hymns, he extolled Śaṅkara. ॥12॥
2.5.50.13: Thus for five thousand years Śukra worshipped Maheśvara, the great Lord, by rites of many kinds. ॥13॥
2.5.50.14: When he did not see the god inclined in the least to grant a boon, he then took up another vow, terrible and extremely hard to endure. ॥14॥
2.5.50.15: Having thoroughly and repeatedly washed away, with the waters of contemplation, the great impurity called fickleness from his mind together with the senses, ॥15॥
2.5.50.16: and having made that jewel of a mind stainless and offered it to the Pināka-bearer, Kavi drank streams of smoke-particles for a thousand years. ॥16॥
2.5.50.17: Seeing Kāvya, firm of mind, performing such terrible austerity, Maheśvara became pleased with the Bhārgava. ॥17॥
2.5.50.18: Emerging from that liṅga, with splendour surpassing a thousand suns, Virūpākṣa, the very husband of Dākṣāyaṇī, spoke to him. ॥18॥
2.5.50.19: Maheśvara said: O treasure of austerity, O greatly fortunate one, son of Bhṛgu, great sage, by this austerity of yours I am ever and especially pleased. ॥19॥
2.5.50.20: Choose as a boon all that your mind desires, O Bhārgava. With love I shall grant all your wishes; there is nothing that cannot be given to you. ॥20॥
2.5.50.21: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of Śambhu, an excellent offer bringing great joy, Kavi was delighted, immersed in an ocean of happiness. ॥21॥
2.5.50.22: His body covered with hair standing on end from the welling flood of bliss, the lotus-eyed brahmin joyfully bowed to Śambhu. ॥22॥
2.5.50.23: Delighted, with the corners of his eyes wide open, placing his folded hands on his head and saying, victory, victory, he praised the eight-bodied one. ॥23॥
2.5.50.24: Bhārgava said: Overpowering all darkness with these rays of yours, you bring to an end the cherished designs of the night-roamers. You blaze in the sky, O jewel of heaven, for the welfare of the three worlds, O Lord of the world — therefore obeisance to you. ॥24॥
2.5.50.25: In the world, beyond all measure, with boundless great splendours you shine on earth and in the sky, eye of all the worlds; you who have driven away all darkness, most excellent one, O cool-rayed moon, filled with floods of nectar — therefore obeisance to you. ॥25॥
2.5.50.26: You are ever the motion on the purifying path, and worthy of worship. Who lives here without you, O life of the worlds? By you, the wind — which when stilled destroys and when moving nourishes all creatures — they are gladdened; O all-pervading one, obeisance to you. ॥26॥
2.5.50.27: O sole purifier of the universe, protector of those who bow, O you whose unique power is fire, without you there is no immortal divine rite for the dead; how would the world breathe? O inner Self of the world, you are fire, granting peace at every step — obeisance to you. ॥27॥
2.5.50.28: O you in the form of water, Supreme Lord, purifier of the world — wondrously you are surely the maker of wondrous good conduct. This universe indeed becomes pure and stainless, O Lord of the universe, through bathing in water; hence I bow. ॥28॥
2.5.50.29: O you in the form of space, by giving room outside and within, this universe here expands, O Lord; from you, O compassionate one, it ever breathes, and by its nature it contracts into you — therefore I bow to you. ॥29॥
2.5.50.30: O you whose self is the earth, you bear the universe here, O all-pervading one. Who other than you, O Lord of the universe, is the foe of darkness? Such as you are, destroy my darkness, O serpent-adorned one, beyond all praise, higher than the highest — therefore I bow to you. ॥30॥
2.5.50.31: O you whose nature is the Self, this world in the form of the moving and unmoving is pervaded by these successions of your forms, O Hara. O you who dwell as the inner Self of all, whose form is in every form, I, your devotee, ever bow, O Supreme Self, O eight-formed one. ॥31॥
2.5.50.32: Thus, joined with these eight forms, O friend of the friendless, you indeed make all this, O you whose form benefits all people; this universe is spread out and widely extended by you, O guide of the prostrate, O supreme goal of the whole host of aims — therefore I bow. ॥32॥
2.5.50.33: Sanatkumāra said: Having thus praised Bharga with this octad on the eight forms, the Bhārgava bowed again and again, his head touching the ground. ॥33॥
2.5.50.34: Thus praised by the exceedingly radiant Bhārgava, Mahādeva lifted that prostrate brahmin from the ground, holding him with his two arms, ॥34॥
2.5.50.35: and spoke with great affection in a gentle voice deep as the rumble of clouds, lighting up the spaces between the directions with the radiance of his teeth. ॥35॥
2.5.50.36: Mahādeva said: O best of brahmins, Kavi, dear one, you are my pure devotee. By this extremely fierce austerity and by conduct befitting your lineage, ॥36॥
2.5.50.37: by the merit of installing the liṅga and by worshipping the liṅga, by the pure and unwavering offering of your mind, ॥37॥
2.5.50.38: and by your holy conduct in the great sacred field of Avimukta, I look upon you with compassion; there is nothing that cannot be given to you. ॥38॥
2.5.50.39: In this very body, having entered the cavern of my belly, you will attain birth as my son by way of my excellent organ. ॥39॥
2.5.50.40: Today I grant you a boon hard to obtain even for my attendants, which I have for the most part guarded even from Hari and Hiraṇyagarbha. ॥40॥
2.5.50.41: The pure lore of mine named Mṛtasañjīvanī, the reviver of the dead, was fashioned by me alone through great power of austerity. ॥41॥
2.5.50.42: Today I grant you that lore in the form of a mantra, O most pure one. You are worthy of that lore, O treasure of pure austerity. ॥42॥
2.5.50.43: Whoever it may be for whom you repeat this lore, the best among the lords of knowledge, with self-restraint, he will truly and surely come back to life. ॥43॥
2.5.50.44: Your splendour will surpass the sun and surpass fire, and in the sky you will be a blazing star. Be the foremost of the planets. ॥44॥
2.5.50.45: Moreover, women or men who undertake a journey facing you—through the fall of your gaze all their undertakings will come to ruin. ॥45॥
2.5.50.46: When you have risen, O one of good vows, marriages and the like, and all religious rites of people here, will bear fruit. ॥46॥
2.5.50.47: And all the lunar days, the Nandā tithis, will be auspicious through conjunction with you. Your devotees will be abundant in vigour (śukra) and have many offspring. ॥47॥
2.5.50.48: This liṅga established by you, called Śukreśa—those men who worship it will attain success. ॥48॥
2.5.50.49: Those who for a whole year, day after day, are devoted to the nakta vow, eating only at night, and who on your day, having performed all water rites at the Śukra well, ॥49॥
2.5.50.50: will worship Śukreśa—hear what their fruit is: those mortals will have unfailing seed, will have sons, and be of abundant virility, ॥50॥
2.5.50.51: they will be endowed with manliness and good fortune, no doubt. All those people will be possessed of learning and partakers of happiness. ॥51॥
2.5.50.52: Having thus granted the boons, the god merged into that liṅga there. Bhārgava too, his mind content, went to his own abode. ॥52॥
2.5.50.53: Thus I have told you, O Vyāsa, how the lore called Mṛtyuñjaya was obtained through the power of austerity. What else do you wish to hear? ॥53॥
2.5.50.iti: Thus ends the fiftieth adhyāya, named The obtaining of the Mṛtasañjīvinī lore, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥50॥
2.5.51.1: Vyāsa said: O Sanatkumāra, all-knowing one, out of your kindness and affection you have let me hear a wonderful and excellent story, full of Śambhu's grace. ॥1॥
2.5.51.2: Now I wish to hear the deeds of the moon-crested Śiva: how he lovingly granted the leadership of his Gaṇas to Bāṇāsura. ॥2॥
2.5.51.3: Sanatkumāra said: Listen attentively, O Vyāsa, to that story of Śambhu, the Supreme Self: how he lovingly granted the leadership of the Gaṇas to Bāṇāsura. ॥3॥
2.5.51.4: In this very story is the noble deed of Śaṅkara, the great Lord; and here too is the battle of Śambhu, who was showing favour to Bāṇa, with Kṛṣṇa. ॥4॥
2.5.51.5: Hear from me the fitting, supreme and most meritorious legend connected with Śiva's sport, which brings delight to the mind and the ears. ॥5॥
2.5.51.6: There was a sage of great intellect, Marīci, son of Brahmā, born of his mind, the eldest and best among all his sons, a Prajāpati. ॥6॥
2.5.51.7: His son was the great-souled Kaśyapa, best of sages, who greatly increased creation and was exceedingly devoted to his father and to Vidhi Brahmā as well. ॥7॥
2.5.51.8: O Vyāsa, that sage Kaśyapa had thirteen wives, daughters of Dakṣa, well-mannered and devoted to their husband. ॥8॥
