2.5.51.9: Among them the eldest was Diti; the Daityas are known as her sons. From the other wives were born sons — the gods and others, together with the moving and unmoving beings. ॥9॥
2.5.51.10: The eldest, Diti, had two first-born sons of great strength: Hiraṇyakaśipu the elder, and after him his younger brother Hiraṇyākṣa. ॥10॥
2.5.51.11: Hiraṇyakaśipu had four sons, foremost among Daityas: Hrāda, Anuhrāda, Saṃhrāda and Prahrāda, in that order. ॥11॥
2.5.51.12: Among them Prahrāda was great, a devotee of Viṣṇu, master of his senses; none of the Daityas were able to destroy him. ॥12॥
2.5.51.13: His son was Virocana, the best of great givers, who gave his own head to Śakra when he came begging in the guise of a brahmin. ॥13॥
2.5.51.14: His son was Bali, a great giver, dear to Śiva, by whom the earth was given to Hari in the form of Vāmana. ॥14॥
2.5.51.15: His own son was Bāṇa, who became a devotee of Śiva: honoured, generous, wise, true to his word, a giver of thousands. ॥15॥
2.5.51.16: Long ago that lord of Asuras, dwelling in the city called Śoṇita, ruled a kingdom, having conquered by force the three worlds and their rulers. ॥16॥
2.5.51.17: By Śaṅkara's grace, the immortals became like servants to that Bāṇāsura, the devotee of Śiva. ॥17॥
2.5.51.18: In his kingdom, apart from the immortals, the subjects were not unhappy; the gods were distressed because of rivalry, being followers of another dharma. ॥18॥
2.5.51.19: Once that great Asura pleased Maheśvara with the Tāṇḍava dance, accompanied by music played with his thousand arms. ॥19॥
2.5.51.20: Delighted by that dance, Śaṅkara, loving to his devotees, became very gracious and looked at him with a compassionate glance. ॥20॥
2.5.51.21: The Lord, ruler of all worlds, the refuge, granter of devotees' wishes, invited that great Asura, son of Bali, to choose a boon. ॥21॥
2.5.51.22: Sanatkumāra said: That great Daitya Bāṇa, son of Bali, best of devotees and wise, bowed to Śaṅkara with devotion and praised the Supreme Lord. ॥22॥
2.5.51.23: Bāṇāsura said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, loving to those who seek refuge, O Maheśāna, O all-pervading one, if you are pleased with me, ॥23॥
2.5.51.24: be my protector always, staying near me as lord of my city; O Lord, be in every way a source of joy to me, together with your son and your Gaṇas. ॥24॥
2.5.51.25: Sanatkumāra said: That Bāṇa, son of Bali, deluded by Śiva's māyā, asked this of Maheśāna, the giver of liberation, who is surely hard to propitiate. ॥25॥
2.5.51.26: Śambhu, loving to his devotees, granted him those boons, and the Lord lovingly dwelt there accordingly, with his Gaṇas and his son. ॥26॥
2.5.51.27: Once, in Bāṇa's city, Hara sported together with gods and Asuras on the lovely bank of the river named Śoṇitaka. ॥27॥
2.5.51.28: The Gandharvas and Apsarases danced and laughed; the sages muttered prayers, bowed, worshipped him and praised him. ॥28॥
2.5.51.29: All the Pramathas leapt about, the seers offered oblations, hosts of Siddhas arrived and beheld Śaṅkara's delight. ॥29॥
2.5.51.30: False logicians perished, as did barbarians and enemies; the Mothers stood facing him, and terrors vanished. ॥30॥
2.5.51.31: The faults of worldly existence left those who were devoted to Rudra in true sincerity; when he was seen, all beings attained supreme joy. ॥31॥
2.5.51.32: Seeing the playful gestures of the women, the sages and Siddhas frolicked; and the seasons too displayed their full power there. ॥32॥
2.5.51.33: Gentle breezes blew, grey with flower pollen, and flocks of birds, greedy for nectar, sang in the trees. ॥33॥
2.5.51.34: And on trees bowed down under the weight of flowers, cuckoos kept calling sweetly, arousing love, in the forests and groves. ॥34॥
2.5.51.35: Then, during that playful sport, the one crested with the crescent moon, intoxicated and touched by unsubdued desire, spoke to Nandin. ॥35॥
2.5.51.36: Candraśekhara said: Bring my beloved Gaurī from Kailāsa, adorned; go quickly from this forest, tell her, and bring the fair one here. ॥36॥
2.5.51.37: Sanatkumāra said: He agreed, saying so be it, went there, and, as Śaṅkara's confidential messenger, bowing deeply with joined palms, spoke to Pārvatī. ॥37॥
2.5.51.38: Nandīśvara said: O Goddess, Maheśvara, God of gods, wishes to see you, his beloved, adorned in beauty; I have spoken at his command. ॥38॥
2.5.51.39: Sanatkumāra said: Then, O best of sages, at his words Gaurī, wholly devoted to her vow of fidelity to her husband, eagerly set about adorning herself. ॥39॥
2.5.51.40: I am coming. Go to the Lord and tell him so at my bidding. Then Nandin, swift as thought, came back to Rudra's side. ॥40॥
2.5.51.41: Then Rudra, intensely agitated by desire, again said to Nandin: Go once more, dear one, and quickly bring Pārvatī. ॥41॥
2.5.51.42: Saying very well, he went to her and said to the lovely-eyed Gaurī: Your husband wishes to see you, charming and fully adorned. ॥42॥
2.5.51.43: O Goddess, Śaṅkara is waiting eagerly to sport with you in many ways. Since your husband is thus sorely afflicted by desire, please go, O daughter of the mountain. ॥43॥
2.5.51.44: Meanwhile all the Apsarases consulted with one another: Having now conceived passion, he is at once eager for the sight of Pārvatī. ॥44॥
2.5.51.45: Whichever shapely woman this Pināka-bearer, the foe of Kāma, would choose, she surely becomes the queen of all divine women. ॥45॥
2.5.51.46: A glance cast in the form of Gaurī would make him sport with the hosts of love's arts; this desire overcomes even the foe of Kāma — so they eagerly said to one another. ॥46॥
2.5.51.47: Whatever woman other than Dākṣāyaṇī is able to touch him, let her go there without fear and enchant the lord of Pārvatī. ॥47॥
2.5.51.48: Then Citralekhā, the daughter of Kūṣmāṇḍa, spoke these words: I dare to touch Śaṅkara in the lovely form of Gaurī. ॥48॥
2.5.51.49: Citralekhā said: The Mohinī form that Keśava once assumed with the wish to delude — resorting, in truth, to that Vaiṣṇava yoga… ॥49॥
2.5.51.50: And then, having seen Urvaśī's transformation of form, Ghṛtācī took the form of Kālī, and Viśvācī the body of Caṇḍikā; ॥50॥
2.5.51.51: Rambhā took the form of Sāvitrī, Menakā likewise that of Gāyatrī, Sahajanyā the form of Jayā, and Puñjikasthalī that of Vijayā. ॥51॥
2.5.51.52: And other eminent Apsarases, not named here, endowed with their own arts, in turn assumed with effort the forms of the Mothers, also not named. ॥52॥
2.5.51.53: Then the daughter of Kumbhāṇḍa, having seen their forms and grasped the matter through the Vaiṣṇava yoga and her own yogic power, imitated them. ॥53॥
2.5.51.54: Ūṣā, daughter of Bāṇāsura, skilled in divine yoga, assumed the form of Pārvatī — divine, most wondrous and auspicious, ॥54॥
2.5.51.55: with feet like great red lotuses, of supreme radiance, endowed with divine marks, granting the objects desired by the heart. ॥55॥
2.5.51.56: Then Girijā, Śivā, the all-knowing inner controller of all, perceiving her intention of love-making, spoke. ॥56॥
2.5.51.57: Girijā said: Since you, friend Ūṣā, have assumed my very form out of desire, O proud one, when the time has come — ॥57॥
2.5.51.58: — in this month of Kārttika, after your season in Mādhava, on the twelfth day of the bright fortnight, in the dreadful onset of night, whoever — ॥58॥
2.5.51.59: the man who will enjoy you, while you, having fasted, lie asleep in the inner apartments — he has been appointed your husband by the gods; with him you will take delight. ॥59॥
2.5.51.60: For from childhood you have been a devotee of Viṣṇu, constantly and unwearied. So be it, she said in her mind, her face bashful. ॥60॥
2.5.51.61: Then the goddess Pārvatī, adorned with festive ornaments, came into Rudra's presence and sported with that Śambhu. ॥61॥
2.5.51.62: Then, at the end of the love-play, the blessed Rudra vanished from sight, together with his wife and his Gaṇas, and accompanied by the gods, O sage. ॥62॥
2.5.51.iti: Thus ends the fifty-first adhyāya, named The sport of Śiva and Śivā, in the account of the story of Ūṣā, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥51॥
2.5.52.1: Sanatkumāra said: Listen also to another episode of Śiva, the Supreme Self, one filled with his affection for devotees and bestowing supreme bliss. ॥1॥
2.5.52.2: Long ago an asura named Bāṇa, made arrogant through ill fate, performed the tāṇḍava dance and pleased Śaṅkara. ॥2॥
2.5.52.3: Knowing Śiva, the beloved of Pārvatī, to be pleased in mind, the asura Bāṇa, with bowed shoulders and joined palms, spoke. ॥3॥
2.5.52.4: Bāṇa said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, crest-jewel of all the gods, by your grace I am mighty. Hear my supreme request. ॥4॥
2.5.52.5: The thousand arms given by you have become a great burden to me; in the three worlds I find no opponent equal to me except you. ॥5॥
2.5.52.6: O God, what am I to do with this thousand of mountain-like arms without a battle, O bull-bannered one? ॥6॥
2.5.52.7: With my arms full of itching, eager to fight the elephants of the quarters, I went about pulverizing cities and mountains; and even they fled away in fear. ॥7॥
2.5.52.8: By me Yama was made a mere soldier, and great Agni a menial; Varuṇa too was made a cowherd, a tender of cows. ॥8॥
2.5.52.9: Kubera was made superintendent of elephants, and Nirṛti a maidservant; and Indra, conquered, was made a perpetual payer of tribute in the world. ॥9॥
2.5.52.10: Tell me of the coming of a battle in which these arms of mine will be shattered by weapons and missiles hurled by enemy hands. ॥10॥
2.5.52.11: Let them fall by an enemy's hand, or let them fell foes by the thousands. Fulfil this wish of mine, O Maheśvara. ॥11॥
2.5.52.12: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing that, Rudra, the remover of his devotees' afflictions, grew angry; filled with great wrath, he let out a most astonishing loud laugh and said: ॥12॥
2.5.52.13: Rudra said: Shame, shame on you, arrogant in every way, lowest of the whole Daitya race! Such speech is not fitting for a devotee, the son of Bali. ॥13॥
2.5.52.14: You will soon obtain a dreadful quelling of this pride of yours: a great battle, suddenly, with a mighty one equal to me. ॥14॥
2.5.52.15: There your mountain-like arms, cut down like firewood and made to fall like plantain stems by weapons and missiles, will drop to the ground. ॥15॥
2.5.52.16: This banner of yours, O wicked one, bearing a human head together with a peacock — when it falls, ॥16॥
2.5.52.17: — the banner set up in the armoury, without any danger caused by wind — then know in your mind that a most terrible battle has arrived. ॥17॥
2.5.52.18: Fixing this in mind, go forth to the dreadful battle with your whole army. For now, go to that dwelling of yours where it the banner stands; all is well for now. ॥18॥
2.5.52.19: And there, O evil-minded one, you will see those great portents of yours. Having said this, the remover of pride, affectionate to devotees, fell silent. ॥19॥
2.5.52.20: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing that, Bāṇa worshipped Rudra with divine bud-like folded palms, bowed to Mahādeva, and went to his own home. ॥20॥
2.5.52.21: Asked by Kumbhāṇḍa, he joyfully told him what had happened. The asura Bāṇa, ever eager, kept watching for that conjunction of events. ॥21॥
2.5.52.22: Then one day, by fate, the asura Bāṇa saw there that banner broken of its own accord, and, delighted, he set out for battle. ॥22॥
2.5.52.23: Summoning his army, accompanied by his eight divisions, he performed the sacrifice for war and looked upon the honey auspicious for battle; ॥23॥
2.5.52.24: and observing every auspicious sign in the quarters, the son of Bali — of great zeal, a great hero, a great chariot-warrior — set forth, ॥24॥
2.5.52.25: pondering in the lotus of his heart: Who will come, and from where — a warrior who loves battle and is master of many weapons and missiles? ॥25॥
2.5.52.26: Let him cut off my thousand arms like firewood; likewise I shall cut him into hundreds here with very sharp weapons. ॥26॥
2.5.52.27: Meanwhile the time arranged by Śaṅkara arrived, when Bāṇa's daughter, well-born, had performed auspicious rites. ॥27॥
2.5.52.28: Having worshipped Mādhava in the month of Mādhava (Vaiśākha) at deep night, she slept in the guarded inner apartments, and was made to experience union as a woman. ॥28॥
2.5.52.29: She was drawn by divine illusion by Kṛṣṇa's grandson (the son of Kṛṣṇa's son), who had been sent by Gaurī; and she wept like one without a protector. ॥29॥
2.5.52.30: He too, having enjoyed her by force, was carried back to Dvārakā within a moment by Pārvatī's companions through divine yoga. ॥30॥
2.5.52.31: Then she, ravished, rose up weeping and, telling her friends many words of grief, resolved on giving up her body. ॥31॥
2.5.52.32: O Vyāsa, she was reminded again by a friend of the fault of her own self; then, recalling that whole earlier account, she became composed. ॥32॥
2.5.52.33: Then Ūṣā, the daughter of Bāṇa, spoke in a sweet voice to Citralekhā, the daughter of Kumbhāṇḍa, O sage. ॥33॥
2.5.52.34: Ūṣā said: Friend, if this man was formerly ordained by Pārvatī as my husband, by what means may he, hidden from us, be rightfully obtained by me? Tell you me. ॥34॥
2.5.52.35: Or in what family was he born, by whom my heart has been stolen? Hearing these words of Uṣā, her friend then replied to her. ॥35॥
2.5.52.36: Citralekhā said: O lady, how shall I bring that man whom you saw in a dream, who is not known to me? ॥36॥
2.5.52.37: When she said this, the Daitya maiden, blinded by passion, became eager to die; and so on that first day she was protected by that friend. ॥37॥
2.5.52.38: Then the very wise Citralekhā, daughter of Kumbhāṇḍa, spoke again to Uṣā, the daughter of Bāṇa, O best of sages: ॥38॥
2.5.52.39: I will remove your distress: if he is to be found in the three worlds, I will bring the man who has stolen your heart. Point him out. ॥39॥
2.5.52.40: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this, she drew on a cloth panel gods, Daityas and Dānavas, as well as Gandharvas, Siddhas, Nāgas, Yakṣas and others. ॥40॥
2.5.52.41: Likewise she drew among them the men of the Vṛṣṇi clan: Śūra, Ānakadundubhi, Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, and Pradyumna, the best of men. ॥41॥
2.5.52.42: Seeing Aniruddha, the son of Pradyumna, drawn there, Ūṣā became bashful and cast her face down, her heart filled with joy. ॥42॥
2.5.52.43: Ūṣā said: That is the thief, the man whom I obtained in the night, friend, by whom the jewel of my heart was swiftly stolen. ॥43॥
2.5.52.44: By his mere touch I became so infatuated. I wish to know him; tell me everything, O lovely one. ॥44॥
2.5.52.45: In whose lineage was he born, and what is his name? Thus addressed, the yoginī told his name and his lineage. ॥45॥
2.5.52.46: Having heard everything about his family and the rest, O best of sages, Bāṇa's daughter, eager and full of longing, spoke. ॥46॥
2.5.52.47: Ūṣā said: Out of affection, friend, devise at once a means to obtain him, a means by which I may gain that beloved, dear as my life. ॥47॥
2.5.52.48: Without him, friend, I cannot bear to live even a single moment. Bring him here with earnest effort and make me happy, friend. ॥48॥
2.5.52.49: Sanatkumāra said: Thus addressed by that daughter of Bāṇa, the minister's daughter was astonished, O best of sages, and became absorbed in careful thought. ॥49॥
2.5.52.50: Then Citralekhā, swift as the mind, having spoken to her friend and having recognised him as Kṛṣṇa's grandson, set out to go to Dvārakā. ॥50॥
2.5.52.51: On the fourteenth of the dark half of Jyeṣṭha, when the third day had passed, within a muhūrta before dawn she reached the city of Dvārakā. ॥51॥
2.5.52.52: The divine yoginī went through the sky in a single instant; and then in the garden of the inner palace she saw Pradyumna's son, ॥52॥
2.5.52.53: sporting with the women and drinking Mādhavī wine, beautiful in every limb, dark-complexioned, sweetly smiling, in the fresh bloom of youth. ॥53॥
2.5.52.54: Then, by her tāmasa yogic power, she covered with a veil of darkness that descendant of Madhu, who had climbed onto his bed, ॥54॥
2.5.52.55: and then, taking that bed upon her head, within the blink of an eye she reached Śoṇitapura, where Bāṇa's daughter was. ॥55॥
2.5.52.56: There she, tormented by love, her mind maddened, was showing various emotions. Then, seeing him brought, she became afraid. ॥56॥
2.5.52.57: In that well-guarded inner apartment, at that new union, no sooner had they begun to make love than it was at once found out ॥57॥
2.5.52.58: by those stationed at the door of the inner apartments, cane staffs in hand, through signs and inferences — the maiden's misconduct being carried on. ॥58॥
2.5.52.59: And he too was seen by them there: a man of divine form, young, handsome, bold, and fond of battle. ॥59॥
2.5.52.60: Having seen him, those men, great heroes, guards of the maiden's inner apartments, reported everything to Bāṇa, the son of Bali. ॥60॥
2.5.52.61: The doorkeepers said: O lord, someone unknown, hidden in the inner apartments by force — who is he? — has violated your daughter, seizing her of his own accord. ॥61॥
2.5.52.62: O lord of the Dānavas, mighty-armed one, look, look at him here, and do whatever is proper; we are not at fault. ॥62॥
2.5.52.63: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing their words, the mighty lord of the Dānavas, having heard of his daughter's defilement, was astonished, O best of sages. ॥63॥
2.5.52.iti: Thus ends the fifty-second adhyāya, named The story of Ūṣā, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥52॥
2.5.53.1: Sanatkumāra said: Then Bāṇāsura, enraged, went there and saw him. His body had taken on a divine grace, and he was in the first bloom of youth. ॥1॥
2.5.53.2: Seeing him, Bāṇa, skilled in battle, his mind gripped by anger, was astonished. Then, as if laughing, he said: What is the reason for this? ॥2॥
2.5.53.3: Ah! A man rich in beauty, daring and steadfast! Who is this ill-fated fellow of deluded mind, whose last hour has come? ॥3॥
2.5.53.4: He has defiled the conduct of my family and my dear daughter. Kill him quickly in your fury with the most dreadful weapons. ॥4॥
2.5.53.5: Or else bind that wicked one, and then, O heroes, guard him with special care in a dreadful, grim prison for a long time. ॥5॥
2.5.53.6: I do not know who this fearless one is, or who this one of terrible valour is. Pondering thus, Śarāsura (Bāṇa), though of great intellect, fell into doubt. ॥6॥
2.5.53.7: Then the evil-minded Daitya ordered an army of ten thousand to advance steadily and slay that hero. ॥7॥
2.5.53.8: Commanded by him, those extremely fierce warriors swiftly surrounded the inner apartments on all sides, shouting, cut, pierce. ॥8॥
2.5.53.9: Then, seeing the enemy army, that Yādava roared and seized a matchless iron club that stood at the door of the inner apartments, ॥9॥
2.5.53.10: and came out of that building like Death with a thunderbolt in hand. With it he killed those servants and went back into the inner apartments. ॥10॥
2.5.53.11: In this way, O best of sages, his eyes red with fury and his strength increased by Śiva's energy, he slew ten thousand soldiers. ॥11॥
2.5.53.12: When a hundred thousand warriors had been slain, Bāṇāsura in his rage took Kumbhāṇḍa with him and challenged that warrior skilled in battle ॥12॥
2.5.53.13: — Aniruddha, son of Pradyumna, of great intellect, protected by Śiva's energy, his body blazing — to single combat in that great battle. ॥13॥
2.5.53.14: Then, with a sword he had taken in the fight, he destroyed ten thousand horses and the finest chariots of the lord of the Daityas. ॥14॥
2.5.53.15: Then, to kill him, Aniruddha seized a spear like the fire of Time at the dissolution, and with it he struck him. ॥15॥
2.5.53.16: Bāṇa was struck hard by that spear on the seat of his chariot, and at that very moment the hero vanished on the spot, together with his horses. ॥16॥
2.5.53.17: When he had become invisible, the unconquered son of Pradyumna looked around in all directions and stood motionless like a mountain. ॥17॥
2.5.53.18: Then that Dānava, a fighter by deceit, struck him again and again with thousands of various weapons while remaining unseen. ॥18॥
2.5.53.19: By trickery that mighty one bound him with serpent-nooses: Śarāsura, the son of Bali, a great hero and a devotee of Śiva. ॥19॥
2.5.53.20: Having bound him and put him inside a cage, he withdrew from the battle. Then Bāṇa, furious, spoke to the very mighty son of his charioteer. ॥20॥
2.5.53.21: Bāṇāsura said: O son of the charioteer, quickly cut off the head of this man, this wicked one who has forcibly defiled my pure and noble family. ॥21॥
2.5.53.22: Cut up all his limbs, sir, and give them to the Rākṣasas; then let the flesh-eaters, too, feast on his blood and flesh. ॥22॥
2.5.53.23: Or kill the sinner by throwing him into a bottomless well choked with grass. Why say more, O son of the charioteer? He must be killed by any means. ॥23॥
2.5.53.24: Sanatkumāra said: On hearing these words of his, the night-roamer Kumbhāṇḍa, righteous in mind and best among good counsellors, spoke to Bāṇa. ॥24॥
2.5.53.25: Kumbhāṇḍa said: This is not a fit deed to do, O lord; let it be reconsidered. My view is that if he is killed, you yourself would be destroyed. ॥25॥
2.5.53.26: This one, O lord, appears equal to Viṣṇu in valour, empowered by the splendid energy of the Moon-crested One (Śiva), your chosen deity. ॥26॥
2.5.53.27: Moreover, by the might of the Moon-browed One, this one has reached this state in battle, firmly grounded in his manly courage. ॥27॥
2.5.53.28: By Śiva's grace this mighty grandson of Kṛṣṇa regards us as mere straw, even though he has been forcibly bitten by serpents. ॥28॥
2.5.53.29: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this to Bāṇa, that Dānava, foremost among those who know statecraft, spoke these words to Aniruddha. ॥29॥
2.5.53.30: Kumbhāṇḍa said: Who are you, and whose son are you, O hero? Tell the truth in front of me. Or by whom were you brought here, you ill-behaved, lowest of men? ॥30॥
2.5.53.31: Praise the heroic lord of the Daityas and bow to him with joined palms, saying over and over the humble words, I am defeated. ॥31॥
2.5.53.32: If this is done, there may be release; otherwise, bondage and worse. Hearing his words, he (Aniruddha) gave a reply. ॥32॥
2.5.53.33: Aniruddha said: Hey, hey, you crony of the vile Daitya, living on morsels from his hand. O night-roamer, O ill-behaved one, you do not know the code of conduct toward an enemy. ॥33॥
2.5.53.34: My view is that for a hero, abject submission and flight are worse than death; they would go against his nature and be a thorn in his side. ॥34॥
2.5.53.35: For a Kṣatriya, death in battle facing the foe is always better. One who counts himself a hero should not stand on the ground with joined palms like a wretch. ॥35॥
2.5.53.36: Sanatkumāra said: He spoke many such heroic words to him. Hearing them, Bāṇa was astonished, and he also grew angry. ॥36॥
2.5.53.37: Then a voice from the sky spoke to calm Bāṇa, while all the heroes, Aniruddha and the minister were listening. ॥37॥
2.5.53.38: The heavenly voice said: O Bāṇa, great hero, you should not give way to anger. You are the son of Bali, O wise one, a devotee of Śiva; reflect on this. ॥38॥
2.5.53.39: Śiva is the lord of all, the witness of all actions, the supreme Lord. This whole world, moving and unmoving, depends on him. ॥39॥
2.5.53.40: He alone is always the creator, sustainer and destroyer of the worlds. He bears rajas, sattva and tamas, and his forms are Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Hara. ॥40॥
2.5.53.41: He is the Lord dwelling within all, the impeller, supreme beyond everything, changeless, imperishable, eternal, and though the master of Māyā, free of qualities. ॥41॥
2.5.53.42: By his will the strong is to be known as weak, O son of the excellent Bali. Knowing this in your mind, be at ease, O great-minded one. ॥42॥
2.5.53.43: The Blessed Lord, remover of pride, skilled in manifold sports, affectionate to his devotees, will now destroy your pride. ॥43॥
2.5.53.44: Sanatkumāra said: Having spoken thus, the voice from the sky fell silent, O great sage. Because of those words Bāṇāsura did not kill Aniruddha. ॥44॥
2.5.53.45: Instead, going to his own inner palace, he drank the finest liquor; and he forgot those words and, perverse-minded, indulged in pleasure. ॥45॥
2.5.53.46: Then Aniruddha, bound by serpent coils fierce with venom, his heart unsatisfied with his beloved, at that very moment remembered Durgā. ॥46॥
2.5.53.47: Aniruddha said: O Goddess, giver of refuge, I am bound and being burnt by serpents. Come, grant me protection, O giver of fame, O you of fierce wrath. ॥47॥
2.5.53.48: O devotee of Śiva, O great Goddess, maker of creation, preservation and dissolution, without you there is no other protector; therefore protect me, O Śivā. ॥48॥
2.5.53.49: Sanatkumāra said: Thus pleased by him, Kālī, lustrous like crushed collyrium, arrived there at the great midnight on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of Jyeṣṭha. ॥49॥
2.5.53.50: With heavy blows of her fists she shattered the cage, reducing to ashes those terrifying arrows that had taken the form of serpents. ॥50॥
2.5.53.51: Having freed Aniruddha and then brought him into the inner apartments, Durgā vanished right there. ॥51॥
2.5.53.52: Thus, by the grace of the Goddess, the power of Śiva, O lord of sages, Aniruddha was freed from distress, became happy and free of pain. ॥52॥
2.5.53.53: Then Aniruddha, son of Pradyumna, having gained victory through Śiva's power, rejoiced on obtaining his beloved, the daughter of Bāṇa. ॥53॥
2.5.53.54: Happy, he sported as before with his beloved; having drunk liquor, his eyes deep red, he then enjoyed himself with Bāṇa's daughter. ॥54॥
2.5.53.iti: Thus ends the fifty-third adhyāya, named The sport of Aniruddha and Ūṣā, in the story of Ūṣā, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥53॥
2.5.54.1: Vyāsa said: O best of sages, when Kṛṣṇa's grandson Aniruddha had been carried off by Kumbhāṇḍa's daughter, what did Kṛṣṇa do? Tell me that. ॥1॥
2.5.54.2: Sanatkumāra said: Then, after Aniruddha had gone, O best of sages, Kṛṣṇa heard the sound of his women weeping and became distressed. ॥2॥
2.5.54.3: And as his kinsmen and Hari, not seeing Aniruddha, kept grieving, the four months of the rainy season passed. ॥3॥
2.5.54.4: Hearing from Nārada that news, and the deeds of the captive, all the Vṛṣṇis, whose deity was Kṛṣṇa, were greatly distressed. ॥4॥
2.5.54.5: Kṛṣṇa, having heard that whole affair, at once summoned Tārkṣya (Garuḍa) and eagerly went to Śoṇitapura for battle. ॥5॥
2.5.54.6: Pradyumna and Yuyudhāna went, and Sāmba, then Sāraṇa, and Nanda, Upananda, Bhadra and others, followers of Rāma and Kṛṣṇa. ॥6॥
2.5.54.7: Joined with twelve akṣauhiṇīs, the bulls of the Sātvatas besieged Bāṇa's city on all sides, from every direction. ॥7॥
2.5.54.8: Seeing the city's gardens, ramparts, watchtowers and gateways being shattered, Bāṇa, filled with rage, sallied forth with an equal army. ॥8॥
2.5.54.9: For Bāṇa's sake, Lord Rudra, with his son, surrounded by the Pramathas, mounted the bull Nandin and came to fight. ॥9॥
2.5.54.10: There arose a most tumultuous, wondrous, hair-raising battle there between Kṛṣṇa and the others and those protectors of Bāṇa headed by Rudra. ॥10॥
2.5.54.11: There was combat between Kṛṣṇa and Śaṅkara, between Pradyumna and Guha, and of Balarāma with Kūṣmāṇḍa and Kūpakarṇa. ॥11॥
2.5.54.12: There was combat of Sāmba with Bāṇa's son, of Sātyaki with Bāṇa, of Garuḍa with Nandin, and of others with others. ॥12॥
2.5.54.13: Brahmā and the other lords of the gods, the sages, Siddhas and Cāraṇas, Gandharvas and Apsarases came in their vehicles and aerial cars to watch. ॥13॥
2.5.54.14: O chief of brahmins, a very fierce battle took place between those of the Yadu lineage and the Pramathas of various forms, down to the Revatīs. ॥14॥
2.5.54.15: Together with his brother Rāma and the wise Pradyumna, Kṛṣṇa waged an incomparable battle with the Pramathas. ॥15॥
2.5.54.16: There battle took place with Agni, with Yama and Varuṇa, with Vimukha, with the three-footed Fever, and with Guha. ॥16॥
2.5.54.17: Between the Vṛṣṇis and the Pramathas of various forms there arose an exceedingly fierce, dreadful, hair-raising battle. ॥17॥
2.5.54.18: It was with many terrifying apparitions, with Koṭarīs at every step, and with shameless, mighty women close by. ॥18॥
2.5.54.19: Śauri (Kṛṣṇa) put to flight Śaṅkara's followers—Bhūtas, Pramathas and Guhyakas—with sharp-tipped arrows shot from the Śārṅga bow. ॥19॥
2.5.54.20: Thus the heroes led by Pradyumna, for whom battle was a great festival, fought a most terrible battle, destroying the enemy army. ॥20॥
2.5.54.21: Seeing his own army being shattered, Rudra, extremely indignant, became greatly angry and roared a very fearsome roar. ॥21॥
2.5.54.22: Hearing that, Śaṅkara's Gaṇas roared and fought, crushing their opponents, strengthened by Śambhu's power. ॥22॥
2.5.54.23: Kṛṣṇa discharged various missiles from the Śārṅga against Pinākin; the trident-wielder, unperturbed, neutralized them with counter-weapons. ॥23॥
2.5.54.24: Against the Brahmāstra, the Brahmāstra; against the wind-missile, the mountain-missile; against the fire-missile, the rain-missile; and against Nārāyaṇa's missile, his own. ॥24॥
2.5.54.25: Kṛṣṇa's army, defeated by the opposing hero, fled; O Vyāsa, it could not stand in battle before the full, mighty splendour of Rudra. ॥25॥
2.5.54.26: When his army had been routed, the glorious Kṛṣṇa, scorcher of foes, released his own watery fever called Śītala, O sage. ॥26॥
2.5.54.27: With Kṛṣṇa's army routed, Kṛṣṇa's cold fever advanced upon Rudra, O sage, burning the ten directions. ॥27॥
2.5.54.28: Then Maheśvara, seeing it coming, released his own fever; and the two fevers, Māheśvara and Vaiṣṇava, fought each other. ॥28॥
2.5.54.29: Then the Vaiṣṇava fever, afflicted by the Māheśvara's might, crying out and finding no safety elsewhere, praised the bull-bannered Śiva. ॥29॥
2.5.54.30: Then Lord Hara, pleased at being praised by Viṣṇu's fever, kind to those who seek refuge, spoke to Viṣṇu's cold fever. ॥30॥
2.5.54.31: Maheśvara said: O cold fever, I am pleased; let your fear of my fever depart. Whoever remembers our dialogue will have no fear of fever. ॥31॥
2.5.54.32: Sanatkumāra said: Thus addressed, Nārāyaṇa's fever bowed to Rudra and departed. Seeing that event, Kṛṣṇa was amazed and filled with fear. ॥32॥
2.5.54.33: Then Skanda, harassed by Pradyumna's floods of arrows, enraged and fiercely indignant on behalf of the Daitya hosts, struck Pradyumna with his spear. ॥33॥
2.5.54.34: Struck there by Skanda's spear, Pradyumna, mighty though he was, shedding blood from his limbs, withdrew from the battle with effort. ॥34॥
2.5.54.35: Struck by Kumbhāṇḍa and Kūpakarṇa with various missiles, Balabhadra too fled; mighty as he was, he did not stand in battle. ॥35॥
2.5.54.36: Then Garuḍa, assuming a thousand bodies and drinking water from the great ocean, wrought destruction with whirlpools of cloud- and ocean-waters. ॥36॥
2.5.54.37: Then Maheśa's mount, the mighty bull, enraged, swiftly and with great force struck him (Garuḍa) with his two horns. ॥37॥
2.5.54.38: His limbs torn by the blows of the horns, Garuḍa, greatly astonished, quickly fled from the battle, abandoning Janārdana. ॥38॥
2.5.54.39: When things had turned out thus, the Lord, son of Devakī, greatly astonished by Rudra's power, quickly spoke to his charioteer. ॥39॥
2.5.54.40: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O charioteer, listen to my words: drive my chariot swiftly, so that I may stand near Mahādeva to speak to him. ॥40॥
2.5.54.41: Sanatkumāra said: Addressed thus by Hari, the charioteer Dāruka, foremost in his own skills, quickly drove that chariot toward Rudra. ॥41॥
2.5.54.42: Then Śrī Kṛṣṇa, bowing with joined palms, having taken refuge with devotion, addressed Śaṅkara, who is affectionate to his devotees. ॥42॥
2.5.54.43: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, loving to those who come for refuge, I bow to you of infinite power, the Self of all, the Supreme Lord. ॥43॥
2.5.54.44: I bow to you, the cause of the origin, sustenance and dissolution of the universe, pure consciousness alone, the supreme Brahman-liṅga, peaceful, absolute, the Supreme Lord. ॥44॥
2.5.54.45: Time, destiny, karma, the individual soul, inherent nature, and matter; the field (body), the vital breath, the self, and the transformations—their aggregate— ॥45॥
2.5.54.46: —this continuous flow, like seed and sprout, is your māyā, O Lord of the world. Here I take refuge in you, the Supreme Lord, who holds it in check. ॥46॥
2.5.54.47: Through various forms assumed by yourself merely in sport, you, Lord of the worlds, surely sustain the gods and others, and by your very nature you slay those who go astray. ॥47॥
2.5.54.48: For you are Brahman, the supreme light, hidden in the Veda (the Brahman made of words), whom the wise see as the stainless Self, absolute like the sky. ॥48॥
2.5.54.49: You alone are the primeval Person, without a second, the fourth (turīya), the seer of the Self, the Lord; you are the cause and yet causeless, and you appear as endowed with transformations. ॥49॥
2.5.54.50: By your own māyā, for the manifestation of all the guṇas, O Blessed Lord, O Master, you are connected with everything and yet distinct from everything, O Maheśvara. ॥50॥
2.5.54.51: Just as the sun, though covered by cloud, illumines by its own light the shadow-forms too, O Lord, so indeed are you, the supreme Seer. ॥51॥
2.5.54.52: Though covered by the guṇa, you are not in the guṇa; self-luminous, you illumine the guṇas, O all-pervading one, O infinite one, O Giriśa, O Śaṅkara. ॥52॥
2.5.54.53: Those whose minds are deluded by your māyā, attached to sons, wives, houses and the like, rise up and sink down in the ocean of sin. ॥53॥
2.5.54.54: He who, having obtained this human world given by fate, with senses unconquered, does not honour your feet—he is to be pitied, a deceiver of himself. ॥54॥
2.5.54.55: By your command, O Lord, I have come to cut off Bāṇa's arms. This proud Bāṇa has been cursed by you yourself, the remover of pride. ॥55॥
2.5.54.56: Withdraw from the battle, O God, so that your curse may not be in vain. Give me your permission, O Lord, to cut off Bāṇa's arms. ॥56॥
2.5.54.57: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, O lord of sages, Śambhu Maheśvara, pleased at heart by Kṛṣṇa's praise, replied. ॥57॥
2.5.54.58: Maheśvara said: You have spoken truly, dear one; the king of the Daityas was indeed cursed by me. By my command you have come to cut off Bāṇa's mace-like arms. ॥58॥
2.5.54.59: What can I do, O lord of Ramā? I am always subject to my devotees, O Hari. How, O hero, could Bāṇa's arms be cut while I look on? ॥59॥
2.5.54.60: Therefore, at my command, make me yawn with the yawning-weapon (jṛmbhaṇāstra). Then do your work as you wish, and be happy. ॥60॥
2.5.54.61: Sanatkumāra said: Thus addressed by Śaṅkara, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, greatly astonished, returned to his own place on the battlefield and rejoiced, O lord of sages. ॥61॥
2.5.54.62: Then Hari, skilled in many weapons, quickly fitting the yawning-weapon to his bow, released it at the Pināka-wielder, O Vyāsa. ॥62॥
2.5.54.63: Having stupefied Giriśa, who was made to yawn by the yawning-weapon, Śauri (Kṛṣṇa) struck down Bāṇa's army with swords, maces and spears. ॥63॥
2.5.54.iti: Thus ends the fifty-fourth adhyāya, named The battle of Bāṇāsura with Rudra, Kṛṣṇa and others, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥54॥
2.5.55.1: Vyāsa said: O Sanatkumāra, all-knowing son of Brahmā, salutations to you. Wonderful is this story, dear one, that you have narrated to me, O sage. ॥1॥
2.5.55.2: When Hara had been made to yawn in battle by Hari with the yawning weapon, and Bāṇa's army had been slain, what did Bāṇa do? Tell me that. ॥2॥
2.5.55.3: Sūta said: Having heard these words of Vyāsa of boundless splendour, the son of Brahmā, lord of sages, replied with a pleased heart. ॥3॥
2.5.55.4: Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O greatly wise Vyāsa, dear one, to the most wonderful story of Kṛṣṇa and Śaṅkara, who conform to worldly play. ॥4॥
2.5.55.5: When Rudra, together with his son and his attendants, had in sport fallen asleep, Bāṇa, the king of the Daityas, went out to fight with Kṛṣṇa. ॥5॥
2.5.55.6: Then, with his horses held by Kumbhāṇḍa as charioteer and bearing many kinds of weapons and missiles, the mighty son of Bali waged an incomparable battle. ॥6॥
2.5.55.7: Seeing his own army destroyed, that lord of the Daityas, exceedingly enraged — the mighty son of Bali — waged an incomparable battle. ॥7॥
2.5.55.8: Śrī Kṛṣṇa too, the great hero, whose great strength was obtained from Giriśa, roared loudly there in the battle, regarding Bāṇa as a mere blade of grass. ॥8॥
2.5.55.9: He twanged his own wonderful bow named Śārṅga, terrifying what remained of Bāṇa's army, O lord of sages. ॥9॥
2.5.55.10: By that great sound born of the twang of the bow, the space between heaven and earth was at once completely filled. ॥10॥
2.5.55.11: Enraged, Hari then drew the bow to his ear and hurled at Bāṇa various sharp arrows resembling venomous serpents. ॥11॥
2.5.55.12: Seeing them coming, Bāṇa, the son of Bali, cut them down before they reached him, with his own arrows released from his bow. ॥12॥
2.5.55.13: Again that mighty Bāṇa, crusher of hosts of enemies, roared; all the Vṛṣṇis, devoted to Kṛṣṇa, trembled, bewildered. ॥13॥
2.5.55.14: Remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, the very proud son of Bali hurled his own arrows at the exceedingly valiant Kṛṣṇa. ॥14॥
2.5.55.15: Kṛṣṇa too, the mighty one, swiftly cut them down with his own arrows before they reached him, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva. ॥15॥
2.5.55.16: Rāma and the other mighty Vṛṣṇis, all aroused and filled with anger, struck down each his own opponent in the battle. ॥16॥
2.5.55.17: Thus for a very long time there took place there a tumultuous battle between the two mighty ones, astonishing to those who hear of it. ॥17॥
2.5.55.18: At that moment the king of birds Garuḍa, becoming exceedingly angry, crushed the entire army of the asura Bāṇa with blows of his wings. ॥18॥
2.5.55.19: Seeing his army crushed and him crushing it, the mighty son of Bali, foremost of Śaivas and lord of the sons of Diti, became extremely enraged. ॥19॥
2.5.55.20: Remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, he, possessed of a thousand arms, swiftly displayed great prowess, unbearable to his enemies. ॥20॥
2.5.55.21: That slayer of heroes simultaneously hurled countless arrows there, separately at each of the Yadus beginning with Kṛṣṇa, and at Garuḍa. ॥21॥
2.5.55.22: With one arrow the mighty one struck Garuḍa, with one Kṛṣṇa, with one Bala Balarāma, O sage, and likewise the others too. ॥22॥
2.5.55.23: Then Kṛṣṇa, of great valour, a form of Viṣṇu and slayer of the gods' enemies, became exceedingly angry in that battle, and the great lord roared. ॥23॥
2.5.55.24: Remembering Śaṅkara, he forcefully struck Bāṇa with excellent arrows shot from the Śārṅga, and at the same time his extremely fierce army. ॥24॥
2.5.55.25: Unperturbed, Hari quickly cut his bow, his parasol and the rest, and, killing his horses with his own arrows, felled them. ॥25॥
2.5.55.26: Bāṇa too, the great hero, roared, greatly enraged, and struck Kṛṣṇa with his mace; he fell to the ground. ॥26॥
2.5.55.27: Then Kṛṣṇa, quickly rising, fought with that enemy, the devotee of Śiva, O divine sage, in keeping with worldly play. ॥27॥
2.5.55.28: Thus for a long time there was a very great battle between the two: Hari-Kṛṣṇa, a form of Śiva, and he Bāṇa, the mighty, foremost of Śaivas. ॥28॥
2.5.55.29: Then the valiant Kṛṣṇa, having fought with Bāṇa for a long time and having gained strength by Śiva's command, became exceedingly angry, O lord of sages. ॥29॥
2.5.55.30: Then the blessed Kṛṣṇa, slayer of enemy heroes, swiftly cut off Bāṇa's many arms with the Sudarśana, at the command of Śambhu. ॥30॥
2.5.55.31: Four of his arms remained, exceedingly beautiful; and by the grace of Śaṅkara he quickly became free of pain. ॥31॥
2.5.55.32: When Bāṇa had lost consciousness and Kṛṣṇa, filled with heroic fervour, was ready to cut off his head, then Rudra arose. ॥32॥
2.5.55.33: Rudra said: O blessed son of Devakī, what I commanded earlier has been done by you, O Viṣṇu, who always carry out my command. ॥33॥
2.5.55.34: Do not cut off Bāṇa's head; withdraw the Sudarśana. By my command, withdraw this unfailing discus; it is always to be held back in regard to my devotee. ॥34॥
2.5.55.35: Formerly I gave you the discus, irresistible in your battles, and victory too, O Govinda; therefore withdraw from the battle. ॥35॥
2.5.55.36: Against Dadhīci, against the hero Rāvaṇa, and against Tāraka and the three cities too, O lord of Lakṣmī, you did not formerly release the discus without my command. ॥36॥
2.5.55.37: You indeed are the lord of yogis, the Supreme Self in person, O Janārdana, devoted to the welfare of all beings; consider this in your own mind. ॥37॥
2.5.55.38: I gave him a boon that he would have no fear of death; that word of mine is ever true. I am fully pleased with you. ॥38॥
2.5.55.39: Formerly this one, proud and intoxicated with arrogance, said to me, give me battle, scratching his itching arms and forgetful of his own true state, O Hari. ॥39॥
2.5.55.40: Then I cursed him: One who will cut off your arms will come; before long you will be stripped of your pride. ॥40॥
2.5.55.41: By my command Hari came here as the severer of your arms. Now, therefore, withdraw from the battle; go to your own home with the bride and bridegroom. ॥41॥
2.5.55.42: Having spoken thus, Maheśvara brought about friendship between the two, and, taking leave of him, went to his own abode with his attendants and his sons. ॥42॥
2.5.55.43: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words of Śambhu and having withdrawn the Sudarśana discus, Kṛṣṇa, victorious and with body unhurt, then went to the inner apartments. ॥43॥
2.5.55.44: Having comforted Aniruddha, who was again united with his wife, he accepted the many heaps of jewels given by Bāṇa. ॥44॥
2.5.55.45: Taking also her friend Citralekhā, the supreme yoginī, Kṛṣṇa then became pleased, his task accomplished by Śiva's command. ॥45॥
2.5.55.46: Bowing in his heart to Giriśa and bidding farewell to the son of Bali, Hari, accompanied by his retinue, went to his own city. ॥46॥
2.5.55.47: On the way, having conquered Varuṇa, who opposed him in many ways, he reached the city of Dvārakā, amid great festivity. ॥47॥
2.5.55.48: Having dismissed Garuḍa, and having looked upon his friends and laughed with them, he then, going into Dvārakā, roamed about as he pleased. ॥48॥
2.5.55.iti: Thus ends the fifty-fifth adhyāya, named The cutting off of Bāṇa's arms and the removal of his pride, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥55॥
2.5.56.1: Nārada said: When Kṛṣṇa had gone to Dvārakā with Aniruddha and his wife, what did Bāṇa do after that? Tell me the truth, O great sage. ॥1॥
2.5.56.2: Sanatkumāra said: When Kṛṣṇa had gone to Dvārakā with Aniruddha and his wife, Bāṇa then became grief-stricken, recalling in his heart his own ignorance. ॥2॥
2.5.56.3: Then Nandī, Śiva's attendant, spoke to the grieving demon Bāṇa, whose limbs were smeared with blood and who was filled with remorse. ॥3॥
2.5.56.4: Nandīśvara said: O Bāṇa, true devotee of Śaṅkara, do not grieve with remorse, sir. Śambhu is indeed compassionate to devotees and bears the name Affectionate to Devotees. ॥4॥
2.5.56.5: Whatever has happened, it happened by his will—consider it so in your mind, O tiger among devotees, and remember Śiva again and again. ॥5॥
2.5.56.6: Fixing your mind on the Primal One, celebrate a great festival constantly; for this Śaṅkara is compassionate to devotees again and again. ॥6॥
2.5.56.7: Then, at Nandī's words, Bāṇa—reduced by the enemy almost to his head alone—gathered his courage and, great-minded, quickly went to Śiva's abode. ॥7॥
2.5.56.8: Having gone there and bowed to the Lord, Bāṇa, all his pride gone, his mind overwhelmed with love, wept, greatly agitated. ॥8॥
2.5.56.9: Praising him with various hymns, bowing down with praises likewise, stamping his feet as was fitting and flinging out his arms, ॥9॥
2.5.56.10: he danced the principal Tāṇḍava, adorned with the pratyālīḍha and other postures, and with stances of various forms headed by the ālīḍha. ॥10॥
2.5.56.11: He made thousands of mouth-sounds together with movements of the brows, and thousands of shakings of the head, displaying arrays of gestures by the thousands. ॥11॥
2.5.56.12: Displaying slowly, step by step, dance movements of various kinds, and likewise drenching the ground with streams of blood, ॥12॥
2.5.56.13: the asura Bāṇa, the great devotee, bowing and forgetful of his own state, propitiated Rudra, the trident-bearer, the moon-crested. ॥13॥
2.5.56.14: Then, the great dance having been performed, the Lord Hara, affectionate to devotees and fond of dance and song, delighted, spoke to Bāṇa. ॥14॥
2.5.56.15: Rudra said: O Bāṇa, dear son of Bali, I am pleased with your dancing. Choose a boon, O lord of demons, whatever is in your mind. ॥15॥
2.5.56.16: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of Śambhu, O sage, the demon-lord Bāṇa then chose as a boon the healing of his wounds, ॥16॥
2.5.56.17: and prowess in arm-to-arm combat, and then imperishable leadership of the gaṇas, and kingship for Uṣā's son in that city called Śoṇitaka; ॥17॥
2.5.56.18: freedom from enmity with the gods, and especially with Viṣṇu; and never again the wicked demon-nature joined with rajas and tamas; ॥18॥
2.5.56.19: especially, devotion to Śambhu, ever unchanging, O sage; affection for Śiva's devotees, and compassion toward all creatures. ॥19॥
2.5.56.20: Having thus obtained these boons from Śambhu, the great asura, son of Bali, his eyes filled with tears of love, palms reverently joined, praised Rudra. ॥20॥
2.5.56.21: Bāṇa said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, loving to those who seek refuge, I bow to you, O great Lord, friend of the lowly, ocean of compassion. ॥21॥
2.5.56.22: Great mercy has been shown to me, O Śaṅkara, ocean of mercy; all my pride has been taken away by you, being gracious, O Lord. ॥22॥
2.5.56.23: You are indeed Brahman, the Supreme Self, all-pervading, Lord of all; your body is the cosmic egg, O fierce Lord; you are Virāṭ, containing all, the Supreme. ॥23॥
2.5.56.24: The sky is your navel, fire your mouth, water your semen, the quarters your ears; heaven is your head, the earth your feet, and the moon is your mind, O Lord. ॥24॥
2.5.56.25: The sun is your eye, the ocean your belly, Indra your arms, Vidhi (Brahmā) Your intellect, Prajāpati your organ of procreation, and Dharma indeed is your heart. ॥25॥
2.5.56.26: The plants are your body-hairs, O Lord, the clouds your hair; the three guṇas are your three eyes; you are the Person, the Self of all. ॥26॥
2.5.56.27: They call the brāhmaṇa your mouth and the kṣatriya your arm; they call the vaiśya born of your thighs and the śūdra born of your feet. ॥27॥
2.5.56.28: You alone are always to be worshipped by all beings, O Maheśvara; worshipping you, a person surely attains supreme liberation. ॥28॥
2.5.56.29: The mortal who abandons you—the beloved Self and Lord—for the sake of perverse sense-objects, drinks poison, rejecting nectar. ॥29॥
2.5.56.30: Viṣṇu, Brahmā, the gods, and the sages of pure heart have taken refuge with their whole being in you, Śaṅkara, the beloved Lord. ॥30॥
2.5.56.31: Sanatkumāra said: Having spoken thus, the son of Bali, the asura Śara (Bāṇa), his limbs thrilling with love, bowed to Maheśvara and fell silent. ॥31॥
2.5.56.32: Hearing this from his devotee Bāṇa, Lord Bhava said, you shall obtain everything, and vanished right there. ॥32॥
2.5.56.33: Then, by Śambhu's grace, Bāṇa attained the status of Mahākāla; as Rudra's attendant he became exceedingly joyful. ॥33॥
2.5.56.34: Thus indeed has been told here, in words pleasing to the ear, this most excellent account of the one named Śara (Bāṇa) together with Śaṅkara—the trident-bearer, the true guru of all gurus, who eternally sports in the midst of all the worlds. ॥34॥
2.5.56.iti: Thus ends the fifty-sixth adhyāya, named Bāṇāsura attains the rank of a lord of the gaṇas, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥56॥
2.5.57.1: Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O Vyāsa, with great love, to the deed of the moon-crested Śiva: how he slew with his trident Gajāsura, the lord of the Dānavas. ॥1॥
2.5.57.2: Formerly, when the Dānava Mahiṣāsura had been slain in battle by the Goddess for the welfare of the gods, the gods attained happiness. ॥2॥
2.5.57.3: His son, O lord of sages, was the great hero Gajāsura; he remembered the slaying of his father, carried out by the Goddess at the request of the gods. ॥3॥
2.5.57.4: Recalling that enmity, he went to the forest for austerity, and, with Brahmā (Vidhi) as his aim, he performed supreme austerity with devotion. ॥4॥
2.5.57.5: I shall be unslayable by men and women who are conquered by desire — having thus reflected in his mind, he became one whose mind was absorbed in austerity. ॥5॥
2.5.57.6: He performed most terrible austerity in a valley of the Himālaya, arms raised upward, gaze fixed on the sky, touching the earth only with his big toes. ॥6॥
2.5.57.7: With his masses of matted locks he shone like the sun at the dissolution with its rays — this noble-minded Gajāsura, son of Mahiṣāsura. ॥7॥
2.5.57.8: From his head arose a smoky fire born of austerity, which, spreading in all directions, scorched the worlds across, above and below. ॥8॥
2.5.57.9: Because of the fire arising from his head, the rivers and oceans were agitated, the stars fell along with the planets, and the ten directions blazed. ॥9॥
2.5.57.10: Scorched by it, all the gods together with Indra (Vāsava) left heaven and went to Brahmaloka and reported: The earth is shaking. ॥10॥
2.5.57.11: The gods said: O Vidhi, scorched by Gajāsura's austerity we are distressed; we cannot remain in heaven, therefore we have come to you for refuge. ॥11॥
2.5.57.12: O Vidhi, bring about his pacification so that the others may live; otherwise the worlds will perish — truly, truly we say this. ॥12॥
2.5.57.13: Thus petitioned by the gods headed by Indra, the self-born Brahmā, with Bhṛgu, Dakṣa and others, went to the hermitage of the foremost Daitya. ॥13॥
2.5.57.14: Seeing him scorching the worlds with austerity, like the sun veiled by clouds in the sky, the Creator, amazed, spoke smiling. ॥14॥
2.5.57.15: Brahmā said: Rise, rise, O lord of Daityas, son of Mahiṣa; you are perfected in austerity. I, the giver of boons, have come, dear one; choose a boon as you wish. ॥15॥
2.5.57.16: Sanatkumāra said: Rising up again and again, the Daitya lord, son of Mahiṣa, gazing at the Lord with his eyes, delighted, addressed the god in a voice choked with emotion. ॥16॥
2.5.57.17: Gajāsura said: Salutation to you, O lord of the gods of gods. If you will give me a boon, may I be unslayable by men and women overcome by desire. ॥17॥
2.5.57.18: May I be of great strength and great valour, ever unconquerable by the gods and others, and, O Lord, the full enjoyer of all the riches of all the guardians of the worlds. ॥18॥
2.5.57.19: Sanatkumāra said: Thus requested by that Dānava, Brahmā (Śatadhṛti), pleased by his austerity, granted him that boon, so very hard to obtain. ॥19॥
2.5.57.20: Having thus obtained the boon, the Daitya Gajāsura, son of Mahiṣa, with a greatly gladdened mind, then returned to his own abode. ॥20॥
2.5.57.21: That great Asura conquered all the directions and the three worlds, and the lords of gods, Asuras and men, the Gandharvas, Garuḍas and serpents— ॥21॥
2.5.57.22: —having conquered all these and others and brought them under his control, the world-conqueror seized the positions of the world-guardians along with their splendour. ॥22॥
2.5.57.23: He occupied heaven (Triviṣṭapa), graced with the beauty of the divine gardens — the very palace of the great Indra built by Viśvakarman himself. ॥23॥
2.5.57.24: In that house of the great Indra, the mighty, high-spirited sole sovereign, who had conquered the worlds, enjoyed himself, his pair of feet worshipped by the gods and others whom he had oppressed, his fierce rule firmly established. ॥24॥
2.5.57.25: Thus, sole sovereign having conquered the quarters, enjoying pleasing sense-objects to his heart's content, he, with senses unconquered, was never satisfied. ॥25॥
2.5.57.26: Thus, as he was intoxicated with lordship, arrogant and acting contrary to scripture, after a long time had passed, an evil intent arose in him. ॥26॥
2.5.57.27: That son of Mahiṣāsura, the Dānava who crushed the gods, greatly tormented the excellent brahmins and ascetics on earth. ॥27॥
2.5.57.28: The evil-minded one tormented gods, men and Pramathas — all of them, and especially those devoted to dharma, remembering his former enmity. ॥28॥
2.5.57.29: Once, dear one, that mighty Dānava Gajāsura went to the capital of Śaṅkara. ॥29॥
2.5.57.30: When the Asura lord arrived, O sage, a great uproar of save us, save us arose there among the dwellers of Ānandavana. ॥30॥
2.5.57.31: When that son of Mahiṣāsura came to the city, crushing all the Pramathas, puffed up with pride in his own might— ॥31॥
2.5.57.32: —at that time the gods headed by Śakra, defeated by him, went to Śiva for refuge, bowed and praised him with reverence. ॥32॥
2.5.57.33: They reported the arrival of that Dānava in Kāśī and the excessive distress of the people there, especially of their leaders. ॥33॥
2.5.57.34: The gods said: O god of gods, Mahādeva, the Asura has come to your city and is causing suffering to your people; slay him, O treasure of compassion. ॥34॥
2.5.57.35: Wherever on earth he sets his foot, there by his weight he makes the immovable earth move. ॥35॥
2.5.57.36: By the speed of his thighs trees fall along with mountain peaks; by the blows of his staff-like arms the rocky heights are pulverised. ॥36॥
2.5.57.37: Because of friction with the hair of his head, the clouds even abandon the sky, and even today they have not lost the dark-blue hue born of contact with his hair. ॥37॥
2.5.57.38: By the force of his breaths the great oceans swell with high waves, and the rivers too, with their whales, become wildly billowing. ॥38॥
2.5.57.39: His height is nine thousand yojanas, and the breadth of this magician's body is just as much. ॥39॥
2.5.57.40: The tawny hue and the restless flicker of whose eyes the lightnings have not given up even today — he is coming swiftly. ॥40॥
2.5.57.41: Whichever direction this unbearable demon approaches, he declares, I am unslayable by men and women who are conquered by desire. ॥41॥
2.5.57.42: Thus the conduct of that demon has been reported to you. Protect your devotees, O Lord of the gods, you who are intent on protecting Kāśī. ॥42॥
2.5.57.43: Sanatkumāra said: Thus entreated by the gods, Hara, intent on protecting his devotees, came there swiftly with the desire to slay him. ॥43॥
2.5.57.44: Seeing that Śaṅkara, affectionate to his devotees, arrived, trident in hand and roaring, Gajāsura roared back. ॥44॥
2.5.57.45: Then there was a great battle between the two, terrible and wondrous, as they raised heroic cries amid showers of various missiles and weapons. ॥45॥
2.5.57.46: Gajāsura, exceedingly brilliant, of great strength and valour, pierced Giriśa, the slayer of demons, with sharp arrows. ॥46॥
2.5.57.47: Then Rudra, of fierce form, with his own exceedingly terrible arrows swiftly cut his arrows into pieces as small as sesame seeds before they reached him, O sage. ॥47॥
2.5.57.48: Then Gajāsura, enraged, rushed at Maheśvara, sword in hand, roaring loudly, today you are surely slain by me. ॥48॥
2.5.57.49: Then he whose weapon is the trident, knowing that the chief of demons who was coming at him could not be slain by anyone else, struck him with the trident. ॥49॥
2.5.57.50: Pierced through by that trident, the demon Gajāsura, regarding himself as made into a parasol held aloft over Śiva, addressed Hara. ॥50॥
2.5.57.51: Gajāsura said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, I am your devotee in every way. I know you as the lord of heaven, O trident-bearer, destroyer of Smara. ॥51॥
2.5.57.52: Death at your hand is deemed most auspicious for me, O Maheśāna, enemy of Andhaka, destroyer of Tripura, all-pervading one. ॥52॥
2.5.57.53: I wish to submit something; hear it, O mine of compassion. I speak the truth, not falsehood; consider it, O Mṛtyuñjaya. ॥53॥
2.5.57.54: You alone are to be revered by the worlds, established above the universe. In time all must die; such a death as this is for my highest good. ॥54॥
2.5.57.55: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing his words, Śaṅkara, the treasury of compassion, the Lord, smiled and replied to Gajāsura, the son of Mahiṣa. ॥55॥
2.5.57.56: Īśvara said: O treasury of great valour, best of demons, noble-minded Gajāsura, I am pleased; choose a boon to your liking. ॥56॥
2.5.57.57: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of Maheśa, the giver of boons, Gajāsura, lord of demons, replied with a pleased heart. ॥57॥
2.5.57.58: Gajāsura said: If you are pleased, O sky-clad one, then always wear this hide of mine, O Maheśāna, purified by the fire of your trident, ॥58॥
2.5.57.59: a hide fitted to your size, pleasant to the touch, won as the stake on the battlefield, beautiful, greatly divine, ever bringing comfort. ॥59॥
2.5.57.60: May it always be fragrant, always exceedingly soft, always spotless, and always a splendid adornment. ॥60॥
2.5.57.61: Even though it endured the blazing fire of great austerity for a very long time, O Lord, this hide of mine — I being a store of holy fragrance — was not burnt; therefore let it be yours. ॥61॥
2.5.57.62: If this hide of mine were not meritorious, O Digambara, how then could it have come into contact with your body on the battlefield? ॥62॥
2.5.57.63: And grant me another boon, if you are pleased, Śaṅkara: from this day onward may your name be Kṛttivāsas. ॥63॥
2.5.57.64: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of his, Śaṅkara, affectionate to his devotees, greatly pleased, said so be it to him, the son of Mahiṣāsura. ॥64॥
2.5.57.65: Again the pleased Maheśāna, who loves his devotees, spoke to the demon Gajāsura, whose mind was made pure by devotion. ॥65॥
2.5.57.66: Īśvara said: This holy body of yours, in this sacred field that is the means of liberation — let my liṅga be here, bestowing liberation on all. ॥66॥
2.5.57.67: named Kṛttivāseśvara, destroyer of great sins, the crown of all liṅgas, granting liberation. ॥67॥
2.5.57.68: Having said this, the Lord of gods, Digambara, took the huge hide of Gajāsura and wore it. ॥68॥
2.5.57.69: A great festival took place on that day, O lord of sages; all the people dwelling in Kāśī, and the Pramathas too, rejoiced. ॥69॥
2.5.57.70: Then the gods headed by Hari and Brahmā, their minds filled with joy, bowed with joined palms and praised Maheśāna. ॥70॥
2.5.57.71: When that lord of demons, Gajāsura son of Mahiṣa, was slain, the gods returned to their own abodes and the world regained its well-being. ॥71॥
2.5.57.72: Thus has been told the deed of Śambhu which reveals his affection for devotees; it leads to heaven, brings fame and long life, and increases wealth and grain. ॥72॥
2.5.57.73: Whoever, observing pure vows, listens to this with love or causes it to be heard, having enjoyed great happiness, obtains supreme bliss at the end. ॥73॥
2.5.57.iti: Thus ends the fifty-seventh adhyāya, named The slaying of Gajāsura, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥57॥
2.5.58.1: Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O Vyāsa, I shall narrate the deed of the moon-crested Śiva: how Hara slew Dundubhinirhrāda, the son of Diti. ॥1॥
2.5.58.2: When the mighty demon Hiraṇyākṣa, son of Diti, had been slain by the god Viṣṇu, Diti in course of time fell into great sorrow. ॥2॥
2.5.58.3: The wicked demon Dundubhinirhrāda, maternal uncle of Prahlāda and a giver of distress to the gods, consoled the grieving Diti with words. ॥3॥
2.5.58.4: Then that deceitful demon, king of the daityas, having comforted Diti, pondered a means: How might the gods be easily conquered? ॥4॥
2.5.58.5: He thought: The heroic great asura Hiraṇyākṣa, together with his brother, was slain through the gods, those deceitful enemies of the daityas, and through Viṣṇu. ॥5॥
2.5.58.6: What is the strength of the immortals, what their food, what their support? How could they be easily conquered by me? Thus he pondered a means. ॥6॥
2.5.58.7: Having reflected many times, the demon ascertained the truth with certainty: On consideration, the brāhmaṇas are surely the cause in this matter. ॥7॥
2.5.58.8: Thereupon the demon Dundubhinirhrāda, enemy of the gods and a great villain, repeatedly ran after brāhmaṇas to kill them. ॥8॥
2.5.58.9: Since the gods feed on sacrifices, and sacrifices arise from the Vedas, and those Vedas rest on brāhmaṇas, therefore the twice-born are the strength of the gods. ॥9॥
2.5.58.10: Certainly all the Vedas rest on brāhmaṇas; the gods, along with Vāsava (Indra), have brāhmaṇas as their strength. No deliberation is needed here. ॥10॥
2.5.58.11: If the brāhmaṇas were destroyed, the Vedas would then perish of themselves; hence, when they have perished, the gods are ruined for good. ॥11॥
2.5.58.12: When the sacrifices go to ruin, the gods, deprived of their food, become powerless and easy to conquer; and then, the gods being conquered— ॥12॥
2.5.58.13: I alone shall become the honoured lord of the three worlds; I shall seize all the imperishable riches of the gods. ॥13॥
2.5.58.14: I shall enjoy only pleasures in a kingdom whose thorns have been removed. Having resolved thus, the evil-minded villain reflected again. ॥14॥
2.5.58.15: Where are the twice-born found in greatest numbers, greatly swelled with brahmanic splendour, accomplished in Vedic study and endowed with the power of austerity? ॥15॥
2.5.58.16: Vārāṇasī is surely the abode of the greatest number of brāhmaṇas. Having first destroyed it, I shall then go on to another holy place. ॥16॥
2.5.58.17: Wherever, in whatever holy places and in whatever hermitages, brāhmaṇas are found, all of them everywhere are to be devoured by me. ॥17॥
2.5.58.18: Thus having formed an intention befitting his race, the wicked, deceitful Dundubhinirhrāda reached Kāśī and killed the twice-born. ॥18॥
2.5.58.19: Into whatever forest the best of the twice-born went to gather sacrificial fuel and kuśa grass, there that evil-minded one would devour them all. ॥19॥
2.5.58.20: So that no one would know it, he kept himself concealed, becoming a forest creature in the forest and an aquatic creature in a lake. ॥20॥
2.5.58.21: Of invisible form, the deceiver, imperceptible even to the gods, would by day remain intent on meditation like a sage, in the midst of the sages. ॥21॥
2.5.58.22: Watching the entering and leaving of the huts, at night he devoured many brāhmaṇas in the form of a tiger. ॥22॥
2.5.58.23: Thus he devoured them fearlessly, not leaving even a bone; in this way many brāhmaṇas were struck down by that wicked one. ॥23॥
2.5.58.24: Once, on Śivarātri, a devotee in his own hut, having performed worship of the God of gods, remained absorbed in meditation. ॥24॥
2.5.58.25: And that Dundubhinirhrāda, lord of the daityas, proud of his strength, assumed the form of a tiger and set his mind on seizing him. ॥25॥
2.5.58.26: But he could not overpower that devotee, who was immersed in meditation, firm of mind in beholding Śiva, and who had performed the protective placement of the astra-mantra. ॥26॥
2.5.58.27: Then the all-pervading Śambhu, Hara, knowing his intention, resolved upon the killing of that demon of wicked form. ॥27॥
2.5.58.28: Just as the tiger was about to seize him, Hara appeared—the three-eyed one, the protecting jewel of the world, whose mind is skilled in guarding devotees. ॥28॥
2.5.58.29: Seeing Rudra coming forth from the liṅga worshipped by that devotee, the demon, in that very tiger form, swelled up like a mountain. ॥29॥
2.5.58.30: Then, even as the dānava looked contemptuously at the all-knowing one, Śiva seized him as he came on and crushed him in the vice of his armpit. ॥30॥
2.5.58.31: Then the five-faced one, he who bears the name Fond of Devotees, struck the five-faced beast on the head with his fist, harder even than a thunderbolt. ॥31॥
2.5.58.32: By that blow of the fist and the crushing in the armpit, the tiger roared in extreme agony, filling heaven and earth, and died. ॥32॥
2.5.58.33: Their minds trembling at that great roar, the ascetics gathered there in the night, following the sound. ॥33॥
2.5.58.34: Seeing there the Lord holding the king of beasts under his arm, they all bowed down and praised Śarva with cries of victory, victory. ॥34॥
2.5.58.35: The brahmins said: Protect, protect us, O God, from this terrible calamity. Show us grace, O Lord; remain right here, O Teacher of the world. ॥35॥
2.5.58.36: In this very form, under the name Vyāghreśa, O Mahādeva, always guard the Jyeṣṭhasthāna. ॥36॥
2.5.58.37: Protect us, the dwellers of this holy place, from other calamities as well; driving away the wicked, O Lord of Gaurī, grant fearlessness to your devotees. ॥37॥
2.5.58.38: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words of the devotees, the moon-crested one, loving to his devotees, said so be it and spoke again to the devotees. ॥38॥
2.5.58.39: Maheśvara said: Whoever beholds me here in this form with faith, I shall without doubt cast down the onset of calamities upon him. ॥39॥
2.5.58.40: A mortal who hears this story of mine and remembers this liṅga in his heart, when entering battle, attains victory without doubt. ॥40॥
2.5.58.41: Meanwhile the gods, together with Indra (Vāsava), arrived, shouting victory and leading a great festive celebration. ॥41॥
2.5.58.42: All the gods bowed to Śaṅkara with love, with joined palms and bent shoulders, and praised with fine words the Lord who is loving to his devotees. ॥42॥
2.5.58.43: The gods said: Victory to you, Śaṅkara, lord of the gods, remover of the distress of those who bow to you, O Lord! By the slaying of this Dundubhinirhrāda we gods have been protected. ॥43॥
2.5.58.44: O you who love your devotees, you should always protect your devotees; and the wicked should be slain by you, O lord of the gods, lord of all, O Master. ॥44॥
2.5.58.45: Having heard these words of the gods, the Supreme Lord, pleased at heart, said so be it and merged into that liṅga. ॥45॥
2.5.58.46: Then the gods, filled with wonder, joyfully went each to his own abode; and those brāhmaṇas too, in great delight, returned as they had come. ॥46॥
2.5.58.47: Whoever hears this supreme account of the origin of Vyāghreśvara, or causes it to be heard, or reads it, or likewise causes it to be read — ॥47॥
2.5.58.48: that man obtains all the desires wished for in his own mind, and hereafter attains liberation, free from all sorrow. ॥48॥
2.5.58.49: This incomparable narrative, whose syllables are the nectar of Śiva's divine play, leads to heaven, brings fame and long life, and increases sons and grandsons. ॥49॥
2.5.58.50: It is supreme, bestows devotion, is blessed, pleases Śiva, and is auspicious; it grants the highest knowledge, is delightful, and is the supreme remover of mental disturbances. ॥50॥
2.5.58.iti: Thus ends the fifty-eighth adhyāya, named The slaying of the daitya Dundubhinirhrāda, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥58॥
2.5.59.1: Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O Vyāsa, with great delight, to the deed of the Supreme Lord: how he slew the demons through his own beloved, by a signal directed at the demon. ॥1॥
2.5.59.2: Formerly there were two great demons named Vidala and Utpala, who could not be slain by a male, great heroes, extremely arrogant because of a boon from Brahmā (Vidhi). ॥2॥
2.5.59.3: By those two men who, through the strength of their own arms, treated the three worlds like straw—by those two demons, O brahmin, all the gods were defeated in battle. ॥3॥
2.5.59.4: Defeated by those two, the gods went to Vidhi for refuge; bowing to him duly, they all reported the matter respectfully. ॥4॥
2.5.59.5: Then Brahmā said to them: Those two are certainly to be slain by the Goddess. Take courage, reverently remembering Śiva together with Śivā. ॥5॥
2.5.59.6: He who bears the name Affectionate to Devotees, the auspicious Śaṅkara together with Śivā, the Supreme Lord, will bring about your welfare before long. ॥6॥
2.5.59.7: Sanatkumāra said: Having said this to them, Brahmā then fell silent, remembering Śiva. And the gods too, having gained joy, then went each to his own abode. ॥7॥
2.5.59.8: Then the divine sage Nārada, at Śiva's prompting, went to their dwelling and loudly extolled the beauty of Śivā. ॥8॥
2.5.59.9: Hearing his words, the two demons became deluded by illusion; tormented by the god of love (the odd-arrowed one), they longed to carry off the Goddess. ॥9॥
2.5.59.10: Those two pondered: When and where will that Śivā be ours, through the favour of fate that has dawned for us? ॥10॥
2.5.59.11: At one time Śambhu was sporting gracefully, and Śivā, out of playfulness, was playing a game of ball, ॥11॥
2.5.59.12: with her friends, joyfully, for fun, in Śiva's presence. ॥12॥
2.5.59.13: Leaping up, displaying the nimbleness of her bending limbs, her eyes troubled by bees delighted by the fragrance of her breath, ॥13॥
2.5.59.14: the ground before her strewn with fine garlands slipping from her braided hair, shining with drops of moisture trickling from the leaf-designs on her perspiring cheeks, ॥14॥
2.5.59.15: enveloped by the radiance of her limbs streaming out through her bursting bodice, her lotus-hands deeply reddened from striking the bouncing ball, ॥15॥
2.5.59.16: the tips of her creeper-like brows dancing with her lovely gaze that followed the ball—thus Mṛḍānī, the Mother of the world, was seen at play. ॥16॥
2.5.59.17: And she was eyed sidelong by the two sons of Diti roaming in the sky, who were as if already taken onto the lap of Death that had drawn near— ॥17॥
2.5.59.18: by those named Vidala and Utpala, arrogant through Brahmā's boon, who by the strength of their own arms regarded the beings of the three worlds as straw. ॥18॥
2.5.59.19: Desiring to carry off that Goddess, tormented by the god of love, the two swiftly came down from the sky, having adopted the magic of Śambara. ॥19॥
2.5.59.20: Assuming by illusion the guise of Śiva's attendants, those two, utterly wicked and of very restless minds, came near Ambikā. ॥20॥
2.5.59.21: Then, by Hara, the slayer of the wicked, regarding them with contempt, the two were recognised in an instant, because of the restlessness showing in their eyes. ॥21॥
2.5.59.22: Then Durgā, destroyer of misfortune, was given a sidelong glance by the god who is the form of all, meaning: These two are demons, not gaṇas. ॥22॥
2.5.59.23: Then she understood that eye-signal of her own lord, O dear one—of Śaṅkara, the Supreme Lord, who delights in great sport. ॥23॥
2.5.59.24: Then, having understood that signal, she who is half the body of the Omniscient One struck down both of them at once with that very ball. ॥24॥
2.5.59.25: Struck by the great Goddess with the ball, those two mighty wicked ones, whirling round and round, fell down, ॥25॥
2.5.59.26: like two ripe fruits falling from their stalk on a palm tree shaken by the wind, or like two peaks of a great mountain struck by the thunderbolt. ॥26॥
2.5.59.27: Having felled those two great demons who were bent on doing what should not be done, the ball then transformed into the form of a liṅga. ॥27॥
2.5.59.28: That liṅga then became known as Kandukeśvara, near Jyeṣṭheśvara, warding off all evil ones. ॥28॥
2.5.59.29: At that very time the gods headed by Hari and Brahmā, and the sages, learning of the manifestation of Śiva (śiva-āvirbhāva), assembled there. ॥29॥
2.5.59.30: Then all the gods, having received boons from Śambhu, went by his command to their own abodes, delighted; and so too the residents of Kāśī. ॥30॥
2.5.59.31: Seeing Śaṅkara together with Ambikā, they joined their palms, bowed, and praised him with devotion and reverence in pleasing words. ॥31॥
2.5.59.32: And Śiva, together with Ambikā, O Vyāsa, the knower of fine sport, affectionate to devotees, having played, went delighted to his own abode with his gaṇas. ॥32॥
2.5.59.33: And the Kandukeśvara liṅga in Kāśī destroys the wicked, and always grants enjoyment and liberation and all desires to the good. ॥33॥
2.5.59.34: Whoever listens to this incomparable narrative with joy, or causes it to be heard, or reads it—whence could he have the fear of sorrow? ॥34॥
2.5.59.35: Having enjoyed here every kind of happiness, manifold and unsurpassed, he attains in the hereafter a divine state, hard to reach even for the gods. ॥35॥
2.5.59.36: Thus, O dear one, I have described to you this most wondrous deed, which shows the affection of Śiva and Śivā for their devotees and brings good to the virtuous. ॥36॥
2.5.59.37: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus and taken leave of Vyāsa, praised by him, my excellent son went through the sky to Kāśī, contemplating the deeds of the moon-crested one. ॥37॥
2.5.59.38: This Yuddhakhaṇḍa within the Rudrasaṃhitā, which yields the fruit of all desires, has been narrated by me to you, O best of sages. ॥38॥
2.5.59.39: This Rudrasaṃhitā has been described by me in full; it is most dear to Sadāśiva and yields the fruits of enjoyment and liberation. ॥39॥
2.5.59.40: Whoever reads this daily—which removes the harassment of enemies—obtains all desires, and then that man attains liberation. ॥40॥
2.5.59.41: Sūta said: Thus the son of Brahmā Nārada, having heard from his father the supreme glory of Śiva and having received the hundred names of Śambhu, became fulfilled, a follower of Śiva. ॥41॥
2.5.59.42: The dialogue of Brahmā and Nārada has been narrated by me in full. Śiva indeed is foremost of all; what more do you wish to hear? ॥42॥
2.5.59.iti: Thus ends the fifty-ninth adhyāya, named The slaying of the daityas Vidala and Utpala, in the fifth khaṇḍa, the Yuddha-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥59॥
